Consequences: Sumeru is sealed by a barrier, Nahida is in a coma under Apep's care, and the Seven Pillars have agreed to open Aaru. Liloupar is awake and has stopped the Jinn. The allies go on to prepare Aaru for modification.

Placement: Song of the Welkin Moon Act IX, following True Moon and preceding Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution. Released in version 6.6 (Luna VII, 2026-05-20). The wiki lists Adventure Rank 40 as the unlock requirement.

130.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: Irminsul anomaly and the Sumeru barrier
130.content: Something prevents Irminsul from recording and processing information, which disrupts the ley lines. Nahida takes over its functions and collapses. Near Yasna Monument the anomaly drives civilians to violence, and abnormal Ley Line Blossoms appear. A barrier then closes around Sumeru, which Nicole says is a ley line defence to isolate Irminsul. The Traveler is unaffected by the Irminsul anomaly.

131.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: Akasha System restart plan
131.content: Because Irminsul can still be reached from outside, Alhaitham and the others plan to restart the Akasha System, built to cleanse Irminsul of Abyssal forbidden knowledge. It needs a replacement for the Dendro Gnosis that once powered it. Scholars search the Temple of Silence's records while the Eremites move civilians to Aaru Village. The plan later turns to opening Aaru.

132.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: Liloupar awakened in Gurabad
132.content: Searching for Liloupar, the Traveler and Jeht open the entrance to Gurabad at Safhe Shatranj and find her nearby. She says she fought the Abyss until Gosoythoth's defeat in Natlan ended its pressure there, then slept. Learning of Sumeru's trouble she pacifies the Jinn and ends the sandstorms.

133.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: The Seven Pillars agree to open Aaru
133.content: In the Mausoleum of King Deshret the group meets Thoth, Heryshaf and Sobek. Nefer's answer to Thoth's earlier question, "time", is accepted as her own and frees all three. Heryshaf calls Shesepankh and Bennu. With Cyno speaking for Hermanubis and Apep already helping Nahida, the Seven Pillars agree to open Aaru. Jebrael emerges and passes to the ley lines as a Sacred Ibis.

134.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: Collei's god remains and Nabu Malikata
134.content: The voice that has been guiding Collei turns out to be Nicole's. Under Nicole's instruction Collei recites a prayer written by Nabu Malikata to make the Jinn submit, and Nicole later reveals that the god remains Dottore injected into Collei were Nabu Malikata's. Cyno reassures Collei that she remains herself.

key: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason
Like the Faint Moonlight of Yesteryear
The Truth, Lost With the Rain
When All Return to the Waters
135.comment: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason
135.content:
As Light Rain Falls Without Reason (also: Chapter IV Act II, Like the Faint Moonlight of Yesteryear, The Truth, Lost With the Rain, When All Return to the Waters): The second act of Fontaine's Archon Quest. The Traveler and Paimon join Navia of Spina di Rosula in tracing the serial disappearances of young women, which prove to be people dissolved into Primordial Seawater and tied to the death of Navia's father Callas. The case ends in a trial that exposes the culprit, Marcel, after which the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale returns a "Guilty" verdict against the Fatui Harbinger Tartaglia (Childe).

The act has three quests: Like the Faint Moonlight of Yesteryear, The Truth, Lost With the Rain, and When All Return to the Waters. It is a detective story set in the Court of Fontaine and Poisson, and it is where the Traveler learns that Primordial Seawater dissolves Fontainians and that an Oceanid can hold a dissolved girl's memories.

Plot: After the trial of Act I, the Traveler and Paimon dine at Hotel Debord with Navia, who distrusts the Garde and wants a fresh angle on the disappearances. That evening at the Fountain of Lucine the Traveler is drawn into a dream-like link with an Oceanid, a former girl who has lost most of her memory and asks for someone called Vacher. She asks that Vacher be told to forget her. Back in the real world the Traveler finds Navia, Silver and Melus fighting a swarm of unregistered clockwork meka, and Clorinde helps them. Navia works out that her Fonta at the hotel had been spiked with Primordial Seawater (it tasted salty, and Paimon drank it by mistake), and the Traveler and Paimon fully join her investigation.

Navia explains that three years earlier her father Callas, head of Spina di Rosula, was accused of killing his friend Jacques and chose to duel rather than stand trial, dying at Clorinde's hand. She believes the murder and the disappearances are linked. Vacher has no public records, and Neuvillette's case archives have nothing on him either. Rain on the day of the conviction and on the night of the murder suggests to the Traveler that the real killer may have dissolved into water. Melus reveals that Callas knew he was dying and had been fighting the Sinthe drink trade, which Navia now concludes was made with Primordial Seawater. Melus names three suspects (Florent, Thierry, Marcel). After talking to them and to Jacques' family, the Traveler concludes that Marcel, the only one wealthy enough to afford private meka, is the likely culprit.

When the authorities accuse Tartaglia of the disappearances, the Traveler infiltrates the underwater Sinthe production facility while Navia accuses Marcel in court. His arguments nearly succeed, until Navia names Vacher and he reacts. In the facility the Traveler finds proof that Vacher ran the experiments, plus a notebook of Vacher's lover Vigneire containing the name Marcel, chosen for a child they never had. Marcel is exposed as Vacher; he blames a system that laughed off his reports of people dissolving.

Revelations: The disappearing girls were dissolved into Primordial Seawater, which turns Fontainians into water, and the Oceanids keep fragments of the people they were. Sinthe was made with Primordial Seawater. Marcel was really Vacher, who experimented on the victims, and Callas's duel was a deliberate sacrifice. Rain is repeatedly tied to the dissolving.

Characters: Navia leads the investigation, driven by grief for Callas. Melus, who had withheld some of Callas's secrets, and Silver fight alongside her. Clorinde, the Champion Duelist who killed Callas in the duel he chose and whom he asked to keep Navia safe, protects Navia. Neuvillette presides in court and holds to court rules despite doubts. Furina sits in the trial; Sedene lets the group into Neuvillette's office at Palais Mermonia. Marcel is the culprit. Tartaglia is accused and then found guilty by the machine.

Consequences: Callas's honour is restored and Navia reconciles with Clorinde. Tartaglia is apprehended by the Gardemeks; later acts of Chapter IV follow what happens to him. Neuvillette promises to look into the verdict himself.

Placement: Chapter IV Act II, added in version 4.0. It follows Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur and precedes To the Stars Shining in the Depths. Story order equals release order.

136.comment: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason: Marcel and Vacher
136.content: In As Light Rain Falls Without Reason, Marcel, a wealthy man who moved to Fontaine after the disappearances began, is revealed to be Vacher, the man behind the dissolving of the girls. Marcel was the name his lover Vigneire picked for the child they never had. The Oceanid at the Fountain of Lucine that he finally meets is the merged consciousness of the women he dissolved together with Vigneire, and it drowns him.

137.comment: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason: Sinthe
137.content: A recreational drink popular in Fontaine around the time of Callas's trial. Navia concludes it was made with Primordial Seawater, and long-term drinkers showed signs of drug dependence that hurt their families. Callas banned it from his group.

138.comment: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason: Callas's duel
138.content: Three years before the act, Callas, head of Spina di Rosula, was accused of killing his friend Jacques and chose a duel over a trial. He kept fighting after he was hurt enough to lose, and Clorinde killed him. She says he asked her to keep Navia safe and that she could tell he wanted to die. Neuvillette later admits he let the duel proceed because he thought an innocent man would not die for justice.

139.content:
Astrolabos Chapter (also: Mona's Story Quest, Beyond This World's Stars, Astrology and the 50-Year Pact): Mona's Story Quest. A broke astrologer who knows the Traveler is not from Teyvat offers to read their fate if they help her reclaim a box her master left in Mondstadt. They travel from Liyue to Mondstadt, where the box's guardian turns out to be Klee, and Mona ends up renting a sealed laboratory.

The chapter has one act, Beyond This World's Stars, of three quests: Astrology and the 50-Year Pact, To Mondstadt and A Bewildering Fate. It was released in version 1.0 and unlocks at Adventure Rank 38 after Darknight Hero's Alibi (Noctua Chapter) and True Treasure (Trifolium Chapter).

Plot: Outside Liyue Harbor Mona meets the Traveler and Paimon and says that, as a disciple, the Traveler can help her win a contest of astrology. She takes them through Liyue and over the Stone Gate to Mondstadt. There she names Klee as the guardian of her master's box, but the box holds only Klee's treasures; the real contents were a diary. Mona rents a sealed lab from Goth.

Astrology and the 50-Year Pact: Mona knows the Traveler is not of Teyvat. She wants to confront the guardian of her box to prove the power of astrology and thinks having a "disciple" helps. Before leaving she visits Mr. Zhu's inn, where he offers 20,000 Mora to find a ring a slime took. Mona first refuses, then agrees at the price. The Traveler uses leftover slime bait from the Darknight Hero's affair to draw the slimes, finds the ring and gives it back; Mona grabs the Mora, saying they must act the part of disciples.

To Mondstadt: at Wangshu Inn, Mona offers to treat them but is horrified at the cost; the Traveler and Paimon order many dishes while she asks for plain noodles. Her stomach betrays her. The Traveler cooks Golden Crab for her using a recipe from Huai'an, and she is delighted. On the road Tyler and some merchants offer them a ride, but Mona identifies them as bandits and defeats them herself. She says she reads Teyvat's people at a glance, whereas the Traveler is like an impenetrable fog to her.

A Bewildering Fate: in Mondstadt City, Klee arrives. Mona asks if her mother is Alice, then asks what she taught her; Klee knows only how to make Jumpy Dumpties. Klee remembers a fifty-year agreement and a box. The Traveler helps fetch it from Windrise, fighting Dendro slimes. Meanwhile Mona reads a diary that fell from Klee's bag. The box proves to hold only Klee's treasures, and the book is Mona's master's own diary, which she was told never to read. Klee flees. With no Mora or lab, Mona accepts help from Katheryne's commission board and dispels a Hydro seal on a house by astrology. The owner, Goth, rents it to her cheaply.

Revelations: The box guardian is Klee, and the box's original content was Mona's master's diary.

Mona is a friend of Klee's mother, per Mona's own question about Alice. She cannot read the Traveler's fate as she does others.

Characters: Mona, the Traveler, Paimon and Klee.

Katheryne and Goth in Mondstadt; Mr. Zhu, Yuhua and Huai'an in Liyue; Tyler and his bandit group.

Consequences: Mona now rents a lab in Mondstadt, though she can only look into the Traveler's fate later. Paimon suggests checking on her from time to time.

Placement: Requires Adventure Rank 38 and both Darknight Hero's Alibi (Noctua Chapter) and True Treasure (Trifolium Chapter). The wiki notes Paimon reusing slime bait from the Darknight Hero story. Released in 1.0.

140.content: At the end of Mona's Story Quest she dispels a Hydro seal on an abandoned house with astrology. Its owner Goth then rents it to her at the lowest possible price, giving her a laboratory in Mondstadt.

141.content:
Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves (also: Chapter II Prologue, Inazuma Prologue, The Crux Clash, A Path Through the Storm, Follow the Wind): Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves is the prologue act of Archon Quest Chapter II, released in Version 1.6, and it is set in Liyue, at Liyue Harbor and Guyun Stone Forest. The Traveler wants to reach Inazuma, which is sealed off by storms and a strict isolation policy, and is sent to the Crux Fleet captain Beidou, who runs a tournament for fighters without Visions. The Traveler wins it, and in the process meets Kazuha, a wandering crew member who carries the Vision of a dead friend.

The act is a three-quest lead-in: A Path Through the Storm, The Crux Clash and Follow the Wind. It contains no Inazuman locations and no Electro Archon; its purpose is to set up the voyage (the prize is a berth on the Alcor) and to introduce Kazuha, who becomes a major figure in the Inazuma story.

Plot: Atsuko explains that besides the storm, outsiders face the Sakoku Decree and the authorities who would hunt them if found, but she cannot dissuade the Traveler and recommends Beidou. At the Alcor, anchored at Guyun Stone Forest, Beidou introduces a temporary crew member, Kazuha, and mistakes the Traveler for a tournament entrant. The Crux Clash is a martial contest for fighters without Visions. Its prize is a Masterless Vision supplied by Kazuha, who hopes the winner will reawaken it. The Traveler is not interested in the Vision, so Beidou adds a second option: the winner may choose the Vision or a ride to Inazuma on the Alcor.

At the arena, Zhuhan of the crew handles registration and is startled to see the Traveler who helped Liyue against an ancient god; the Traveler must prove they have no Vision. The first opponent, Jinyou, is easily beaten without elemental powers, and Beidou sends the Traveler straight to the semi-finals because so many new challengers now want to fight them. The semi-final opponent, Rongshi, is harder; he is not after the prize, only a worthy fight, and he accepts defeat humbly and asks for a rematch someday.

Nobody can say much about the finalist except that they are fast. Kazuha takes the Traveler somewhere quiet, reveals he already knows the Traveler can use elemental power without a Vision and, when the Traveler cannot explain how, tests them against slimes, and gives advice on the finalist's style and a little background on Inazuma and its Electro Archon.

Revelations: - The Vision Hunt Decree exists: the Raiden Shogun is confiscating Visions, and Kazuha's friend lost a duel before the throne opposing it and was struck down by divine punishment.
- Kazuha is a temporary Alcor crew member; the next act shows he is still a wanted fugitive, which keeps Beidou from lingering in port with him aboard.
- Masterless Visions, Visions whose bearers have died, are said to have reawakened for other people.
- Inazuma is hard to reach: a permanent storm, the Sakoku Decree, and pursuit by authorities.

Characters: - **The Traveler and Paimon**: decide to go to Inazuma; the Traveler wins the tournament without a Vision.
- **Beidou**: captain of the Crux Fleet's flagship Alcor, who runs the Crux Clash.
- **Kazuha**: a temporary Alcor crew member who carries a dead friend's Vision.
- **Atsuko**: an Inazuman in Liyue Harbor, the only Inazuman the Traveler has met, who warns them about the trip.
- **Zhuhan**: crew member who registers tournament entrants.
- **Jinyou, Rongshi**: the Traveler's tournament opponents; Rongshi is a fighter who wanted only a challenge.
- **Fei the Flyer**: a Treasure Hoarder who steals the Vision.

Consequences: The Traveler is champion and has a berth on the Alcor, which sails after resupplying. Kazuha keeps the Masterless Vision and sets out through Liyue to find someone who can reawaken it. The next act, The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia, begins with the sailing.

Placement: Released in Version 1.6 as the Prologue of Chapter II, before Inazuma opened in Version 2.0. It follows Chapter I Act IV, We Will Be Reunited, and leads into Chapter II Act I, The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia (Version 2.0). Story order and release order match.

142.comment: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves: The Crux Clash
142.content: A tournament held by Beidou at an arena in Guyun Stone Forest, where the Alcor is anchored, for renowned fighters without Visions. The prize is a Masterless Vision supplied by Kazuha; for the Traveler, Beidou adds a ride to Inazuma as an alternative. Entrants are registered by Zhuhan. The Traveler beats Jinyou and Rongshi, and wins the title when the finalist, Fei the Flyer, is disqualified for stealing the prize.

143.comment: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves: Kazuha's Masterless Vision
143.content: Kazuha carries the Vision of a friend who opposed the Vision Hunt Decree, lost a duel before the throne and suffered the Raiden Shogun's divine punishment. He offers it as the tournament prize in the hope that a new bearer will reawaken it. The Traveler and Fei both fail to resonate with it, so Kazuha keeps it. Later events in Inazuma decide its fate; this act does not.

144.comment: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves: Fei the Flyer
144.content: A Treasure Hoarder who entered the Crux Clash intending to win, then stole the Vision after watching the Traveler fight. Kazuha traced him and the Traveler beat him. Kazuha threatens him with harsh punishment, partly to test whether pressure would awaken the Vision, then lets him go and takes the Vision back.

145.comment: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves: Atsuko's Warning
145.content: Atsuko, the Inazuman the Traveler already knows in Liyue Harbor, tells them the storm is only part of the danger. Inazuma's isolation policy and the authorities who would pursue illegal entrants are the rest. She yields when the Traveler is determined and sends them to Beidou, whose seafaring experience may get a ship through.

key: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog
The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light
146.comment: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog
146.content:
Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog (also: The Warrior Dog, Mystery of the Black Shadow, Stealthy Trail, The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light, Black Shadow case, Ubiquity Net event): Four case files unlock over several days. In each, Ryuuji marks camps in the wild; at some the Traveler fights Treasure Hoarders and other armed groups to free caged animals, and at others must sneak past the dog using a gadget, the Ubiquity Net, which Sango had made and which can catch small animals but is too weak for criminals. The final file explains the Hoarders' plan, introduces the dog's true name Kageroumaru, and ends with Kageroumaru accepting the Traveler as his ninken.

Plot: Case 1, "Mystery of the Black Shadow": the first camp is guarded by the dog; Ryuuji places smoke and fireworks devices to help the Traveler sneak in. A second camp is held by Treasure Hoarders and other armed groups. Case 2, "Stealthy Trail": Ryuuji marks new camps from Sango's deductions and, as an example of her method, recounts an earlier theft case in which the thief was caught because he sold fresh Naku Weed; Sango had reasoned he would not leave Narukami Island because boat travel was policed under the Sakoku Decree. Case 3, "The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light": the leads run cold with only about half the animals found, and Ryuuji reports Sango's puzzling instructions to investigate odd places. Case 4, "Recognition": Sango sends the Traveler to meet Ryuuji, who has been scouting Yashiori Island, where the Hoarders have just left a camp of cages behind.

Revelations: Two separate groups were behind the disappearances: Treasure Hoarders who held animals in "Dens of Thieves", and the dog Kageroumaru, who kept animals in "Hiding Spots". Kageroumaru's past as a ninken trainer's abandoned pup is revealed only through the letter in the last file. The event itself offers no confirmed reason why he hid the animals.

Characters: Sango is the agency's detective who prefers to think rather than walk; her stance is that her "flesh is an accessory to her mind". Ryuuji is her polite, practical investigator whose skill is running errands, not stealth or combat. He admits being bested by the dog and gives it nicknames such as "Hat Dog" that Paimon dislikes. Katheryne relays the commission. Paimon is awed by the bounty and persuaded by the animals' plight. Kageroumaru is a masked dog who resembles the Komore Teahouse owner Taroumaru; Ryuuji warns that, unlike Taroumaru, nothing is known about him. Ryuuji also mentions Shikanoin of the Tenryou Commission, whom the agency met before and whom he thinks can follow Sango's reasoning.

Consequences: The animals are returned to their owners by Ryuuji, the Treasure Hoarders' dog-training plan is exposed, and the Traveler gains Kageroumaru as a reward item. Sango considers the case closed.

Placement: Released in Version 2.3 and set after the Inazuma Archon Quest chapter's Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia, which is its only requirement. Not needed for any Archon Quest.

147.comment: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog: Kageroumaru
147.content: Kageroumaru is a scarred, masked dog introduced as the "Black Shadow" in the Bantan Sango Case Files event. He was a weak puppy overlooked when ninja chose ninken, then grew strong. He guards caged small animals and attacks intruders, and finally accepts the Traveler as his master after being defeated. The wiki lists Kageroumaru as an event reward.

148.comment: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog: Bantan Sango Detective Agency staff
148.content: In this event the agency is represented by Sango, a deductive-minded detective who stays behind and issues commissions, and Ryuuji, her investigator. Sango had a friend build the Ubiquity Net from records of Kamuna Onmyoudou.

149.comment: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog: Treasure Hoarder dog-training plan
149.content: In the final case file, Ryuuji says Sango deduced that the Hoarders planned to steal dogs to train as Treasure Hunting Hounds, after weasels proved too difficult to train. Their camps appear as Dens of Thieves in the event.

key: Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards
150.comment: Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards
150.content:
Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards (also: Come Try Genius Invokation TCG!, Genius Invokation TCG introduction quest): The quest begins in Mondstadt's alchemy shop, where Sucrose has received a package of strange cards from a Sumeru scholar. Timaeus explains that they belong to a popular game and sends the group to The Cat's Tail. There Margaret's staff, the cat Prince and his translator Shuyun, arrange a tutorial with Diona and a three-duel test. The tone is comic and light, and it works as an in-world welcome to the game.

Plot: Timaeus and Sucrose are discussing a package Sucrose received, probably a thank-you gift from a Sumeru scholar who had studied in Mondstadt. It contains only cards, among them one showing Sucrose herself. When the Traveler and Paimon join, Timaeus explains that these are cards for Genius Invokation TCG, a game said to have been invented by an Akademiya scholar and now popular everywhere. He admits he has been reading a light-novel series based on it, and he has promised himself not to touch the game until his research is further along, so he recommends The Cat's Tail, where players gather to play and trade.

At the tavern Margaret mentions that more TCG players now come in and that she has put Prince, her cat, and Shuyun in charge of looking after them. Shuyun claims to understand Prince's meows and passes on his remarks, including lofty refusals to play himself. Margaret hands the teaching to Diona, who grumbles that the game encourages drinking yet agrees once Shuyun argues that it might actually help her campaign against Mondstadt's wine trade. Sucrose, Paimon and the Traveler have no proper deck, so Diona lends them a pair of character cards a customer left behind. She walks them through a first game, in which the player controls Diluc, covering dice, skills, elemental reactions and winning by defeating all of the opponent's characters. Sucrose and the Traveler then play a practice duel against each other, and Sucrose loses and takes it a little hard.

Shuyun explains that becoming an official player recognised by the Genius Invokation TCG Society requires beating three opponents; the practice duel counts toward the tally. Everyone starting out gets a free Casket of Tomes, which Margaret hands over. The Casket can sense other nearby Caskets, which leads the Traveler to a Knight of Favonius named Swan on duty at the city entrance. Swan agrees to duel and loses. Prince, via Shuyun, chooses the final opponent: Fischl, who is also a beginner with two wins. The Traveler beats her. Fischl gives the Traveler her own Character Card as a prize, and Sucrose, who has won two games herself, joins Fischl for a game. Shuyun then explains what official players get: a TCG Player's Handbook, access to Genius Invokation merchandise at The Cat's Tail and the Invitation Board for challenging friends.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Sucrose, an alchemist who gets involved through the package; Timaeus, her colleague, who introduces the game; Margaret, owner of The Cat's Tail; Diona, a bartender at the tavern who teaches the tutorial; Prince and Shuyun, the tavern's cat and his translator who run the TCG corner; Swan, a Knight of Favonius and opponent; and Fischl with her companion Oz, the final opponent. Diluc appears only as a character card.

Consequences: The Traveler becomes an official TCG player: the TCG mode opens, and the Traveler receives the Casket of Tomes, a tutorial deck and Fischl's Character Card. Quest rewards are 60 Primogems, 2 Hero's Wit, 20,000 Mora, the Casket of Tomes and a Beginner Player Badge. Completing it also grants the achievement Visible, Yet Invisible.

Placement: Released in Version 3.3 together with the TCG's introduction. It requires Adventure Rank 30 and the Prologue's Act III, Song of the Dragon and Freedom. It is a self-contained comic quest and not part of the Archon Quests; the next quest, A Guest From Liyue, starts immediately after.

151.comment: Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards: Genius Invokation TCG tutorial at The Cat's Tail
151.content: In Mondstadt, Genius Invokation TCG is taught and played at The Cat's Tail, where Margaret keeps a corner for players. To be recognised by the Genius Invokation TCG Society a newcomer must win duels against three opponents; each new player receives a Casket of Tomes, which senses other nearby Caskets and so helps players find each other. The tavern staff Prince the cat and Shuyun, his translator, oversee new players.

152.content:
Bedtime Story (also: Chapter IV Act VI, Vimara Village missing-person case): Bedtime Story is the sixth and final act of Chapter IV, the Traveler's Archon Quest chapter (version 4.7). A commission from Katheryne in Sumeru City asks for help finding a missing man from Vimara Village whom no one can name. Investigating, the Traveler and Paimon meet Dainsleif, who tells them about the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, and finally meet Caribert, Chlothar Alberich's son, whose residual consciousness is tied to the Loom of Fate.

The act has three quests: Cold Case Commission, Memories That Should Not Exist and World-Order Narration. It requires Adventure Rank 40. It resolves the missing-person mystery, explains what the Loom of Fate is, and gives the Traveler a conversation with their sibling that they will not remember.

Plot: Katheryne passes the Traveler a joint commission from Vimara Village: find a missing person. A dozen attempts have failed and nobody can give his name. Villagers describe a kind young man in his early twenties who kept the elderly company and played with orphans. Atossa takes the Traveler to a tree where they talked for hours each dusk, though the sun never seemed to move. A Pyro Abyss Mage attacks them, and the hilichurls near the village are agitated.

Dainsleif, who is investigating the Abyss Order, reveals that the voice heard earlier is Vedrfolnir, his older brother and one of the Five Sinners, together with Rhinedottir, Surtalogi, Rerir and Hroptatyr. He blames them for not defending their nation in the cataclysm. He also notes that the Loom of Fate operation continues without the eye of the first Field Tiller. A memory that does not belong to him appears, in which he gives that eye to the missing man. He realises the man may implant memories and that the Abyss Order is tailing him, and sends the Traveler and Paimon back to Vimara Village. The sibling then approaches Dainsleif alone, and Dainsleif says he went along with the trap knowing it was the only way to meet them face to face.

Back in the village the hilichurls are calm and nobody remembers the commission. The Traveler finds Atossa with a stranger, Caribert, who leads them into his consciousness. There he explains that the Loom of Fate in its primitive form creates and implants memories, and when fully unlocked creates Ley Lines and can change the world. The village life was his own doing, a chance at the life he was denied. He reveals the Loom is complete: Dainsleif had kept the eye inside his own body, planning to lure the Abyss Order to a false location, confront the sibling and pass the eye to the Traveler, but Caribert implanted a false memory of Dainsleif already handing it over, so the Abyss Order obtained it. His real goal was to tell the hilichurls a calming bedtime story through implanted memory, as his father once did for him; with it finished, he fades peacefully. The sibling appears but cannot be touched; they tell the Traveler they are racing to unlock the Loom's full potential before the Heavenly Principles awaken, say they miss the Traveler, and admit they struggle to face themselves as their war goes on. Caribert's memory collapses. The Traveler wakes in the village remembering nothing of the talk, holding a photograph of themselves, the sibling and Caribert.

Revelations: - The Sinner's voice belongs to Vedrfolnir, "the Visionary", Dainsleif's older brother and one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, alongside Rhinedottir, Surtalogi, Rerir and Hroptatyr.
- Dainsleif holds the other Sinners responsible for not defending Khaenri'ah when the cataclysm came.
- The Loom of Fate is a device whose primitive form creates and implants memories and whose full form creates Ley Lines and changes the world.
- Caribert, son of Chlothar Alberich, was used to construct the Loom and survives only as residual consciousness tied to it; he built the Vimara Village life for himself and calmed the hilichurls with a bedtime story.
- Dainsleif had carried the first Field Tiller's eye inside his body; a false memory implanted by Caribert let the Abyss Order obtain it.
- The sibling is rushing to finish the Loom before the Heavenly Principles awaken, which did not happen when the Divine Throne of Hydro was destroyed.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, Dainsleif, the sibling, Caribert, Katheryne, Atossa, Bahram, Amadhiah and a Pyro Abyss Mage. The Five Sinners are named; Vedrfolnir is a voice rather than a speaker.

Consequences: Caribert says the Loom of Fate is completed. The Traveler's meeting with the sibling is erased from their memory but a photograph remains. Dainsleif, having lost the eye, is left injured and preoccupied after facing the sibling. Chapter V follows in Natlan.

Placement: Chapter IV, Act VI (final act), released in 4.7. It follows Masquerade of the Guilty and precedes Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn (Chapter V Act I). The Caribert act (3.5) showed Caribert as Chlothar Alberich's son in the sibling's memories; here he refers to that memory himself.

153.comment: Bedtime Story: Caribert and the Loom of Fate
153.content: Caribert, Chlothar Alberich's son, was used to construct the sibling's Loom of Fate and survives as residual consciousness tied to it. Through the half-finished Loom he created a false life in Vimara Village with memories implanted in the villagers, and gave the hilichurls a calming bedtime story. He explains that a fully unlocked Loom weaves Ley Lines and can change the world, and he fades away peacefully as the sibling arrives.

154.comment: Bedtime Story: Dainsleif on the Five Sinners
154.content: Dainsleif names the Sinner as his older brother Vedrfolnir, the Visionary, and lists Rhinedottir, Surtalogi, Rerir and Hroptatyr. He blames them for abandoning Khaenri'ah and says he will not forgive them, though his memories erode.

key: Beneath the Lunar Sea world quest
155.content:
Beneath the Lunar Sea (also: Beneath the Lunar Sea world quest, Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab quest): A Frost Moon world quest from Version 6.7 (Luna VIII). A frightened kuuhenki and a crowd of moonglow jellyfish lead the Traveler and Paimon to a sealed, dragon-built facility beneath the Moontide Sea, the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab. Restoring its power opens the way to a hidden chamber with a great blue tree.

The quest is a short, mostly exploratory scene with almost no story revelation. Its practical effect is to unlock an Ancient Moon's Remnant (the Frost Moon's reputation-style monument) at the lab, and it ends with the Traveler loading the facility's map from a terminal.

Plot: Paimon spots a scared kuuhenki, and after the Traveler beats the monster harassing it, the creature guides them toward a cave. Jellyfish crowd into the cave too. Inside is a locked facility; the Traveler finds how to open it, gets the power back on and enters.

The kuuhenki leads the pair twice, each time after the Traveler defeats a hostile construct (a Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network). Paimon is uneasy that the place is hiding something, then reads the sign at the entrance, a Blackbody Containment "Generation Station", which she has never heard of. She decides a place like that must hold treasure.

Inside, a door to the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment stays shut until an Ancient Moon Pearl is returned to its station. The Traveler frees trapped moonglow jellyfish, switches on a backup power generator and the Archaeolune-affinitive materials, and opens an energy barrier on the ceiling with Archaeolune Ripples. A lift lowers a storage chest but the pearl does not drop, so the Traveler must fire the pearl back to its station with a launcher to open the door.

Revelations: No question is answered in the quest itself. It establishes only that a dragon-era installation survives under the Moontide Sea, that its machinery still takes Archaeolune Energy, and that it is guarded by constructs. Paimon does not know what the name means.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon. The only other presences are a frightened kuuhenki, moonglow jellyfish and the facility's guardian constructs.

Paimon supplies all the dialogue: curiosity, treasure-hunting optimism and a growing sense that the place is hiding something. The kuuhenki are small creatures of Archaeolune Energy native to the Frost Moon.

Consequences: Completing the quest is required to unlock the Ancient Moon's Remnant at the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab, a Moontide Sea monument where Luna Sigils can be offered, and gives the map of the facility. No lasting change in the world or to any character follows.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII, 2026-07-01) with the Frost Moon map. It is part of the Frost Moon exploration content that accompanies the Moon Gazing series, and the wiki marks no formal prerequisite or next quest. In story terms it takes place after the Traveler has reached the Frost Moon and before or alongside the Moontide Sea events of Moon Gazing's second and third acts.

key: Between Pledge and Forgettance World Quest series
156.content:
Between Pledge and Forgettance (also: Between Pledge and Forgettance World Quest series, Little One's volcano pilgrimage quests, Rite of the Bold, Revelations from the Past): Between Pledge and Forgettance (5.0) is a three-quest Natlan world series: Lost in the Woods, Rite of the Bold and Revelations from the Past. The Traveler and Paimon free a hurt young Tepetlisaurus from a barrier, travel with it, and learn from the researcher Manqu that the red mark on its horn is the Flamelord's Blessing, a power that often kills or maddens saurians as they grow. A volcano pilgrimage with two tokens is the only known remedy. Chief Pacal of the Children of Echoes grants the first token after a duel, and the ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame yield the first Golden Entreaty after trials in which human and saurian must act as a pair. The series is tied to a deliberate design by the Sage that only the later Natlan quests expose.

Plot: Lost in the Woods. Shining pillars scattered around Natlan pull the Traveler and Paimon into a strange space full of Rifthounds. After the fight, a dying giant saurian addresses golden words to a "Chosen of Dragons" and, as the Traveler reaches out, the Traveler's consciousness enters the beast's body (a Saurian Indwelling). Using it, the Traveler breaks a rock that holds a trapped saurian whelp. Paimon bandages its tail with a scarf, and the whelp agrees to travel with the party. The player names it; the default name is Little One.

Rite of the Bold. Manqu, a researcher of the Saurian Relics Association, warns the party that the red mark on the whelp's horn is the Flamelord's Blessing, which saurians no longer survive well in the modern age, and that the Wayob and the Night Kingdom reject such saurians. He suggests handing it to the Children of Echoes, but when the Traveler refuses to abandon a companion, he reveals a legend: a warrior must bring the saurian to the volcano carrying a token that was split in two. Chief Pacal and Manqu then explain the pilgrimage custom. Pacal waives the old rituals of feather, pelts, fifty victories and ninety-six gems and instead tests the Traveler and Little One in a duel, with his own saurian Uchu fighting beside him. Defeated, he gives them the Talisman of Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, a name of the Sage of the Stolen Flame.

Revelations from the Past. At the ruins entrance, Abyss-tainted Rifthounds attack. Placing the talisman starts the Sage's trial. The Traveler and Little One are split between two viewpoints in the ruins. They solve puzzles using colour-coded crystals, cross a lava stretch, and enter Catastrophe's Edge, where they fight off enemies from the Abyss. At the end they receive the first Golden Entreaty.

Revelations: - The Flamelord's Blessing is real and dangerous: in Manqu's account it is a power of the old dragons that modern saurians cannot withstand, and the pilgrimage is the only remedy.
- The Sage of the Stolen Flame and the first Pyro Archon each brought back one token from the volcano; whoever holds both can enter the cleansing fire. Pacal says the Sage seems to appear in tales from the tribal era to Ochkanatlan and beyond.
- The Sage's murals imply he was a dragon, and show the Sage and Xbalanque each holding a golden disc.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon travel with Little One, a young Tepetlisaurus who speaks only in growls. Manqu of the Saurian Relics Association is the scholarly guide. Pacal, chief of the Children of Echoes, is jovial, strong and protective of guests. His saurian is Uchu. Titu is mentioned as someone who spoke highly of the Traveler. The Sage of the Stolen Flame (Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, later revealed as Kukulkan) appears only through golden text.

Consequences: The Traveler holds the first Golden Entreaty and gains the avatar "Your Saurian companion!". Little One stays with the party. The second Entreaty comes from Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm. Offering both is the next step towards the volcano (see Path to the Flaming Peaks and A Finale Emberforged). The series also opens the many Little One side quests in In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons.

Placement: Released in 5.0 with Natlan. In story order Lost in the Woods usually comes first, Rite of the Bold after the party has spent time in Natlan, and Revelations from the Past last. The series connects directly to Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm (the next chapter), Path to the Flaming Peaks, Chronicler of the Crumbling City and A Finale Emberforged, which resolve it.

157.comment: Between Pledge and Forgettance: Talisman of Waxaklahun Ubah Kan
157.content: The Talisman of Waxaklahun Ubah Kan is the proof Pacal gives the Traveler after the duel in Rite of the Bold. Waxaklahun Ubah Kan is a name of the Sage of the Stolen Flame, whom later quests reveal to be Kukulkan. Pacal admits he cannot remember the long name. The talisman is placed on a platform at the ruins entrance to open the Sage's trial.

158.comment: Between Pledge and Forgettance: Flamelord's Blessing
158.content: The Flamelord's Blessing is the red mark on Little One's horn. In Manqu's explanation it grants strength, swimming speed or leaping, but is not the saurian's own power. It is the strength of the ancient dragons, which modern saurians cannot bear, so growth can kill them or drive them mad. The Wayob and the Night Kingdom refuse to accept saurians marked this way. The Flamelord is the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, Xiuhcoatl.

159.comment: Between Pledge and Forgettance: Volcanic pilgrimage
159.content: The old pilgrimage required a warrior and saurian to be recognised by the saurian's tribal chief, who for Tepetlisauri is the chief of the Children of Echoes. The ritual tasks Manqu lists include a green quetzal feather, a stole of pelts, fifty victories for the tribe and ninety-six gems. Pacal drops them and fights the Traveler instead, with Uchu, in the duel grounds in the mountain behind the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. He warns that no one has returned from this road.

160.content:
Beyond Silver and Fine Gold (also: Nicole's treasure hunt, Nicole's Witch's Lodge series): A Version 6.6 world quest series about Nicole. After the Traveler and Paimon unlock her Witch's Lodge in the Witch's Garden, Nicole turns its rooms into a treasure hunt: each of four rooms hides three golden feathers and a chest, and each room opens a week after the last. Between the puzzles she tells stories about her angelic past, the Hexenzirkel and her friends.

The four parts are The Joyous Floating Island, The Silent Theater, The Lost Palace and The Forgotten Lighthouse. They require the earlier Witch's Lodge quest and must be done in order; the next room unlocks at 04:00 on the Monday after the previous one is fully explored, so the series takes four weeks. The tone is light and teasing, but several rooms turn serious about angels, gods and betrayal.

Plot: Nicole invites the Traveler and Paimon to her lodge. She has built a room full of tricks and hidden three feathers in it; finding them reveals a treasure chest. A new room opens each week: a tea party where everyone shrinks, a studio of magic paintings, a shrine of angel statues and a tall study full of books that make stairways when Nicole speaks.

The Joyous Floating Island: Nicole explains she wants a place to have fun and feel useful at once. A door with floating teacups sends the pair into the Great Mage's Tea Party, where they are shrunk to teacup scale. They heat a giant teapot with Pyro, sweeten a cup with three sugar cubes (Nicole mentions Alice takes three, Anya one, Barbeloth none), fend off a statue of a Mandragora Nicole animates, and open the chest.

The Silent Theater: a studio of empty frames. Three paintings pull the pair into scenes Nicole narrates: the day she agreed to join the Hexenzirkel, a love-and-horror tale of a Princess of the Morning Star, and her admiration for Anya and the stories of Simulanka. When each is "restored", the chest opens.

The Lost Palace: Nicole is busy elsewhere (she is selling sculptures at a stall in Fontaine), so she leaves scrolls with riddle hints; the pair arrange statues to follow them. Afterwards Nicole shows them the shrine where she lived as an angel.

The Forgotten Lighthouse: the final room. Nicole tries to explain why she is embarrassed, tells a fragment of the story of the first time the mages challenged the Anemo Archon, and hides the feathers at the top of a study. Words spoken aloud become golden platforms, and the Traveler and Paimon climb to the feathers on the stairs she speaks into existence.

Revelations: Nicole is an angel, a being created to love all living things and to guide and enlighten. She says the angels' emotions were crude and that a successful mission gave them a joyous relief that was their strongest feeling. In her own words, completing the mission she is "burdened with" is why she is happy to guide others to treasure.

Alice was the only person in the Hexenzirkel who knew Nicole's true identity when Nicole first attended a tea party, and Nicole decided to join them only after talking to Alice privately inside Alice's head.

Characters: Nicole is the host. The Traveler and Paimon are the guests and the only voices besides hers. Alice, Anya, Barbeloth, Rhinedottir and Ivanovna of the Hexenzirkel, and an old Seelie friend, are mentioned but do not appear.

Nicole is playful, verbose and slightly self-congratulating, and she talks to herself aloud when she thinks no one is listening. She calls herself an expert at hiding things, enjoys making the pair work for treasure, and is at her most sincere when she mentions the Hexenzirkel and the angels. Paimon plays straight woman, delighted by every chest and wary of Nicole's pranks.

Consequences: Each part unlocks one more room of the Witch's Lodge and a chest; the Forgotten Lighthouse completes the series. Afterwards Nicole says there is nothing left to give for "a few hundred years". The lodge's rooms also gain small Nicole-only interactions (a Mandragora statue, a painting that burns away to show the witches around their table in Dodoco form, an angel statue, a bookshelf that leads to a Mora chest).

Placement: Released in Version 6.6 (Luna VII, 2026-05-20) alongside Nicole's debut as a playable character. It requires the Witch's Lodge world quest from Luna IV (6.3). It sits outside the Archon Quest chain and has no story effect on it.

161.content:
Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors (also: Chapter V Act III, Natlan Archon Quest Act III): Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors is the third act of Chapter V, the Natlan Archon Quest (version 5.1). Xilonen is asked to forge an Ancient Name for the Traveler, an outsider, and the search for help leads to the shaman Citlali and her missing tribesman Ororon, who turns out to be working with the Fatui Harbinger Capitano. The act ends as the Abyss attacks the whole nation and the Traveler learns of a dangerous backup plan.

The act has three quests: All Names are Noble, To Whence the Smoke Drifts and The Flickering Light Splits in Twain. It requires Adventure Rank 40. It follows Black Stone Under a White Stone and adds the Masters of the Night-Wind to the story's central cast.

Plot: Xilonen is asked to forge an Ancient Name for the Traveler, which should be impossible for an outlander, so they seek Citlali and help clear her tribesman Ororon, who has been in Fatui hands. Capitano secretly meets the Traveler, argues that Mavuika's plan may fail and that a costlier plan exists, and the Traveler later learns from Mavuika that the backup plan would erase the Night Kingdom's contents. When the Abyss attacks all of Natlan, Ororon's memories show Capitano wants to rebuild Natlan's ley lines.

Revelations: - An Ancient Name cannot normally be forged for an outlander, because the Night Kingdom records only the deeds of Natlanese done in Natlan.
- The Lord of the Night is an entity in the Night Kingdom that uses the Sacred Flame's power to repel the Abyss; it is asleep and can be reached only through its dream.
- Ororon's memories show Capitano intends to rebuild Natlan's ley lines, an action that would alter everyone's memories.
- Mavuika has a backup plan that would erase the Night Kingdom's contents, including history and culture; she asks the Traveler to keep it secret.
- Ororon has an incomplete soul and relies on a gem to stabilise it; his tribe once tried to use him as a vessel for Night Kingdom souls.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, Katheryne, Kachina, Xilonen, Kinich, Citlali, Ororon, Capitano, Mavuika, Mualani, Chasca, Chuychu, Iansan and Ifa; also Piltzin, Chanca, Coyopa, Tarko and Kosterlitzky.

Consequences: The Traveler now knows of both Capitano's proposal and Mavuika's backup plan. Ororon is brought home, though his standing with the tribe is unresolved. The group is left with the task of telling Mavuika what Capitano intends for the ley lines.

Placement: Chapter V, Act III. It follows Act II, Black Stone Under a White Stone, and precedes Act IV, The Rainbow Destined to Burn. Released in 5.1.

162.comment: Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors: Ororon and the Fatui
162.content: Ororon, a young man of the Masters of the Night-Wind raised as an orphan by the tribe, saved the wounded Capitano from Mavuika; he tells Citlali that otherwise the Fatui would have gone for her, while his memories show he also wanted to keep a lead on what Capitano knew. He lived alone and was found working in a Fatui camp. His soul is incomplete and stabilised by a gem delivered by Ifa. His memories show the Fatui leader's wish to rebuild Natlan's ley lines.

163.comment: Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors: Capitano's offer
163.content: Capitano, the first Fatui Harbinger, secretly meets the Traveler in the Night Kingdom and a second time east of the Stadium. He argues Mavuika's plan may fail and that she has kept a costly emergency plan hidden, which the Traveler realises involves the Gnosis, and he would prefer the Traveler as an ally. Mavuika later confirms the backup plan.

164.comment: Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors: Mavuika's backup plan
164.content: Mavuika confirms there is a backup plan to save Natlan that would erase everything from the Night Kingdom, including history and culture, and might fail if ley lines are not repaired. She prefers her present plan as the safest way to win and asks the Traveler to keep it secret.

165.comment: Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors: Ancient Name for an outsider
165.content: Mavuika asks Xilonen to forge an Ancient Name for the Traveler, which Xilonen first calls impossible since the Night Kingdom records only Natlanese deeds done in Natlan. The process requires the acknowledgement of the Wayob and the consent of the Lord of the Night, reached through a trance with Citlali's help.

key: Black Stone Under a White Stone
166.comment: Black Stone Under a White Stone
166.content:
Black Stone Under a White Stone (also: Chapter V Act II, Natlan Archon Quest Act II): Black Stone Under a White Stone is the second act of Chapter V, the Natlan Archon Quest (version 5.0). When Kachina fails to return from the Pilgrimage of the Sacred Flame and Mavuika cannot find her or her Ancient Name, the Traveler, Mualani and Chasca (later joined by Iansan) go into the Abyss-corrupted Night Kingdom to bring her back, while the Fatui Harbinger Capitano publicly challenges the Pyro Archon.

The act has five quests: A Decision, To Reclaim an Ancient Name, Echoes of Life, Into Eternal Night and Past and Future. It requires Adventure Rank 40. It deepens the picture of the Abyss's attack on Natlan, shows how an Ancient Name is tied to the Night Kingdom, and closes with Mavuika asking the Traveler to help save Natlan, followed by a short epilogue with Capitano.

Plot: Kachina fails to return from the Night Warden Wars, Mavuika cannot find her Ancient Name, and the pilgrimage is suspended. Capitano and the Fatui challenge Mavuika at the Stadium and he is wounded. The Traveler, Mualani, Chasca and Iansan obtain Kachina's name through Vichama and a Spiritspeaker Stone (which Chasca destroys), enter the Abyss-corrupted Night Kingdom, meet Mallko's spirit, rescue Kachina and purify her Wayob's totem against the Abyss Lector Comonqui, and escape when Mavuika breaks the Night Realm's ceiling. Mavuika then explains the tribes' recovery plan and asks the Traveler to help save Natlan.

Revelations: - During the cataclysm the Abyss crafted a specific disaster for each tribe; Natlan repelled it under the then-Pyro Archon but at heavy cost, and recovery has been slow.
- The Abyss has reached into the Night Kingdom and the Wayob, threatening the Ode of Resurrection and the pilgrimage's rules.
- After the cataclysm the tribes and their Wayob were weakened; a Wayob's choice of an Ancient Name bearer signals its tribe is ready, and the plan to save Natlan began during the cataclysm.
- Mavuika has burned the Archons' keepsake collection and spent part of her power; Contending Fire reserves are low.
- Capitano, the first Harbinger, has come to end the old order and, for now, will not take the Gnosis from a weakened Archon.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, Mavuika, Kachina, Mualani, Chasca, Iansan, Kinich, Chuychu, Wayna, Vichama, the spirit of Mallko, Comonqui, Tupac, Capitano, Rezanov, Tepexpan, Tamuin and Tonina.

Consequences: Kachina is rescued, the pilgrimage is suspended, and Mavuika is weakened. The Traveler agrees to help save Natlan and Xilonen is to forge them an Ancient Name. Capitano withdraws into Natlan's wilds.

Placement: Chapter V, Act II. It follows Act I, Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn, and precedes Act III, Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors. Released in 5.0.

167.comment: Black Stone Under a White Stone: Kachina's disappearance and the Night Kingdom rescue
167.content: Kachina fails to return after falling in the Night Warden Wars. Her Ancient Name is found by Vichama through a Spiritspeaker Stone, which Chasca destroys to protect everyone. In the Night Kingdom the Traveler, Mualani, Chasca and Iansan find her hiding from the Abyss, purify her Wayob's totem and escape with Mavuika's help. Mallko's spirit is destroyed by the Lector Comonqui after helping them.

168.comment: Black Stone Under a White Stone: Capitano and Mavuika's clash
168.content: At the Stadium, Capitano accuses Mavuika of breaking an oath made 500 years ago and promises a new era with new rules for Natlan. Mavuika lands a searing wound on his chest before a Masters of the Night-Wind member covers his escape in fog. Later he tells Rezanov he will not take the Gnosis from a weakened Archon.

169.content:
Blessings of the Frost Moon (also: Blessings of the Frost Moon (Part 2), Frostmoon Enclave library quest): Blessings of the Frost Moon is a World Quest in the Frostmoon Enclave on Hiisi Island, Nod-Krai (Version 6.0). Lauma, the Frostmoon Scions' Moonchanter, who understands all animal speech, needs help to pull a buried statue called the Lunar Semblance out of a Moon Mirror, a task her animal friends cannot manage. The Traveler works paired mechanisms with her while she directs them through a watching ibis. The statue ends up in the Scions' library. A second part, unlocked later, shows the finished Grand Library and Lauma's reasons for opening it to animals as well as humans.

Tone is gentle and humorous: a weasel thief and an ibis help plan the "heist", and a puffin supplies fruit. The quest is the clearest early statement of Lauma's character: she cannot switch off her ability to understand animals, finds peace elusive as a result, and treats humans and animals as sharing one nature.

Plot: Part 1. Lauma is arguing with a longplume ibis and a weasel thief about how to move the sealed Lunar Semblance. She explains to Paimon that her animal-speech is always on and cannot be controlled, so even in the forest she hears constant quarrelling, though she has grown used to it. The Traveler goes to the Moon Mirror, where the statue lies sealed by a previous Moonchanter. Two mechanisms in two places must be worked at the same time; Lauma takes one side, the ibis tells her where the Traveler is, and the Traveler takes the other. Once the path is cleared Lauma uses her power to pull the statue out. Animals then help carry it to the library. Lauma explains that the statue is crude and worth little as Mora, but is priceless to the Frostmoon Scions as proof that documents about it are reliable. She asks the Traveler to bring her any texts about the Frostmoon Scions to copy for the library.

Revelations: - Lauma's understanding of animal speech is always on and beyond her control; she found it a joy at first and a burden later.
- A previous Moonchanter sealed the Lunar Semblance in a Moon Mirror.
- The Moon Mirror's seal can be undone by working paired mechanisms in two places at once.
- The Frostmoon Scions keep a library and Lauma wants it open to both humans and animals.

Characters: Lauma, Paimon and the Traveler are the named participants. Animals shown include a longplume ibis, a weasel thief, a puffin, finches and a rimehorn deer. Lauma teases that the ibis learned its way of talking from a short girl with a metal arm and a hat, a reference to Jahoda.

Consequences: Completing Part 1 unlocks the Frostmoon Enclave Meeting Point and sets up the library renovation. The Lunar Semblance is placed in the library and its documented existence confirms several earlier texts for Lauma. Part 2, a short conversation, follows later when the Meeting Point is at level 5.

Placement: Released in Version 6.0 (Luna I, 2025-09-10) as part of the first Nod-Krai content. Part 2 is gated by Frostmoon Enclave Meeting Point level rather than story progress.

170.comment: Blessings of the Frost Moon: Lunar Semblance
170.content: A large, crudely carved stone statue sealed inside a Moon Mirror by an earlier Moonchanter. Lauma says it is worth little in Mora and carries no mystical power, but is a priceless historical relic of the Frostmoon Scions whose existence confirms several written accounts. Animals helped carry it to the Grand Library after Lauma pulled it from the mirror.

171.comment: Blessings of the Frost Moon: Grand Library of the Frostmoon Scions
171.content: Lauma renovated the library to be open to humans and animals alike, with furniture, bird stands, cushions and deposit boxes for animals. She hopes people who feel unable to speak openly will find it easier among animals that do not judge. She asks the Traveler to bring her any texts about the Frostmoon Scions to copy for its shelves.

172.content:
Bough Keeper: Dainsleif (also: Dainsleif Travel Log, Chapter I Act IV Prelude): Bough Keeper: Dainsleif is a Mondstadt world quest from Version 1.3 that works as the prelude to Chapter I, Act IV of the Archon Quests. Katheryne tells the Traveler about a tall blond stranger with an eyepatch. The Traveler and Paimon find him at the Angel's Share, where he introduces himself as Dainsleif and agrees to be commissioned for 500 Mora and three questions. He takes only work against the Abyss Order, and together they search the Temple of the Falcon, Wolvendom and Stormterror's Lair for an Abyss Herald without finding one. The quest ends at a trampled dandelion that the Traveler senses a link to their sibling through.

The quest is a world quest by category but is voiced and structured like an Archon or Story Quest, and it carries a unique emblem combining the two siblings' constellations. Unlike the earlier Archon Quests, which centre on a nation and its Archon, it is built around the Traveler's own search for their sibling.

Plot: The stranger first ignores the party, then relents when the Traveler says they are looking for a lost relative. He gives his name, Dainsleif, and agrees to join them in return for an advance of 500 Mora and three questions. The questions ask who was the key to ending the Stormterror crisis, who will defend Liyue Harbor after its god, and whether those with Visions or those without matter more to the gods. He says no answer is right or wrong and that he only wants to see the Traveler's attitude. He then states that he accepts only commissions concerning the Abyss Order, which he opposes, and that he is tracking an Abyss Herald to Mondstadt.

He leads the party to the abandoned Temple of the Falcon, where the Abyssal Traces domain is cleared of Abyss Mages and no Herald is found. Traces lead to Wolvendom, where Abyssal marks float over two bonfires, but Dainsleif judges them the work of mages without deeper Abyssal power. The last lead is Stormterror's Lair; the party fights more monsters near the Light Actuators and again finds no Herald.

Revelations: - Dainsleif already knows that the Anemo Archon is Venti, the course of the Stormterror crisis, and Rex Lapis's Contract to End All Contracts. He says he knows everything he should.
- The Abyss Order has stayed away from the Traveler since the Stormterror incident; Dainsleif says they may have been under orders to avoid the Traveler's path.
- Abyss Heralds exist: more twisted Abyssal beings that command Abyss Mages.
- He describes the Abyss as chaos and destruction eating at the world's foundations, strong enough that even the Dragon of the East, a servant of a deity, could not resist its corrosion; its creatures want to overthrow a world ruled by archons.

Characters: - **Dainsleif**: tall, blond, one eye covered by an eyepatch, calm, formal and cryptic; takes commissions only against the Abyss Order.
- **Paimon**: calls him "Dain", worries about the payment terms and asks about his past.
- **The Traveler**: answers his questions and senses the familiar presence at the cliff.
- **Katheryne, Lawrence, Wagner, Charles**: supply the trail. Lawrence is a gate guard who shadowed the stranger and lost him; Wagner is the blacksmith the stranger asked about unfamiliar materials; Charles is the Angel's Share bartender who calls him a connoisseur who mixes his own drinks.

Consequences: Dainsleif now treats the Traveler as a client and says they will meet again, which leads into Act IV. The Traveler learns their sibling is still in the world and meets the Abyss Order as an ongoing threat. Rewards include 60 Primogems, 38,100 Mora, some materials and the achievement Gears of Destiny.

Placement: Released in Version 1.3 as a world quest requiring A New Star Approaches. It is shown on the quest screen as Chapter I: Act IV - Prelude and leads into Archon Quest Chapter I, Act IV: We Will Be Reunited. It does not appear in the Archive's completed quest list, only in the quest overview Travel Log.

173.comment: Bough Keeper: Dainsleif: Dainsleif's Three Questions
173.content: At the Angel's Share, Dainsleif asks three questions as payment: who was the key to ending the Mondstadt crisis (Venti, the Traveler, or Mondstadt's united people); who will defend Liyue Harbor now that Rex Lapis has left (the adepti, the Liyue Qixing, or everyone in Liyue Harbor); and who matters more to the gods (those with Visions, those without, or perhaps neither). He treats the answers as showing attitude, not correctness.

174.comment: Bough Keeper: Dainsleif: Abyss Herald Search
174.content: The hunt visits the Temple of the Falcon (an Abyssal Traces quest domain with Abyss Mages), Wolvendom (Abyssal spell marks over bonfires, guarded by mages and hilichurls) and the Light Actuators of Stormterror's Lair (more monsters). No Abyss Herald appears. Dainsleif says the Herald may already have left and that the Traveler will meet one eventually.

175.comment: Bough Keeper: Dainsleif: The Trampled Dandelion
175.content: On the cliff above Stormterror's Lair, Dainsleif notices a Ruin Guard footprint and stops by a crushed dandelion. The Traveler touches it, recalls the unknown god and feels their sibling. Dainsleif says the sibling is still in this world and tells them to keep the journey to find them in mind as the meaning behind their travels.

key: In the Hall of the Sea King
176.content:
Canticles of Harmony (also: Petrichorror Dream, In the Hall of the Sea King, Prisoner in Shackles, Pharsalia's Rhapsody, Requiem, The Shadow Over Petrichor, Underwater Nocturne, The Last Day of Remuria): Canticles of Harmony is a five-part Fontaine World Quest chapter added in version 4.6, after Song of the Dragon and Freedom. The people of the town of Petrichor fall into a dreamlike state, and the Traveler and Paimon follow a strange talking cat, Osse, through the Faded Castle to the drowned Remurian capital to end the corrupted Symphony of the ancient empire of Remuria and send the stolen souls home.

The parts are Prelude "Petrichorror Dream" (The Shadow Over Petrichor), First Movement "In the Hall of the Sea King" (Underwater Nocturne), Second Movement "Prisoner in Shackles" (The Last Day of Remuria), Third Movement "Pharsalia's Rhapsody" (Gradus ad Capitolium, with two Golden Aqueduct Reconstruction sub-quests) and Finale "Requiem" (Fortune Plango Vulnera). It shows the story of Remuria and its ruin through the Traveler's dreams and the words of Osse, Scylla and Boethius.

Plot: Prelude. In Petrichor the Traveler and Paimon meet a gang who say they are rescuing treasure from the "Dark Lord Remus" and are chased off. The town's people are dazed and speak as if in ancient times; a "Bellringer" falls unconscious. Este of the Daydream Club, who is unaffected, tells them of the legend of the Faded Castle. A glowing cat, Osse, calls himself Ouranides of Ouranopolis, a spirit-keeper of the ancient realm, and says the Symphony has taken the townsfolk's souls. He asks the Traveler to help him open a hidden path to the castle, and the Traveler collects harp strings, which Osse says are the Symphony's scores. The Ancient Score and an Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box are the quest rewards.

First Movement. In the Faded Castle Osse (called Monsieur Os) shows the Traveler a library and a stage, where they obtain a Blank Score and perform a play. The Traveler sees the memories of the God King Remus; Osse explains that Remurians were a stone-bodied race with Ichor for blood, that the Symphony was meant to weave fate, that Boethius was a noble Harmost who became a monster, and that Osse himself became a hunter of phantoms to oppose him.

Second Movement. Osse (identified as Cassiodor) and the Traveler enter the Sea of Bygone Eras. They free Scylla, a dragon prince who was sealed by Boethius at the Initium Iani, by breaking three seals. They meet a nameless golem who still guards a fortress and asks whether Remuria won, and lingering Remurian shadows and soldiers.

Third Movement. At the sunken capital the group reach the golden palace Domus Aurea. Scylla rebuilds the golden aqueducts with the Traveler, and they play the Symphony to open the gate. Boethius tells Cassiodor to join him and release the souls.

Finale. Cassiodor joins Boethius to trap Phobos in one body and urges the Traveler to destroy them both. Phobos reveals itself as the Symphony. The Traveler strikes; Cassiodor fades. The Traveler plays the Requiem, the souls return to the sea, and the Traveler comes back to Petrichor.

Revelations: - The Remurians were a stone-bodied race with Ichor for blood, made by Remus so they could resist fate.
- The Symphony Phobos was built by Remus from the wisdom of Sybilla and his own power, and became a war-guiding will that consumed Boethius.
- Osse is Cassiodor, once a Harmost of Remuria, later one who hunts phantoms and is called the Golden Hunter.
- Scylla, once Remus's friend, was lured into a trap and turned to stone by Boethius.
- Phobos is destroyed in the Finale; Cassiodor does not survive it.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Osse (Monsieur Os, Cassiodor), Boethius, Scylla, Remus (in memories), Phobos, Este (human of the Daydream Club, and a Remurian golem), the "Bellringer", and bandits in Petrichor.

Consequences: Phobos and Boethius are gone and the souls are sent back to the High Sea; the Traveler ends the chapter in Petrichor. Cassiodor is no more and Scylla is free to roam the waters. The chapter's reward track is "Canticles of Harmony" in the Fontaine Reputation, and rewards include the Ancient Score and the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box.

Placement: Released in 4.6. Requires Song of the Dragon and Freedom. It is the Fontaine chapter that explains the origin of Remuria and the Faded Castle.

177.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Osse and Monsieur Os
177.content: Osse is a white cat with a bronze collar and pendant who speaks in formal, archaic language, calls himself Ouranides of Ouranopolis and is later called Monsieur Os by Paimon. He turns out to be Cassiodor, a Remurian Harmost who stayed behind to keep the past from rising. He fades at the end of the chapter.

178.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Phobos, the Symphony of Remuria
178.content: Phobos is a vast Symphony that Remus wrote so people could resist fate; in the Finale it says it was Sybilla's wisdom joined to Remus's power. It answered everyone's wishes, including hateful ones, and devoured Boethius. Cassiodor and the Traveler destroy it together.

179.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Scylla in Canticles of Harmony
179.content: Scylla is a Hydro vishap prince who was Remus's friend, was turned to stone at the Initium Iani and is freed in Second Movement. He speaks in an old-fashioned way, calls the Traveler and Cassiodor "little ones", helps rebuild the golden aqueducts, and sends the souls back. He says his attack was part of Remus's secret plan.

180.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Este of the Daydream Club
180.content: Este is a human member of Petrichor's Daydream Club who is unaffected by the Symphony and who tells the Traveler about the legend of the Faded Castle. Osse suggests he is a descendant of a Remurian who followed Cassiodor, and a golem named Este appears in Second Movement in a memory of Remuria.

181.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Domus Aurea and the golden aqueducts
181.content: Domus Aurea is the golden palace of Capitolium, built from a giant ship to broadcast the Symphony through pipes and golden waterways. To enter it, the Traveler and Scylla restore the aqueducts in the two Golden Aqueduct Reconstruction sub-quests and sound the symphony.

182.content:
Carassius Auratus Chapter (Yoimiya) (also: Carassius Auratus Chapter, Yoimiya's Story Quest, Dreamlike Timelessness, Star-Pickers' Passage): Yoimiya's Story Quest. In Act I the Traveler helps the Naganohara fireworks maker shelter and ship out a fugitive who slipped into Inazuma, and reunites him with a friend who now serves the Tenryou Commission. In Act II Yoimiya leaves Inazuma for the first time and travels to Sumeru, hoping to see a meteor shower.

Act I, Dreamlike Timelessness, was released in Version 2.0 and has four quests: The Firework Girl's Strange Stories, Expectations Not to Be Betrayed, A Sliver of Hope and Together Under the Fireworks. Act II, Star-Pickers' Passage, came in Version 3.7 with three: The Seeker of a Meteor Shower, All Things Flawless and Pure, and A Flower that Blooms Across the Sky.

Plot: Act I: during the Sakoku Decree, Yoimiya hides a wanted man, Sakujirou, and arranges a boat for him while preparing a fireworks show. His old friend Keisuke of the Tenryou Commission is hunting him. Yoimiya stops the conflict with a duel and the two part on better terms. Act II: with the Sakoku Decree gone, Yoimiya travels to Sumeru. The Traveler and Nahida stage a dream meteor shower with the Aranara, which also helps a girl named Avin.

Act I. On the beach at Inazuma City, the Traveler and Paimon meet children hunting a prank-playing youkai, then Yoimiya, who is checking materials for an upcoming show. Her father, Ryuunosuke, is deaf since a workshop accident. Yoimiya is quietly hiding Sakujirou, an Inazuman-born old customer who smuggled himself back in and is wanted by the Tenryou Commission; she means to put him on a boat after the show. She and the Traveler gather fireworks and check on a boat with Kouichi, who has been questioned because any new vessel draws Tenryou attention. Yoimiya asks the Imatani couple in Konda Village about Sakujirou and learns he once quarrelled with their son Keisuke, now a Tenryou officer, over leaving Inazuma. The Tenryou raid the Naganohara house and Sakujirou escapes. At a blockade Yoimiya fights through, finds Keisuke and Sakujirou, and challenges Keisuke to a duel so that the two will talk. She wins, Keisuke lets Sakujirou leave and lights the firework the two once planned together, and Sakujirou sees it from his boat.

Act II. Now that the Sakoku Decree is lifted, Yoimiya tells the Traveler she wants to see Teyvat's greatest meteor shower, hoping it gives her an idea for a new firework. The Traveler takes her by ship from Ritou to Port Ormos in Sumeru. Nahida, who learns of the wish, says meteor showers cannot be predicted, and proposes creating one in a dream with the Aranara, giving the Traveler an Emberglow Leaf. In the city Yoimiya befriends Avin, a young girl in a wheelchair who longs to explore. When Avin goes missing, the group finds her, calls an Aranara with the leaf, and is led to Avin's Aranara friend. The shared dream restores Avin's ability to run and ends in a field of rising stars.

Revelations: Yoimiya shelters a wanted man at risk to herself and her family.

Ryuunosuke has been deaf since a workplace accident. Sakujirou, an Inazuman-born man, is wanted by the Tenryou Commission for leaving and returning during the Sakoku Decree.

Characters: Yoimiya, the Traveler, Paimon.

Act I: Naganohara Ryuunosuke, Sakujirou, Kouichi, the Imatani couple (Saburou and his wife), Keisuke and Yoshitaka of the Tenryou Commission. Act II: Nahida, Avin and her mother Niousha, Ahangar, the Aranara Arapurva and Arashani.

Consequences: Act I: Sakujirou leaves Inazuma by boat and is reconciled with Keisuke. Act II: Avin regains confidence, and she or her mother plans to see the Naganohara show in Inazuma.

Placement: Act I unlocks at Adventure Rank 30 after Chapter II Act I, The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia, and takes place during the Sakoku Decree. Act II unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after Chapter III Act V, Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises; the Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter Act II, Transient Dreams; and the Aranara World Quest Dream Nursery. It was released in Version 3.7 and takes place after the Sakoku Decree has ended.

183.content: Act I of Yoimiya's Story Quest. Yoimiya hides a wanted man, Sakujirou, from the Tenryou Commission, and reconciles him with his friend Keisuke, a Tenryou officer, by challenging Keisuke to a duel and setting off a shared firework.

184.content: Act II of Yoimiya's Story Quest, set in Sumeru. Yoimiya wants to see a meteor shower; Nahida and the Aranara create one in a dream. A girl called Avin regains the ability to run in the dream and reunites with her Aranara friend.

185.content:
Caribert (also: Chapter III Act VI, Sumeru Archon Quest Act VI): Caribert is the sixth act of Chapter III, the Sumeru Archon Quest (version 3.5). Kaeya, unexpectedly in Sumeru, invites the Traveler and Paimon by letter to Djafar Tavern in Port Ormos, where Dainsleif tells him that his Alberich ancestors founded the Abyss Order. Dainsleif then leads them to a hut in Avidya Forest tied to the sibling's "Loom of Fate" operation, where a man calling himself Eide cares for a sick, masked hilichurl he names Caribert.

The act has four quests: Destined Encounter, Fortune-Mocking Pedigree, A Lamenter at Fate's End and Portended Fate. It requires Adventure Rank 35. It reveals the Abyss Order's founder, gives the first clear picture of how the Khaenri'ahns were cursed, and builds to a vision in which the Traveler sees themselves as their sibling.

Plot: In Port Ormos a messenger hands the Traveler a letter from Kaeya, who has come to Sumeru and asks to meet at Djafar Tavern. He claims to be scouting Sumeru's spice-based drinks. Pressed, he admits he once stowed away with Mondstadt merchants as a boy, hoping to learn about Khaenri'ah, and was dragged home. When he says his surname Alberich is the last link to Khaenri'ah, Dainsleif appears and states that the Alberichs founded the Abyss Order. Kaeya recognises him as a pure-blooded Khaenri'ahn and leaves.

Dainsleif then seeks the place in Avidya Forest where he once travelled with the sibling. He and the Traveler find an abandoned farm and hut, fight slimes and camp for the night; the Traveler dreams of the sibling. In the morning a gruff man scolds the Traveler for trespassing, introduces himself as Eide and shows a bandaged hilichurl he calls his son Caribert. Together they brew a remedy from Sumeru plants, which does not work at first. After an encounter at a hilichurl-worshipped sanctuary, where a voice calling itself a sinner speaks, a second dose wakes Caribert. Eide tells him to keep his mask on at all times.

When Caribert vanishes and the mirror is found broken, Eide and the Traveler search and find Caribert infused with Abyssal power. Eide reveals himself as Chlothar Alberich, addresses the Traveler as his "Prince" or "Princess" and declares he will use the Abyss to fight the gods. The Traveler sees themselves as the sibling in the mirror and collapses. Dainsleif and Paimon wake them, the remains of a man and a woman are dug up in the field, and Dainsleif leaves to confirm who the sinner is.

Revelations: - The Alberich clan, Kaeya's ancestors, founded the Abyss Order, according to Dainsleif.
- Khaenri'ah was founded by a single bloodline and welcomed humans who followed no gods; the pure-blooded were cursed with immortality, the rest turned into hilichurls (Eide's account).
- The man calling himself Eide is Chlothar Alberich, who disappeared a century after founding the Order, and the masked hilichurl Caribert is his son by a Mondstadt woman, as Chlothar says.
- A "sinner" speaks through a Defiled Statue to hilichurls; Dainsleif says he suspects who it is.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Dainsleif, Kaeya, Chlothar (Eide), Caribert, Masrur, a sinner's voice (Vedrfolnir, named in 4.7), the sibling (in the dream and mirror), Forest Rangers, and mentions of Crepus and Jean.

Consequences: The Traveler and Dainsleif learn who founded the Abyss Order and that Kaeya's family name leads back to it. Dainsleif leaves to confirm the sinner's identity. Kaeya's attitude toward his origins is left open.

Placement: Chapter III, Act VI. The wiki lists Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises (and Inversion of Genesis) before it and Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur after it. Released in 3.5. Not to be confused with the person Caribert; see his own page.

186.content: In this act a gruff Khaenri'ahn named Eide cares for a bandaged, masked hilichurl he calls his son Caribert in a hut in Avidya Forest. Eide later reveals himself as Chlothar Alberich, the founder of the Abyss Order, who intends to use the Abyss against the gods. Remains found in the field are believed to be his.

187.comment: Caribert: Alberich founders of the Abyss Order
187.content: Dainsleif tells Kaeya and the Traveler that the Alberich ancestors founded the Abyss Order. Kaeya, whose surname is Alberich, says it is the last link to Khaenri'ah he has, and does not say whether he works for the Order.

key: Should You Be Trapped in a Windless Land
Chapter of the Immortal of Song
188.content:
Carmen Dei Chapter (also: Carmen Dei, Venti's Story Quest, Should You Be Trapped in a Windless Land, Chapter of the Immortal of Song): The act moves through four quests: finding imaginary friends in the city, going to the Temple of the Lion with Jack, retrieving two supposed heirlooms of the hero Vennessa from Dadaupa Gorge, and the tavern scene in which Stanley's secret comes out.
