Consequences: Elchingen and Kautilya are taken away by the Corps of Thirty to face judgement. The tournament is put on hold until it can be run safely, with Haniyyah taking care of the Fungi, and the Traveler and Paimon, having technically passed the Ultimate Trial, are treated as hosts. Yurochka remains as a loose end near Chatrakam Cave.

Placement: Released in Version 3.2 as a Flagship Event, set after the Sumeru Archon Quest. Event quests are not part of the main storyline, and many in-world people did not know about the tournament, as its own rules state.

315.content: A Fungi-commanding tournament held at Port Ormos. Contestants capture four Fungi, give them Floral Jelly and use a Wisdom Orb; weapons and direct fighting between tamers are banned, and the Corps of Thirty referees. The top eight win Mora, a title and the right to keep their ace Fungus.

316.content: A device developed for the tournament, using Amurta's "Intellectual Boost" technology, that registers and commands a Fungus. It has a hidden backdoor command that Elchingen used against the Traveler's Fungi; Bongo-Head, whose orb the Traveler had switched off, was unaffected.

317.content: A former Eremite beast tamer who tested the Wisdom Orb and guides the Traveler. She calls herself an illiterate nobody and plans to win in order to destroy all Fungi, including her partner Pyro-1. After the final she apologises and cares for the surviving Fungi, renaming Pyro-1 Kindlejoy.

318.content: Presented as a quiet Fontaine businessman who sponsored the tournament with sixty million Mora and offered his whole fortune to whoever passes his Ultimate Trial. He is later revealed as a Fatuus working for Il Dottore and is arrested by the Corps of Thirty.

319.content: The Amurta researcher who organises the Nilotpala Cup and whose disclaimer reserves interpretation of the rules to himself. He is exposed alongside Elchingen and arrested.

320.content: Fungi named in the event. Bongo-Head is the Traveler's Floating Hydro Fungus, named by Paimon; Twirly-Whirly is Layla's Floating Anemo Fungus; Blitzara is Yae Miko's Whirling Electro Fungus, named by Souka; Kindlejoy is Haniyyah's Pyro Fungus, formerly Pyro-1.

321.content:
Farewell, Archaic Lord (also: Chapter I Act II, Liyue Archon Quest Act II): Chapter I Act II of the Archon Quest, set in Liyue Harbor. With Rex Lapis dead and his body hidden by the Qixing, Childe introduces the Traveler and Paimon to Zhongli, a consultant at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, who offers to get them to the Geo Archon's vessel if they help him prepare the Rite of Parting.

The act has seven quests: An Organization Known as Wangsheng, Moonfinger, Three Poignant Perfumes, The Realm Within, Downtown, Guizhong and Zhongli's Treat. It is a long errand sequence through the harbor and surrounding countryside, and it ends when Ganyu delivers Ningguang's invitation to the Jade Chamber. Released in version 1.0.

Plot: At Liuli Pavilion Childe introduces Zhongli, who says he can bring the Traveler to the Exuvia if they help with the Rite of Parting. They buy jade, make perfumes, borrow a bell from Madame Ping, order kites and workers, and get Everlasting Incense from Bubu Pharmacy. The act ends with Ningguang's invitation to the Jade Chamber.

**An Organization Known as Wangsheng.** At Northland Bank, Ekaterina tells the Traveler that Childe has found someone to break the stalemate and is waiting at Liuli Pavilion. Childe presents Zhongli as a consultant at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and a trusted contact of the Fatui. Zhongli explains that the parlor organises burials, that the age of the adepti is ending, and that the Qixing have broken tradition by not holding a memorial for a deceased adeptus. He asks the Traveler to help prepare the Geo Archon's last rites, the Rite of Parting, and the Traveler agrees; only by taking part can they again see the god's form. Zhongli says the Fatui are merely financial sponsors, that he does not know and does not wish to know what Childe gains from it, and that his own concern is that Liyue's traditions endure.

Revelations: The Qixing have hidden the Geo Archon's vessel, the Exuvia; Childe deduces that it is in the Golden House.

Zhongli is introduced as a funeral-parlor consultant who says the Geo Archon is also an adeptus; Madame Ping is an adeptus who keeps a domain inside her teapot; Ningguang, in her letter, speaks of cutting the "entwining dark threads" together with the Traveler.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Zhongli; Childe (Tartaglia); Ekaterina; Ganyu.

Also Hongru (Liuli Pavilion), Shitou, Bolai, Ying'er, Madame Ping, Granny Shan, Tic, Tac and Toe, Qiqi, Baizhu, Iron Tongue Tian, and Ningguang (appearing only through Ganyu's letter and the story).

Consequences: Everything needed for the Rite of Parting is gathered except the final pieces. The Traveler now has an invitation to the Jade Chamber and a rendezvous with Zhongli at Dihua Marsh, leading into Act III, A New Star Approaches.

Placement: Chapter I Act II, after Of the Land Amidst Monoliths and before Act III, A New Star Approaches. Released in version 1.0.

322.comment: Farewell, Archaic Lord: Zhongli and the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor
322.content: Zhongli presents himself as a Wangsheng consultant, says the parlor arranges burials so the dead pass in peace, and takes on the Rite of Parting to give Rex Lapis a proper farewell. Childe introduces Zhongli as a trusted associate of the Fatui and jokes that the parlor does not dabble in killing, "well, ostensibly".

323.content: The Geo Archon's vessel, which Zhongli says is traditionally called the Exuvia. Childe says the Tianquan Ningguang has forbidden anyone from accessing it; later, when Ekaterina reports overhearing that the Qixing have taken over the Golden House, Childe concludes the Exuvia is kept there.

324.content: A small harbor tavern with a resident storyteller, where Zhongli treats the Traveler to dinner. Iron Tongue Tian tells how Ningguang shreds her research and scatters the "paper snow" from the Jade Chamber, and Ganyu appears there to deliver the invitation.

325.content:
Felis Fuscus Chapter (also: Felis Fuscus, Lyney's Story Quest, The Forgotten Thief, The Phantom Thief's Reappearance, The Magician's Secret, The Truest Thing, The Interview, Phantom Weasel): Lyney's Story Quest, set in the Court of Fontaine. Ten years after a thief called the Phantom Weasel vanished, a poster announces the return. The Great Magician Lyney recruits the Traveler and Paimon as temporary assistants to find the culprit. They clear the name of Cesar, a dead stage magician wrongly branded the thief, expose his killer, and then learn the thief was someone else.

The chapter has one act, The Forgotten Thief, made of four quests: The Phantom Thief's Reappearance, The Magician's Secret, The Truest Thing and The Interview. It was released in version 4.0 and unlocked after As Light Rain Falls Without Reason. It also reveals how Lyney and Lynette came to learn magic from Cesar, and what they hid from him.

Plot: Charlotte reports that the Phantom Weasel, a thief never caught ten years ago, is back. Lyney offers to investigate and has the Traveler and Paimon help look into Cesar's death. They find Cesar's former apprentice Lorenzo is hiding something, are attacked, and find Cesar's diary and workshop. Lorenzo admits he killed Cesar and was the Phantom Weasel. The next day Lyney performs Cesar's old trick at the Opera Epiclese and reveals Jemma was behind it. Jemma later turns herself in.

The Phantom Thief's Reappearance: Charlotte tells the Traveler that ten years ago the magician Cesar fell to his death during a performance and the Gardes found stolen goods among his belongings, so he was thought to be the thief. A poster at the Opera Epiclese announces the Weasel is back. Lyney offers help and says they should check whether Cesar faked his death, starting with his fiancee Jemma at the Poisson cemetery. Jemma hides something.

The Magician's Secret: at Hotel Debord the Traveler meets Lorenzo, a former magician and Cesar's apprentice turned businessman, who threatens Edmondo and storms out. Lyney leads them out of town, where pursuers attack and flee on discovering he is a Vision bearer. Jemma says she is threatened whenever she looks into Cesar's death. In the sealed workshop they find Cesar's diary about two children he agreed to train. Lyney confronts Lorenzo, who admits to sabotaging Cesar from jealousy and to being the Phantom Weasel, then is taken away by Gardes. Lyney holds a memorial for Cesar.

The Truest Thing: Lyney performs a show alone at the Opera Epiclese, and at the interval Lynette reveals Jemma was the real Phantom Weasel. The twins confront her privately. Jemma tells a sad history and does not confirm the facts. Lyney reveals that he, not Jemma, wrote the letter, to draw her out because the twins felt indebted to Cesar. He then performs the final act, Cesar's old trick, and vanishes in a sea of flowers. At the cemetery he tells the Traveler about his past with Lynette and Cesar.

The Interview: at the Steambird, Charlotte tries to interview the twins and says Jemma has turned herself in and admitted to being the real Phantom Weasel. Paimon notices Lyney is now using Rainbow Roses in his tricks, which Lynette notices. She says she had only been acting to distract Charlotte, and asks the Traveler to keep the Rainbow Rose Lyney gave them.

Revelations: Cesar was killed by his apprentice Lorenzo, and Cesar was not the Phantom Weasel. The thief was Jemma, who manipulated Lorenzo.

Lyney and Lynette studied under Cesar for ten days while hiding their real purpose, and the twins arranged the letter to flush Jemma out. Jemma later turns herself in and admits to being the Phantom Weasel.

Characters: Lyney, Lynette, the Traveler and Paimon.

Charlotte, Cesar (deceased), Jemma, Lorenzo, Edmondo, Abagnale, and the Gardes Bruno and Lori.

Consequences: Cesar's name is cleared, Lorenzo is arrested and Jemma turns herself in as the real Phantom Weasel. Charlotte's article is overtaken by the news of Jemma's arrest.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after As Light Rain Falls Without Reason (Chapter IV Act II). Released in 4.0 on 2023-08-16. The wiki notes it is blocked at step 5 by Unfinished Comedy.

326.comment: Felis Fuscus Chapter: The Phantom Weasel
326.content: A notorious thief in Fontaine ten years before the Archon Quest who was never caught and robbed rich and poor alike. When the magician Cesar died, stolen goods were found among his things and he was blamed. His apprentice Lorenzo first confessed to being the Weasel after killing Cesar, but the twins revealed that Jemma was the real thief, using Lorenzo as a tool. She later turned herself in.

327.comment: Felis Fuscus Chapter: Cesar the magician
327.content: A stage magician who died in a fall during a performance ten years before the quest. He agreed to train Lyney and Lynette for ten days, not knowing their secrets, and was wrongly believed to be the thief. His diary and workshop helped Lyney prove he was sabotaged by Lorenzo.

328.content:
Film Notes (also: Film Notes World Quest series, "Outlander Brigade!", Mushounin, Xavier's second film): In "Outlander Brigade!" the Traveler finds Xavier midway through a troubled shoot at the Kamisato Estate's request, is offered the lead role, and plays two scenes of "When the Wind of Death Blew Towards the Blond Samurai" before the supporting actors walk out. Over a meal at Uyuu Restaurant, Rikuto's story of Seishimaru helps Xavier see what is wrong. In Mushounin, Koharu and Sasano are brought back and three new scenes are filmed at Komore Teahouse, Nazuchi Beach and a cliff on a small island east of Narukami Island.

Plot: Opening. Furuta, the Kamisato Estate's butler, tells the Traveler that Xavier, a young Fontainian, had received money from the Tenryou Commission for a film that the commission was not satisfied with, and then came to the Yashiro Commission, the body responsible for arts and the humanities, for help. Ayato agreed and sent Koharu, whom Furuta worries is not fond of Xavier.

The first shoot. Xavier reminds the Traveler of an earlier agreement that they would play the lead, and gives scripts for Act I, Scenes II and III. Sasano and Koharu are already weary after eleven takes. The script is Xavier's adaptation of a novel by Kayabuki Ikkei; Sasano recalls that Ikkei's manuscripts were always rejected by Yae Publishing House. In the story the two supporting characters sacrifice themselves so the lead can go on, which Sasano and Koharu find senseless. Xavier criticises stiff delivery and forgotten lines, and both actors quit.

Rikuto's advice. Xavier retreats to Uyuu Restaurant. Okazaki Rikuto, the owner, overhears the premise and remarks that a hero who charges into unwinnable fights with no hesitation seems hardly human. He tells a legend: Seishimaru's samurai parents were executed after an apparent error at work, and Seishimaru sought revenge on the Wakayama family who carried out the sentence, whose head was a childhood friend. Xavier decides to write a new script and asks to meet at Komore Teahouse the next day.

Revelations: - Xavier's first script here is an adaptation of a novel by Kayabuki Ikkei, whom Sasano knows only as an author Yae Publishing House kept rejecting.
- Rikuto uses the Seishimaru legend to show a man whose revenge is aimed at someone who only followed orders, which pushes Xavier to rework the film.

Characters: Xavier (a Fontainian aspiring director), Koharu (a Kamisato household servant), Sasano (supporting actor), Furuta (Kamisato butler), Okazaki Rikuto (Uyuu Restaurant), Yamada Hifumi, Yamamoto and Tanaka (toughs turned extras in Mushounin), Paimon and the Traveler. Kamisato Ayato, Thoma and Kayabuki Ikkei are only mentioned.

Consequences: Both quests give Adventure EXP, Primogems, Mora and Hero's Wit; Mushounin also gives Mystic Enhancement Ore. The film is completed. Co-Op mode is locked during the shoots, and the Serenitea Pot is unavailable for part of the first quest.

Placement: Released in 2.8. It requires Omnipresence Over Mortals (the Inazuma Archon Quest) and "The Seventh Samurai", the earlier world quest featuring Xavier. It has no bearing on later Archon Quests.

329.content: In-universe, Rikuto tells Xavier an Inazuman legend of Seishimaru, whose samurai parents were executed, and who sets out to take revenge on the Wakayama family that carried out the sentence. Xavier's "Mushounin" script retells it with film characters, including Wakayama Keisuke, who lets Seishimaru choose by a blind point between a sword and a temari ball whether they will fight or sever their bonds.

330.content: Xavier is a theatrical Fontainian filmmaker working in Inazuma. He calls the Traveler his dear friend and says they were the first friend he made in Inazuma. He loves art over commerce but his scripts confuse his actors. In this series he works with funding and staff granted by Kamisato Ayato.

key: The Blazing Stars Ring in Fortune
The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes
331.content:
Fleeting Colors in Flight (also: Lantern Rite 2022, Version 2.4 Lantern Rite event, The Blazing Stars Ring in Fortune, Sky-Gazers, Land-Walkers, The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes, Flameplume Starflowers, Oceanic Defender event): The story is told in three parts: "The Blazing Stars Ring in Fortune" (Ningguang and Keqing introduce the fireworks show, and Zhongli suggests a storytelling approach to get Keqing to rest), "Sky-Gazers, Land-Walkers" (the gift round with Keqing, then the discovery that fireworks have been stolen from Qingce Village) and "The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes" (the trap for the thieves, the story at the Jade Chamber and the show itself). Along the way the adepti, Qiqi, Baizhu, Yanfei, Xingqiu and Chongyun appear. The mood is warm and humorous, with an underlying theme about balancing duty and rest.

Plot: Part I, The Blazing Stars Ring in Fortune: At Yujing Terrace Ningguang explains that the festival this year will include a fireworks show organised by the Ministry of Civil Affairs, with Keqing responsible. Keqing is seen revising plans, adding Qingce Village to the show's range and refusing to rest. Pengyi gives the Traveler a Launch Tube for designing fireworks. Ningguang worries about Keqing's long hours and asks the Traveler to help. At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and then Third-Round Knockout Zhongli advises that a story containing the message would work better than a lecture.

Part II, Sky-Gazers, Land-Walkers: Keqing asks the Traveler to introduce her to the adepti so she can deliver Qixing gifts. They visit Madame Ping, Cloud Retainer at Mt. Aocang, and Xiao at Wangshu Inn, and meet Qiqi and Baizhu on the way. Pengyi then reports that all the fireworks at Qingce Village have been stolen. The Traveler and Keqing follow footprints and meet Xingqiu and Chongyun, who have caught a Treasure Hoarder while escorting the Feiyun Commerce Guild's festival supplies. Keqing promises to find the stolen fireworks herself.

Part III, The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes: Keqing finds the stolen stash and waits with the Traveler for the hoarders to return. The Millelith's approach scares the hoarders into abandoning the fireworks; Keqing and the Traveler confront their leader Xingxiu and force a surrender. The Traveler meets Zhongli and Paimon invents a story with his help. At the Jade Chamber the Traveler tells Keqing a story of a chef who works himself to ruin, she recognises the message and admits she wishes she could slow time. The Fireworks Show begins, and everyone wishes each other a happy Lantern Rite.

Revelations: Keqing, privately, thinks Cloud Retainer is wary of mortal rule and wants a good first impression from the Qixing. Cloud Retainer asks Ganyu, Shenhe and Keqing to look out for one another, and tells Keqing that Ganyu forgets food and rest when busy and must be made to eat and sleep. Cloud Retainer says Moon Carver felt he could not simply roam into Liyue Harbor under the agreement that left the city to the Qixing, and went travelling instead. The Qixing now bear the daily running of Liyue.

Characters: Main: the Traveler, Paimon, Keqing, Ningguang, Zhongli. Others: Pengyi and Jingcheng (Ministry of Civil Affairs), Hu Tao, Xiangling, Guoba, Madame Ping, Yanfei, Cloud Retainer (Xianyun), Ganyu, Shenhe, Qiqi, Baizhu, Xiao, Verr Goldet, Granny Ruoxin, Xingqiu, Chongyun, Hongxing (guild attendant), Yun Jin, Kangsheng, Xingxiu, Xiuyong and the Treasure Hoarders. The finale cameo list includes Beidou, Xinyan, Smiley Yanxiao, Huai'an and Qiqi.

Consequences: The stolen fireworks are recovered, the thieves are handed to the Millelith and the show goes ahead. Keqing agrees to take a break and see it with the Traveler. Post-quest, Yun Jin is performing at Qingce Village at Granny Ruoxin's invitation, Xingqiu and Chongyun are lingering there, and the Traveler can speak with Zhongli, who spends the festival idly visiting Third-Round Knockout.

Placement: Released in Version 2.4 as a Flagship Event (with a Co-Op mode). It required Adventure Rank 28, the Archon Quest Chapter I Act III (A New Star Approaches) and Interlude Chapter Act I (The Crane Returns on the Wind). It follows the 2021 Lantern Rite and precedes later Lantern Rite events such as A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon.

332.comment: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Fireworks Show
332.content: The Ministry of Civil Affairs' first big fireworks show at Lantern Rite, organised by Keqing with Ningguang as head organiser. Fireworks are placed across Liyue, including Qingce Village, and fired together at a chosen moment. Ningguang explains that fireworks descend from firecrackers used by Liyue's ancestors for warding off beasts and signalling. The best view is said to be from the Jade Chamber.

333.comment: Fleeting Colors in Flight: The fireworks theft
333.content: Treasure Hoarders steal the fireworks placed at Qingce Village and elsewhere and stash them, planning to use them to cause a distraction on opening night and rob the harbor. Xingqiu and Chongyun catch one hoarder, Kangsheng, who insists he is mistaken. Keqing finds the cache and the Millelith corner the hoarders led by Xingxiu.

334.comment: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Keqing and the chef's story
334.content: Ningguang asks the Traveler to persuade Keqing to rest. Zhongli proposes a story, built from advice from Cloud Retainer, Yanfei and Xingqiu, about a chef who will not delegate or eat, falls ill and loses his customers. Keqing listens at the Jade Chamber, tells the Traveler the lesson is something she knows but forgets, and lets herself enjoy the show.

335.comment: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Gifts for the adepti
335.content: Keqing brings gifts from the Qixing to Madame Ping, Cloud Retainer and Xiao. Madame Ping receives seasonal goods, silk and flower seeds; Cloud Retainer receives a modified firework (chosen because she likes gadgets); Xiao is given food and declines to thank. Keqing hopes to give the adepti a good impression of mortal governance.

key: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn
336.comment: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn
336.content:
Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn (also: Chapter V Act I, Natlan Act I, Natlan! A New Adventure): Act I of Chapter V is the Traveler's arrival in Natlan. The Traveler and Paimon meet Kachina of the Children of Echoes, follow her to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, and meet Mualani and Kinich. They watch the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, a tournament that decides who fights the Abyss, and then visit Mualani's village, where the Traveler purges fresh Abyssal corruption from Mualani's gravely wounded friend Atea but cannot undo the old damage; she has only days to live.

Act I has three quests: "Natlan! A New Adventure", "Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame" and "Home of the Hot Springs". It requires Adventure Rank 40, and a quick start was offered from 5.0 until 6.0 to players who had completed "A New Star Approaches" (Adventure Rank 28). The Traveler cannot gain Pyro from the local Statue of The Seven, learns that Natlan's Pyro Archon is a human, and learns the basics of the tribes, Saurian companions, Ancient Names and the Ode of Resurrection.

Plot: **Natlan! A New Adventure.** After a farewell from Charlotte, Navia, Clorinde and Furina at Romaritime Harbor, the Traveler and Paimon sail to Natlan and find a village in a canyon. Kachina is told by her teammates that they are leaving her for the Pilgrimage. The Traveler offers to help and she guides them around the village, to the black stone that represents the tribe's Wayob and to the chief, Pacal. At the stadium city they meet Mualani, Kinich and his companion K'uhul Ajaw. The Pilgrimage is open only to Natlanese, so the Traveler cannot join. The group has dinner at the Weary Inn.

**Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame.** Mavuika opens the tournament with an address to the contestants. The Traveler and Paimon watch from the stands as Kachina and Mualani clear the team stage. Two disqualified contestants, Tepexpan and Tamuin, threaten Kachina and are stopped. Kachina wins her one-on-one matches, including a duel with her friend Mualani, and earns a place in the Night Warden Wars with Chasca, Iansan, Kaiulani and Kibangu.

**Home of the Hot Springs.** Mualani takes the Traveler to her village, the People of the Springs. Atea explains that outsiders must acclimate in the artificial springs first. During the night the Abyss attacks. Atea has destroyed an Abyssal pylon but is gravely wounded. The Traveler purifies the Abyssal energy from her wounds, as they once did for Dvalin, but the damage is too deep to heal. At a party the next day Atea tells Mualani and the Traveler she has only a few days to live and gives the Traveler her talisman to hand to the Pyro Archon.

Revelations: - Natlan's Pyro Archon, Mavuika, is a human, and opens the Pilgrimage in person.
- The Pilgrimage produces Contending Fire, which fuels the Sacred Flame that keeps the Abyss from invading; the tournament also picks who fights in the Night Warden Wars.
- Ancient Names mark those chosen by the Wayob, and the Ode of Resurrection can revive only those who hold them; fallen bearers go to the Night Kingdom.
- Natlan has six tribes: the Children of Echoes, Scions of the Canopy, People of the Springs, Masters of the Night-Wind, Flower-Feather Clan and Collective of Plenty.

Consequences: Kachina becomes a Night Warden War fighter, Mualani and Kinich become the Traveler's guides, and Atea's talisman is left with the Traveler. Act II follows: the Night Warden Wars are won, but Kachina falls in battle and Mavuika cannot find her in the Sacred Flame.

Placement: Follows Chapter IV Act VI "Bedtime Story" and is the first act of Chapter V. It was released in 5.0 alongside Act II, with Acts III and IV in 5.1.

337.comment: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn: Atea's talisman
337.content: Atea is a respected member of the People of the Springs and a friend of Mualani; long unable to fight or enjoy the springs since being impaled by an Abyssal monster, she volunteers for night patrol and is gravely wounded destroying an Abyssal pylon. The Traveler cannot heal the old Abyssal contamination. Atea hands her talisman to the Traveler to give to the Pyro Archon.

338.comment: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame
338.content: The Pilgrimage is a tournament held in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Teams collect Contending Sparks before one-on-one duels. It produces Contending Fire, which keeps the Sacred Flame burning, and chooses the Natlanese who fight in the Night Warden Wars.

key: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles World Quest series
Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble
339.content:
Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles (also: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles World Quest series, Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble, Institute Survey Anchor quests): Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles is a world quest series added in version 4.1. After the explosion that wrecked most of the Fontaine Research Institute, the surviving staff recruit outside adventurers. The Traveler and Paimon go through a slow qualification review, then escort a senior researcher named Nacker into the floating ruins of the Central Laboratory. A reporter from The Steambird, Chronie, follows them.

The series is a comedy of paperwork and institutional self-protection wrapped around a real danger: unstable Arkhium left over from the experiment of Edwin Eastinghouse. It consists of one main quest, "Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble", and two child quests that retrieve the last two Survey Anchors. It requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (the Fontaine prologue) to be completed.

Plot: The Traveler is told by Katheryne at the Adventurers' Guild in Fontaine, or runs into a recruiter named Desnos at the Qualifications Review Representative Office, that the Fontaine Research Institute needs outside help recovering assets from its ruined Central Laboratory. Before anyone may start, the Traveler must pass a layered qualification review. After a fight with two Recon Log Meks in the office and stacks of forms, the Traveler is assigned to escort Nacker, a senior researcher who once worked under Edwin Eastinghouse, to the ruins. The political reporter Chronie of The Steambird attaches herself to the group.

The first test is retrieving a Survey Anchor, a device that monitors Arkhium energy flow. The Traveler clears an obstruction at the Materials Office and takes the Anchor without the protective instruments the Institute normally requires, which impresses the staff. At the new Institute the co-administrators Raimondo and Choiseul praise the feat, deflect Chronie's questions, and send the group to collect the last two Anchors from the dormitories and the Institute of Clockwork Applications. Having passed the review, the Traveler goes with Nacker to the floating ruins and helps start a plan to land them safely.

A second, unplanned explosion scatters components of the Arkhium inhibitor. Raimondo and the Traveler stabilise the large Arkhium and shut down the Experimental Field Generator. Nacker has vanished. Raimondo blames him for stealing a core and detonating the Arkhium as a diversion; Chronie suspects the Institute is hiding how dangerous the ruins still are. The Traveler may either keep to Raimondo's version or tell Chronie everything.

Revelations: - The Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering was once the technological centre of the Court of Fontaine. The explosion of Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment destroyed most of it.
- The Central Laboratory ruins float, held up by a Gravity-Altering Field. The Institute plans to land them with an Experimental Field Generator running on a "Tri-State Arkhium".
- Survey Anchors measure Arkhium energy flow and are physically harmful to approach without instruments.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Desnos, the recruiter; Nacker, a senior researcher who once worked under Edwin; Chalmet and Conjat, Institute staff; Raimondo and Choiseul, who run the new Institute; and Chronie, a political affairs journalist for The Steambird. Edwin Eastinghouse appears only through other people's accounts.

Consequences: The Traveler becomes an Honorary Senior Researcher. The ruins are made safer for the moment but can explode again. Nacker and the Arkhium Kinetic Core are missing. Chronie goes away with a story critical of the Institute, or with the full truth if the Traveler tells it.

Placement: Requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, the Fontaine prologue. Released in version 4.1. The two Anchor-retrieval quests are children of the main quest and are completed in either order.

340.comment: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles: Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment
340.content: According to Nacker, Edwin Eastinghouse was developing a field generator powered by Arkhium that could lift an entire block of buildings. The Arkhium ore powering its Arkhium Kinetic Core exploded, leaving most of the Institute in ruins. The Generator itself survived. Raimondo says the core was the result of his own joint research with Edwin.

341.comment: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles: Survey Anchors
341.content: Survey Anchors are Institute devices used to monitor the strength of Arkhium energy flows. Proper retrieval needs special instruments, and exposure makes people ill. The Institute locks them up because they kept being stolen. Retrieving an Anchor serves as part of the qualification review for outside applicants, and Nacker says it consumed a lot of antiemetics.

342.comment: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles: Chronie of The Steambird
342.content: Chronie is a journalist in the political affairs section of The Steambird. She follows Nacker and the Traveler, asks pointed questions about Arkhium safety and the sale of research assets, and refuses to be fobbed off. She gets sick from Anchor radiation but keeps going.

343.comment: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles: Raimondo and Choiseul
343.content: Raimondo and Choiseul are the co-administrators of the new Fontaine Research Institute. Raimondo, a Senior Technician, drives the Tri-State Arkhium plan and welcomes the Traveler as an Honorary Senior Researcher. Choiseul handles reviews and public statements and is evasive when Chronie presses him.

344.content:
For a Tomorrow Without Tears (also: Prologue Act II, Mondstadt Archon Quest Act II): For a Tomorrow Without Tears is Act II of the Mondstadt Prologue, the first Archon Quest chapter. After the Four Winds temples are cleared, the Traveler returns to Mondstadt, is made an Honorary Knight of Favonius and joins the bard Venti in a plan to cure the dragon Stormterror, who is really Dvalin, of the corruption the Abyss Order is exploiting. The plan needs the Holy Lyre der Himmel, which must be obtained, recovered from the Fatui and repaired with Dvalin's tears. At Starsnatch Cliff an Abyss Mage turns Dvalin against them and the lyre is broken.

The act is where Venti's identity as Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, comes into the open, where Jean and Diluc become active allies, and where the Fatui and Abyss Order stop being background threats. It requires Adventure Rank 10 and ends with the cliff confrontation that sets up Act III.

Plot: The act begins with Shadow Over Mondstadt. Near the Goth Grand Hotel the Traveler finds Jean refusing a masked Fatui diplomat, Anastasia, who offers to have the Fatui "put an end" to the dragon; Jean rebukes her for proposing to destroy one of the Four Winds of Mondstadt. Back at the Knights' headquarters, Lisa examines the crystal the Traveler picked up in the forest and finds that it gives off energy harmful to Vision users, so the Traveler pockets it again, keeping quiet about why. Jean names the Traveler an Honorary Knight.

Paimon recognises the presence that clung to the crystal in a boy running through the streets, and the party follows his footprints with Elemental Sight. The boy is Venti. He sings of Stormterror and the reason for the dragon's rampage, and recognises the Traveler. When the Traveler takes out the crystal it has been purified, so Venti realises the Traveler's power can save Dvalin. He sends them to the great tree at Windrise, where the Hero of Mondstadt is said to have ascended to Celestia. After the Traveler beats an Eye of the Storm, Venti explains that Dvalin is suffering from a degradation that the Abyss Order is exploiting. His own earlier attempt to cure the dragon had gone wrong when the Traveler's unexpected arrival left him poisoned, though he had since recovered.

Venti's remedy is the Holy Lyre der Himmel, kept at the Favonius Cathedral. He asks Sister Gotelinde for it, even telling her he is Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, and she takes him for a madman. The Traveler asks properly, but borrowing it needs papers signed by the Grand Master, the Seneschal and the community representative, since it is currently used only for Ludi Harpastum. The Traveler sneaks into the vault, but a Fatui Electro Cicin Mage teleports in and takes the lyre, and a guard spots the Traveler. Venti's wind carries the party to the Angel's Share, where Diluc, the owner, gives them a quiet table and misdirects the pursuing Knights.

Revelations: - Venti is Barbatos, the Anemo Archon. He tells Gotelinde so (she does not believe him), Dvalin addresses him by that name, and Jean shows she has known for some time and keeps calling him Venti.
- Stormterror is Dvalin, one of the Four Winds, and has been degraded by something the Abyss Order manipulates. Jean already knows of Dvalin's past; the wider public treats Stormterror as a vicious dragon.
- The Teardrop Crystals are Dvalin's tears, and the Traveler can purify them.
- The Fatui are involved and hostile to Mondstadt's approach: a diplomat urges killing the dragon, a Fatui mage steals the Holy Lyre, and an agent invokes Signora.

Characters: Traveler: Honorary Knight, bearer of the power that purifies the crystals. Paimon: recognises Venti by his presence. Venti: bard and Anemo Archon, trying to heal his dragon friend. Jean: Acting Grand Master, constrained by office, acting privately with Diluc. Diluc: owner of the Angel's Share, who supplies information and shelter. Lisa: studies the crystal. Dvalin: the afflicted dragon, whose tears are the key material. Gotelinde: the Cathedral sister who refuses the lyre. The Traveler's sibling appears only in the final cutscene.

Consequences: The Holy Lyre is destroyed and Dvalin flees, now believing he was betrayed. Diluc takes on the job of tracking the Abyss Mage. These lead directly into Act III, where an Abyss Mage is killed at the winery, the Lair is entered and Dvalin is finally purified.

Placement: Prologue Act II, after The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (Act I) and before Song of the Dragon and Freedom (Act III). Released with version 1.0. Requires Adventure Rank 10.

345.comment: For a Tomorrow Without Tears: Holy Lyre der Himmel Plot
345.content: The Holy Lyre der Himmel is a sacred instrument kept at the Favonius Cathedral and in this period used only for Ludi Harpastum. Borrowing it formally needs signatures from three authorities. After a Fatui mage takes it, the party recovers it in poor condition and repairs it with Teardrop Crystals, which are Dvalin's tears, but the Abyss Order's interference at Starsnatch Cliff destroys it.

346.comment: For a Tomorrow Without Tears: Starsnatch Cliff Confrontation
346.content: At Starsnatch Cliff, Venti plays the restored lyre to call Dvalin. Before the dragon can listen, a Cryo Abyss Mage turns him against Venti, calling the bard a deceiver. Dvalin flies off in a rage, the lyre is wrecked, and Diluc and Jean resolve to hunt down the mage.

key: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku
347.comment: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku
347.content:
From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku (also: Byakuyakoku world quest series, Enkanomiya world quest series): From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku is the World Quest series, added in version 2.4, that introduces Enkanomiya, a hidden realm beneath Inazuma whose old name is Byakuyakoku. The Traveler and Paimon come to recover the Bloodbranch Coral, pass through a gate with the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep, and are drawn into a trial in the ruined kingdom. A helper named Enjou guides them, then proves to be an Abyss Order agent.

The series has two quests: The Entrance to Tokoyo and The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent, the latter in three parts (The Trail of Drake and Serpent, The Heart of Ouroboros, Dreams in the Gaps). It is gated behind the earlier Enkanomiya quest The Still Water's Flow.

Plot: Sent to Enkanomiya to fetch the Bloodbranch Coral, the Traveler and Paimon find no sign of people but discover a great gate. A second door opens with the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep. Inside a ruined library they meet Enjou, who calls himself clerical staff for a trial, says the realm's true name is Byakuyakoku, and says the next step is to enter the central tower, the Dainichi Mikoshi. A barrier protects it, and the kingdom's national treasure, the Golden Bridle, can break it. Enjou finds the Bridle at the back of the library.

At the tower Enjou asks to break the barrier himself. Inside, the central device is triggered and Ever-night falls. A Sinshade (a "Shade of Tokoyo", the remnant of a former inhabitant's thoughts) named Aru appears and explains the next trial: restore the Reins of Revival, a treasure able to make spirits of the Ever-night speak. The Reins are the Golden Bridle plus three fragments hidden around the tower, at The Narrows, The Serpent's Heart and the Evernight Temple. Enjou stays behind; the Traveler gathers the fragments.

Revelations: - Enkanomiya's real name is Byakuyakoku; the ruin first reached was its library (Enjou's account).
- The Dainichi Mikoshi provides the realm's imitation of sunlight, called White-night, which is separate from the Ever-night.
- Sinshades are remnants of the thoughts of Byakuyakoku's former people.
- Enjou is an Abyss Lector of the Abyss Order.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Enjou (Abyss Lector, Abyss Order), Aru (a Sinshade) and Tsuyuko, who receives the Bloodbranch Coral. Madam Kokomi is mentioned only.

Consequences: Tsuyuko learns the Abyss Order has infiltrated Enkanomiya and expects Kokomi to have to deal with it. Enkanomiya's White-night and Ever-night cycle and its Sinshades are established for the later Enkanomiya quests.

Placement: Released in 2.4. In-game it follows The Still Water's Flow, a prior Enkanomiya quest that is not written as a separate entry here.

348.comment: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku: Enjou
348.content: Enjou presents himself in Byakuyakoku as clerical staff assisting a trial, guides the Traveler to the Dainichi Mikoshi, then leaves. He is later revealed as an Abyss Lector of the Abyss Order who says he seeks records older than the tower. He is defeated in battle and departs, warning that Paimon might betray the Traveler.

349.comment: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku: Reins of Revival
349.content: A national treasure of Byakuyakoku made of the Golden Bridle and three fragments hidden at The Narrows, The Serpent's Heart and the Evernight Temple. Restored, it can make the spirits of the Ever-night speak. Aru, a Sinshade at the Dainichi Mikoshi, assigns the Traveler to reunite it.

key: From One Case to Another World Quest series
350.content:
From One Case to Another (also: From One Case to Another World Quest series, Pakpaka Flying School mystery, Saurus Cracker case): From One Case to Another is a four-part Natlan world quest series added in version 5.2. At Pakpaka Flying School in the Scorchwind Trial Grounds, a young student named Taruka suspects the cheerful instructor Lamizana of plotting something dangerous around an upcoming air race. The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One investigate and end up uncovering a scheme to steal and sell Saurians.

The tone is comic. Almost everyone misreads everyone else: Taruka's suspicions are half right, the real villain is a travelling merchant, and the Traveler is briefly accused of being an accomplice. The quest uses the Saurian Indwelling feature for some stealth and tracking.

Plot: **Incidents Are Ever Sudden.** Passing through a Recon Ring above the Scorchwind Trial Grounds brings the party to Pakpaka Flying School, where Temach introduces a training course with prizes. After the party passes it, the flashy instructor Lamizana gives out rewards, bickering with Taruka. Taruka asks the Traveler to investigate: he overheard Lamizana discussing something dangerous with an outsider, with phrases about being on time on race day and meeting at the north camp the next night.

**Beat the Clock: 24 Hours.** The party waits until the next evening, then uses an Iktomisaurus to sneak into the camp. They overhear two voices arranging a delivery of "goods" before the air race. Quilla, a travelling merchant, spots the Little One. A box of Saurus Crackers is knocked over elsewhere in the camp, drawing the Iktomisaurs, and the party slips away. Back at the school, Paran asks the Traveler to stand in for a contestant who has dropped out of the race against Taruka's sister Lliwa.

**An Air Race and an Alibi.** The Traveler races Lliwa. Lliwa's Saurian falters mid-race, and Taruka and his Qucusaurus Oberon go missing. Iktomisaurs attack Lamizana. He then confesses to a plan: he had arranged for young Saurians to stage a fake attack on Taruka at the finish line so that he could rescue the boy and impress Lliwa. Quilla suggests the real culprit is a Saurian trafficker named Hawka, mentions a blond youth with a white pet, and the group wrongly points at the Traveler and Paimon. The party escapes and goes back to the scene.

**Farewell, Final Saurus Cracker.** Following a scent, the party finds a letter from Hawka at Quilla's camp, revealing Quilla as the mastermind. They find Oberon in a cave; after he leaves, Quilla drops her "good merchant" act and sets her Saurian Furball on them. The Little One and Oberon win in a turn-based style fight. Taruka had already escaped by himself, Lamizana apologises, and the school offers its figurative open doors to the party.

Revelations: - Quilla, the apparently honest travelling merchant, is behind the scheme, as Paimon concludes from Hawka's letter and Quilla admits when cornered. She works with Hawka.
- Hawka, a Saurian trafficker, is Paran's uncle, who was exiled from the tribe long ago.
- Lamizana's "dangerous plan" was an ill-advised staged rescue to impress Lliwa; Quilla's group turned it into a real kidnapping.

Characters: Taruka (a young student at Pakpaka Flying School) and his Qucusaurus Oberon, his older sister Lliwa, Temach and Cisik of the flying school, the flashy Lamizana, the organiser Paran and his companion Carrewoof, the merchant Quilla and her Saurian Furball. Hawka appears only in his letter. Also the Traveler, Paimon and the Little One.

Consequences: Taruka and Oberon are safe, Lamizana apologises and offers compensation, and Quilla flees with Furball. Taruka asks the Traveler for the secret of getting along with young Saurians and says he wants to become the best adventurer of the Flower-Feather Clan and one day enter Ochkanatlan with Oberon.

Placement: Released in version 5.2, with no required quest. The second part starts after waiting for the next evening; An Air Race and an Alibi begins when the player approaches the Tribal Totem Pole of the Flower-Feather Clan; the last quest starts automatically.

351.comment: From One Case to Another: Taruka
351.content: Taruka is a young student at Pakpaka Flying School who is protective of his sister Lliwa and doubtful of Lamizana. He is clever and articulate, tends to see conspiracies, and strictly manages the diet of his Qucusaurus Oberon. He asks the Traveler to investigate, escapes captivity on his own, and ends the series wanting to become the clan's best adventurer.

352.comment: From One Case to Another: Lamizana
352.content: Lamizana is a boastful, charming senior figure at Pakpaka Flying School, fond of giving advice and of feeding Oberon Saurus Crackers. His plan to look like a hero in front of Lliwa goes badly wrong, and he is quick to apologise at the end, offering compensation and accepting a threatened kick from the Little One.

353.comment: From One Case to Another: Quilla
353.content: Quilla poses as a well-travelled merchant who trades in many kinds of goods (Paran says she deals in a wide variety). She is in fact a villain working with Hawka. She admits it only when cornered, and is better at talking than fighting.

354.comment: From One Case to Another: Paran and Hawka
354.content: Paran runs much of the practical work at Pakpaka Flying School, with Carrewoof. His family was exiled from the tribe, which makes some people treat him badly. Hawka, his uncle, is a Saurian trafficker exiled long ago, who is trying to lure Paran into his scheme.

355.content:
Golden Slumber (also: Golden Slumber series, Lost in the Sands, Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand): A four-quest Great Red Sand world quest series from Version 3.1. The Traveler and Paimon find a lost research party in the desert: the scholar Tirzad, the merchant's associate Nachtigal, and the Eremite mercenaries Jebrael and his daughter Jeht. Exploring King Deshret's ruins with the machine Benben, they are hunted by the Eremite leader Samail, and Jebrael gives himself to the Golden Slumber to stop him.

The series examines the gap between the Akademiya's picture of King Deshret as a tyrant and the faith his people had in him. It centres on Jebrael's secret past in the Eremite group Thutmose, the murder of Jeht's mother, and the Golden Slumber, a collective dreamland within the king's throne room. It leads straight into The Dirge of Bilqis, which continues Jeht's story.

Plot: Looking for Tirzad's missing party, the Traveler finds the group in a sinkhole and works with them to escape through ruins. They find a strange machine, Benben, which opens the sealed doors of the Khemenu Temple and a mural-hidden passage to the Mausoleum of King Deshret. Fatui and Eremites under Samail capture Benben, but the group recovers it. Samail pursues the Scarlet Sand Slate and Benben to the throne at Khaj-Nisut, where Jebrael enters the Golden Slumber to free the others and close the door.

Bonifaz, a Mondstadt merchant at Aaru Village, rented two Sumpter Beasts to the scholar Tirzad, who studies desert ruins with Nachtigal and two hired mercenaries. Contact stopped two days earlier, so the Traveler searches and finds the party at the bottom of a sinkhole with Jebrael and Jeht. Together they escape through a ruin, where Jeht finds the machine Benben, which makes Tirzad's Scarlet Sand Slate light up. Benben opens the Khemenu Temple and a mural-hidden passage to the Mausoleum of King Deshret, where a trap separates the group. Fatui and Eremites led by Samail take Benben; the group recovers it and Samail flees. At Khaj-Nisut, Samail uses Jeht as a hostage to force Jebrael to speak the prayer that opens the Golden Slumber. Samail enters and gains control of the building, so Jebrael follows to free the others and fades into the Slumber as the door seals. Jeht says she will go back to her father's original tribe, the Tanit.

Revelations: Jebrael was once a member of the Eremite group Thutmose and used his knowledge for it. Jeht's mother Ufairah, a researcher, was valuable to Samail for her knowledge of the desert and King Deshret. After Jeht was born, Jebrael began to doubt the morality of Thutmose's missions and planned to leave with his family, but Samail found out and killed Ufairah to make him stay. Samail was after King Deshret's treasures using Benben and the Scarlet Sand Slate, and the Fatui were working with the Eremites.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Jeht, Jebrael, Tirzad, Nachtigal, Bonifaz, Samail and Benben.

Jebrael is a taciturn former Eremite who works as a mercenary; Jeht is his friendly daughter who later returns to the Tanit; Tirzad is a scholar with Akademiya assumptions; Nachtigal is Bonifaz's associate; Bonifaz is a Mondstadt merchant in Aaru Village; Samail is the Eremite leader and villain; Benben is the machine that opens the ruins. Katheryne issues the commission.

Consequences: Jebrael is lost to the Golden Slumber, and Samail is also taken into it. Jeht goes back to the Tanit and the story continues in The Dirge of Bilqis, where she buries her parents' remains in the Eternal Oasis. Tirzad writes his paper on King Deshret's ruins.

Placement: Released in Version 3.1 and set in the Great Red Sand. Requires only The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. The Dirge of Bilqis (3.4) can begin a Daily Reset after finishing Golden Slumber; Old Notes and New Friends is the other listed follow-up.

356.content: In the Golden Slumber series, Jebrael is a former Eremite of Thutmose who left after Samail murdered his wife Ufairah. Samail pursues King Deshret's treasures. At Khaj-Nisut both enter the Golden Slumber, a collective dreamland, and Jebrael sacrifices himself so that Jeht and the others escape.

key: Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste Continued
Alliance of Artists to Overthrow the Evil Organization
357.content:
Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste (also: Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste Continued, Salsa and the evil organization, Alliance of Artists to Overthrow the Evil Organization): The series is five regional quests (Belleau, Court of Fontaine, Central Beryl, Southeast Beryl and West Beryl) that can be done in any order, plus a follow-up, Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste - Continued, that unlocks after all five. Each regional quest starts by opening a chest after a nearby Water Volume Detection Crystal puzzle. The Traveler then moves one object under Salsa's direction to a spot that follows the natural lines of the scenery. The tone is gentle comedy about taste, art and a child's earnest, slightly muddled view of the adult world. Each quest gives Adventure EXP, 20 Primogems and Mora, and the regional ones also open a scenic viewpoint.

Plot: Opening. In the first meeting, Paimon wonders why a puzzle looks so strange and decides the Adventurers' Guild uses such puzzles to train rookies. A girl named Salsa interrupts, introduces herself as the future of Fontaine's art scene, and, hearing that the Traveler and Paimon are adventurers, fears they belong to the "evil organization" in green that has spoiled the scenery. When they offer help she recruits them to rearrange the objects.

The task. The camera moves to a fixed overhead view. Salsa explains that nature has its own flow of lines, for example the pattern of the flower bushes, and that the ugly objects look wrong because they break it. The Traveler lifts the object, tries a few spots (Salsa notes when a placement is no better than before) and puts it on a natural line. Salsa is delighted and speaks about points, lines and planes being in harmony.

Salsa across the meetings. She leaves hurriedly to get home before her parents return and says she pretends to study when they are back. In a later meeting she frets that she has a compulsion disorder she read about in a book, and Paimon and the Traveler suggest a doctor. In another she admits she had forgotten her homework and the interruption spared her a scolding. In the last she asks whether the battle will ever end, then founds the "Alliance of Artists to Overthrow the Evil Organization and Protect the Future of Fontaine", naming herself number zero and the Traveler and Paimon members one and two. In one meeting she also says she complained to Katheryne at the Guild and got only the stock phrase "ad astra abyssosque".

Revelations: - The strange objects are not traps or Guild training aids: Ubu, an adventurer, made them as installation art.
- Salsa's parents work at the Fontaine Research Institute and are often away; Salsa says that is why she can slip out to sketch.

Characters: Salsa is a quest-only child NPC, a would-be painter who describes herself as a great artist and insists she is not a small child; she calls Paimon "Lil' Miss". The wiki describes her as light-skinned with long blonde hair and purple eyes. Ubu is a quest-only adventurer in the Adventurers' Guild who describes himself as an installation artist and is touchy about criticism. Paimon and the Traveler appear throughout; Katheryne is mentioned only.

Consequences: Each quest gives Adventure EXP, Primogems and Mora, and the five regional ones unlock viewpoints. The Continued quest ends the series with the Hydro Monument raised and the argument between Salsa and Ubu unresolved. Neither Ubu's vow nor Salsa's alliance is followed up in the material read.

Placement: Released in 4.0 with the Fontaine launch as optional world-quest content. The wiki gives the Archon Quest The Outlander Who Caught the Wind as the requirement, and the Continued quest follows the five regional ones. It has no bearing on the main plot.

key: The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit
358.content:
Grus Nivis Chapter (Kamisato Ayaka) (also: Grus Nivis Chapter, Kamisato Ayaka's Story Quest, Ayaka's Story Quest, The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit): Kamisato Ayaka's Story Quest. Ayaka finds the name Tsubaki in her late mother's notebook and asks the Traveler to help her find and visit Tsubaki, bringing a gift. The search leads to the discovery that Tsubaki was her mother's own secret persona, and Ayaka resolves to live without regrets.

The chapter has one act, The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit, released in Version 2.0, with five quests: A Private Commission, Woven Wishes, Food From Afar, Lasting Promise and With You. It is a quiet story about friendship, grief and the freedoms Ayaka's rank has denied her.

Plot: Ayaka asks the Traveler to accompany her to meet Tsubaki. She commissions a kimono and recovers stolen silk from ronin at Ritou, then tries to cook foreign food and fails, so the Traveler cooks instead. Following the notebook they find a hidden box under Tenshukaku and a second notebook, which shows Tsubaki and her mother were one person. Ayaka and the Traveler finish at a festival on Amakane Island.

A Private Commission. Ayaka tells the Traveler she found a note in her late mother's things naming Tsubaki, someone neither she nor Ayato had heard of. Custom requires a gift, and she would normally bring her brother but asks the Traveler instead.

Woven Wishes. Ayaka orders a kimono to her own design from Ogura Textiles & Kimonos, but the Sakoku Decree has cut off good Liyue silk. At Ritou, Kurisu of the International Trade Association says vagrants have stolen a silk shipment. Ayaka offers to help and, without revealing herself, drives off the ronin. Kurisu offers the silk free; Ayaka pays.

Food From Afar. At Kiminami Restaurant, the owner Anna tells the Traveler that Ayaka had few friends as a child because ordinary families feared her rank. An explosion follows from Ayaka's cooking attempt. The Traveler cooks Mushroom Pizza instead, and gives Anna the recipe. Ayaka thinks Tsubaki may be a fox envoy. She gives the Traveler a white heron hairpiece.

Lasting Promise. Following the notebook, they find a hidden box beneath Tenshukaku holding a second notebook. Ayaka learns her mother and Tsubaki were the same person, who had many wishes but was bound by duties to the clan and the commission.

With You. At Amakane Island's festival, Ayaka draws a prayer panel: she wants an Inazuma where everyone is happy, while the Traveler wishes to reunite with their sibling. Ayaka performs a dance to thank them.

Revelations: Tsubaki was Ayaka's mother herself; the name appears in her notebooks.

The notebooks show Ayaka's mother had many unfulfilled wishes because of her duties in the clan and the commission.

Characters: Kamisato Ayaka, the Traveler and Paimon.

Ogura Mio (Ogura Textiles & Kimonos), Kurisu (International Trade Association), Kiminami Anna (Kiminami Restaurant).

Consequences: Ayaka learns about her mother's hidden wishes and resolves to live without regrets. She forms a closer friendship with the Traveler, and gives them a white heron hairpiece.

Placement: Unlocks at Adventure Rank 30 after Chapter II Act I, The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia. Released in Version 2.0 and set during the Sakoku Decree, as Ayaka's difficulty in obtaining Liyue silk shows. No later acts exist as of 7.1.

359.content: A name found in a notebook belonging to Ayaka's late mother. Ayaka and the Traveler search for her, and discover that Tsubaki was her mother herself, who had many desires she could not fulfil because of her clan and commission responsibilities.

360.comment: Grus Nivis Chapter (Kamisato Ayaka): Ayaka's friendship
360.content: Anna, who runs Kiminami Restaurant, says Ayaka has been well regarded but had few friends because ordinary families avoided her out of fear. She is glad Ayaka now has the Traveler as a friend.

361.content:
Grus Serena Chapter (also: A Thousand Moonlit Miles, Xianyun's Story Quest, Grus Serena Chapter Act I): Grus Serena Chapter is Xianyun's Story Quest. In its one act, A Thousand Moonlit Miles, the adeptus formerly known as Cloud Retainer visits her disciples in human form, takes the name Xianyun, and helps the Traveler restore the memories of an elderly woman, Yuandai, who turns out to be a former crane in her care. It ends with Xianyun moving to Liyue Harbor.

It unlocks after The Crane Returns on the Wind at Adventure Rank 40. The tone is gentle and family-centred: a story of disciples, caring from a distance, and how adepti handle the passing of time among mortals.

Plot: Paimon visits Mt. Aocang and meets Cloud Retainer in human form. She goes to see Ganyu and Shenhe, takes the name Xianyun, and at Wanmin Restaurant meets Shuyu and her grandmother Yuandai, who has dementia. The group retraces Yuandai's past, then uses Xianyun's Suspensus Somnium Mechanism to restore her memory. Yuandai was a crane, Xianyun's follower, and reverts to her crane form. Shuyu becomes Xianyun's first disciple in the human world.

Xingqiu recalls a nameless heroine of chivalric novels who cleared spirits and bandits during a drought around fifty years ago and met an exorcist from Mt. Tianheng. The places tied to her are Wangshu Inn, Qingyun Peak and an area north of Jueyun Karst. At each, Yuandai recalls parts of her life, including the pills she took, and the group returns to Mt. Aocang for the device that helps her remember. Xianyun then moves to Liyue Harbor and sells some belongings, with Zhongli authenticating them.

Revelations: - Yuandai was originally a long-lived wild crane, taken in by Cloud Retainer, not a human heroine.
- The merchant who gave Yuandai medicine at Wangshu Inn was Xianyun in disguise.
- Xianyun was also the white crane who helped the sick Shuyu.

Characters: Xianyun (Cloud Retainer), Paimon and the Traveler; Ganyu, Shenhe, Xiao, Xingqiu, Zhongli; new characters Yuandai and Shuyu.

Supporting cast includes Huixin, Chef Mao, Madame Ping, Shaozu, Wenliu and Qingji. Xianyun is shown as warm, proud and bluntly practical, quietly caring for those she has taken in.

Consequences: Yuandai returns to her crane form and flies off, losing her sentience. Xianyun moves to Liyue Harbor and takes Shuyu as her first disciple in the human world, and adopts the name Xianyun in place of the title Cloud Retainer.

Placement: Released in Version 4.4 as Xianyun's Story Quest; requires The Crane Returns on the Wind (Interlude Chapter, Act I) and Adventure Rank 40. Xianyun's move to Liyue Harbor happens in this act.

362.comment: Grus Serena Chapter: Yuandai and Shuyu
362.content: Shuyu is a girl whose grandmother Yuandai has dementia. Yuandai was a long-lived crane taken in by Cloud Retainer, who took human form by a potion, married an exorcist from Mt. Tianheng and lived in seclusion. After her memory is restored she returns to crane form. Shuyu becomes Xianyun's first disciple in the human world.

363.comment: Grus Serena Chapter: Suspensus Somnium Mechanism
363.content: A device kept at Mt. Aocang that releases a soft breeze and an adeptal tune. It puts listeners in a relaxed, semi-hypnotic state that helps lost memories surface. Xianyun uses it on Yuandai and the Traveler.

364.content:
Hangout Event: Barbara (also: Barbara's Hangout Event, Wellspring of Healing, Barbara Hangout): Hangout Event: Barbara is a replayable, choice-driven story for Barbara, the Favonius Cathedral deaconess, added in Version 1.4. It has one act, Wellspring of Healing. The Traveler is asked to find Barbara, helps her avoid an overeager fan, tidies the Cathedral and shares a drink with her. It is lighthearted, low-stakes and has no effect on the main story.

Players need 2 Story Keys, Adventure Rank 26 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom to start it. Different choices lead to five named endings. It is permanent, repeatable content, not a limited-time event.

Plot: After Victoria's request, the Traveler finds Barbara in Wolvendom. Hearing Albert approach, Barbara does not want to deal with him yet. The Traveler can chase Albert away, which is decided by a hidden score from the conversation. If it goes badly, Albert keeps searching and the day ends on an anticlimax (Untimely Enthusiasm). Otherwise Barbara goes to check on Tunner while the Traveler returns to the Cathedral, where Victoria asks them to clean it for Barbara.
Barbara then returns and offers the choice of drink. If the Traveler picks the new drink at The Cat's Tail, Barbara goes ahead and is swamped by a group of fans. Persuading each fan to leave her alone, or failing to, still ends with the two relaxing over drinks (A Holiday in Mondstadt).

Revelations: The act reveals very little lore. It is character material: Barbara is well known and sought out by admirers, and the Church sisters worry when she is away for long. It also shows that Wolfhooks from Wolvendom, Sweet Flowers from Whispering Woods and Jueyun Chili from Liyue are what go into her Chilibrew.

Characters: Barbara, the Traveler and Paimon are the main characters. Sister Victoria, Albert (leader of the Barbara Fan Club) and Tunner appear early on.

Branch characters include the merchant Caishan, the wounded Uwe (a Treasure Hoarder), and fans at The Cat's Tail named Herman, Schulz and Susie.

Consequences: The Hangout Event has no lasting effect on the main story. Completing endings grants rewards (Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, talent or ascension materials and Barbara's special dish), and endings can be displayed as Lingering Moments in the Serenitea Pot mansion.

Placement: Released in Version 1.4. It unlocks after Song of the Dragon and Freedom but sits outside the main-story timeline: a day in Mondstadt with no dated events.

365.comment: Hangout Event: Barbara: Barbara Fan Club
365.content: In Barbara's Hangout Event, Albert leads the Barbara Fan Club, a group of enthusiastic admirers who look for Barbara around Mondstadt. Barbara does not want to meet Albert in Wolvendom, so the Traveler either sends him away or leads her off. Later, fans at The Cat's Tail crowd Barbara until the Traveler persuades them to leave her in peace. They are portrayed as harmless and over-eager.

366.content: Chilibrew is the drink at the center of Barbara's Hangout Event. Her home-made version needs Jueyun Chili and Sweet Flowers, which the Traveler and Barbara collect around Stone Gate and Whispering Woods. On another route the merchant Caishan gives them a Liyue Chilibrew in exchange. The ending for the home-made brew is The Taste of Hard Work, and the one for the Liyue version is A Fiery Flavor From Liyue.

367.content:
Hangout Event: Beidou (also: When the Crux Shines Bright, Beidou Hangout Event, Beidou's Hangout): Beidou's Hangout Event, a replayable, choice-driven side story in which the captain of the Crux fleet invites the Traveler aboard the Alcor to celebrate the fleet's return from Inazuma. It has one act, When the Crux Shines Bright, and five endings, depending on which of three routes you take: sailor training, a quiet treasure hunt, or a day of business in Liyue Harbor. It unlocks after the Inazuma Archon Quest Omnipresence Over Mortals.

Unlocking needs two Story Keys, Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest Omnipresence Over Mortals; it arrived in Version 2.3. The act holds five quests: A Special Guest (the hub), Life on the High Seas, Beneath the Surface, Guili Plains Treasure Hunt and Qingce Village Treasure Hunt. Hangout Events as a whole are replayable permanent content, so none of this is limited to a time window.

Plot: In A Special Guest the Traveler returns to the Alcor and is greeted by cheerful crew (Sea Drake, Furong, Huixing) who want to recruit them after hearing of the end of the Vision Hunt Decree. Beidou declines to let the crew press the Traveler, then offers a choice. Interested in sailor life, the Traveler goes to training; otherwise Beidou takes them aside to talk about a map she found.

**Sailor training.** Beidou explains that new recruits are split into the Shield of the Crux (survival, navigation, entertainment) and the Spear of the Crux (naval fighting and cargo deals). Choosing the Shield leads to Life on the High Seas; choosing the Spear leads to Beneath the Surface.

**Treasure hunt.** Beidou found a battered treasure map in an Inazuman pirates' wreck. She asks the Traveler to read it. Naming Guili Plains starts the Guili Plains Treasure Hunt; naming Qingce Village starts the Qingce Village Treasure Hunt.

Revelations: Beidou, in her own words, was homeless and about five or six years old when she reached a fishing village near Wangshu Inn and was taken in by the village chief. After the chief fell ill and died the following winter and the catch shrank, the villagers blamed her and drove her out, citing her name: Beidou is the Northern Dipper constellation, whose Alcor star is read as an omen of death, and some villagers shouted that the Northern Dipper controls death. She tells the Traveler this at the empty village (known to its former residents as "Downriver"). The Traveler can answer that they too might be called cursed, and Beidou accepts the company: she will share the blame, as captain, for anyone who tries to scapegoat the Traveler.

Characters: Beidou (captain of the Crux; confident, generous, and fond of drinking) carries the event. The Traveler is the player-chosen guest, and many dialogue options colour the mood. Notable recurring Crux crew: Sea Drake, Furong, Huixing (navigator), Yinxing (surgeon), Xu Liushi (lookout), Juza (chief mate), Mora-Grubber (accountant). One-route characters include Golden Alligator and his Treasure Hoarders (Guili), the villagers of Qingce (Granny Ruoxin, Ji, Wenjing, Pops Xing, Ren, Changping, Defu), Mr. Iron Abacus, Nei and Wai, and the Millelith squad.

Consequences: Each ending is a self-contained "Memory"; no ending changes the open-world story or any other quest. Rewards scale with how many endings the player has unlocked (Primogems, Adventure EXP, Hero's Wit and other items). The Guili route establishes that the Crux will give former Treasure Hoarders a path to honest work, and the Qingce route that villagers treat the fleet as an ally whose members come from their villages.

Placement: Release order: 2.3 (hangout system introduced earlier in 1.4). Story order: set after the Traveler returns from Inazuma, so after the Archon Quest Omnipresence Over Mortals and after the Vision Hunt Decree has been abolished. Characters refer to the Traveler as the person who ended it and to the Liyue Harbor event as past.

368.comment: Hangout Event: Beidou: Beidou's Childhood and the Name Beidou
368.content: In the Life on the High Seas photography route the Traveler brings Beidou to the empty fishing village near Wangshu Inn. She says it was once called Downriver because the villagers came from a place called Upriver, who taught her fishing. At five or six she chased a stray dog that had snatched half a rice bun; the dog collapsed and died, and fishermen fed her, and the village chief took her in. A year or two later the chief died, the catch fell, and the villagers called her a bringer of bad luck and drove her out, shouting about the Northern Dipper and death. She learned her name was a constellation, with the Alcor as an omen of death, only then. She recounts it without self-pity.

369.content: A Treasure Hoarder leader who is digging for treasure on Guili Plains when Beidou arrives. He panics at her name, begs mercy for his men, and is spared. He and his crew choose to leave banditry for port work offered by the Crux, and later share a poem clue to a second treasure. He wants to join the Crux someday; Beidou says nothing is impossible if they earn her crew's respect.

370.comment: Hangout Event: Beidou: Mr. Iron Abacus and the Guyun Deal
370.content: Mr. Iron Abacus is the warehouse owner in Beidou's covert deal in Liyue Harbor. When the Millelith raid the meeting, they find only ordinary sacks, so Beidou's presence works as a decoy while her accountant Mora-Grubber runs the actual transaction. The event portrays the Crux as an armed carrier that also trades goods outside strict official channels.

371.comment: Hangout Event: Beidou: Beidou's Philosophy of Favours
371.content: In Qingce Village, Beidou says she is not an arbiter like Ningguang or Yanfei; her strength is trading favours. She argues that favours keep people connected and form an invisible net that catches anyone who falls, and that these bonds, not law, are what the Crux has survived on. She admits some of her solutions are "stupid" but says the point is that nobody leaves feeling cheated.

372.comment: Hangout Event: Beidou: Crux Training Staff
372.content: Yinxing is the Crux's surgeon and has Beidou's full authority to keep unfit recruits ashore. Huixing is the fleet's navigator, deciphering old charts with books Beidou obtains. Xu Liushi is the lookout, once a laughingstock for a drunken fall into the sea, and credits Beidou's judgment for his place. Juza is the chief mate who schedules the training. Together they show that Beidou lets each person master a role so the fleet does not rest on her alone.

373.content:
Hangout Event: Bennett (also: Bennett's Hangout Event, Fantastic Voyage, Bennett Hangout): Hangout Event: Bennett is a replayable, choice-driven story for the Adventurers' Guild member Bennett, released in Version 1.4, with one act, Fantastic Voyage. Bennett asks to adventure with the Traveler, and whichever outing they pick, his famously bad luck shapes the day. It is a comedy with no effect on the main story.

It requires 2 Story Keys, Adventure Rank 26 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom. There are six endings. Permanent, repeatable content.

Plot: Around town, Bennett needs materials. With Wind Comes Glory is out of stock, the Good Hunter turns them away because the cook, Sara, is busy with a meal order for a delegation from Snezhnaya, and Mondstadt General Goods seems to be offering 50% off everything. When Blanche finally appears she says the shop is closed and the promotion was for the day before (ending: Fruitless Anticipation).
In the wilds, Bennett suggests a stroll in a dandelion meadow. The dandelions have been stripped of seeds, a monster camp is empty and its chests hold only vegetables and a little Mora, and the weather turns into a thunderstorm. Jack arrives to take Bennett home because his dads have been asking for him, and the weather clears the moment he goes (Hasty Farewell).

Revelations: The act confirms that Bennett's bad luck is a long-running, widely known fact, that Benny's Adventure Team has dwindled to Bennett alone, and that his former teammates left because of the danger, without bitterness.

Characters: Bennett and the Traveler are the main characters.

Depending on the route: Sara, Blanche and the shops of Mondstadt (town); Jack (wilds); Royce (Thermadon ruins); Katheryne is mentioned in the Eya ruins.

Consequences: No lasting effect on the main story. Rewards are given per ending (Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, talent or ascension materials, Bennett's special dish), and endings can be shown as Lingering Moments in the Serenitea Pot.

Placement: Released in Version 1.4. It unlocks after Song of the Dragon and Freedom but sits outside the main timeline, with no dated events.

374.comment: Hangout Event: Bennett: Benny's Adventure Team
374.content: In Bennett's Hangout Event, Bennett says Benny's Adventure Team is now a team only in name, because he is the only member left. Royce, Heckler and Jack were once part of it; they left because of the accidents that follow his bad luck. Katheryne has kept the team registered out of pity. Bennett hopes its name will one day be known all over Teyvat.

375.content: Royce is a former member of Benny's Adventure Team who left after repeated accidents. In the Thermadon ruins route he is trapped alongside Bennett and the Traveler, blames Bennett, then asks for food. If he eats the Ominous Dish he falls ill; if refused, he parts ways with Bennett, wishing him well.

376.content:
Hangout Event: Chongyun (also: Signs of Evil, Chongyun Hangout Event, Chongyun's Hangout): Chongyun's Hangout Event, a replayable, choice-driven side story. The earnest young exorcist approaches the Traveler on Liyue Harbor's wharf asking whether they have seen any evil spirits. The one-act event, Signs of Evil, branches on whether the Traveler tells him his leads are far-fetched (popsicles, children and the Wanwen Bookhouse) or humours him (the Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill), and ends in one of six outcomes, none of which changes the wider story.

It was added in Version 1.4 with the Hangout Event feature and requires two Story Keys, Adventure Rank 26 and completion of the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom. Its quests are Hard to Track, Distant Gaze, The Exorcist's Path, Popsicles and Their Curious Uses, For A Child's Smile, Test of Courage, The Bottom of Things, Sudden Discomfort, Ever Deeper, Killjoy and Independent Actions. The tone is gentle and comic: Chongyun takes everything seriously, and the humour comes from the gap between his earnestness and what the Traveler finds.

Plot: In Hard to Track Chongyun explains that he is an exorcist, that all demons and monsters are "evil spirits" to those who practise exorcism, and that he protects Liyue's people from them. He praises the yakshas and says exorcists and yakshas have long guarded Liyue together, one openly and one in secret. He then lists several clues he has gathered, including a flyer for the Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill. The Traveler's choice here forks the event.

**Branch one: A Curious Gaze.** If the Traveler says the clues sound far-fetched, Chongyun grows dejected, his pure-yang energy heats him, and he eats a popsicle to cool down. A boy, Dalong, watches them. The boy admires the popsicle, saying he and his sister are poor and rarely eat snacks. Giving the boy one popsicle sends him off happy and the pair visit Wanwen Bookhouse to check Chongyun's clues (given by his friend Xingqiu), find them unreliable, and then follow a last snippet to Wuwang Hill. There they find strange smoke Chongyun says an evil spirit left, fight the hilichurls around it and cannot catch the spirit, but he counts the trip a success. Ending: Blessing in Disguise. Giving the boy both popsicles instead leaves Chongyun short; the Traveler helps him make more at Wanmin Restaurant. A cooling mix or sweet mix works. A "curious" mix with spicy ingredients sends Chongyun haywire and ends the event: Can't Beat This Heat. With good popsicles, they take some to Dalong and his sister Little Le, play hide-and-seek and share cold noodles. Ending: Idle Amusements.

**Branch two: To Take a Test of Courage.** If the Traveler humours him, they join the Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill, where couples are being frightened by staged scares. The staff (run by Zhouliang, with Fu San'er) are annoyed by Chongyun's questions. Drinking a potion can leave Chongyun suffering from unstable yang energy, requiring cooling recipes (Cryo Slime condensate or Cryo Whopperflower nectar) in Sudden Discomfort. In The Bottom of Things or Ever Deeper the Traveler learns the "ghost" is a staff member in costume, and in Killjoy must decide how to tell Chongyun. Telling him ends the route at Nothing Gained or Small Regrets, depending on the path.

Revelations: The event establishes that Chongyun regards exorcist work as an ordinary job that simply must be done, that he respects the yakshas, and that in the Qianqian ending he weighs good and evil in each spirit rather than treating every ghost as an enemy. It also reaffirms that his pure-yang energy needs regular cooling to stay under control.

Characters: Chongyun leads; the Traveler is the player guide. Dalong and Little Le are siblings, young children who say they are poor; Dalong hurries off to Chihu Rock with his popsicle. Zhouliang and Fu San'er run the Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill, with other staff and visitors (Uncle Jia, Lu Zheng, Dandan, Junjun, Chan'er) appearing in the scares. Xingqiu is mentioned as the friend who passed Chongyun the rumours.

Consequences: No ending changes any other quest or the wider story. Rewards scale with the number of endings unlocked; the six endings are Blessing in Disguise, Idle Amusements, Can't Beat This Heat, Nothing Gained, Goodbyes and Small Regrets.

Placement: Release order: Version 1.4, alongside the hangout system itself. Story order: it requires the Liyue Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom, so it takes place after Rex Lapis' apparent death and the Traveler's Liyue adventure. Nothing in the event depends on later story.

377.comment: Hangout Event: Chongyun: Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill
377.content: A staged "haunted" attraction at Wuwang Hill where visitors, often couples, are frightened by staff in costume. Chongyun hopes it hides a real evil spirit. The staff, led by Zhouliang, treat it as entertainment and resent being questioned; a real ghost, Qianqian, is present in one branch.

378.content: The ghost of a young child at Wuwang Hill. She fears Chongyun's pure-yang energy, which she believes could make her disappear, and she asks the Traveler to lead him away. After scaring off the staff, she is spared by Chongyun on the condition that she never harms anyone.

379.comment: Hangout Event: Chongyun: Dalong and Little Le
