379.content: Dalong is a boy who approaches Chongyun and the Traveler hoping for a popsicle for himself and his sister Little Le; the siblings say they are poor and seldom get snacks. In the best path Chongyun plays hide-and-seek with them and serves cold noodles, and the children invite him to play more.

380.content: Chongyun keeps popsicles on hand to suppress his pure-yang constitution, which makes him run hot and can destabilise when he is stressed. The event lets the Traveler make cooling or sweet versions at Wanmin Restaurant from Mist Flowers and Qingxin, or Valberries and Sunsettias, while a spicy "curious" version backfires.

381.content:
Hangout Event: Diona (also: Diona's Hangout Event, The Cat and the Cocktail, Diona Hangout): Hangout Event: Diona is a replayable, choice-driven story for Diona, the bartender of The Cat's Tail, released in Version 1.5, with one act, The Cat and the Cocktail. The Traveler visits The Cat's Tail, where Diona is out of ingredients and exasperated with her drunken customers, and joins her either in finding the bar's missing cats or in hunting for ingredients for a new special cocktail. It is a comedy with no effect on the main story.

It requires 2 Story Keys, Adventure Rank 26 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom. There are five endings. Permanent, repeatable content.

Plot: Cats branch: the Traveler helps Diona find three cats (Roger, Nelson and Paisley) around Mondstadt, using a cat toy for one and cat food for another. Depending on later choices the story ends either with the cats behaving unpredictably (The Unfathomable Felines) or with the cats coming home and The Cat's Tail starting a cat party (Cat Party).
Cocktail branch: Diona decides to use the herbal soup that samachurls make in Dadaupa Gorge as a base for a new cocktail. A hunter told her the soup smells overwhelming. She and the Traveler go to the gorge and meet Allan, a hunter who works with her father.

Revelations: Little lore is revealed. The act confirms that Diona thinks of herself as a professional bartender and is annoyed by adults who cannot control their drinking, that her father Draff drinks heavily and takes part in hunts with Allan, and that The Cat's Tail is a popular bar with resident cats.

Characters: Diona and the Traveler are the main characters.

Supporting characters include Margaret and Nimrod at The Cat's Tail, Draff and Allan in Dadaupa Gorge, the Dawn Winery's Connor and Elzer, and the cats Roger, Nelson and Paisley.

Consequences: No lasting effect on the main story. Rewards are given per ending (Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, talent or ascension materials, Diona's special dish), and endings can be shown as Lingering Moments in the Serenitea Pot.

Placement: Released in Version 1.5. It unlocks after Song of the Dragon and Freedom but sits outside the main timeline, with no dated events.

382.comment: Hangout Event: Diona: The Cat's Tail Bartender
382.content: In Diona's Hangout Event she works the bar at The Cat's Tail, which is known for specialty drinks and its cats. She refuses to compromise on her recipes: any drink made by her hands, she says, can only be a good one. Customers love the cocktails, which is why she is often out of ingredients.

383.comment: Hangout Event: Diona: Samachurl Herbal Soup
383.content: A strong-smelling soup made by samachurls in Dadaupa Gorge. Diona hears of it from an adventurer and wants it as a base for a cocktail. In the hangout it proves powerful enough to sober up Draff immediately, but Diona decides it is probably unusable in a drink.

384.content:
Hangout Event: Faruzan (also: A Confounding Conundrum, Faruzan Hangout Event, Faruzan Hangout, A Mysterious Senior...?, Essential Classic, Early Learning Mechanism, Wanderings of a Lonesome Shadow): Faruzan's Hangout Event, a single-act, branching side story added in Version 3.5. Tighnari asks the Traveler to help bring the veteran Haravatat researcher Faruzan to Pardis Dhyai for help with banned research, and the Traveler finds her cornered by Akademiya administrators over her lack of teaching or collaboration. Depending on the Traveler's choices the story becomes a reading course for Collei, a children's-toy collaboration with Kshahrewar and Acara Crafts, or a trip into the desert about a machine called the Ruin Wanderer, where Faruzan is reunited with an old companion. There are five endings.

The act is A Confounding Conundrum. It needs Adventure Rank 40, two Story Keys, and completion of the Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and the story quest The Unanswerable Problems. It opens with A Mysterious Senior...? and then splits into three lines: Essential Classic, Early Learning Mechanism and Wanderings of a Lonesome Shadow.

Plot: Tighnari is waiting at Pardis Dhyai for Faruzan and sends Collei, who is nervous around her, with the Traveler to Sumeru City to find out why she is late. They find Faruzan being pressed by an Akademiya official, Nadwah, to either teach a course or join a collaborative project, because Haravatat students and other advisers have complained that she does neither. She puts the matter off, and the Traveler has a private word with Collei.

The player then chooses how to help. Either they help settle her Akademiya problem first, choosing between a Haravatat course and a Kshahrewar collaboration, or they find a pretext to take her to Pardis Dhyai. Helping with the course leads to Essential Classic, in which Faruzan founds a reading course for Collei as a public pilot, hunts for teaching material and learns how much taste in books has changed. Helping with the collaboration leads to Early Learning Mechanism, in which she designs a puzzle toy and a reference book for Acara Crafts. Taking the pretext route leads to Wanderings of a Lonesome Shadow, in which she repairs Collei's companion Karkata and is drawn into a desert mystery. Every route ends with a short ending scene; the five endings are Stories of the Past, Knowledge is Wealth!, The Gardener and the Nursery, Start Over, and "Welcome Back, Faruzan."

Revelations: Faruzan's old machine Tamimi spent roughly a hundred years searching for her until its Restitution Module wore out, carrying letters from her teacher and family. Raed, who leads the desert expedition, passed off other wreckage as the "Ruin Wanderer" in an attempt to mislead the Akademiya.

Characters: Faruzan is proud, insists on "Madam", is affectionate toward Collei, scornful of the present Akademiya's priorities but respectful of Kshahrewar's methods. Collei is anxious around her but trusts the Traveler. Tighnari is the quiet organiser of the real task. Nadwah, Anis, Mamdouh, Maddah, Kamal and Raed are minor figures of the individual branches. Karkata and Tamimi are the machines.

Consequences: No branch changes Teyvat's main story. The event settles Faruzan's standing in the Akademiya for the player (course, collaboration or neither), shows her bond with the Traveler, and leaves Karkata repaired with parts from the desert. Whether Tighnari and Collei learn of Tamimi depends on the ending.

Placement: Released in Version 3.5. It requires the Sumeru Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and is therefore set after Sumeru's main story. Describing Faruzan generally should not assume any single ending.

385.content: Tamimi is a machine from Faruzan's past. Her teacher and friends remodelled its Self-Repair function into Self-Learning so it could search for her and deliver letters. In the desert it was known as the Ruin Wanderer. After roughly a hundred years its Restitution Module was failing. Faruzan cannot yet repair it and uses the replacement parts for Karkata instead, promising to revive it later.

386.content: A puzzle toy devised by Faruzan for Acara Crafts: rings of different sizes are moved one at a time between poles and a larger ring may not sit on a smaller one. It follows the Tower of Hanoi puzzle. Seven layers need 127 moves.

387.comment: Hangout Event: Faruzan: Tales of Shahryar
387.content: A popular series from a hundred years ago, written by a Vahumana researcher who studied folk legends. Faruzan remembers it as a classic and cannot find it now; the storyteller Maddah says its author kept extending it instead of writing an ending and abandoned it. The more lasting Legend of Antara was the same author's original draft.

388.content:
Hangout Event: Gorou (also: The Canine General's Special Operations, Gorou Hangout Event, Gorou's Hangout Event): Hangout Event: Gorou is a branching, player-choice side story added in version 2.3 (Act I, "The Canine General's Special Operations"). Gorou, general of the Watatsumi Island resistance, spends a day on Narukami Island with the Traveler. He is rattled by Yae Miko's teasing, secretly answers readers' letters for a magazine under the pen name "Ms. Hina", and wants to recover a buried box of fallen soldiers' belongings. The tone is light and warm with one quietly sad thread. Five endings are possible.

The event needs two Story Keys and first requires the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals" and the story quest "Warriors' Dreams Like Spring Grass Renewing". Everything starts from one scene near Yae Publishing House and fans out into five branches, each closing on a one-line ending card. The branches are alternate versions of the same day, not a continuous chronology.

Plot: The first choice splits the day. Telling Gorou to ignore Yae Miko leads either to the readers' letters (endings "The Smiling Send-Off" or "That's, Uh...") or to the box left on Nazuchi Beach (ending "Final Remembrance"). Offering to help him overcome his weakness leads to seeking advice or role-play training (endings "Tactical Retreat" and "Desserts Are the Best!").

Revelations: - Gorou writes the advice column of Yae Publishing House's magazine "That's Life" as "Ms. Hina". Readers see a gentle older-sister figure and write to him as a friend. He enjoys it: people in the army are reserved with a general, but letters remove that distance.
- Yae Miko oversees marketing for the magazine and rescued it from cancellation; she remains the final approver for the shop's books.
- Gorou does not realise the fan club's Ms. Hina is himself; he is never told in this event.
- The box Gorou buried held soldiers' everyday keepsakes, left for their families because weapons and armour were broken or hard to carry.

Characters: Gorou is the lead; the Traveler is his confidant. Yae Miko (Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine and chief editor of Yae Publishing House) teases him in the opening scene. Also present, depending on branch: Aratani and Kuroda of Yae Publishing House; Shuuhei, Miwa and other soldiers on Watatsumi Island; the soldier Hiroaki; the Ms. Hina fan club (Nobuhiro, Hiroshi, Yuka); Katheryne; Kozue of Komore Teahouse; the dog Taroumaru; and the Treasure Hoarders Kousuke and Yasuhisa.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. Its value is characterisation: Gorou off the battlefield, shy, kind and a little overwhelmed by Inazuma's clever people.

Placement: Released in version 2.3. It is set after the Watatsumi Island war and the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals", with Sangonomiya Kokomi governing and Gorou as her general. Watatsumi Island is at peace with the Shogunate, so Gorou can travel Narukami Island. No later-version content (6.x to 7.1) was found that revises the event.

389.comment: Hangout Event: Gorou: Ms. Hina Advice Column
389.content: In Gorou's hangout, "That's Life" is a monthly Yae Publishing House magazine whose advice column is signed "Ms. Hina". Gorou writes it. The editors have staff copy each letter by hand and strike out names. Fans think of Ms. Hina as a gentle, understanding older sister who is weaker on romance questions, and a fan club formed. As recited by Nobuhiro, its rules are: do not pry into Ms. Hina's identity, make no controversial statements as club members, do not force the message on the uninterested, and keep improving oneself. Gorou has no idea the fans mean him.

390.comment: Hangout Event: Gorou: Nazuchi Beach Memorial Box
390.content: Gorou's buried box held water bottles, towels, knee guards and similar ordinary items, each marked with its owner's name, left by soldiers who expected to die in the Nazuchi Beach battle. He buried it hastily during the retreat. The Adventurers' Guild dug it up while investigating the theft of Taroumaru's reserve fund from Komore Teahouse by a five-person Treasure Hoarder gang led by Kousuke, hiding below Tenshukaku. After Gorou and the Traveler catch them, Katheryne returns the box and Gorou takes it to Watatsumi Island for the families. He tells himself that next time he must be stronger.

391.comment: Hangout Event: Gorou: Gorou and Yae Miko
391.content: Throughout the event Yae Miko teases Gorou about his tail and ears, clearly enjoying herself. Gorou's side is not fear of her power but discomfort at being read: her smile and unhurried gaze make him feel he has nowhere to hide. He says he can handle her in battle but not in everyday conversation. The Traveler's impersonation of her fails because he trusts the Traveler.

392.content:
Hangout Event: Kaeya (also: Kaeya's Hangout Event, Shenanigans and Sweet Wine, Kaeya Hangout): Hangout Event: Kaeya is a replayable, choice-driven story for Kaeya, the Knights of Favonius Cavalry Captain, released in Version 3.8, with one act, Shenanigans and Sweet Wine. The Traveler meets Kaeya far from home in Port Ormos in Sumeru, where he is on a Knights business trip, and spends the following days with him: watching and joining a theatre troupe, returning to Mondstadt, or going on to Liyue. It is a light, witty story with no effect on the main story.

It requires 2 Story Keys, Adventure Rank 35, and the Archon Quest Caribert plus the Story Quest Secret Pirate Treasure. There are five endings. Permanent, repeatable content.

Plot: Opening: in Port Ormos Kaeya, travelling alone and bored, jokes about luring a Dusk Bird onto his shoulder, and greets the Traveler warmly. He proposes making his business trip a joint trip and, since the Knights count all expenses on a trip as travel expenses, treating it as a chance to live a little.
Stage branch (Questions): at Port Ormos a troupe is performing a drama about Prince Qubad, who rejects his father's war. When the actor playing Qubad is missing, Kaeya fills in, wearing Sailwind Shadow. He improvises, asks the audience if they believe in fate and throws the prop intaglio to the Traveler. The Traveler's answer shapes the scene, and Kaeya ends it by having the prince defy fate and leave. The ending is named Questions.
Mondstadt branches: if the Traveler declines to spend public money, Kaeya packs and they return to Mondstadt; he gives the Traveler a lamp as a souvenir. From there:
- A Boat Untethered: Kaeya, wanting to relax, takes the Traveler to the Cathedral plaza. Sister Grace has a problem, which the Traveler explains to Venti at the Angel's Share. A group including Barbara and Diona later gathers in the plaza to prepare a new song, and Kaeya hesitates to join; Venti gives him a poem and invites him to sing with everyone.
- The Grapes of Warmth: they visit Dawn Winery, where Kaeya teases Diluc and picks grapes with Tunner, who asks Kaeya and the Traveler to read a letter from his son, Guy.
- Our Sun: back at the winery, Kaeya and Adelinde, with the Traveler, share a home-cooked meal; Klee turns up to rescue Kaeya from a grounding.

Revelations: Little new lore is revealed. It adds personal detail: Kaeya's work for the Knights extends to travel, the Dawn Winery's staff think of him as family, and he says that people who owe him favours are either his friends or his informants.

Characters: Kaeya and the Traveler are the main characters.

Mondstadt: Venti, Barbara, Diona, Sister Grace and the bards (Poems Dedicated to the Wind); Jean, Lisa, Albedo and Klee; Diluc, Elzer, Tunner, Adelinde and Connor at Dawn Winery. Sumeru: the theatre troupe including Darbil, Zabi and Tus. Liyue: Captain Wu, Guangzhi, Aunt Zhang and Mr. Bai.

Consequences: No lasting effect on the main story. Rewards are given per ending (Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, talent or ascension materials, Kaeya's special dish), and endings can be shown as Lingering Moments in the Serenitea Pot.

Placement: Released in Version 3.8. It unlocks after the Archon Quest Caribert and the Story Quest Secret Pirate Treasure. The act sits outside the main timeline.

393.content: In Kaeya's Hangout Event, Albert Rich is the alias Kaeya uses in Liyue Harbor to pose as a wealthy, bored young lord from Mondstadt in order to bait a swindler. The wiki notes the name echoes Kaeya's family name, Alberich.

394.comment: Hangout Event: Kaeya: Prince Qubad play
394.content: In Port Ormos, a travelling troupe performs a drama about Prince Qubad, who refuses to let his father wage war and chooses exile instead. Kaeya takes over the missing role, improvises, and gives the Traveler the prop intaglio, Prince Qubad's Intaglio, when the Traveler first completes the quest. Tus, a caravan owner, praises the performance and invites Kaeya to visit his caravan.

key: The Pendulum of Weal and Woe
395.content:
Hangout Event: Kaveh (also: The Pendulum of Weal and Woe, Kaveh Hangout Event, Kaveh Hangout, The Sixth Proposal, A Refuge in the Sands, Past Mementos, Treasure and True Interest): Kaveh's Hangout Event, a single-act, branching side story added in Version 3.7. The Traveler finds the architect Kaveh depressed in a tavern after the sixth rejected design for a vague, stingy client, and follows him through one of several routes: a children's library in the desert village of Aaru, a hunt for sponsors with the merchant Dori, a locked box of his mother's mementos, or a scam that exploits his former classmate's architecture training centre. There are five endings.

The act is The Pendulum of Weal and Woe. It requires Adventure Rank 40, two Story Keys, and completion of the Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and the story quest The Illusions of the Mob. The first quest, The Sixth Proposal, leads to three branch quests: A Refuge in the Sands, Past Mementos and Treasure and True Interest.

Plot: In The Sixth Proposal Kaveh argues with a client, Badawi, who keeps asking for changes to a design in the desert. The Traveler meets him afterwards in a tavern, where Kaveh asks whether art is a divine gift or the product of one's own struggle and asks the Traveler to keep another secret. The Traveler then chooses what to do. Helping Kaveh convince the client leads to A Refuge in the Sands. Doing something else to clear his mind leads to Past Mementos. Elsewhere, when the talk turns to his money troubles, Kaveh remembers a former classmate who offers him a lucrative teaching job, which leads to Treasure and True Interest.

In A Refuge in the Sands the pair follow Badawi and learn that he is a former Eremite mercenary who has been disguising himself as a merchant because he feared being cheated; the building is a library for children in the desert, to be built at Aaru Village. The Traveler can propose a slightly different style, which sends the group to Aaru and ends in Blueprint for the Future, or a search for sponsors, which goes through Dori and ends in A Done Deal. In Past Mementos Kaveh digs out a box of his mother's old things and a locked notebook; the Traveler can look for her old acquaintances, ending in Leisurely Gathering after a dinner at Pardis Dhyai, or make a trip to places Kaveh loves, ending in Beneath the Stars. Treasure and True Interest ends in First Class.

Revelations: Kaveh is the son of a gifted architect, Faranak, who now lives in Fontaine; she left the locked notebook and her old things to him, and his father died when Kaveh was a child. Badawi, who commissions the library, used to be an Eremite mercenary. Dori already owned most of Aaru Village.

Characters: Kaveh is the lead; the Traveler and Mehrak accompany him. Badawi is the client and former mercenary. Dori is the merchant and creditor. Alkami is the exploitative former classmate. Zaha Hadi is a retired professor who taught his mother. Alhaitham, Tighnari and Cyno appear in the friendship-oriented routes, and Cyno in the training-centre case.

Consequences: No branch changes Teyvat's main story. Each ending settles one thread for the player: a library design for Aaru Village, funding through Dori, a closer link between Kaveh and his friends, a reflection on his art, or students freed from a debt scam.

Placement: Released in Version 3.7. It requires the Sumeru Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and is set after Sumeru's main story. Describing Kaveh generally should not assume any single ending.

396.content: Badawi is the client of Kaveh's sixth proposal. He is an older former Eremite mercenary who hid his identity from Kaveh because he feared swindlers. He wants an affordable library for the children of the desert, placed at Aaru Village. He is stingy because he is saving the Mora himself.

397.content: A Kshahrewar graduate and former senior classmate of Kaveh who runs an architecture training centre. He pushes students into loans with a lender named Fakhr and promises a wealth that architecture rarely gives. After Kaveh and the Traveler expose him, the matra close the centre and investigate.

398.content: A locked notebook that Faranak left behind when she moved to Fontaine. Kaveh could not open it as a child. In the Wondrous Times branch he reads her diary and a message addressed to him about forming connections beyond one's art.

399.content:
Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu (also: The Gang's Daily Deeds, Kuki Shinobu Hangout Event, Shinobu's Hangout Event): Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu is a branching, player-choice side story added in version 2.7 (Act I, "The Gang's Daily Deeds"). After three Arataki Gang members are arrested for illegally posting flyers, deputy Kuki Shinobu bails them out and spends the day repairing the damage, with the Traveler as her improvised "Chief Advisor". Depending on choices, the day leads to a forced shift at the Grand Narukami Shrine, a reunion with her sister, a manhunt for runaway gang members, or a misunderstood job interview. It is a comic story about Shinobu's patience and her real attachment to the gang. Five endings are possible.

The event needs two Story Keys and first requires the Interlude "Perilous Trail" and the story quest "Rise Up, Golden Soul". The branches are alternatives of one day, not a continuous chronology. The running idea is that Shinobu fixes the gang's mess with law, bookkeeping and discipline, and that the "Gang Bylaws" she invents are how she hopes to make them behave.

Plot: Shinobu's first plan is to scold the three and make them apologise. The Traveler's choices lead along five routes. Defending them sends everyone to the Grand Narukami Shrine, where the gang had posted flyers and met Yae Miko (ending "Unexpected Wages" or "Time For Some Secret Dealings..."). Proposing written rules sends Shinobu after the boys scattering through town (endings "Official Business!" or "Doom Arrives Just the Same"). Standing back lets her discipline them herself; the three then follow her, with the Traveler, to Uyuu Restaurant (ending "The Arataki Gang Community Service Chronicle").

Revelations: - Shinobu, once a trainee at the Grand Narukami Shrine at her family's arrangement, quit because of the strict etiquette and constant monitoring at home. She later studied bookkeeping, worked as an editor and, by her own account, studied law in Liyue. She wears a mask so people do not pry.
- Shinobu has a sister, Miyuki, who works as a shrine maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine (she mentions dealing with matters in Tatarasuna earlier), and who agrees to keep Shinobu's gang membership secret from their family.
- The Arataki Gang has no formal rules until Shinobu writes the Gang Bylaws in this event.
- The Kairagi group at the beach was handing supplies to Fatui skirmishers.

Characters: Shinobu is the lead; the Traveler is her "Chief Advisor". Arataki Itto and gang members Mamoru, Akira and Genta recur. Yae Miko and shrine staff (Inagi Hotomi, Maki) appear in the shrine branches, plus Shinobu's sister Miyuki. Tenryou Commission figures include Kujou Sara, Doushin Uesugi and Doushin Amano; Norika is a merchant. Shopkeepers Shimura Kanbei and Aoi, and a boy, Shouta, are apologised to.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. It adds the Gang Bylaws as a running joke and shows Shinobu choosing the gang over her family's expectations. In the final branch it also shows her doing legal consulting work introduced by Kujou Sara.

Placement: Released in version 2.7. It is set after the Interlude "Perilous Trail". No content from 6.x to 7.1 was found that revises the event.

400.comment: Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu: Gang Bylaws
400.content: Shinobu's improvised rulebook for the Arataki Gang: Article 1 - no damage to others' property; offenders repay the full loss through a gang loan, with their gang assets such as Onikabuto and Genius Invokation cards frozen until it is paid. Article 2 - no bullying small children; offenders apologise sincerely and are banned from gang activities such as Lavender Melon roasting until the victim forgives. Article 3 - when one gang member is in trouble, all come to help (in a later scene, insubordination is punished by reciting the bylaws from memory). Additional notes, such as Clause 36 of Article 2, are quoted in class. Shinobu runs a quiz as a deterrent.

key: Stick It to the Man flyer
401.comment: Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu: Arataki Gang Flyer Incident
401.content: Itto designed flyers himself (his gang members call them avant-garde), including slogans like "Stick It to the Man, Join the Arataki Gang!" and "Arataki Numero Uno Itto: Ousting His Foes Like a Sumo Supremo!". Mamoru, Genta and Akira posted them around Inazuma City, the Grand Narukami Shrine path, Shimura's and Tsukumomono Groceries, and were arrested. The flyers are the cause of every branch of the event.

402.comment: Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu: Shinobu and the Grand Narukami Shrine
402.content: Shinobu was once a trainee at the Grand Narukami Shrine; the placement was arranged by her family. She remembers nagging about etiquette and interrogations after each shift, and left to become anything but a shrine maiden. She finds it hard to refuse Yae Miko, who knows the history, and wears her mask partly to avoid being recognised there.

403.content:
Hangout Event: Layla (also: Ever Silent Stars, Layla Hangout Event, Layla Hangout, Drowsy Evening Star, The Wisdom Seelie, A Change of Pace, blessing from the stars): Layla's Hangout Event, a single-act, branching side story added in Version 3.6. The Traveler meets Layla, a worn-out Rtawahist student at the Akademiya who cannot finish her thesis and is secretly being helped by an unknown "blessing from the stars". Depending on the Traveler's choices they trace a legendary "Wisdom Seelie" through the House of Daena and Layla's old failures, help her prepare for her thesis defence, or take her out for a break. Some routes reveal that the helper is a second self who emerges when Layla faints from exhaustion. There are six endings.

The act is Ever Silent Stars. It requires Adventure Rank 40, two Story Keys and the Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises. It opens with Drowsy Evening Star and then branches into the Wisdom Seelie investigation (The Wisdom Seelie and its follow-ups) or a "change of pace" line (A Change of Pace, with The Helper and Fresh Air).

Plot: At the Akademiya the Traveler meets Layla, who is rushing out of the House of Daena. She is behind on her thesis and has had little sleep for days. She explains that her homework and papers keep getting finished before their deadlines without her remembering, and she has been calling this a "blessing from the stars". She does not want to rely on it, but time is short and she hopes a rumoured Wisdom Seelie, who answers questions left in two astrology books, will help with the thesis. The Traveler can go with her to investigate the Seelie or suggest she rest.

In the Seelie investigation, the Seelie refuses to answer because it says she meant to copy its answer, and leaves a chain of riddles instead. The riddles lead to places from Layla's past failures. The Traveler can follow them to the end, which gives The Price to Pay and Its Returns, take a break to fight monsters, which gives Once Bitten, Twice Shy, or gather information from students, which leads to a night watch and That Which Remains Unspoken. In the "change of pace" line, the Traveler helps Layla borrow equipment, rehearse her thesis defence, or relax outdoors; these routes lead to A Matter of Course, The Stars' Expectations and A Moment of Respite.

Revelations: Layla's "blessing from the stars" is a second personality that takes over when she loses consciousness from anxiety and exhaustion. The Wisdom Seelie legend is a rumour that grew from its activity.

Characters: Layla is the lead, shy, apologetic and exhausted but determined. Her second self is poised and practical. Other characters include Rabah, Katayoun, Hunayn, Latifah, Mundhir, Munirah, Azzam and Katheryne; each appears in one or two branches only.

Consequences: No branch changes Teyvat's main story. The endings settle whether Layla learns of her other self, whether she gains confidence or keeps leaning on it, and whether she rests.

Placement: Released in Version 3.6, between Faruzan's and Kaveh's Hangout Events. It requires the Sumeru Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and is set after Sumeru's main story. Describing Layla generally should not assume any single ending.

404.comment: Hangout Event: Layla: The Wisdom Seelie
404.content: A rumour in the House of Daena of a strong, metal-bodied Seelie that answers questions placed in astrology books. In Layla's Hangout Event the "Seelie" is revealed to be Layla's second persona. Students attribute abilities to it, such as freezing water and calling meteors, that are exaggerated tales of her night-time activity.

405.content: An astrology enthusiast and equipment collector whom Katheryne introduces. He lends his celestial equipment to Layla if she can explain her research to him.

406.content:
Hangout Event: Lynette (also: Lynette Hangout Event, Checks & Cats, Lynette hangout): Lynette's Hangout Event is a one-act, voiced, branching story in Fontaine released in Version 4.5. Its act, "Checks & Cats", is built from five quests (A Decision, Mask, Break, Detectives, Closure) and ends in one of five endings. The Traveler meets Lynette outside Hotel Debord just after the opening of her first-ever acting role, hiding from the reception with a stray cat she has named Bonnie. Whether she goes back to the party, helps the cat, or does neither decides the whole day. Throughout, the event leans on her established traits: she conserves social energy by switching between named "modes", she reads people through tells, and she is quietly devoted to her twin Lyney.

Plot: **A Decision.** Outside Hotel Debord, Lynette tells the Traveler she has just accepted a leading role in a masked mime show, The Lost Puppet, directed by Merieux. She is playing a puppet, so no lines and no facial expressions are needed. The show opened well, but the reception afterwards drained her, so she left to enter "standby mode". She met a collared, hungry cat she named Bonnie, and cannot decide between returning to the party and finding Bonnie's owner. Lyney had Freminet build her a card-box device, the Fateometer, for such moments. Her first draw is botched when the box jams and the cards fall, so she hands the decision to the player. The Traveler can send her back to the reception (Mask), help Bonnie (Detectives), let the Fateometer decide, or suggest doing neither, which can end the event as "Standby Mode".

**Mask.** At the reception, reporters and critics pour praise on The Lost Puppet while Lynette answers in minimal stock phrases. She has a name for her power-saving conversation style, "tea party mode", but the interview burns far more energy than a normal tea party. Furina, also a guest, gives a more measured opinion and mentions that an earlier draft of the script was more complex. Back with her envelope containing the group photo, Lynette finds an anonymous letter telling her that she is a heartless puppet who has ruined the work and must give up the lead. Merieux blames a rival, but the investor Maloney lets slip that the role was first meant for the actress Gillian. Gillian, living in the Fleuve Cendre, confirms it. With the troupe's actor Jaiques, the group reads the original script and the official script side by side and finds that the original ending, a lone dance among ruins for dead companions, is far more demanding and moving than the simplified stage version. Lynette proposes that Gillian take the lead for the second half of the show at the Opera Epiclese.

Revelations: - The anonymous letter in the Mask branch is the work of Ginna, Gillian's younger sister, not a professional intimidator or a rival troupe; Lynette judges her feeling to be indignant but not malicious.
- The detective branch discloses that Lynette was abducted by the head of the Lefevere family at a dinner party and rescued by Arlecchino, and that this is how the twins joined the House of the Hearth.
- The same branch shows Lyney working with Chevreuse as a consultant on a smuggling case without telling Lynette, and using the acting job to keep her away from a case that touches the Lefevere name.
- The Closure path names the mastermind of the smuggling ring as Elodie, a Gardes officer who is an illegitimate Lefevere descendant, planted in the Gardes before the family's fall and kept there afterwards.

Characters: Lynette is the focus: her modes (standby, event, tea party, search, deduction, serious), her reluctance about fame, her talent for reading tells, and her protectiveness toward the weak. The Traveler is her main companion and the player's choices drive the story. Bonnie, a cat, appears throughout the story and is the thread connecting the branches.

Consequences: Each ending ends the day but not the characters' ongoing lives. Nothing in the event changes the main storylines of Fontaine. Depending on the branch, it leaves the Traveler with a closer bond to Lynette, a restored troupe (Gillian in the lead role), or a closed smuggling case.

Placement: Released in Version 4.5, after the Fontaine Archon Quest chapters. It requires completion of 'Masquerade of the Guilty' and the story quest 'The Little Oceanid'. It is a side story and does not advance the main plot.

407.comment: Hangout Event: Lynette: Endings of Hangout Event Lynette
407.content: The act has five endings. "A Roaring Success!" (Mask, with the late choice): a new group photo after the Gillian-led show. "A Seat in the Audience" (Break): Lynette relaxes in the audience. "Adventurers, Investigators, and Cats" (Closure): tea with Bonnie after the arrest. "Save the Kitty!" (Detectives): the Traveler and Lynette leave the case to the Gardes and go to rescue animals. "Standby Mode" (A Decision): the Traveler suggests doing neither task and the day is spent doing nothing.

408.content: A box of twenty numbered cards that Lyney had Freminet make for Lynette, so she can let a random draw decide things. The cutoff number is whatever she decides at the time. In the event she uses it for the question of whether to return to the reception or help Bonnie, but the box jams and the cards fall. The player receives it as a quest reward.

409.comment: Hangout Event: Lynette: The Lost Puppet
409.content: A masked mime show with no spoken lines and no facial expression, written and directed by Merieux and staged at the Opera Epiclese. Its protagonist is a dancing puppet who realises that her failing legs are the aging of her components. In the original script, she ends by dancing alone among ruins for her dead companions until her parts fail. In the commercial version, she is welcomed into a lavish stage and left uncertain about whether anyone will appreciate her. Lynette plays the lead in the first half of the opening run; Gillian takes it for the director's cut.

410.comment: Hangout Event: Lynette: Imitation Sinthe smuggling case
410.content: In the detective branch, a new drug that imitates Sinthe is made in a hidden base, carried in thin sealed bags swallowed by animals, floated in weighted barrels as dead drops and shipped abroad as "overseas adoptions" by the Humane Society. The researcher Pierre Lefevere and the director Bernard are made to appear as the culprits. In the Closure path, the Gardes officer Elodie is revealed as the coordinator who kept them apart and meant to sacrifice both.

411.content: A Gardes officer who introduces herself to Lynette and the Traveler as an investigator of the case. In the Closure path, she claims to be the last of the Lefevere family (Chevreuse names her a Lefevere), who hid her origin and used her post to organise the smuggling ring. She resents the family that made her an infiltrator, and her plan relies on blaming Pierre and Bernard.

412.content:
Hangout Event: Ningguang (also: The Jade Chamber's Returning Guest, Ningguang Hangout Event, Ningguang's Hangout): Ningguang's Hangout Event, a replayable, choice-driven side story set after the Liyue Harbor crisis. Short of staff because her three secretaries are running an auction, Ningguang asks the Traveler to cover as her assistant for a day. The Traveler either schedules a serious working day, or a day off, and the event ends in one of five outcomes: an auction that reclaims her lost treasures, a lunch-and-informants day, a chess-piece commission, a fishing-and-treasure outing, or a trip to Northland Bank.

It was added in Version 2.4 and requires two Story Keys, Adventure Rank 28 and completion of The Crane Returns on the Wind (Liyue's Archon Quest conclusion). It holds eight quests: The Jade Chamber Once More (hub), Time Off!, Endless Smoke, Starting From Zero, Liyue Millennial, Business as Usual, Auction Games and Exchanging Intelligence. It shows the private person behind her polished public image: her humble origins, her grief for the original Jade Chamber, and the care she takes of the children she uses as informants.

Plot: In The Jade Chamber Once More the Traveler arrives at the Jade Chamber to find Ningguang and her secretaries Baishi, Baiwen and Baixiao in need of a stand-in. The secretaries must run an important auction the next day, leaving Ningguang's day-to-day work without cover; she wants someone trusted who has no conflict of interest. Baishi briefs the Traveler: 133 unscheduled items, 17 of them high priority, including meetings with the Eight Trades, tax revisions, Keqing on land-conveyance deals and the guilds. The Traveler then drafts a schedule.

**Rigorous schedule.** Choosing a serious, well-ordered day leads to Business as Usual. The next morning the Traveler wakes Ningguang, has breakfast with her, collects her tailored clothes from Lanyang, and attends a lunch banquet at Liuli Pavilion with a businesswoman, Luo Qiao, who asks for advice on getting into the Luminescent Spine trade. Ningguang advises against it, saying the price far exceeds likely profit and the hype may be engineered. After the banquet the Traveler chooses between telling Ningguang her secretaries will be fine (Exchanging Intelligence) or going to check on them (Auction Games).

**Simple schedule.** Choosing a single day off sends the Traveler to Time Off! Baishi worries but agrees, noting Ningguang rarely rests. Next morning Ningguang can spend the day on something she never has time for (Liyue Millennial) or something she never has the chance to do (Starting From Zero or Endless Smoke).

Revelations: Ningguang's Jade Chamber sacrifice hurt her badly. She grew up in a humble family, worked odd jobs, and associates fish with childhood. She distrusts the Fatui-linked Northland Bank and knows her reparations demand still sours relations. She regards Beidou as a business partner who supplies rare treasures but also costs her investment opportunities.

Characters: Ningguang and the Traveler lead. Her secretaries Baishi (daily schedule and image), Baiwen and Baixiao (experienced tasks) appear in the hub. Others by route: Gou San'er and Bolai (Starting From Zero), Ekaterina and Andrei of Northland Bank (Endless Smoke), Hongru and Luo Qiao (banquet), Lanyang (tailored clothes), Ying'er of Scent of Spring and Xingxi of Mingxing Jewelry (chess figurine), Xiaofei, Yingfeng and Little Bin (auction bidders), the children Zhizhi, Little Long and Nannan, and the merchants Lao Ke and Big Xu.

Consequences: Each ending is a Memory with no effect on later quests. Rewards scale with the number of endings completed (Primogems, Adventure EXP, Hero's Wit, Guide to Prosperity, Prithiva Topaz Fragments and Qiankun Mora Meat).

Placement: Release order: Version 2.4. Story order: after The Crane Returns on the Wind, the finale of the Liyue Archon Quest, since Ningguang refers openly to the Jade Chamber's sacrifice and the battle against Osial, and to Fatui reparations. It precedes any later Liyue material.

413.content: A strategy board game of Ningguang's own design, based on classical chess with different rules, pieces and boards. She has made over thirty editions, wants it to carry Liyue's culture, and plans a commemorative set of the battle for Liyue Harbor with limited-edition figurines.

414.comment: Hangout Event: Ningguang: The Jade Chamber Auction
414.content: In Auction Games Ningguang sells ordinary items from her private collection to hand-picked bidders at inflated prices. She explains that she was not trying to profit: after the Jade Chamber fell, many of her belongings were salvaged and resold, and every bidder holds one. She offers to refund them in exchange for the return of her property.

415.comment: Hangout Event: Ningguang: Luminescent Spine Speculation
415.content: A rumour that a Fontaine merchant will pay a premium for Luminescent Spines inflated their price. Ningguang warns Luo Qiao off, saying the current price is far above what the end product can earn, and later finds Lao Ke and Big Xu ruined by it.

416.content: Three children whom Ningguang treats as helpers and friends. She teaches them to observe, analyse and think critically but never business. When two merchants coach Nannan to lie, Ningguang is angry, gives Nannan the repaired comb (a gift from her mother, who has left Liyue Harbor), and lets Nannan decide the punishment.

417.content: In Endless Smoke Ekaterina greets Ningguang coldly, citing the reparations Ningguang imposed on the Fatui after the Liyue Harbor battle, which Northland Bank paid. After a brief visit the staff order surveillance of Ningguang, which she reads as a sign of guilt. She warns the Traveler that the bank is more than a commercial organisation.

418.content:
Hangout Event: Noelle (also: Noelle Hangout Event, Noelle's Hangout Event, Chivalric Training, Knightly Exam Prep, Maid-in-Training, Studious Maid): Noelle's Hangout Event is a two-act branching side story in which the Traveler spends time with Noelle, the Knights of Favonius' maid who dreams of becoming a knight. Act I (Chivalric Training) follows her small efforts to improve; Act II (Knightly Exam Prep) is about her anxiety over the Knights' selection exam. The Traveler's choices decide which of six endings each act reaches.

It is a Hangout Event, played with Story Keys. Each act is a tree of short quests: the Traveler's dialogue choices change what Noelle does, and some paths end in a failed hangout instead of an ending. The tone is warm and comic, with Noelle's earnestness, over-preparation and difficulty saying no driving most of the jokes. Nothing in it alters the main story.

Plot: Act I: Noelle asks the Traveler for help with her "chivalric training". Act II: with the exam looming, she studies herself ragged until the Traveler steers her toward a trip to Liyue, a mock adventurer's exam, or practising knightly roles.

**Act I - Chivalric Training (summary-level).** Noelle asks the Traveler for guidance in the Knights' library. Paths lead to errands around Mondstadt and the merchant Alois, strength training, or a rest at Good Hunter and Beatrice's date problem, ending in a paper rose or a study of love books.

**Act II - Knightly Exam Prep.** After the Traveler returns from Liyue, Noelle is found cooped up in the library. She works for the Knights as a maid but must still pass the selection exam to become a knight, has failed it several times, and says it is about half a year away. She plans to sleep two hours less a day to study and nearly faints. The Traveler offers three routes: a change of scenery (Journey to Liyue), facing the stress by taking another exam (Adventurer's Entrance Exam), or imagining herself passing (Noelle Rides Out).

Revelations: No main-story revelations. The event shows how Noelle sees herself and her exam.

Noelle has failed the Knights' selection exam several times and becomes anxious and blank when something unexpected happens in an exam. She works for the Knights as a maid and still needs to pass it to be an official Knight. She once got Amber to teach her to make Baron Bunnies, and finds she is not suited to being an Outrider.

Characters: The Traveler and Noelle.

Mondstadt: Katheryne, Cyrus (branch master of the Adventurers' Guild), Charles, Payne, Marjorie, Alfry, Margaret, Raymond, Glory and Beatrice. Liyue: Chef Mao, Dugu Shuo, Sha'yin, Iron Tongue Tian, Qian and Guanhai. Act I: Alois, Henning and Quinn. Jean, Kaeya and Amber are discussed as models but do not appear in the Act II quests read.

Consequences: No lasting canon change; the event is a self-contained character study. The real exam is never taken.

Placement: Act I was released in Version 1.4 and Act II in Version 1.5. Act I requires the Mondstadt Archon Quest (Song of the Dragon and Freedom) and Act II follows the Liyue Archon Quest A New Star Approaches, since Noelle has just welcomed the Traveler back from Liyue. It is a side story with no fixed place in the in-world timeline.

419.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Knights of Favonius selection exam
419.content: In this event Noelle says she has failed the Knights of Favonius selection exam several times. It assesses knowledge, including a thesis on chivalry and Favonius bladework, and combat. She has already worked for the Knights as a maid for some time but must pass it to be an official Knight. The exam is described as about half a year off at the start of Act II and is never actually held.

420.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Adventurer's Entrance Exam
420.content: Cyrus, the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild branch master, was drafting a new entrance exam when Noelle asked for a trial. It has knowledge, survival-cooking and Ruin Guard combat parts; passing two of three succeeds. Noelle never intended to join the Guild, and Cyrus tries to recruit her anyway.

421.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Black-Back Perch Stew
421.content: At Wanmin Restaurant, Chef Mao's signature stew is very spicy. Noelle insists on the local version rather than a milder one, finishes it with difficulty and learns afterwards that the soup is not normally drunk.

422.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: The Maid-Knight's Tale
422.content: A storyteller at Third-Round Knockout turns Noelle's cleaning of a hilichurl camp and a Ruin Guard memento into an exaggerated legend. The audience half-believes it and recognises Noelle, who had wanted it corrected.

423.content: A Liyue boy who suspects Noelle of loitering at Hanfeng's Ironmongers, then asks to see her greatsword and Geo Vision. He hopes to get a Geo Vision himself one day.

424.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Baron Bunny (Noelle's attempt)
424.content: Noelle once got Amber to teach her to make Baron Bunnies. Her copy uses Pyro Slime Condensate and crushed Valberries but fails in the field, one reason she concludes she is not suited to be an Outrider.

425.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Marjorie's lost monocle
425.content: A fragile monocle imported from Sumeru goes missing from Marjorie's shop. Noelle and the Traveler trace a flapping sound to a finch nest on a rooftop and recover it without troubling the Knights.

426.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Waiting tables at the Angel's Share
426.content: Imitating Kaeya's intelligence work, Noelle ends up working a waitress shift for Charles, serving a drunk regular, Payne, and forgetting to gather intelligence. Charles says the customers were happier that night and talks of hiring waiting staff.

427.content:
Hangout Event: Sayu (also: Yoohoo Art: Seichou no Jutsu, Sayu Hangout Event, Sayu's Hangout Event): Hangout Event: Sayu is a branching, player-choice side story added in version 2.2 (Act I, "Yoohoo Art: Seichou no Jutsu"). Sayu, a young ninja of the Shuumatsuban who would rather nap than work, tells the Traveler she has been given a mission to ambush them, though she has no intention of doing it. Together they dodge her shrine-maiden supervisor Kano Nana, try to help Sayu grow taller, and uncover who forged the order. The tone is gentle and funny, with a tender thread about Sayu's absent sensei and her fear of disappointing people. Six endings are possible.

The event needs two Story Keys and first requires the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals". The branches are alternate versions of the same few days, not a single timeline. Throughout, Sayu is portrayed factually as a child-like, sleepy, earnest ninja: she is anxious about her height, hides in disguises, and wants to be useful to someone she trusts.

Plot: At Chinju Forest Sayu explains her grievance: she sleeps constantly to grow taller, yet has not grown, and the shrine maiden keeps assigning chores. The Traveler can tell her sleep alone will not help, advise on quality of sleep, or urge her not to neglect her work. The first two lead to hiding and eating schemes; the third leads to a day of ninjutsu training. In parallel the forged-order mystery resolves in one of two ways, depending on whether the Traveler thanks Kano Nana and drops the matter or keeps investigating.

Revelations: - Sayu is a member of the Shuumatsuban, the ninja corps that handles tasks for the Yashiro Commission, usually assigned errands such as carrying documents and organising tools rather than missions.
- Kano Nana is the Grand Narukami Shrine's shrine maiden and acts as Sayu's supervisor; Ayaka says Sayu's sensei asked her to watch over Sayu's progress, which is partly why she assigned Kano Nana.
- Sayu's sensei taught her ninjutsu and left suddenly; she never learned their name and is unsure what they were.
- The ambush order was forged by Ogawa, a Yashiro Commission courier, under coercion from the Kairagi who held his daughter.

Characters: Sayu is the lead; the Traveler is her helper and eventual confidant. Kano Nana, the shrine maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine, is her supervisor. Kamisato Ayaka appears in the "Shuumatsuban Suspicions" Face-Off scene. Ogawa (Yashiro Commission courier), his daughter Kotomi, the Kairagi leader Inou, Tenryou Commission member Aoki, and Kiminami Anna of Kiminami Restaurant also appear.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. It deepens Sayu's characterisation: she is sleepy and avoidant but also caring, and moved by a child's thanks.

Placement: Released in version 2.2. It is set after the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals" and the Watatsumi war, with the Yashiro Commission and Shuumatsuban in normal operation. No content from 6.x to 7.1 was found that revises the event.

428.content: Sayu's sensei taught her ninjutsu, was patient and strong, and never pushed her to do more work. They measured her height on a tree with a rope marker and told her nothing is more satisfying than growing. They left suddenly for "important matters" and asked Ayaka to watch over Sayu. Sayu never asked their name and only half-remembers whether they described themselves as a ninja. She says the Traveler reminds her of them.

429.comment: Hangout Event: Sayu: The Forged Ambush Order
429.content: Ogawa, a Yashiro Commission official responsible for delivering orders to the Shuumatsuban, was forced by the Kairagi Inou to forge a Commission order for an ambush of the Traveler; his daughter Kotomi was taken. He assigned it to Sayu because she never completes confrontational jobs and Kano Nana oversees her. When the Traveler learns of the order, Kano Nana checks with the Yashiro Commission and confirms it did not come from them. In the helpful branch the Traveler and Sayu stage a fake ambush report, Sayu swaps places with the hostage, and the Tenryou Commission arrests Inou.

430.comment: Hangout Event: Sayu: Kano Nana and Sayu
430.content: Kano Nana is the shrine maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine who also takes work from the Shuumatsuban. Sayu regards her as a "bane" because she always finds Sayu's napping places and turns them into training grounds. Kano Nana is stern but dutiful, protective of the Traveler's safety and cautiously proud of Sayu's real skills.

431.content:
Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou (also: Trap 'Em by Storm, Heizou Hangout Event, Shikanoin Heizou's Hangout Event, Heizou Talks Fraud, Ryuuji Case): Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou is a branching, player-choice side story added in version 2.8 (Act I, "Trap 'Em by Storm"). Ryuuji of the Bantan Sango Detective Agency commissions the Traveler to find the missing Tenryou Commission detective Shikanoin Heizou, who is actually investigating a feeling that something is missing on Watatsumi Island. Depending on choices, the Traveler follows him through a trade-smuggling case, a staged anti-fraud play with Arataki Itto, or the old "Ryuuji Case" murder. Five endings are possible.

The event needs two Story Keys and first requires the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals", the story quest "Transient Dreams" and the story quest "Rise Up, Golden Soul". The branches are alternate paths, not one timeline. Heizou is shown as talkative and theatrical in public and more thoughtful and uncertain in private, with an intuition he trusts more than evidence.

Plot: If the Traveler agrees to investigate, the trade-smuggling case ("The Missing Thing") ends in "Memories Do Not Evaporate". Otherwise, Heizou goes back to the Police Station ("Report back"), where Kujou Sara makes the Traveler his temporary supervisor. There the Traveler picks a case file: the anti-fraud play "Heizou Talks Fraud" (endings "Free Onikabuto Lunch" and "The Three Undeceivables"), or one of the other two files, which sends the story to Sango's complaint letter and the "Long-Sealed Mystery" about the Ryuuji Case (endings "There's One Secret" and "The Famous Detective's Principles").

Revelations: - Heizou is a special detective of the Tenryou Commission (rank: Doushin) and cousin of the shrine maiden Kano Nana. Sango dislikes him; Ryuuji admires him.
- Watatsumi Island runs caravans to bring in food and medicinal herbs that its poor soil cannot grow; some of the goods are untaxed, so Gorou hid the truth from Heizou until the Traveler's presence made him reconsider. The Kanjou Commission is drafting a commodity tax bill that exempts needed goods.
- In the Ryuuji Case, Takatsukasa Isamu used Shiroyama's family as leverage; Shiroyama killed Isamu with a two-part poison that Ryuuji unwittingly helped deliver. Heizou's private conclusion is that Kujou Takayuki ordered it and planned to blame Ryuuji.

Characters: Heizou is the lead; the Traveler and Paimon are his partner and supervisor. Ryuuji and Sango (Bantan Sango Detective Agency) open and close the main branches. Gorou, Todoroki, Tokuda, Masashi and Shibata appear on Watatsumi Island. Kujou Sara, Uesugi and Owada appear at the Police Station. Kano Nana, Etsu, Iba and Arataki Itto appear in the anti-fraud branch; Takatsukasa Chika, Isamu's daughter, in the Long-Sealed Mystery ending.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. It shows Heizou's dual nature and adds background to the Kujou Clan, the Police Station and Watatsumi Island's trade difficulties. Whether the Ryuuji Case truth is revealed is a branch choice.

Placement: Released in version 2.8. It is set after the Watatsumi war and "Omnipresence Over Mortals", with the Sakoku Decree already ended. No content from 6.x to 7.1 was found that revises the event.

432.comment: Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou: Ryuuji Case
432.content: Years before the story, the head of the Police Station, Takatsukasa Isamu, died of poison. Ryuuji, his assistant, who regarded him as a foster father, was convicted within a week on a conviction signed by Kujou Sara and jailed. Sango's investigation then identified the forensic doctor Shiroyama, who died by suicide before he could be tried. Heizou's private reading: a harmless-looking cold medicine and an expensive fish-liver paste combined into a lethal poison; Shiroyama had once worked for the Kujou Clan, and Kujou Takayuki directed it. Ryuuji, who delivered the paste, does not know this. Sango believes Heizou is hiding something. Whether the truth is revealed depends on the player's choice.

433.comment: Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou: Watatsumi Island Trade Case
433.content: Watatsumi Island cannot grow enough food or medicinal herbs. To ease this Kokomi set up caravans under the farmer Todoroki, but Ritou's taxes are heavy. Nobushi and Treasure Hoarders prey on the caravans, and Todoroki also appears to buy scarce goods, including medicinal herbs, outside legal channels; a torn bill bears the name Foreign Trade Association, which Heizou does not recognise. Gorou concealed the arrangement from Heizou until the Traveler's presence and Heizou's offer to stay as a safeguard. A new commodity tax bill from the Kanjou Commission would exempt needed goods.

434.comment: Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou: Heizou Talks Fraud
434.content: Heizou's public-awareness play about scams. Etsu and Iba, both former fraud convicts, play the scammers; Arataki Itto plays a Doushin who must resist offers that are too good to be true. In the end Heizou's lesson is "Don't get greedy and you won't be needy; stay alert and you won't get hurt." The Tenryou Commission approved the project.

435.content:
Hangout Event: Thoma (also: A Housekeeper's Daily Chores, Thoma Hangout Event, Thoma Hangout): Hangout Event: Thoma is the branching Hangout Event for Thoma, the Kamisato Clan's housekeeper, added in version 2.2 and unlocked after Omnipresence Over Mortals. Thoma wants to thank the Traveler for helping during the Vision Hunt Decree by spending a day off with them. Depending on the Traveler's choices, the day ends in one of six endings: a housekeeping class, a knitting lesson, a vigil with a grieving ninja dog, sweaters for stray animals, a trip to Ritou, or a quiet scheme to rescue the Yashiro Commission from a price-gouging merchant.

It is a single act, "A Housekeeper's Daily Chores", made of ten quests in a decision tree. Requirements are Adventure Rank 30, two Story Keys and completion of Omnipresence Over Mortals. The event shows Thoma at ease: a cook, seamstress and animal lover, but also a capable fixer who settles the Yashiro Commission's problems through contacts and does not care much about reputation. As a Hangout Event it is optional, and only one route is played per run.

Plot: After overhearing the samurai Kazumasa and Furusawa grumble about him, Thoma shrugs it off. The Traveler's choices then pick one of six routes. Over tea at Komore Teahouse the Traveler suggests a housekeeping class (a full class, or a quiet knitting lesson). Among the strays in Hanamizaka, Thoma and the Traveler either keep a grieving Shuumatsuban ninken company or knit sweaters for the animals. In Ritou the two tour the town and swap gifts, Thoma giving a Lucky Omamori. If the Traveler objects to the gossip, Thoma instead quietly brings a price-gouging merchant to heel for the Yashiro Commission.

Revelations: - Thoma grew up in Mondstadt. His father returned to Inazuma and stopped writing, so Thoma sailed to find him with Dandelion Wine as a gift. A storm sank the boat and he drifted to Inazuma on wreckage (Ritou route).
- Thoma's mother gave him the omamori his father had given her, just before he left Mondstadt (Ritou route).
- He feeds strays because simple bonds are what he values most. He describes himself to powerful people as an expendable servant boy who must always consider what they want.

Characters: Thoma (host) and the Traveler (guest). Also: the Yashiro Commission samurai Kazumasa and Furusawa, the shopkeeper Ogura Mio, the housewives Yuuko and Yuuri, the elder Nagano, the Kamisato servants Hirano, Furuta and Koharu, Kiyoe, Yuusaku, Yasutake, Sakai, Kazuaki of the Shuumatsuban and the ninken Inu Shoushou, Qiuyue, Kaede and Keiichi in Ritou, and Kurisu, mentioned in passing. Kamisato Ayato and Kamisato Ayaka are referred to but do not appear.

Consequences: No lasting change to the main story. Depending on the route, Thoma holds a first housekeeping class, adds the Traveler to those who remember an unnamed Shuumatsuban ninja, clothes strays for winter, gives the Traveler a Lucky Omamori, or settles a festival supply dispute at Yuusaku's expense.

Placement: Released in version 2.2 with the Hangout Event feature. It takes place after Omnipresence Over Mortals and refers back to the Vision Hunt Decree. Some Ritou dialogue differs if the Traveler has completed Transient Dreams. Nothing after version 7.1 is used.

436.comment: Hangout Event: Thoma: Thoma's housekeeping class
436.content: In two routes of Thoma's Hangout Event, he and the Traveler organise a housekeeping class at the Yashiro Commission headquarters, open to any gender or age. In the widely advertised route (Popular Class) a full room attends, including Kazumasa and Furusawa, brought by Yuuko. In the quiet route (Alone Time) few attend and Thoma teaches the Traveler to knit instead. These are route-specific outcomes.

437.content: Inu Shoushou is a red Shiba ninken with a scar by one eye, in black stealth gear, who belonged to a Shuumatsuban ninja who left on a dangerous sea mission and did not return. It waits on a beach north of Konda Village and refuses food. Kazuaki gives Thoma the owner's blunt training kunai, and the dog becomes more affectionate when Thoma and the Traveler keep it company.

438.comment: Hangout Event: Thoma: Thoma and the stray animals
438.content: Thoma feeds stray cats and dogs under a sakura tree in Hanamizaka whenever he visits Komore Teahouse. He says it began when a stray shared shelter with him on a rainy day after an elder turned him away. In the New Clothes! route he knits sweaters for them, naming Petal, Darko and Goldilocks.

439.comment: Hangout Event: Thoma: Thoma's trip to Ritou
439.content: On the Ritou route Thoma tours the town with the Traveler. He tells how he arrived from Mondstadt looking for his father, recalls the town's freer days, and praises the quiet lookout he visits every time. He buys a necklace and bracelet at the Chuyu Trading Company, accepts sweets from a grateful merchant, and is deeply touched by a Windwheel Aster from the Traveler, giving them a Lucky Omamori in return.

440.comment: Hangout Event: Thoma: Yuusaku and the ceremonial implements
440.content: Yuusaku is a merchant on Narukami Island who once sold the Yashiro Commission defective ceremonial goods, was exposed by Thoma, and was held by the Tenryou Commission. He bears a grudge and raised his prices when the Commission's festival shipment sank. In the Unforeseen Circumstances route Thoma privately cuts off Yuusaku's trade and loan terms until he apologises and offers to sell at half price.

441.content:
Hangout Event: Yun Jin (also: A Song That Knows Grace, Yun Jin Hangout Event, Yun Jin's Hangout): Yun Jin's Hangout Event, a replayable, choice-driven side story. Days before a major performance, the star of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe vanishes to a dangerous spot in search of inspiration, and the Traveler brings her back. The one-act event, A Song That Knows Grace, then branches: a thank-you night that ends in a tangle with fake reporters or in a relaxed meal and a photograph, or a crash course in acting from Yun Jin herself. There are five endings.

It was added in Version 2.4 and requires two Story Keys, Adventure Rank 28 and completion of The Crane Returns on the Wind. Its quests are Countryside Wandering (hub), After the Curtain Falls, Backstage Suspicions, Half a Day's Leisure and First Glimpse of Meaning. The title is a partial quotation of a Chinese saying about hearing a stringed song and understanding the deeper meaning, associated with the friendship of Bo Ya and Zhong Ziqi, according to the wiki's trivia.

Plot: In Countryside Wandering the Adventurers' Guild's Katheryne introduces Yunning, manager of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe, who is frantic: Yun Jin has left a note saying she has gone to Lingju Pass to find inspiration for the "Divine Maiden" play. The Traveler finds her there, defeats a Ruin Hunter threatening her, and learns why she went. Yun Jin was inspired by Shenhe's remarks about the divine damsel, whose real behaviour was less heroic than the opera shows, and wanted to feel genuine danger to deepen her portrayal. She admits she was close to a breakthrough and does not promise to stop, but returns. At the Guild, Yunning begs the Traveler to talk her out of dangerous practice. The Traveler's answer forks the event.

**Agree with Yunning (safety first).** Yun Jin promises to rehearse in safety and invites the Traveler to meet at the Heyu Tea House after her show. This leads to After the Curtain Falls.

**Side with Yun Jin.** She is delighted. Yunning, panicking, asks the Traveler to keep her busy until the next show, and when the Traveler is cast as a would-be student, Yun Jin agrees to give informal lessons, meeting at the bridge at Feiyun Slope. This leads to First Glimpse of Meaning.

Revelations: Yun Jin pursues realism: she joins in dangerous experience to understand a character, writes to performers from many nations, and calls acting her bread and butter. She cherishes the audience members who truly appreciate nuance. The tabloids once ran a story casting her as a diva after she left an interview, so Yunning now handles all interview requests. The troupe's rules forbid taking private gifts from patrons.

Characters: Yun Jin and the Traveler lead. Yunning is the troupe's manager and a worrier. Katheryne appears at the Guild. Others by route: Maksim and Gentry Maocai (admirers), Boyi and Shiyun (self-declared Steambird staff), Chen the Sharp and Dongsheng (food stalls) and Shenhe (mentioned only).

Consequences: No ending alters the main story. Rewards scale with the number of endings unlocked (Primogems, Adventure EXP, Hero's Wit, Guide to Diligence, Prithiva Topaz Fragments and Cloud-Shrouded Jade). Within the event, Boyi's business is set to be investigated by the Millelith, and Shiyun is offered a chance to write for the real Steambird.

Placement: Release order: Version 2.4. Story order: after The Crane Returns on the Wind, since Yun Jin and others refer to the Traveler having defeated an ancient god and the Fatui at Liyue Harbor, and to the Jade Chamber battle.

442.content: The manager of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe. She is very protective of Yun Jin, anxious about risks to her health and the troupe's schedule, and insists all interview requests go through her.

443.comment: Hangout Event: Yun Jin: Boyi and Shiyun
443.content: Boyi poses as the editor-in-chief of The Steambird and Shiyun as his journalist. Shiyun is a new employee bound by an extortionate contract, who is sympathetic to Yun Jin. Boyi plans a sensational story from a false interview. Yun Jin and the Traveler trick him into leading them to evidence, and Yunning reports him to the Millelith.

444.comment: Hangout Event: Yun Jin: Chen the Sharp's Stall
444.content: A barbecue stall at Chihu Rock famous for Grilled Tiger Fish and frequented by Yun Jin. In the event Chen is experimenting with a milk tea he heard about from a Mondstadt merchant, and Yun Jin turns the leftover drinks into a guessing game.

445.comment: Hangout Event: Yun Jin: Yun Jin's Acting Methods
445.content: In First Glimpse of Meaning Yun Jin teaches three approaches: relive the real emotion, substitute familiar experiences for unfamiliar ones, or choreograph and rehearse every detail. She says all three are valuable and that she will use any method that improves her performance.

key: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...
Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters
Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief...
Make Bright the Arrows, Gather the Shields...
For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...
446.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...
446.content:
Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... (also: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters, Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief..., Make Bright the Arrows, Gather the Shields..., For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...): Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... is a three-quest world quest series in the Sumeru desert from version 3.4, set among the Tanit tribe. The Traveler, Paimon and their friend Jeht become the target of the Tanit matriarch Babel, who wants control of the Eternal Oasis and of the Traveler's jinni. Babel sends assassins, tells each side the other has joined the Fatui, and is finally confronted and killed by Jeht, who leaves the tribe behind.

The series follows Apocalypse Lost and Rejoice With Me, for What Was Lost Is Now Found. Its titles come from biblical passages on the fall of Babylon (Babel in the Hebrew Bible), and Babel the matriarch is its antagonist. It is a story about a manipulative adoptive mother, a daughter who chooses a friend over her tribe, and what Jeht does with the name of her real mother.

Plot: Yuften, a Tanit farmer, asks the Traveler to find a lost caravan carrying a supply called Anahitian Blessing. The trail of broken boxes leads to a hilichurl camp and an abandoned rug, which look staged, and Eremite assassins then ambush the Traveler and Paimon, claiming Jeht sent them to keep them in the desert. The Traveler reports to Babel, who promises protection and says Jeht is away on tribal duties.

The next day Babel says Jeht may have betrayed the tribe to the northerners (the Fatui) and asks the Traveler to find her and bring her back. At a Fatui outpost the Traveler finds documents and a frightened soldier, Orest, who says Jeht was captured, escaped her cage and killed a Fatui. Letters reveal a plan to move her to a canyon hideout. There the Traveler finds the wounded Jeht, who first attacks them, believing she has been betrayed. After she is calmed down, assassins from the Tanit arrive, sent by Babel. Jeht and the Traveler compare stories: Babel told Jeht the Traveler had joined the Fatui and told the Traveler the same about Jeht. They confront Babel at the Tanit Camps. Babel admits she wants the Eternal Oasis and the Traveler's jinni for the Tanit and to rebuild a desert nation. Jeht refuses to harm the Traveler and tells the tribe she is Ufairah Hindi's daughter. Babel sets the tribe on them, and Jeht defeats and kills Babel. Jeht, now homeless, leaves the camps with Benben.

Revelations: - Babel tells the Traveler and Jeht the other has joined the Fatui, in order to set them against one another. She wants to keep the Eternal Oasis and to be Prophetess of Nabu Malikata.
- Fatui documents say the Tanit agreed to hand a young woman over to the Fatui desert expedition for experiments, and to lure her into a pre-arranged ambush.
- Jeht says she has killed or removed several elders at Babel's command, and that her mother is Ufairah Hindi.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Jeht, Babel, Benben (a companion of Jeht who appears at the end), Yuften (a Tanit farmer), the Tanit Falcons Nayram and Rezki, Mendas (seen beside Babel), Eremite assassins including Bouhanu, and Fatui soldiers Orest, Ilyusha, Yevgraf, Lieutenant Ruslan Snezhevich and Captain Zoya Snezhevna. Mentioned: Professor Froderock, Lieutenant Muldoon, Ufairah Hindi, Jebrael, Aderfi, Azariq, Masseira.

Consequences: Babel is dead, the Tanit Camps are left deserted, and Jeht, now outside the tribe and expected to be called a traitor along the trade routes, takes her mother's name and goes her own way with Benben.

Placement: Requires Apocalypse Lost and Rejoice With Me, for What Was Lost Is Now Found. The wiki lists Apocalypse Lost directly before this series. Released in 3.4. The three quests follow each other, the second starting automatically after the first, and the third after the second.

keysecondary: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters
447.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...: Babel, matriarch of the Tanit
447.content: Babel is the matriarch of the Tanit, a desert tribe, and the adoptive mother of Jeht. She is courteous and tender in public, calls the Traveler "esteemed Master of the Jinni", and tells each side that the other has betrayed them. Her aim is control of the Eternal Oasis and of the goddess Nabu Malikata's legacy, with Jeht as her heir. She dies at Jeht's hand.

448.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...: Jeht and Ufairah Hindi
448.content: Jeht is a Tanit whom Babel raised as her own daughter. In this series she refuses to kill the Traveler, says she is the daughter of Ufairah Hindi and Jebrael (an outsider mother and a father Babel calls a traitor), and chooses her mother's name over the tribe's. She leaves with Benben, saying that she is now the head of her own house.

449.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...: Eternal Oasis in this series
449.content: Babel treats the Eternal Oasis as the central pillar of Tanit faith: whoever holds it claims the sovereignty of Nabu Malikata, the Queen of All Oases. Jeht says the goddess is long gone and cannot be revived. Babel says that she is absent only in appearance and will return. The Tanit say they are its defenders.

450.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...: Fatui desert expedition in Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters
450.content: A Fatui desert expedition led by Captain Zoya Snezhevna and Lieutenant Ruslan Snezhevich received a young Tanit woman, Jeht, from the tribe for experiments, after a plan to ambush her. The transfer was code-named Red Ball Express. She escaped her captors, and the expedition's mission failed. Professor Froderock Fronkonsteen is the scientist the documents address.

key: Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard
An Ark That Used to Be a Soul
451.comment: Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard
451.content:
Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard (also: An Ark That Used to Be a Soul, Court of Eternal Bliss quest): Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard is a World Quest series in Snezhnaya, added in version 7.0, that contains a single quest, An Ark That Used to Be a Soul. It ends the hunt for the three missing fragments of the Eye of Graeae, the talking device the Traveler and Paimon call "Goggles". Once all three are recovered, the Traveler opens the door to the Court of Eternal Bliss at the Ruined Hvergelmir and learns what Goggles was built for.

It begins at the Ruined Hvergelmir in the White Birch Snowgrave area (Pale Crown Palace subarea) and requires the Archon Quest chapter "Gunfire in the Silent Lands" plus the three sibling series: Hesperides of Love and Hate, In the Dwelling of Life and On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb. Each of those yields one Pebble, which together are the three power fragments. The finale is a two-phase boss fight against Aksinya and then the Primordial Human.

Plot: Having collected the three fragments, the Traveler and Paimon go to the door of the Court of Eternal Bliss at the Ruined Hvergelmir. Goggles explains that his maker, Aksinya, once of Hvergelmir (the research body of the Belyi Tsar), built him to guide a great power toward a "Tomorrow": a world without suffering, envy, or the line between humans and gods. He fears what recovering his last power may do to his purpose. The Traveler and Paimon tell him he can choose once he remembers everything. They open the gate by feeding Kresnik Energy to the Tsar's White Birch.

Inside, Goggles vanishes and Aksinya appears. She says he has gone where he belongs. He was never meant to take back an old body: he is the "Proto-Man", the Key that completes the Belyi Tsar into the true Primordial Human. The vessel is the still-living husk of the long-dead Tsar, a body Hyperborea tried to forge from the flesh of the Cryo Dragon Sovereign Nibelung. That experiment once dragged Hyperborea into the Shadow Realm and froze Snezhnaya, but the Tsar later awoke and accepted the role of the failed project's successor.

Aksinya states her goal: to spread the Shadow Realm over the world so that love and joy never fade and every moment feels as fulfilling as the first, ending desire, envy and change. The Traveler observes this means a world without change, and she agrees, since in her view time wears love away. When the Traveler and Paimon reject it, she says there will still be a place for them, and teleports away into the Shadow Realm, so the Traveler chases her while her ritual proceeds.

Revelations: - Goggles (the Eye of Graeae's consciousness) is the "Proto-Man", a Key created by Aksinya at Hvergelmir to complete the Belyi Tsar into the Primordial Human.
- Hyperborea tried to forge the Tsar's body from the Cryo Dragon Sovereign Nibelung; the Tsar's husk was still living when the Traveler arrived.
- Aksinya intends to spread the Shadow Realm across the world as a changeless realm of lasting love.
- The Primordial Human says he engineered his own fragmentation and the betrayal of Aksinya by Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis.

Characters: - The Traveler and Paimon, who refuse a changeless world.
- The Eye of Graeae ("Goggles"), who becomes the Primordial Human and then leaves only a mechanical shell behind.
- Aksinya, Hvergelmir's former researcher and the Tsar's Court Jester, presented here as the series' antagonist, though sympathetic and ultimately self-doubting.
- The Primordial Human, the awakened Belyi Tsar's body with Goggles' mind in it.

Consequences: The Traveler no longer has Goggles as a companion, only the empty Eye of Graeae. Aksinya's plan and the fight with the Primordial Human end there. After collecting all three fragments, Co-Op Mode (including the Serenitea Pot and Miliastra Wonderland access) is disabled until the quest is finished, as the wiki notes. Completing the quest awards the achievement "A Thousand Affections Caught in a Sigh" and the character avatar card of Aksinya.

Placement: Story order: it is the capstone of the Snezhnaya Eye of Graeae arc and comes after the three sibling series, which can be done in any order. It also requires the Archon Quest "Gunfire in the Silent Lands". Release order: added in version 7.0 with the other Snezhnaya World Quest series.

452.comment: Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard: Proto-Man and the Primordial Human
452.content: In Aksinya's account the "Proto-Man" is a Key, created at Hvergelmir to complete the Belyi Tsar into the Primordial Human. Goggles is revealed to be this Key. In the finale the Primordial Human appears as the giant mechanical Velikan of Light, Svarod, speaks with Goggles' restored memory, and asks the Traveler to stop both himself and Aksinya.

453.comment: Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard: Aksinya's Tomorrow
453.content: Aksinya's plan is to cover the world in the Shadow Realm so that love and joy never fade.
