In her view time erodes love, so this realm would hold every feeling at its first fullness, which also means ending desire, envy and change. The Traveler rejects this as a world without change. By the end she doubts her own reasoning.

454.content:
Hereafter (also: Hereafter: The Trail of Pervases, Hereafter: All is Well, Hereafter: Return to the Mountains, Pervases temple restoration quest): A small Version 2.4 Liyue series. The Traveler buys grilled tiger fish to honour the Yaksha Pervases, meets Xiao and the reformed Wang Ping'an, and helps rebuild Pervases's neglected temple over three days.

It requires the quest Butterfly's Dream, and each of its three quests (The Trail of Pervases, All is Well, Return to the Mountains) becomes available only after the daily reset. The series is a gentle follow-up to earlier encounters with Wang Ping'an, once called "Starsnatcher".

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon buy fish at Wanmin Restaurant, intending a third portion as an offering to Pervases. Near the temple they meet Xiao and rescue Wang Ping'an from attackers. Wang Ping'an plans to restore the temple. Over later visits the temple is repaired, with Millelith guarding the site, and he stays to write a book about the Vigilant Yaksha.

Paimon wonders why nobody maintains the temple of Yakshas who defended Liyue Harbor; Xiao goes quiet and then says they did not do their duty for recognition. After helping Wang Ping'an, the Traveler is told to return once work has begun. On the second visit workers are building and the Ministry of Civil Affairs has posted Millelith. Wang Ping'an fears deliveries may be attacked, so the Traveler defeats nearby Treasure Hoarders, who say they did not know the temple belonged to an adeptus and promise to leave it alone. Wang Ping'an then asks for Sandbearer Wood. On the final visit the temple is complete and the Traveler lights incense at the censer.

Revelations: No major revelation. The series shows Wang Ping'an's change of heart and gives a glimpse of Xiao's attitude to remembrance.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Xiao and Wang Ping'an, plus Millelith and Treasure Hoarders as background.

Xiao appears only at the start and is reserved: he says the Yakshas did not act for recognition. Wang Ping'an is a former thief shown rebuilding the shrine and writing about the Vigilant Yaksha.

Consequences: Pervases's temple is repaired and guarded, and Wang Ping'an stays as its keeper. The Traveler can offer incense there whenever they want.

Placement: Released in Version 2.4. It requires Butterfly's Dream and runs as a daily-gated trio of quests. The wiki notes a separate Fontaine quest called Hereafter..., unrelated to this one.

455.content:
Hesperides of Love and Hate (also: Through the Gates of Ivory, Procrustes' Iron Bed, Bell Ringing at Dusk, House of the Soulless, The Sun's Gilded Apple, Fellfrost Peak series): Hesperides of Love and Hate is a three-part Snezhnaya World Quest series added in version 7.0, set at the House of Hesperides on Fellfrost Peak. The Traveler and Paimon are invited to what is billed as a Snegovik wedding for Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess. It turns out to be a ritual meant to take a fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power from Ikhor, the "groom", and the house keeps looping each time a bell rings eight times.

The parts are "Through the Gates of Ivory", "Procrustes' Iron Bed" (with two sub-quests, "House of the Soulless" and "The Sun's Gilded Apple") and "Bell Ringing at Dusk". It runs concurrently with In the Dwelling of Life and On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb, and one of its rewards is the Pebble of Freezing Heart, which unlocks An Ark That Used to Be a Soul.

Plot: Through the Gates of Ivory. In a snowstorm the party climbs Fellfrost Peak and finds a lamp that eases the cold. A young man, Ikhor, tells them a woman he did not know told him to leave a house and he simply obeyed, because for him a strong wish must be granted. He lives at the House of Hesperides, home of Lady Pavlina, princess of the Snegovik and other fae, and says she is preparing a wedding, an important "ritual". The Eye of Graeae senses a piece of its body in him. He gives them a wedding invitation, since only guests may enter, and guides them through monsters to the door.

Inside, the host Aglaya welcomes them as guests, explains Larisa's earlier wedding and warns them away from forbidden rooms. After entertainments and a nap the party hears the bell strike eight and goes to the chapel with the Snegovik guests. Pavlina speaks of a people who were soulless and chased love because they longed for a soul, and calls Larisa's death the last page of a tragic chapter. She calls for Ikhor, who wears an icy collar, and he agrees to give "what we've been wishing for". As Pavlina raises her sword, Aksinya appears, objects, and turns Ikhor into a doll-like puppet. A portal to the Shadow Realm takes Aksinya and Pavlina away. The Traveler dreams of an endless wedding rehearsed again and again, wakes in a room, and learns from Paimon and the Eye that the ritual repeats because Pavlina can only draw the power bit by bit. Aksinya sends a message through the Eye saying she has trapped Pavlina for now, to take Ikhor's fragments away before the bell strikes eight, and that she will send a map.

Revelations: - The "Snegovik wedding" is a ritual to take the soul or power of the loved one; Snegovik, created without flesh and blood, have incomplete souls.
- Ikhor is a fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power in a Prime Ice body. He and the Eye each call the other "me".
- Pavlina is one of the people who betrayed Aksinya (the Eye says this if the Traveler has seen the Pale Crown Palace series).
- Pavlina's aim is to give her people souls; Aksinya opposes her because she wants the power for the Eye.

Characters: - Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess and host.
- Ikhor, the gentle, wish-granting "groom".
- Aglaya, the polite hostess who tells the story of Larisa.
- Aksinya, the Eye's creator, fighting Pavlina from the Shadow Realm.
- The Eye of Graeae and Paimon, who guide the Traveler.

Consequences: Pavlina's ritual is stopped before it can offer up Ikhor's power, and the Traveler receives the Pebble of Freezing Heart. Ikhor is gone and Pavlina has vanished into mist. This is one of the three fragments needed in Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard. Aksinya, if the Traveler has not yet met her, introduces herself as the Eye's maker and says that she shares its goal.

Placement: Story order: after the Snezhnaya Archon Quest chapter, one of three parallel series (with In the Dwelling of Life and On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb) that all lead to Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard. Conditional dialogue changes depending on what the Traveler has already seen. Release order: version 7.0.

456.comment: Hesperides of Love and Hate: Pavlina's ritual
456.content: At the House of Hesperides, Pavlina holds a "wedding" at which Ikhor is to offer his soul so that the Snegovik can gain souls. The bell strikes eight times, the house resets, and each cycle lets Pavlina take a little more of the power in the Eye of Graeae's fragments.

457.comment: Hesperides of Love and Hate: Ikhor
457.content: Ikhor is a calm young man whose manner Paimon finds childlike, with a Prime Ice body who grants any wish he is asked for. He says he does not feel cold and calls the Eye of Graeae "me". Pavlina uses him as the sacrificial "groom" and, in Procrustes' Iron Bed, pierces him with her sword and absorbs him as golden energy.

458.comment: Hesperides of Love and Hate: Larisa
458.content: Larisa was a Snegurochka, described by Aglaya as the most beautiful of them. According to Aglaya her human husband betrayed her, she killed him, and the broken vow then took her own life. Her fury raised a blizzard that froze lightning in mid-fall. Pavlina called her a friend, and Ladon says plants thrived under her care in the garden.

459.content:
Historia Antiqua Chapter (also: Sal Flore, No Mere Stone, Zhongli's Story Quest): Historia Antiqua Chapter is Zhongli's Story Quest, in two acts. In Sal Flore he and the Traveler accompany two self-described archaeologists to the ruins of the god Havria and learn why the God of Salt really fell. In No Mere Stone, a missing-miners commission leads them to the sealed Azhdaha and his benevolent consciousness.

Both acts treat Zhongli as the former Rex Lapis living as a consultant. The chapter is about memory: how history is written, who preserves it, and what Morax feels when old friends and old gods resurface.

Plot: Act I: The Traveler meets Zhongli at the Pearl Galley with a Fatui archaeologist, Kliment, and a second, Wanyan. They search Guyun Stone Forest and Sal Terrae, open a sealed ruin, and Zhongli exposes both as treasure seekers. Wanyan is a follower of Havria who wanted proof that Morax killed her. Zhongli shows that Havria's own followers betrayed and killed her, then asks the Traveler to be a record of history. Act II: Zhongli helps investigate missing miners at The Chasm, finding that a small girl lured them for a corrupted Azhdaha, and that the expert Kun Jun is Azhdaha's benevolent consciousness.

Act I ends with Zhongli deciding to keep the truth in the Traveler, who has seen many worlds. He throws Havria's relics into the sea. Act II ends with Azhdaha re-sealed, the miners saved, and the benevolent half learning that Morax has stepped down as the Geo Archon. Zhongli also refuses to say what he knows of Khaenri'ah's fall.

Revelations: - Havria, the God of Salt, was betrayed and killed by her own followers, not by Morax; the survivors fled to Liyue and Morax protected them.
- Zhongli is the former Rex Lapis, and treats the Traveler as a keeper of memory.
- The little girl and Kun Jun are two halves of Azhdaha: a corrupted body and a benevolent consciousness.

Characters: Zhongli, the Traveler and Paimon; Act I adds Kliment and Wanyan (Havria appears only in the story told); Act II adds Uncle Dai, Kun Jun, Katheryne and Azhdaha.

Act II also includes Wanyu, Ling and the miners. Zhongli is shown as courteous and dry, a former archon who prefers contracts and records to force.

Consequences: Havria's relics are cast into the sea; Wanyan loses her proof and Kliment his chalice. Azhdaha is re-sealed with the miners saved, and the benevolent consciousness departs. The Traveler is treated by Zhongli as an ally for preserving Liyue's history.

Placement: Act I (Sal Flore) was released in Version 1.1, requires A New Star Approaches and Adventure Rank 40. Act II (No Mere Stone) requires Sal Flore and We Will Be Reunited, per the wiki. Zhongli is the former Geo Archon, so the Archon Quest's revelation precedes these acts.

460.content: In Sal Flore, Zhongli shows that Havria was benevolent and was killed by her own followers with a sword, after which many of them were turned to salt. Survivors fled to Liyue and Morax's care, later returning to break the sword. Wanyan, a follower, believed Morax was responsible; Zhongli corrects this.

461.content: Kun Jun is the stone-reading expert hired by Uncle Dai, who is later revealed to be Azhdaha's benevolent consciousness. He can see the memories of stones. His search for Dragonfall is a pretext for finding Zhongli and eventually helping to re-seal his own corrupted half.

key: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind
Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom
462.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind
462.content:
Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind (also: Homebound Anecdotes, For a Reunion Without Tears, Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom, Alice's memory bubble event, Luna V Mondstadt event): Part I sends the Traveler and Paimon to Stormbearer Coast, where they walk through a Klee-themed version of the story's opening and meet Venti, Dvalin, Alice and Nicole. Part II has volunteers replay the Holy Lyre theft and chase, with Fatui roles played by Guild members and friends. Part III shows the bubble polluted by a nascent Abyssal power that makes Dvalin a corrupted threat, which Venti, Diluc, Jean, Varka and the Traveler must defeat before a bubble-world crisis becomes real. Afterwards Jean and the Knights realise home is wherever they are together.

Plot: Part I, Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Paimon and the Traveler read Jean's letter (the Wild Hunt threat in Nod-Krai is neutralised and the expedition is returning) and go to the beach across from Starsnatch Cliff, the spot where their journey began. They explore a Special Story Mode full of oddities (Jumpy Dumpty mines on a tree, a Klee version of the Statue of the Seven) and meet Venti and Dvalin, then Alice and Nicole. Alice and Nicole explain that the "bubble" is a world built from Venti's memories at the Knights' request, so returning knights can catch up on events they missed. The Traveler is asked to test it. Jean explains her plans for the reception and Varka turns up unexpectedly.

Part II, For a Reunion Without Tears: With Varka, Jean, Diluc, Venti and others, the Traveler enters the bubble for the Holy Lyre der Himmel sequence. Guild members and Knights play the Fatui, Fischl plays an Electro Cicin Mage who steals the lyre, and Amber, as gliding champion of the Fatui, runs it across Mondstadt. After the performance a banquet at the Cathedral follows, where Jean and Barbara discuss home, and Varka, Venti and the Traveler talk on top of the Anemo Archon Statue.

Part III, Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom: The bubble has turned Abyssal. Inside, the Traveler's group finds Mondstadt overrun and the corrupted Dvalin beyond saving, and they must kill the bubble's Dvalin in Stormterror's Lair. The real Dvalin arrives and fights alongside them. Alice then explains the Abyss's nature, and Jean sends her to confinement for blasting fish.

Revelations: Alice and Nicole's bubble magic builds an interactive world from memories, but without safeguards it can develop causal knock-on effects; here the removal of the Traveler's Dvalin purification let a nascent Abyssal power take hold. Alice describes the Abyss's essence, according to the Hexenzirkel's view and Barbeloth's interpretation, as the hatred of "fates that will not come to pass". Alice also mentions that her friend Rhinedottir's decision to tap into the Abyss ended the possibility of a future in which she stayed pure.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Jean (Acting Grand Master, in charge of the reception); Varka (Grand Master, returned early); Venti and Dvalin (Anemo Archon and his dragon); the Hexenzirkel mages Alice and Nicole (creators of the bubble); Klee; Diluc; Barbara, Amber, Mona, Fischl and Oz, Albedo, Durin, Mika, Lisa, Kaeya, Noelle and Rosaria in reenactment roles; Hertha, Cyrus, Charles and the event NPCs Hedwig and Horken in minor roles.

Consequences: The bubble is stabilised and looped so the returning knights can experience it at leisure. Klee plays in it with Alice and Nicole. The Knights' welcome celebration is held in a modest form, Jean's worry that Varka would be upset about the celebration is eased, and Alice goes to solitary confinement for fish blasting at Starfell Lake. The event adds no new plot to the Archon Quest.

Placement: Released in Version 6.4 (Luna V) as a Flagship Event, requiring Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III "Song of the Dragon and Freedom"; the Archon Quest "True Moon" and the Lupus Majoris Chapter Act I are recommended for the best experience. It takes place in Mondstadt after Varka's expedition and the Nod-Krai crisis, with the Snezhnaya arc still ahead.

463.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Alice and Nicole's memory bubble
463.content: A magic Alice and Nicole created at the Knights' request: a small world built from Venti's memories and reproduced by volunteers, where returning knights can relive the Traveler's adventures. It is unstable and must be debugged; Nicole offers hints by communication bubble. Without a purification step the bubble developed a nascent Abyssal power and had to be repaired, after which it was set to loop.

464.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Part III Abyssal Dvalin
464.content: In the alternate version of events the bubble creates, Dvalin broke free of a seal and is thoroughly corrupted, so purification would kill him. Venti, Varka, Diluc, Jean and the Traveler defeat him in the bubble's Stormterror's Lair. The real Dvalin joins at the end, and Varka delivers the final blow with the Abyssal core as the target.

465.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Varka's homecoming celebration
465.content: Varka asked that there be no grand reception, but Jean wanted the returning expedition to know they are still family. The compromise is a small Mondstadt-style festival with food, drink, sparring, glider shooting and the bubble. Varka thanks the Traveler for their help in Mondstadt and Natlan and sits with them on the Anemo Archon Statue.

key: fates that will not come to pass
466.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Unchosen fates
466.content: Alice's explanation that the Abyss is rooted in the hatred of the possibilities that were eliminated when something else happened; even trivial choices (a lunch order) cut off other versions of a person. She says the Hexenzirkel, and particularly Barbeloth, hold this view and that the bubble allowed some of these fates to come close to reality.

key: True Tales of the Violet Garden
The Strange Tale of Suikou's Tipsy Tincture
What the Blue Flowers Left Behind
A New Painting in Pale Scarlet
467.content:
Hues of the Violet Garden (also: True Tales of the Violet Garden, Legends of the Kasen, The Strange Tale of Suikou's Tipsy Tincture, What the Blue Flowers Left Behind, A New Painting in Pale Scarlet, The Palace, Dyed in Black, Irodori Anecdotes): Across four acts the Traveler greets guests as they arrive at Ritou's harbour: Albedo and Klee from Mondstadt, with Venti arriving by accident; Xingqiu with calligraphers and Theater Mechanicus players from Liyue; then Kazuha. Each guest finds an anonymous excerpt from the legend of the Five Kasen, and the excerpts and the guests' troubles gradually connect. A new light-novel volume goes missing, Xingqiu's signature trouble is solved, and Albedo paints the poets' portraits using the guests as models. The fourth act connects the story to the downfall of the Raiden Gokaden, five Inazuman forging schools, and an old failed sword commission. At the end Ayato admits he and Miko staged the hunt to help Kazuha find the truth.

Plot: Act I, The Strange Tale of Suikou's Tipsy Tincture: The Adventurers' Guild gives the Traveler a commission from Miko to guide Irodori Festival guests. Albedo, Klee and Venti arrive; a novel volume is missing; Sara catches Venti as a suspected intruder; Albedo takes inspiration from a Suikou excerpt and paints Venti as Suikou. Act II, What the Blue Flowers Left Behind: Xingqiu arrives with a second excerpt, and the Traveler and Albedo find that his calligraphy is why he came early. Act III, A New Painting in Pale Scarlet: Kazuha arrives with a third excerpt, the group plans author seals to help Xingqiu, and Ayaka and Venti bring a paper that reveals more writing in water. Kazuha begins to talk about his family. Act IV, The Palace, Dyed in Black: Kazuha learns the cause of the old sword failure and the group finds a hidden letter, then Albedo's last portrait is revealed.

Revelations: The old sword failure was sabotage. The forging diagram for a Goshintou had been altered so that even skilled Isshin smiths could not succeed, and the blame fell on the Kaedehara Clan. The saboteur was an eccentric who called himself Kunikuzushi, defeated the Yashiro head's party and warned that he would destroy the rest of the Raiden Gokaden if the story spread. Both families kept silent, which, as Ayaka says, let later generations exist. Ayato staged the poem hunt, partly on Miko's idea, so that Kazuha could find this out and so that the Kaedehara and Kamisato descendants could rely on each other.

Characters: Albedo, Venti, Xingqiu, Klee, Kazuha, Ayaka and Ayato in the main acts, with Kujou Sara, Yae Miko and the Traveler. Event NPCs include Hirayama, Onodera, Zhenyu's editors, Xu of the Feiyun Commerce Guild, Satomi and Kadenokouji Kenzaburou, Asakawa, Fushizome, Kayabuki Ikkei and others. The Irodori Anecdotes also feature Itto, Gorou, Kokomi, Sayu, Thoma, Yoimiya and the Raiden Shogun.

Consequences: Kazuha learns the truth about his family's failure and chooses not to pursue old grievances. Ayaka learns that her ancestor kept the same secret. Ayato's two-sided purpose is explained to the Traveler. Xingqiu's signing problem is addressed with author seals. The Irodori Festival goes ahead, with the event's poems, themed challenges and floral courtyards.

Placement: Released in Version 2.6 as a Flagship Event and set in Ritou after the Archon Quest "Ritou Escape Plan". The recommended story quests are Ayato's The Firmiana Leaf Falls and Kokomi's and the Shogun's story quests. Scaramouche appears here only as the Balladeer in a portrait and in the letter's past history; his later story as Wanderer is not part of this event.

468.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: Five Kasen
468.content: Legendary Inazuman poets who took turns each year to present a poem collection to the Shogun; their works are the reason for the Irodori Festival. The poets are known by colours (green Suikou, blue Aoi no Okina, red Akahito, white Sumizome, black Kuronushi) and little is reliably known of them. In this event Ayato devised the version of the legend that guides Kazuha.

469.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: Raiden Gokaden
469.content: In Ayaka's account, the five best Inazuman forging schools, tied to the Yashiro Commission; today only the Amenoma art remains, the Isshin Art is lost although the Kaedehara Clan descends from it, and three schools vanished quickly, which fuelled rumours of a plot.

470.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: Kunikuzushi
470.content: The name given by an eccentric who sabotaged the Kaedehara Clan's Goshintou in Yoshinori's day, asked about "Niwa", defeated the Yashiro head's party and told Yoshinori to pass his name to "her". The wiki identifies him with Scaramouche; the event only implies this through the Balladeer portrait.

471.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: Irodori Festival
471.content: Held in Ritou in this event to honour the Five Kasen, show off modern light novels from Yae Publishing House and welcome foreign guests, with guides, poetry, performances and a flower display. Miko organises and Ayato helps as head of the Yashiro Commission.

472.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: A Legend of Sword
472.content: A light-novel series by Zhenyu, a pen name of Xingqiu, illustrated by Albedo. Its latest volume disappears in Act I. Xingqiu has trouble signing copies in a neat hand.

473.content:
Hyperion's Dirge (also: Hyperion's Dirge Chapter, Narrow Inquiry, Temple Inquiry, Serpent's Heart Inquiry, Helios-Forger): A version 2.4 world quest series in Enkanomiya. A proud shade who calls himself Aberaku, Helios-Forger, says he built the Dainichi Mikoshi, the solar chariot that lit the sunless land, yet was imprisoned and his soul scattered. The Traveler recovers three fragments of it so that he can rest.

The fragments lie at the Narrows, the Evernight Temple and the Serpent's Heart. Once Aberaku is whole he remembers everything and tells how the light of the Dainichi Mikoshi drove off the Dragonheirs of the Depths, how nobles then used it to seize power through puppet Sunchildren, and how he was jailed for opposing that. As thanks he gives the Traveler the Divine Bridle, a badge of the Sunchild's office.

Plot: Aberaku introduces himself theatrically. Paimon asks about the Helios, and he explains it is the Dainichi Mikoshi. He asks the Traveler to find three pieces of his shattered soul.

At the Narrows he speaks of how his creation brought joy and saved the nation from the Bathysmal Vishaps and wonders why he cannot rest; his bones are enshrined here and monsters hold the fragment. At the Evernight Temple he says he was jailed on a child's orders but bears the child no hate, since the Sunchildren were only puppets, and that he was held in a high, dark, ice-cold place; his body and clothes were enshrined in several places to honour his work, which split his soul. The Traveler recovers his sacred crown. At the Serpent's Heart he says he was betrayed and left to rot after the Helios was made, and the Traveler wins back his sacred robes. Back with Aberaku, now whole, he tells the full story.

Revelations: Byakuyakoku was terrorised by the Dragonheirs of the Depths until the light of the Dainichi Mikoshi drove them off. When peace came, greedy nobles led the people to worship the Mikoshi and proclaimed the rule of the Sunchild over the land, using the child as a puppet. Aberaku opposed this, was accused of high treason by the Sunchildren and imprisoned.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Aberaku, a shade.

Aberaku's original name is Abrax; his title is Helios-Forger. The wiki profile also calls him a sage enlightened by the Tokoyo Ookami. The Sunchildren are mentioned but not met.

Consequences: Aberaku's soul is whole and he can rest, though his closing remark afterwards is that all his talent and ability came to nothing. The Traveler keeps the Divine Bridle.

Placement: Released in Version 2.4 with Enkanomiya as a world quest series. Like Erebos' Secret, it requires From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku, so either can be done first.

474.content: Aberaku no Mikoto, born Abrax, is the creator of the Dainichi Mikoshi (the Helios) in Enkanomiya. He was imprisoned by the Sunchild and died; his memories remain as a shade. The wiki profile says he lived about 6,000 years ago, was a pupil of Istoria, and travelled to Enkanomiya (then Delphi Pytho) shortly before the war of funerary flame, becoming trapped there.

475.content:
Ignis Purgatorius Chapter (also: Ignis Purgatorius, Arlecchino's Story Quest, When the Hearth-Flame Goes Out, The Child Who Doesn't Exist, Sea Breeze Rendezvous, Birds in a Cage, Into the Sunlight): Arlecchino's Story Quest, set in Poisson. A rumour of a 'phantom child' no one remembers has spread through the House of the Hearth, and Arlecchino has moved the whole House to the town to find her. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet secretly shelter the girl, Clervie, and the Traveler helps. Arlecchino reveals that Clervie was her friend, killed years ago in a duel, and the quest ends with Clervie being let go in peace.

The chapter has one act, When the Hearth-Flame Goes Out, of four quests: The Child Who Doesn't Exist, Sea Breeze Rendezvous, Birds in a Cage and Into the Sunlight. It was released in version 4.6 and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty. It shows the Harbinger as a ruthless and honest head of a household who rewrote the cruel rules she inherited.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon visit Poisson and find the House of the Hearth staying there. Freminet has been sheltering a girl named Clervie who no one else remembers. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet try to quietly resolve it. Arlecchino learns of it, warns the Traveler, then explains that Clervie died long ago. She lets the siblings duel her, allows the 'traitors' to leave with their memories erased, and releases Clervie at dawn.

The Child Who Doesn't Exist: in Poisson the Traveler meets Lyney, who says that Father has moved the family there during trouble elsewhere. Arlecchino says a rumour that a 'phantom child' is among the House has spread and she wants to find the culprit. Freminet leads the Traveler, Paimon and Lyney to Clervie, who has been following the House for about half a month. She says there were two rosters, one for an ideal candidate and one for execution, and that no one leaves the House alive. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet agree to find a way to grant her wish to go where the sun can shine.

Sea Breeze Rendezvous: the Traveler finds Arlecchino on the shore with Childe, who has come looking for Skirk and heard a rumour that she betrayed the House. She admits she is not a Fontainian and that duels in the House once ended in death. The siblings find that Clervie cannot go into sunlight and that her name is not on the execution roster. At night the Traveler and Paimon find Clervie leaving town and learn she fears being sent to Dottore.

Birds in a Cage: Arlecchino tells them she has known all along and orders them to Palais Mermonia. She says that betrayal is not tolerated, lets the Traveler off as a guest, and promises not to punish the siblings if Clervie is gone. At the Palais she gives Neuvillette a written proposal to withdraw her forces from Fontaine over time, and he accepts. Afterwards she agrees to let the guests stay, on condition that they help the House when the time comes.

Into the Sunlight: at ruins on Mont Esus East, Arlecchino tells her history. She decides to kill Clervie's shade again. Lyney begs her to stop and Lynette, Freminet and Chapleau back him. She duels the siblings, with the Traveler joining them, and wins easily. She then offers a potion of her flames that will erase the memory of the House, and the 'traitors' take it and leave. Clervie is told the truth, accepts it, and fades at dawn.

Revelations: The 'phantom child' is Clervie, the daughter of the previous Harbinger Crucabena, killed in a duel with the young Arlecchino years ago.

Arlecchino, whose real name she says is Peruere, killed Crucabena and rewrote the House of the Hearth's rules. Before that, the House made orphans fight each other, and those who survived were hurt or given to Dottore. She is also not Fontainian.

Characters: Arlecchino, the Traveler, Paimon, Lyney, Lynette, Freminet, Clervie.

Childe, who visits Arlecchino on the shore. Neuvillette, who accepts her proposal at Palais Mermonia. Children of the House including Filliol, Chapleau, Tonia and Teucer, as well as Crucabena (in flashback).

Consequences: Clervie is released and the 'traitors' who drank the potion leave the House with no memory of it. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet stay. Arlecchino and the Traveler part with an acknowledged bond, though she says they may be on opposite sides in future.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Chapter IV Act V, Masquerade of the Guilty. Released in 4.6, so it follows the Fontaine Archon Quest in release order.

476.content: The 'phantom child' of the Ignis Purgatorius Chapter. As Arlecchino tells it, Clervie was Crucabena's daughter and the friend of the girl who became Arlecchino. She died in a duel with that friend after deciding death was the only escape from the House. A shade of her at age six was somehow formed from the shadows in Arlecchino's blood. She fades at dawn after being told the truth.

477.comment: Ignis Purgatorius Chapter: Potion of Arlecchino's flames
477.content: After the duel, Arlecchino offers any member who wishes to leave a potion made from her searing flames. Whoever survives it loses memories of the House, which in her words 'kills' that life so they can be released. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet each have a bottle available but decline it.

478.content:
Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls (also: Spiritseeking Scrolls, Night-Wind Letter, Vision of Ashen Desolation, The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil): Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls was a limited-time flagship event of Version 5.2 (28 November to 16 December 2024) set among the Masters of the Night-Wind in Natlan. Ororon asks the Traveler for help when a spirit-duffer named Leyla loses his spirit during a clairvoyance attempt. With Citlali the Traveler recovers it and learns that a stranger called Kokuchuu was after the location of the vanished Mare Jivari.

Alongside the story the event offered three gameplay modes tied to clairvoyance (gathering roaming spirits, banishing disruptive foes and arranging fragments of a woven scroll). Its main reward was the sword Calamity of Eshu. Because it was an event, the story is canon but not known to every player or character.

Plot: Ororon invites the Traveler to the Masters of the Night-Wind. Citlali has been blocking him from saving a comatose man, Leyla, whose spirit is lost after a clairvoyance session. Citlali joins in, reads Leyla's lingering visions, discovers they lead to Sanhaj's relic and the Mare Jivari, and calls his spirit home. The stranger behind it escapes.

The story runs over three volumes: Night-Wind Letter, Vision of Ashen Desolation and The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil. Leyla, a man with no spiritual sensitivity, is physically present but spiritless. Citlali and Ororon first disagree over how to help him, then work together through two approaches: gathering roaming spirits, and reading the visions his body and a relic produce. The trail reveals that a stranger planted the relic as bait.

Revelations: Kokuchuu was after the location of the Mare Jivari, and Leyla was used as bait in a plan to get a real clairvoyant to examine Sanhaj's relic.

Characters: Citlali, Ororon, the Traveler and Paimon.

Leyla, a member of the Masters of the Night-Wind who lacks spiritual sensitivity; Matla, the tribe's witch doctor; and Kokuchuu, an Inazuman-dressed stranger who is listed under Enjou on the wiki. Leyla's parents appear only in report.

Consequences: Leyla recovers and begins training under Ororon. The Traveler keeps the shard and map. Citlali marks Kokuchuu and plans to follow him.

Placement: Released 28 November 2024 in Version 5.2 as a flagship event. It required Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III. Completing Chapter V Act IV, The Rainbow Destined to Burn, was recommended for the best experience. It takes place in the Masters of the Night-Wind territory in the Tezcatepetonco Range.

479.content: In the Masters of the Night-Wind a spirit-duffer is a person with no spiritual sensitivity: they cannot sense or command spirits and cannot cast the tribe's spells. Because the tribe's healing and problem solving all rely on dealing with spirits, ordinary treatments fail on them. Forcing a spirit-duffer into clairvoyance is possible but dangerous, and Leyla's case shows why.

480.content: Kokuchuu is the name used by a stranger in Inazuman dress who befriends Leyla and proposes the dangerous hypersensitization therapy. Citlali judges that he used Leyla to get a clairvoyant to view Sanhaj's relic and learn where the Mare Jivari lay. He was never captured. In the quest he presents himself as a friendly helper.

481.comment: Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls: Sanhaj's bow shard
481.content: A broken shard of the bow Sanhaj used in the Battle of the Mare Jivari. It carries strong spiritual energy and was used as a medium by Leyla. Ororon feels it is connected to his ancient name. Citlali gives it to the Traveler together with a map of the Mare Jivari's last known location.

482.content: Kokuchuu's name for immersing a spirit-duffer in spiritually rich substances so they may glimpse spirits. Citlali says the Masters of the Night-Wind once offered a similar treatment but outlawed it, since it carried severe risk and rarely worked.

483.content:
Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter (also: Imperatrix Umbrosa, Raiden Shogun's Story Quest, Ei's Story Quest, Reflections of Mortality, Transient Dreams): The Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter is the Raiden Shogun's Story Quest. In Act I, Reflections of Mortality (Version 2.1), the Traveler brings Ei, the Electro Archon, out of her Plane of Euthymia to walk through Inazuma City. In Act II, Transient Dreams (Version 2.5), Ei confronts the memories of the catastrophe five centuries ago and her sister Makoto, defeats her own puppet in a duel and abolishes the Sakoku Decree.

Both acts take place after the Archon Quest Omnipresence Over Mortals. Act I has four quests: The Lonesome Euthymia, To Traverse the Mortal Plane, The Fabric of Constancy and To Hear Mortal Hearts. Act II has three: Cleansing Light, Farewell to the Past and Radiant Sakura. The chapter shows Ei beginning to take a living part in rule, and settles her relationship with the Shogun puppet.

Plot: Act I, Reflections of Mortality. Thoma, Kamaji and Ippei are worried because the Shogun wants private time, the storms around Inazuma are advancing, and the Kujou Clan has lost control over its vassals after Kujou Takayuki's dealings with the Fatui and his poor health. Kamaji goes to see Takatsukasa Susumu. At the Grand Narukami Shrine, Yae Miko gives the Traveler a pass to see the Shogun, who at Tenshukaku does not recognise them and behaves strangely. Ei speaks through the puppet and takes them to her plane, saying she has disabled most of its functions because it clings to the old protocols she wants to change, and the puppet resists change so only Miko may see her. She says a small change to the Shogun could stop the storm. The Traveler asks about her view of Eternity, and Paimon suggests she take a walk.

Outside, Ei notes that the market has changed. She has no Mora because as an Archon she never shopped. At Tomoki's stall she tries Dango Milk, likes it, and her praise keeps him from dropping the product. At the Yae Publishing House she browses novels but cannot grasp fiction. She decides she should not hamper human lives for her pursuit of eternity. The Traveler takes a photo, and Ei is surprised that it shows only one person; they remind her she can exist in more than one form, like the puppet. She says Inazuma has changed a great deal and perhaps she held on too tightly.

Revelations: - Ei has disabled most of the puppet Shogun's functions while she tries to change its old protocols.
- Ei can occupy the Shogun's body in the real world, and sees herself as one being with several forms.
- Ei has never dealt with Mora or shops, and enjoys Dango Milk.
- The Takatsukasa Clan tried to take the Tenryou Commission from the Kujou by pressuring Kamaji.

Characters: - **Raiden Shogun**: the Electro Archon Ei and her puppet, the chapter's protagonist.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: bring Ei into the city and then fight beside her.
- **Yae Miko**: Guuji who lends the pass, and governs for Ei when she retreats.
- **Thoma, Kujou Kamaji, Ippei**: Inazuman retainers and officials concerned for the Shogun.
- **Tomoki, Kuroda**: a stall owner and a publishing house editor.
- **Takatsukasa Susumu**: leader of the Takatsukasa plot.
- **Kitamura, Furuyama, Fujiki, Fukami**: memory echoes from the Sacred Sakura.
- **Makoto**: Ei's late sister, first Electro Archon.

Consequences: Ei takes an active role in governing Inazuma. The Shogun puppet becomes her kagemusha. The Sakoku Decree is abolished. The Kujou Clan gets more time. Susumu and the Takatsukasa are checked.

Placement: Act I is Version 2.1; Act II, Transient Dreams, is Version 2.5. Both require Omnipresence Over Mortals and Adventure Rank 40; Act I is a prerequisite for the Kaedehara, Kamisato Ayato and Yae Miko chapters, and Act II is also required for Yae Miko's. Story order and release order match.

484.content: The Shogun that Ei made to rule in her place. In Transient Dreams it turns against Ei, believing she is suffering erosion; after a duel in Makoto's consciousness it accepts that she is not, and becomes her kagemusha.

485.comment: Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter: Furuyama and the memory echoes
485.content: Memories of the catastrophe 500 years ago that appear from the Sacred Sakura's roots. Furuyama, a tea specialist in Ei's entourage, accepts life's end as Makoto's teaching. Kitamura, Fujiki and Fukami are samurai who feared for Inazuma and take heart when Ei returns. They fade once the Ley Lines can no longer sustain them.

486.content: Takatsukasa Susumu tries to replace the Kujou Clan as Tenryou Commissioner by pressuring Kamaji at a hidden base guarded by ronin. Ei interrupts, says only someone who defeats her can hold the office, and Susumu backs down. Kamaji duels her instead.

key: In the Dwelling of Life world quest series
487.content:
In the Dwelling of Life (also: In the Dwelling of Life world quest series, Okurov quest series, Flamefeather Valley quest series, Nastya's quest): In the Dwelling of Life is a seven-part world quest series added in 7.0 in Flamefeather Valley, Snezhnaya. The Traveler and Paimon find a small girl named Nastya, who has branches growing from her head, asleep in a crate of loot, and escort her home to Okurov, a village sealed off from the outside world. There they learn that a "Doctor Moreau" has been leading the villagers into a ritual that turns people into a single eternal "Perfect Tree", and that the doctor is really the bio-alchemist Koshchei. Nastya chooses the ritual anyway, and the series ends with the Traveler recovering a fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power.

The series parts are: A Sprout Without a Gardener; Transplanted From "Yesterday" to "Tomorrow"; Down in the Dumps; Back on One's Feet; Forbidding Doors of Melancholy; To Rest in a Forgotten Field; and Chorus of Solace. Each title echoes a line from Nelly Sachs's poem "Chorus of the Consolers" (the final title echoes the poem's own title), according to the wiki's trivia; this is an observation of the title pattern, not an in-game statement.

Plot: At the Morepesok train station, the Traveler and Paimon overhear Vinezka and her fiance Jary. Jary has been hired by criminals to blast open a tunnel to the abandoned town of Okurov, and Vinezka fears the local legend of a firebird that lures people into the valley and devours them. The Traveler takes the job. In the valley they defeat a Volkodlak gang led by "The Anvil" and find Nastya asleep in a crate; she lives in Okurov and speaks of a guardian called Zhara. She leads them through the tunnel toward her home. In the end Nastya enters the ritual, dissolves into glowing blue algae and joins the Perfect Tree.

In A Sprout Without a Gardener, The Anvil claims the "treasure" he stole from Okurov is inside the blocked tunnel and tries to enforce a hundred-times penalty on Jary. The "treasure" turns out to be Nastya, who fears she has been kidnapped by Volkodlak again, says she has slept in the dark for what felt like a short time, and clears the path with a magic hook. A newspaper in a wrecked carriage praises Okurov's warm weather, its exceptional doctor and its open-door policy; the air near the tunnel's end is unnaturally warm.

In the second quest, Nastya describes her town's belief that the assembly hall is the true home. She idolises "Doctor Moreau", whom she also calls "Doctor Birdie", who taught that becoming family means growing branches and leaves until everyone is the same. She calls outsiders "Badbugs", who in her telling are burned to feed the soil, and they play a game of "Catch the Bug" that she secretly uses to lead the party among hostile Leshy she regards as family. Then Zhara, a huge winged creature, attacks.

Revelations: Okurov's "Doctor Moreau" is Koshchei the Deathless, a Snezhnayan bio-alchemist and former Hvergelmir member. His notes say the Perfect Tree grants great strength but regresses language, and that the "final ceremony" aims to turn the participants into embryos of a new, emotionless existence; pain, sorrow and individual love are to be cast off for eternal life, though the notes admit love might be the only thing that does not fade. The warm air, the blue algae and the Leshy are all products of this work. Zhara is Koshchei's guardian creature.

Characters: Nastya, a child of Okurov who idolises "Doctor Birdie" and Furiosa; Koshchei (as Doctor Moreau); Zhara; the Leshy including Aunt LePuy and Ove; Furiosa; the Eye of Graeae; Aksinya; Vinezka and Jary; "The Anvil". The Traveler and Paimon escort Nastya throughout.

Nastya's mother, who has apparently already joined the tree, appears only through Nastya's words. Zhara can only be told apart from other constructs by its humanoid upper body and branch "mask" per the wiki. Nastya is a young child and should be portrayed as innocent and trusting, not as a villain.

Consequences: Nastya is gone, and the ritual's power is recovered as a crystal fragment for the Eye of Graeae, which helps its quest to rebuild its body. Aksinya now knows the Traveler and shares the Eye's goal. Koshchei is dissolved, and the experiment has ended in Okurov. The wiki says that visiting Nastya's home afterwards shows a young Juvenile Tree Segment named Shar living there with blue algae by the bed.

Placement: Released 7.0 as part of the Snezhnaya launch. The wiki lists it as concurrent with Archon Quest Chapter VII Act I quests "On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb" and "Hesperides of Love and Hate", with "Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard" next. No separate prerequisite quest is stated for the world quest series.

488.comment: In the Dwelling of Life: Okurov
488.content: Okurov is a hidden village in Flamefeather Valley, unlocked during the series. Its name references the 1908 novel The City of Okurov by Maxim Gorky, per the wiki. Its air is warm enough to help "pretty leaves" grow, its townsfolk see the assembly hall as home, and its Leshy residents include former villagers who did not complete the ritual. The way in is a collapsed rail tunnel leading from the Morepesok side, which Jary was hired to blast open.

489.comment: In the Dwelling of Life: Nastya
489.content: Nastya is a young child from Okurov with branches growing from her head, found asleep in a crate. She is cheerful, proud of being "the smartest child", loyal to the doctor and to Furiosa, and eager to see the world outside the valley for the first time while longing for her mother. Her choice at the end is shown as hers; the quest treats it as tragic and does not call her foolish.

490.comment: In the Dwelling of Life: Zhara
490.content: Zhara is an Immortal Construct made by Koshchei, with a humanoid upper half, long blonde hair and branches masking her eyes. She guards Okurov from "Badbugs" (outsiders), attacks the Traveler twice and is subdued at the great tree. Aksinya stops her from reviving. The name echoes the Russian word for heat and the Firebird of folklore.

key: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons
In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons World Quest series
Someday, We All Must Walk Alone
491.comment: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons
491.content:
In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons (also: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons World Quest series, Little One side quests, Someday, We All Must Walk Alone): The series gathers the Little One side quests: A Saurian Lover's Ordinary Days, Feeling Like Fish Today!, Friends of Fire and Water (5.2), Gifts and Gifts in Return, Is "Intensity" Really the Key? (5.5), Lies and Promises, Lights, Kamera, Action!, Sauro-Vet's Dilemma (5.2), Special Friends, Stones, Coconuts, and Saurian Traffickers (5.2), Tepetlisaurus Hide-and-Seek, The Lone Isle Named Night (5.2), Treasures and Collectors, Waiting For Seeds to Sprout and Weighty Wings. They can be done in any order. Most are light errands that show Little One meeting other saurians and humans in Natlan. The final quest, Someday, We All Must Walk Alone (5.5), unlocks only after the main Little One quests are finished and a few hidden interactions around the map are completed. In it Little One takes a photograph with the Traveler and Paimon, then leaves on its own.

Plot: The side quests share one setup. After Lost in the Woods, Little One travels with the Traveler and Paimon, and each quest starts from something Little One does or finds: catching fish, digging up a seed, meeting a group of alpacas, hiding among other Tepetlisauri, gifting its collected treasures, wanting to star in a film, or discovering a hidden chamber on the Isle of Night. Paimon narrates and mothers it; the Traveler handles the practical and puzzle work. Several quests take place in other tribes' territory, such as the Flower-Feather Clan range, and bring in local NPCs with their own saurian partners.

Someday, We All Must Walk Alone is the capstone. Once every Little One quest and a handful of unmarked puzzles are done, Little One leads the group back to the Rest Area where they first met, has found a Kamera, and sets up a group photograph. Afterwards it shows that it wants to go its own way. Paimon cries and makes the Traveler promise they will meet again; Little One tucks one photograph into its shell, nuzzles Paimon and the Traveler, and plods off.

Revelations: The series makes few story revelations of its own. It shows that Little One understands more than it can say and that it has quietly kept hold of keepsakes from the journey. In the closing quest Little One sets up the photograph and then departs; the narration says the Traveler recalls the mix of feelings in its eyes at the foot of the Sacred Mountain.

Characters: Little One is a young Tepetlisaurus with a red Flamelord's Blessing mark on its horn and a scarf from Paimon tied to its tail. It speaks only in growls and is treated as "he" by Paimon and the Traveler in several lines. It is energetic, curious, a hearty eater, and loyal. Paimon is protective and tearful at the parting; the Traveler is calmer but affected. Other quest NPCs include Icayo, Imix and Kulahaw, Linaha, Ma'chah and Yoleehe, Wayna, Mazkal, Qax, Quipia, and Akatanga, each tied to one quest.

Consequences: Completing Someday, We All Must Walk Alone ends Little One's time with the party. It gives the achievement Then You Will Be Free to..., the avatar "Till We Meet Again", 20 Primogems, a Photo With Travel Companions and Mora. After it the souvenirs in the Rest Area disappear, except for the Unhatched Saurian Egg.

Placement: Most side quests released in 5.0 with Natlan; Friends of Fire and Water, Sauro-Vet's Dilemma, Stones, Coconuts, and Saurian Traffickers and The Lone Isle Named Night joined in 5.2; Is "Intensity" Really the Key? and Someday, We All Must Walk Alone arrived in 5.5. In story order the side quests can be done any time after Lost in the Woods, but the finale quest should be done after A Finale Emberforged and all other Little One content.

key: Someday We All Must Walk Alone
492.comment: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons: Someday, We All Must Walk Alone
492.content: Someday, We All Must Walk Alone is the final quest of the series. In the Rest Area where they first met, Little One shows the Traveler and Paimon a Kamera (a camera-like gadget), performs a move Paimon recognises as the Mighty Meaty Fireball, and takes a photograph with them. It then says goodbye. Paimon tearfully makes it promise to come find them if it needs help, and tells it to stay healthy and big. Little One nuzzles them and leaves.

493.comment: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons: Kamera and the Mighty Meaty Fireball
493.content: Lights, Kamera, Action! is the quest in which the Traveler shoots a film starring Little One, and Akatanga appears in it. In the farewell quest Paimon recalls Akatanga as a would-be director who used his Kamera backwards and guesses Little One got its Kamera from him. Paimon also recognises a pose of Little One's as the Mighty Meaty Fireball, and the three say the phrase for the photograph. It is a light, comic detail contrasted with the parting.

494.content:
In the Mountains (also: In the Mountains world quest, Dragonspine frozen shards quest): A Dragonspine world quest from Version 1.2. Iris, an adventurer at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp, complains of strange unmeltable ice blocking expedition routes. The Traveler thaws glowing shards from that ice, follows them up the mountain and opens the way to the summit.

The quest requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind and starts by talking to Iris at the camp. Completing it opens the Frostbearing Tree offering system, the Peak of Vindagnyr domain and the Cryo Hypostasis boss, as game-side unlocks. It is a gameplay-driven quest with little dialogue lore.

Plot: Iris tells the Traveler about hard ice that will not melt in fire and a cavern near the summit that breathes a strange powerful wind. The Traveler thaws a shard in the ice, sees a blue orb fly toward the summit, and later thaws two more. Reaching the top, they find a floating pillar and a hollow beneath it, and report back to Iris.

Iris suggests looking at a large slab of ice on the mountain's outer edge. When it is thawed with Scarlet Quartz, a blue orb flies off toward the summit and a new Frostbearing Tree grows. Paimon and the Traveler try to climb the summit cavern but are driven back by the cold and the air current, so they return to the camp. Iris explains that earlier expedition teams were turned back by the ice and that blue plants cluster near it, pointing to the Entombed City outskirts and Starglow Cavern. After thawing the other two shards the Traveler follows the road past a Statue of The Seven to the summit and sees a giant pillar. The three shards have frozen again on it, so the Traveler thaws them a second time. The ice under the pillar then shatters, revealing a large space below. Iris thanks them and promises to send explorers.

Revelations: No question is answered. The quest only establishes that the ice shards belong to a floating pillar at the summit (later called the Skyfrost Nail) and that a chamber lies beneath it.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon and Iris.

Iris is an adventurer at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp who organises expedition parties and warns the Traveler to prepare well before going up the mountain.

Consequences: Iris can resume organising expeditions now that the ice can be melted. The summit becomes reachable, and the Peak of Vindagnyr domain and Cryo Hypostasis become accessible as game features. The achievement for restoring the Skyfrost Nail is granted.

Placement: Released in Version 1.2 with the Dragonspine content. It follows The Outlander Who Caught the Wind in requirements and is a companion to the Dragonspine quest A Land Entombed, which uses the same mountain and ruins.

key: wooden house on the ice farewell
495.content:
In the Tranquility of Cycles (also: Chulkaturin's last quest, Chulkaturin's farewell, wooden house on the ice farewell): In the Tranquility of Cycles is a short 7.0 world quest in Snezhnaya's far north. It ends the story of Chulkaturin, an ancient fae who lives in a wooden cabin built on a floe of ice and refuses to set foot on Snezhnayan land. When the Traveler and Paimon return, the ice is melting and the cabin is about to sink. He declines to come ashore, thanks them, asks to be left alone, and the house sinks as the ice melts.

The quest is the third part of a chain begun in Ever Beneath the Waves and continued in The Sunken Ship Sailed Past, Ringing No Bells. Completing it grants the achievement "The Cherry Orchard Has Been Sold" (per the wiki).

Plot: The Traveler finds Chulkaturin's cabin tilted toward the sea. Paimon calls to him; he answers from inside and agrees that the ice is going, but will not leave. Rather than argue, the Traveler can try to persuade him, offer to pull him ashore or suggest rebuilding on ice, and he rejects each. He asks them to stop breaking the ice, stop towing the house and let him go, then asks for a last goodbye. The house makes no further answer.

In the earlier quests the Traveler cleared brash ice and towed the cabin toward shore in Ever Beneath the Waves, and in The Sunken Ship Sailed Past, Ringing No Bells helped him reach crates of materials so he could expand and reinforce it. Chulkaturin says he overloaded the floe himself in a wish to restore a measure of his people's former glory and dignity.

The cabin, he says, bears all his history and is his last place. Leaving would cut him from his roots; a new house would not be built from the snow poplars he grew up alongside, and new ice would not bear the weight of the past. He fears that on land, where the future is unpredictable, few of his choices would still be his own. He asks the Traveler for a last farewell instead of rescue.

Revelations: Chulkaturin's earlier statements stand: he calls himself the last scion of old snowfield-dwelling nobility, a relic of an era that "still belonged to the fae", uprooted from the land over three hundred years ago, whose snow poplars were all cut down. This quest adds that he sees the past as inseparable from his life and that he would need to atone for it before he could start a new one. What he must atone for is not explained.

Characters: Chulkaturin, an old fae speaking from inside the cabin; the Traveler and Paimon. Chulkaturin addresses them as "shorebound travelers" and finally as friends.

His voice is formal, archaic and gentle. He thanks them repeatedly and never argues angrily. Paimon is the one who panics, pleads and offers practical alternatives.

Consequences: Chulkaturin and his house are gone from the ice. The Traveler's choice here is limited to how to say goodbye (the options in the wiki text are to plead, offer to help, or accept) and does not change the outcome.

Placement: Released in 7.0 as an ordinary open-world quest in northern Snezhnaya, available after completing The Sunken Ship Sailed Past, Ringing No Bells. It has no link to the Archon Quest.

496.comment: In the Tranquility of Cycles: Chulkaturin
496.content: Chulkaturin is an old fae who has lived 321 years in a wooden cabin on a floe, built from felled snow poplars, never setting foot on Snezhnayan land. He calls himself the last scion of old snowfield-dwelling nobility. He speaks in a courtly, archaic manner and addresses the Traveler and Paimon as "travelers by the shore". He asks them not to save him in the end and sinks with his home.

497.content:
In the Wake of Narcissus (also: Search in the Algae Sea, Savior's Wake, Waking from the Great Dream, Rowboat's Wake): In the Wake of Narcissus is a four-act Fontaine World Quest series added in version 4.2. It concludes the Narzissenkreuz storyline begun in Ann of the Narzissenkreuz and Ancient Colors. The Traveler, Paimon, Ann, Seymour and a hilichurl-bodied scholar called Caterpillar pursue the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, trace what happened to Mary-Ann, and reach the founder in the Primordial Sea.

The acts are Search in the Algae Sea, Savior's Wake, Waking from the Great Dream and Rowboat's Wake. The series is entered through the quest Initial Facts and its reward track is "In the Wake of Narcissus" in the Fontaine Reputation.

Plot: Act I, Search in the Algae Sea. The group deduce who Mary-Ann in Annapausis is, find the pieces of the Holy Blade in the Morte Region, and fight Jakob at the Tower of Gestalt, who dies when the Doomsday Clock strikes.

Act II, Savior's Wake. They descend and sink the Tower of Ipsissimus beneath the Ordo, leaving Caterpillar and Seymour behind.

Act III, Waking from the Great Dream. In the Primordial Sea the Traveler defeats Narzissenkreuz, and Ann forgives him.

Act IV, Rowboat's Wake. With Narzissenkreuz as guide they reach Mary-Ann in Annapausis, who chooses to live as herself; he fades, Seymour returns to Mamere and Caterpillar leaves.

Revelations: - The Mary-Ann of Annapausis is the Oceanid Lyris merged with Mary-Ann Guillotin; the Narzissenkreuz Institute was an orphanage run by the Oceanid Lyris.
- Narzissenkreuz is Rene, one of the circle around the Institute (Jakob lists Alain, Rene, Director Lyris, Mary-Ann and himself), who became the Ordo's master and tried to save the world from the apocalypse foretold in the prophecy.
- Ann is a being born from Mary-Ann's dream (Caterpillar's and the group's deduction, confirmed by Mary-Ann and Narzissenkreuz), and the adventure-team members are Oceanid-born shapes of that dream.
- The Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz can be any object of significance, and it can separate a will from water.
- Jakob dies when the Doomsday Clock strikes, after reversing the Seal of Chymical Marriage.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Ann, Seymour, Caterpillar, Jakob, Al, Jak, Narzissenkreuz (Rene), Mary-Ann, and Mamere. Lyris and Alain Guillotin are discussed. Petit Chou and Al are mentioned as friends Ann may never see again.

Consequences: Jakob is dead, the Ordo's plan is broken and Narzissenkreuz fades in the Primordial Sea. Mary-Ann chooses to leave Annapausis and live as herself with Ann; Seymour returns to Mamere and Caterpillar goes off alone. The Traveler receives the Sword of Narzissenkreuz and the series' reward track.

Placement: Released in 4.2. Requires Initial Facts, which the wiki places after Mary-Ann's Story, Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog and the Unfinished Comedy series. It is the last of the Ann/Seymour/Narzissenkreuz arcs.

498.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Narzissenkreuz (Rene)
498.content: In Waking from the Great Dream the Traveler faces Narzissenkreuz in the Primordial Sea, where he offers to save as many people as he can and demands the Holy Blade. After defeat he apologises to Ann. In Rowboat's Wake Mary-Ann calls him Rene. He spends the last of his power helping Ann and Mary-Ann and then asks to be left in the Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe.

499.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Jakob's death and the Seal of Chymical Marriage
499.content: In Search in the Algae Sea the Traveler fights Jakob at the Tower of Gestalt. After the Holy Blade is forged he says he has reversed the Seal of Chymical Marriage and predicts Rene's return. The Doomsday Clock then strikes twelve and crushes him.

500.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Caterpillar
500.content: Caterpillar is a hilichurl-bodied scholar who helps the Traveler and Ann with deductions, jokes dryly, and counts himself among the "things that used to be human". He calls Narzissenkreuz "Master" but disagrees with his theories. He says he owes Lanoire the rest of a story, and at the end sets off alone.

501.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Mary-Ann (the Annapausis)
501.content: Mary-Ann in Annapausis is the fused form of the Oceanid Lyris and the human Mary-Ann Guillotin. She keeps the dream-world warm and tries to push visitors away, but accepts her past when Ann shows her a treasure image and when Rene appears. Afterwards she decides to live as herself and travel with Ann.

502.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Seymour's choice
502.content: Seymour is Alain Guillotin's creation, first met in Ancient Colors. In Rowboat's Wake Mary-Ann tells him his old orders are void and asks what he wants to do. He decides to return to Mamere, who is waiting in Merusea Village and plans an art trip with him.

503.content:
Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (also: Chapter V Act V, Natlan Archon Quest finale, Incandescent Ode): The act has five quests (Subterranean Ruins; As the Sun Rises and Sets; Journey of Stars and Flames; Where All Hopes Lie; When All Becomes a Monument) and requires Adventure Rank 40. It follows "All Fires Fuel the Flame"; the act's navigation lists "A Space and Time for You" and "Paralogism" as what comes next. The travel log recap frames it as the end of Natlan's millennia-long war against the Abyss, with the nation facing a hopeful future that its sacrifices have paid for. Within the act: Capitano appears in a dream, the Traveler is given the Ancient Name "Tumaini" (hope), the final battle with Gosoythoth is won, and the aftermath settles Mavuika's fate and points the Traveler toward Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai.

Plot: **Subterranean Ruins.** The Traveler dreams of the Night Kingdom and sees Capitano and Guthred leading "soldiers" toward a destined place; a rift shows on Capitano's chest.

**As the Sun Rises and Sets.** Mavuika, Xilonen and Citlali plan the descent, and the tribes hold a send-off feast. Ororon's ritual on the Traveler's dream identifies Guthred, and Mavuika confirms that Capitano is Thrain, a legendary hero of Natlan from five hundred years ago. Xilonen delivers the Ancient Name "Tumaini" and tests it at the Sulfurous Veins, where it draws in unusual numbers of souls that the group helps to the Night Kingdom.

**Journey of Stars and Flames.** The Traveler reveals the Ancient Name at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, and Mavuika takes them into the Night Kingdom. They split: Mavuika seeks the enemy's core, the Traveler its lair, aided by departed allies and Guthred.

**Where All Hopes Lie.** Mavuika and the Traveler, empowered with Pyro by the Lord of the Night, destroy the dragon-formed Gosoythoth.

**When All Becomes a Monument.** After a ceremony honouring the Traveler, Ronova demands Mavuika's death at Ochkanatlan, and Capitano offers himself instead. See revelations and consequences.

Revelations: - The Traveler's Ancient Name is "Tumaini" (hope); this is the first time in Natlan's history that an outsider has received one. Its power is so great that it attracts souls from beyond Natlan.
- Capitano is Thrain, the "Sentinel Knight" of Khaenri'ah and one of Natlan's legendary heroes of five hundred years ago.
- With Khaenri'ahn technology, Capitano's heart was modified to convert memories and souls from the Ley Lines into knowledge; after the catastrophe five hundred years ago he gave up that capacity and used his heart as a vessel for the souls of his comrades and many Natlanese. By merging his existence with the Lord of the Night he means to become master of the Ley Lines and change the rules so they can go home.
- Capitano, like many Khaenri'ahns, regards himself as innocent of what the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah did, and wants revenge on Ronova for the curse of immortality by turning it into a paradox: if he gives his life for the Lord of the Night she receives the death she demands, yet his immortality negates that death.
- Guthred says he is a story created by the Masters of the Night-Wind.
- Ronova is called the Ruler of Death in the act's dialogue, and the watching rift above Ochkanatlan is attributed by Citlali to her.
- Capitano had asked the Tsaritsa to cancel his mission to take the Pyro Gnosis, and she agreed.

Characters: Mavuika, the Pyro Archon, leads the plan. Xilonen forges the Ancient Name and Citlali interprets the souls it draws. Kachina, Mualani, Kinich and Chasca represent the tribes, and Ororon's ritual reveals Guthred. Capitano, a Fatui Harbinger and Khaenri'ahn, appears in a dream and then at Ochkanatlan. The dead helpers include Atea, Vichama, Mallko, Bona, Cocouik and Chuychu. Gosoythoth is the final enemy; Ronova and Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, appear at the end.

Consequences: Faced with the paradox, Ronova keeps the curse of immortality and relinquishes her demand for a death, telling Capitano to use it to fulfil his final wish. He sits on the Throne of the Primal Fire with the souls he carried, guiding them back to the Night Kingdom and, as Citlali puts it, granting the Lord of the Night eternal life by fusing his existence with hers. The Lord of the Night, grateful for the chance to live forever, apologises for having once thought so little of how long a life lasts, and returns to the Night Kingdom. Mavuika accepts that Natlan still needs a leader and lives; the five present pay respects to Capitano. Natlan is at peace, the Traveler is a celebrated hero, and Mavuika's briefing sends the Traveler toward Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai (the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter, beginning with the prelude "The Journey Home").

Placement: Chapter V, Act V; released in version 5.3 (the change history of the act and of all five quest pages lists 5.3). It follows "All Fires Fuel the Flame" and precedes the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter, whose prelude is "The Journey Home" (5.8). The act page lists "A Space and Time for You" and "Paralogism" as the next quests.

504.content:
Interlude Chapter (also: Interlude Archon Quest, Interlude Chapter Acts): The Interlude Chapter is a set of four self-contained Archon Quest acts. They do not form one story; each follows up on the quest that unlocks it. Act I, The Crane Returns on the Wind (Liyue), covers the rebuilding of the Jade Chamber and Shenhe. Act II, Perilous Trail (Liyue), sends a party into the Chasm after Xiao's lost comrade. Act III, Inversion of Genesis (Sumeru), deals with Scaramouche and Irminsul. Act IV, Paralogism (Mondstadt), is Albedo's trial during Windblume.

The chapter works as a place for stories that grew out of earlier main-story or region content but did not belong in the main chapters. Acts I and II revisit Liyue after the Chapter I finale, Act III follows the Sumeru Archon Quest, and Act IV returns to Mondstadt. The Traveler and Paimon are present throughout, and the Traveler's search for their sibling stays in the background rather than driving any act.

Acts: **Act I, The Crane Returns on the Wind (Version 2.4, Liyue).** Ningguang announces the rebuilding of the Jade Chamber and a contest to gather its materials. The Traveler befriends Shenhe, raised by the adeptus Cloud Retainer, and the sea monster Beisht attacks as the Chamber rises.

**Act II, Perilous Trail (Version 2.7, Liyue).** The Traveler, Yanfei, Yelan, Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu fall into a looping space beneath the Chasm where Xiao is searching for his fallen comrade Bosacius.

**Act III, Inversion of Genesis (Version 3.3, Sumeru).** The imprisoned Scaramouche enters Irminsul with the Traveler, learns Dottore's role in his past, and erases himself; he is later restored and given a new name.

**Act IV, Paralogism (Version 5.6, Mondstadt).** During Windblume, Albedo is tried for murder in a staged trial and then uses a Hexenzirkel trial to turn the young dragon Mini Durin into a human.

Requirements: Each act has its own unlock conditions on the wiki. Act I needs A New Star Approaches (Chapter I Act III). Act II needs A New Star Approaches plus Transient Dreams, Rise Up Golden Soul, Wherefore Did the Spiritstone Descend? and A Teapot to Call Home: Part I, with Adventure Rank 40. Act III needs Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises (Chapter III Act V) and A Strange and Friendless Road, with Adventure Rank 40. Act IV needs Inversion of Genesis and Traveler Observation Report with Adventure Rank 40.

Placement: The chapter sits beside the main Archon Quest chapters, not in sequence with them. The acts come in the order I to IV but each is timed by what it follows: Act I and Act II after the Liyue finale, Act III after Sumeru, and Act IV after Traveler Observation Report. The wiki notes that a long-time player caught up at Act I's release would play it after the Inazuma Archon Quest.

Characters: Recurring through all four acts are the Traveler and Paimon. Each act brings its own cast: Shenhe, Ningguang, Xiao and Cloud Retainer in Act I; Yanfei, Yelan, Itto, Shinobu and Xiao in Act II; Nahida, Scaramouche and Dottore in Act III; Albedo, Jean, Kaeya, Hertha and the Hexenzirkel in Act IV.

Consequences: Act I shows Liyue handling a calamity as a community, and Shenhe begins to find her place among people. Act II tells Xiao what became of Bosacius. Act III frees Scaramouche from a false history and sets him on a path of his own. Act IV clears Albedo and gives Durin a new life as a human. None of the four acts changes the main Archon Quest plot.

505.content: The Interlude Chapter is a set of four unconnected Archon Quest acts: The Crane Returns on the Wind (Liyue, 2.4), Perilous Trail (Liyue, 2.7), Inversion of Genesis (Sumeru, 3.3) and Paralogism (Mondstadt, 5.6). Each follows up on the quest that unlocks it rather than continuing a single story.

key: The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call
506.content:
Inversion of Genesis (also: Interlude Chapter Act III, Interlude Act III, The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call, A Dance of Destruction, The Kabukimono's Finale, As Though Morning Dew): Interlude Chapter Act III. The defeated Scaramouche, held prisoner in Sumeru, joins the Traveler and Nahida in a trial run through Irminsul to look for hidden data on the Traveler's sibling. There he sees that Dottore engineered the tragedy of his past in Tatarasuna, and tries to erase himself from history.

The act has four quests: The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call, A Dance of Destruction, The Kabukimono's Finale and As Though Morning Dew. It was released in Version 3.3 and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and the first act of the Acer Palmatum Chapter. It sits between Perilous Trail and Paralogism in the Interlude Chapter.

Plot: Paimon and the Traveler visit Nahida and find Scaramouche in her sanctuary. Inside Irminsul he learns Dottore's role in his past and erases himself from Irminsul; the world forgets him, and the Traveler must find him and help Nahida restore his memories. He is then given a new name.

Four quests. The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call: two Akademiya scholars tell a ghost story about Tatarasuna, then Nahida, Scaramouche and the Traveler enter Irminsul, where he sees Dottore at work and erases himself. A Dance of Destruction: in Inazuma the Traveler checks what changed. The Kabukimono's Finale: Nahida confirms the erasure from a backup record, the Traveler finds him, and his memories are restored. As Though Morning Dew: he accepts a future and a name.

Revelations: Dottore, under the name Escher, sabotaged the Tatarasuna furnace, killed Niwa and picked the puppet Scaramouche as a future Fatui comrade. Scaramouche learns this inside Irminsul.

The Traveler's sibling once lived with Pierro for a time in Khaenri'ah, where he served as a royal mage. Irminsul can be revised by erasing a person from it, but the erasure does not alter the Traveler, and Nahida keeps a backup of Scaramouche's memories. Rukkhadevata told the Traveler that no one can erase themselves from existence, not even her.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Nahida; Scaramouche (later the Wanderer).

Dottore (as Escher, in a recorded memory), Pierro (mentioned and reported to), Niwa Hisahide (in the memory), Amenoma Tougo, Hirotatsu, Furuta, Xavier, Aqaba and Sawada. Kazuha and the Kamisato siblings are discussed but do not appear.

Consequences: Scaramouche has erased himself from Irminsul and the world forgets him, but he is restored through Nahida's backup, gains an Anemo Vision, receives a new name from the Traveler, and agrees to help the Traveler. Dottore is his target for revenge.

Placement: Third act of the Interlude Chapter, released in Version 3.3 between Perilous Trail (Act II) and Paralogism (Act IV). It requires the Sumeru Archon Quest through Chapter III Act V and the first act of the Acer Palmatum Chapter.

507.comment: Inversion of Genesis: Tatarasuna Furnace Memory
507.content: Within Irminsul the Traveler and Scaramouche see a memory of Tatarasuna. Niwa Hisahide and a man called Escher discuss using Crystal Marrow in the furnace to make the area prosperous, but workers fall ill and die. When Niwa confronts Escher, Escher stabs him; he is actually Dottore, who wants to see a malevolent heart placed into the puppet, and he reports to Pierro that he has found a puppet who could become a comrade.

508.comment: Inversion of Genesis: Scaramouche Erases Himself
508.content: After learning the truth, Scaramouche shields himself from Nahida's monitoring, asks the Traveler whether the past can be changed, reads the hesitation as a yes, and enters the heart of Irminsul to erase himself so Niwa and his friends can have a better fate. The world forgets him, though the Traveler, who is not recorded in Irminsul, remembers.

509.content: After the erasure, the Traveler finds Inazuma's history changed in detail. A catastrophe in the furnace 400 years ago still occurred; Niwa and another smith purged it at the cost of their lives. The other smith's orphaned son nursed hatred that his descendants inherited, and around 100 years ago the head of that family began killing Raiden Gokaden smiths until the Kamisato and Kaedehara clans killed him. The Kamisato siblings still lead their clan.

510.comment: Inversion of Genesis: Naming the Wanderer
510.content: At the end of the act Nahida says he should have a name, and he asks the Traveler to choose one. He also asks the Traveler to tell the Raiden Gokaden's descendants that he caused their downfall and says he will accept their punishment.

511.content:
Invitation of Windblume (also: Invitation of Windblume event, Ode to Flower and Cloud, Missive of Cloud and Fog, Realm of Fog and Wind, Dream of Wind and Flowers, Peculiar Wonderland): Invitation of Windblume was a Version 1.4 flagship event (19 March to 5 April 2021) celebrating Mondstadt's Windblume Festival. With no commissions to take during the festival, the Traveler and Paimon become assistants to Venti, who is selling love-poem lessons to townsfolk, then trail a string of small festival errands (a missing admirer, a buried "threat", an alchemical flower, two friends locked in a temple). In the finale the Traveler is chosen as the year's Windblume Star and makes the formal flower offering to Barbatos.

The tone is light and community-minded: the event is a catalogue of how ordinary Mondstadters celebrate love and freedom, and it reuses well-known characters in small domestic roles. It is limited-time content and not universally known in-world.

Plot: Part I (Ode to Flower and Cloud). The Traveler and Paimon find that the Guild and townsfolk have no work for them during the festival. Flora, the florist, explains the Windblume Festival as a day of love and freedom and mentions how people dispute what a Windblume is: Flora favours the dandelion, while Quinn, the fruit seller, insists on the Windwheel Aster. Venti, running a poetry class in the plaza, enlists the two as assistants: the Traveler gives advice to townsfolk such as Marvin (a young man whose father opposes his sweetheart), Ellin (who wants to leave flowers for the Acting Grand Master) and Albert (head of Barbara's fan club) while Venti signals approval or caution. Kaeya enrols as a student on condition of homework and a fee of Applebloom Cider.

Part II (Missive of Cloud and Fog). Collecting homework, the Traveler runs an errand for Kaeya's drinking companion Nimrod, who wants help with a gift for his wife. Kaeya's own homework is a single line in the hilichurl tongue. At the Cathedral Barbara receives a note saying something precious to her has been stolen and buried; Rosaria calms her, the Traveler follows the map to a spot near Dawn Winery, defeats Treasure Hoarders, and digs up a box holding a gift of a Windblume from an admirer.

Part III (Realm of Fog and Wind). Sucrose and Timaeus cannot read an old alchemical recipe for a "Windblume", so the Traveler takes it to Albedo's camp on Dragonspine; his version produces a sweet flower and Sucrose claims a larger "Tetratanic Sweet Flower" is a true ancient recipe. Bennett's homework is missing because he and Razor were trapped on opposite sides of a mechanism at the Thousand Winds Temple, guarded by a Ruin Guard; once freed, Bennett recites his poem, which includes a flower name Razor suggested (Wolfhook). At Angel's Share Kaeya explains the Windblume Star: a rare honour, performed alongside the Acting Grand Master.

Part IV (Dream of Wind and Flowers). The Traveler is named Windblume Star, meets Jean in the plaza and offers a Windblume of their choice to Barbatos at the ceremony. Venti then takes them to Stormterror's Lair, where disorderly wind currents must be calmed. Venti closes by telling the Traveler that, in his view, Windblumes do not exist yet are all around, and that each citizen makes their own choice. Dvalin flies overhead at the end and finds the gift prepared for him.

Revelations: Nothing in the event changes the main story. It adds festival lore through dialogue: the Windblume Festival is a festival of love and freedom, the Windblume is a plant nobody can identify, and the Windblume Star is an honour for someone who has made great sacrifices or proved themselves over the festival period. Albedo judges the alchemical recipe, from a forgotten era, to be innovative in its thinking and worth trying.
