Venti's remark that Windblumes "don't exist, yet they are all around us" affirms the old Mondstadt custom of letting everyone pick their own flower.

Characters: Venti, whose role as paid poetry teacher covers for his godhood and prompts Paimon's teasing, plays opposite Kaeya's mischief. Jean appears as Acting Grand Master and ceremony partner; Lisa, Barbara, Rosaria, Bennett, Razor, Sucrose, Timaeus, Albedo, Diluc and Katheryne have small parts. Townsfolk Flora, Quinn, Marvin, Ellin, Albert, Nimrod and Marjorie provide the festival colour.

Consequences: No lasting plot change. The event's weapon, Windblume Ode (a four-star bow), and its refinement material are obtained in the event shop.

Placement: Released in Version 1.4, event window 19 March to 5 April 2021, with the shop open until 12 April. The prerequisite is the Prologue Archon Quest (Song of the Dragon and Freedom) and Adventure Rank 20; the story takes place in Mondstadt at the time of that year's Windblume Festival.

512.comment: Invitation of Windblume: The Windblume Star
512.content: In Dream of Wind and Flowers Kaeya describes the Windblume Star as one of Mondstadt's greatest honours, normally given to someone who has made major sacrifices for the city or proved themselves over the festival. The Star attends the Windblume Ceremony with the Acting Grand Master and makes the people's offering to the Anemo Archon. The Traveler holds the title for that year.

513.comment: Invitation of Windblume: Venti's poetry class
513.content: During the event Venti charges fees (in Mora or alcohol) to teach festival-goers to write love poems. Kaeya enrols with a deal that Venti must grade his homework and be paid in Applebloom Cider; Albert, Ellin, Marvin, Timaeus and Bennett are the other named students. The Traveler and Paimon act as assistants who give advice while Venti signals with hand gestures. The class is a comic device in the event; it is not a recurring institution.

514.comment: Invitation of Windblume: Barbara's buried treasure
514.content: A note appears at the Cathedral claiming something precious to Barbara is buried near Dawn Winery. Barbara fears for her sister Jean; Rosaria stays composed, and when Treasure Hoarders are cleared the box proves to hold a Windblume and a note of admiration. Venti suspects a particular person but does not say.

key: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness
This Ain't Your Daddy's Iridescence Tour
515.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness
515.content:
Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness (also: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life, Rock'n'Roll Tour, This Ain't Your Daddy's Iridescence Tour, Puppy Union, Xtreme Carnival Ensemble, Trillion Trinket Trawl, A Meeting of Melodies, Iridescence Tour Tickets): Dvorak's investors had cancelled his own plan for a music festival about the war, so he joins Itto in holding it with the Arataki Gang instead. Itto secures Watatsumi Island as the venue with Gorou's help, after asking Ms. Hina for advice by letter, and Kokomi supports the plan. The Traveler and Paimon fetch the supplies and music lovers needed to ready the stage over several days. At the party Itto and Paimon sing a new song about a reborn Onikabuto. Meanwhile Heizou finds traces of a wartime pet-rescue organisation, and Kokomi and Gorou privately discuss a secret joint operation with the Yashiro Commission. The Raiden Shogun, who has seen paper notes thrown towards Tenshukaku, attends with Miko.

Plot: First Leg, This Ain't Your Daddy's Iridescence Tour...: an invitation leads the Traveler to Watatsumi Island, where Itto and Dvorak explain their plan and the legend of the dog. Heizou and Shinobu arrive with invitations and melons, and Dvorak gives the Traveler a checklist of tasks to prepare the venue. Glorious Finale, ...It's the Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness!: the venue is ready, friends arrive, Itto and Paimon give a duet, and the final scenes reveal what Kokomi, Gorou, Miko and Ei make of it.

Revelations: Heizou's letters, left at the venue, trace the Puppy Union: a pet-treatment and pet-trade organisation registered with the International Trade Association during the war, whose emblem was a dog in a bamboo hat, which quickly dropped its registration after the war and was funded through at least six layers of transfers. Its hidden backers were the Foreign Trade Association, closely tied to Sangonomiya, and Komore Teahouse, with the Yashiro Commission behind the curtain. Kokomi and Gorou say it was a joint venture of Sangonomiya and the Yashiro Commission that saved some lives, including some on the Shogunate side.

Characters: Itto leads the festival with Shinobu. Dvorak organises the music. Heizou investigates the dog story. Gorou and Kokomi help with the venue. Thoma, Yoimiya, Miko and the Raiden Shogun are guests. Sayu appears as a daruma in the open world, and Itto's gang members Mamoru, Akira and Genta appear in the cutscene.

Consequences: The festival is a success, the dog's story is not resolved, and Dvorak says the feeling matters more than the dog. Itto invites the Traveler to perform next time. The Shogun and Miko discuss avoiding war. Kokomi and Gorou keep their wartime secret.

Placement: Released in Version 4.6 as a Flagship Event and set in Inazuma after the Archon Quest "Ritou Escape Plan". It follows Itto's earlier Almighty Arataki Great and Glorious Drumalong Festival on Amakane Island, and continues the Iridescence Tour that began in Fontaine and reached Liyue during the Lantern Rite. Dvorak was previously in the Version 3.4 event The Exquisite Night Chimes. The war the legend refers to is the conflict between Narukami and Watatsumi Islands that Dvorak calls not long past.

516.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: Dvorak
516.content: A musician from Fontaine and one of the main organisers of the Iridescence Tour, who travels a lot. He appeared in Liyue's Lantern Rite and now helps Itto stage the rock festival on Watatsumi Island. He heard of the rescuing dog in Ritou while the war was on and wrote a song about it, then rewrites it for Itto as a song about an Onikabuto. He tells Paimon the point of rock is hearing your own story in the music.

517.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: Iridescence Tour
517.content: An international music tour covering all seven nations, begun in Fontaine, that Itto adapts into his own rock festival with Dvorak. Xinyan's Lantern Rite concert in Liyue was an earlier stop.

518.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: Puppy Union
518.content: In the wartime story, a pet-treatment and pet-trade organisation registered in Ritou, with a dog in a bamboo hat as its emblem. Heizou traces its funding to Sangonomiya-linked and Komore Teahouse money. Kokomi and Gorou call it a secret joint venture with the Yashiro Commission that saved lives on both sides. Whether a single rescuing dog existed is left open.

519.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: I Got Reincarnated as an Onikabuto
519.content: The song Itto and Paimon sing at the finale. It names a raven, a bake-danuki, a weasel thief, a General Crab and an unagi, then promises rebirth as a beetle. Dvorak says it grew out of the dog story and describes it as soft rock. Heizou, Thoma and Yoimiya each read it differently.

520.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: Ms. Hina
520.content: A popular persona in Yae Publishing House's That's Life advice column. In this event Itto says she told him to ask Gorou for help with the venue, a standing sign of her arrives as a gift from a 'Ramen Buddy' (apparently Miko), and Gorou and Kokomi both feel her face is oddly familiar. The Traveler and Paimon keep quiet. According to the Gorou wiki page, Miko invented the pen name.

key: Khvarena of Good and Evil series
Girdle of the Sands Pari quest
521.content:
Khvarena of Good and Evil (also: Khvarena of Good and Evil series, The Hymn of Tir Yazad, Sign of Apaosha quest, Girdle of the Sands Pari quest): A seven-quest Sumeru world quest series from Version 3.6, set in the northern desert. The Traveler and Paimon meet Sorush, a Pari who believes she must sacrifice herself to remove the corrupting Sign of Apaosha, and help her gather five Great Songs of Khvarena. The Order of Skeptics' leader Nasejuna turns out to be using them, and the Pari's history from the cataclysm is revealed.

The series contrasts two ideas of duty: Sorush's wish to sacrifice herself and the Pari elder Zurvan's insistence that Pari fulfil their own duties. It also reveals that the Skeptics' own history was largely myth, that the Pari and Khaenri'ahn fighters including Dainsleif fought the Abyss together 500 years ago, and that Zurvan met Dainsleif.

Plot: The Traveler finds a buried drum linked to an unfinished Adventurers' Guild commission about the Sign of Apaosha. Katheryne asks them to contact the isolated Order of Skeptics. They meet the Pari Sorush, who names the Traveler her Yasnapati. She must find two other Pari, Mihir and Rashnu, to earn the Twin-Horned Chaplet from the elder Zurvan, then gather five Great Songs for the Rite of Chinvat. Nasejuna betrays them at the last Song, and the group finally cleanses the tree Harvisptokhm.

The Splendorous Sky That Day: In Gavireh Lajavard the Traveler finds a drum and a note, and Katheryne explains the Akademiya wants the Sign of Apaosha, a strange phenomenon possibly tied to the cataclysm, investigated. After a fight with a Skeptic, Sorush appears and takes the party to Nasejuna, who says the Sign reflects the Abyss and corrupts the land, and that the Great Songs of Khvarena must be gathered for the Rite of Chinvat. Zurvan tells Sorush to prove herself by finding Rashnu and Mihir.

Asipattravana Itihasa: Mihir is found trapped by purple mist in Asipattravana Swamp, weakened by polluted energy. The group helps her complete a cleansing pilgrimage. Sorush and Mihir quarrel, but both agree Pari must do their duties themselves.

Awakening's Real Sound: In the Hills of Barsom Nasejuna tells the history of the Barsom and the Kory Drums, made in honour of Barsom's familiar, which has since stopped answering the Skeptics. The Traveler finds the carvings and drums, plays the ritual, and wakes Rashnu, who reveals she threw the drums away because they disturbed her sleep.

As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Zurvan refuses the chaplet because Sorush is not a Bloomguard, until Sorush prays to the Khvarena and grows one. The first Great Song is at Sunyata Lake; Nasejuna points out the rest. At the last Song, in a Khaenri'ahn factory he calls Dahri, Nasejuna reveals he has only pretended to worship Sorush and wants the Songs to release the Abyss's seal. The Traveler defeats him and an Abyss Herald, and he flees.

The Hymn of Tir Yazad: The group places the Songs at Tunigi Hollow and opens the path to the Harvisptokhm. Sorush sees a vision of the cataclysm, then in the Gaokerena collects Spenta Hearts and performs the Rite of Ab-Zohr, making a Flower of Sanctity bloom. The Sign of Apaosha vanishes and the tree regrows.

Revelations: Nasejuna feigned devotion to Sorush to take the Great Songs and release the Abyss's seal. The Skeptics' own histories are largely myth. The Sign of Apaosha is cleansed by the Rite of Ab-Zohr, not by Sorush's sacrifice.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Sorush, Nasejuna, Zurvan, Mihir and Rashnu.

Sorush is a proud Pari who becomes the Traveler's partner and a Bloomguard. Nasejuna is the Skeptics' leader and the series' betrayer. Zurvan is the Pari elder who guards the Songs' secrets. Mihir and Rashnu are Pari: Mihir was stationed in Asipattravana Swamp to suppress corruption, Rashnu was asleep in the Hills of Barsom. Aryadeva, an absent Skeptic elder, is described but not met. Dainsleif and the one-armed sage appear only in vision and testimony.

Consequences: The Sign of Apaosha is gone and the Harvisptokhm has regrown. Nasejuna escapes. Zurvan expects the Traveler to meet Dainsleif soon. Sorush becomes a Bloomguard and gains confidence.

Placement: Released in Version 3.6 and set in the northern desert, in the Girdle of the Sands area. It is independent of the Archon Quest and requires only The Outlander Who Caught the Wind.

522.comment: Khvarena of Good and Evil: Nasejuna's Betrayal
522.content: In Khvarena of Good and Evil, Nasejuna leads the Order of Skeptics and presents himself as a guide to Sorush. At the Khaenri'ahn factory where the last Great Song lies, he reveals he only wanted the Songs to release the Abyss seal. He fights the Traveler with an Abyss Herald and flees.

key: King Deshret and the Three Magi
523.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi
523.content:
King Deshret and the Three Magi (also: Chapter III Act IV, Sumeru Archon Quest Act IV, The Missing Village Keepers, Cry From the Eleazar Hospital, Secret of the Scorching Desert): The fourth act of Sumeru's Archon Quest. Village Keepers, scholars of the desert who tend its villages, are going missing, and rumours say King Deshret has returned. The Traveler, Paimon, Cyno, Candace, Dehya and Alhaitham of the Akademiya trace the kidnappings to an Akademiya-backed plot, find the buried ruins of King Deshret's civilisation, and learn that the sages mean to create a new god.

The act has three quests: The Missing Village Keepers, Cry From the Eleazar Hospital and Secret of the Scorching Desert. It pairs the Traveler with Cyno and Alhaitham in the desert, shows Dehya's standing among the Eremites, and uncovers the Akademiya's own plan for a god to replace Kusanali.

Plot: The Traveler, Cyno, Candace, Dehya and Alhaitham investigate the disappearance of Village Keepers around Aaru Village, where rumours say King Deshret is returning. Radical Eremites confess that a masked "envoy" gave them incense to lure the Keepers out, and Alhaitham, who stayed behind, leads the group to an abandoned Eleazar hospital where one Keeper is found. He reveals that the Akademiya's misinformation drives radicals to act and that it monitors Cyno through the Akasha, so the culprits have gone the opposite way, into the desert.

There Dehya bargains with the Eremite leader Rahman, offering her own arm as a pledge for her friends' honesty. After an earthquake the group falls into buried ruins of King Deshret, where Alhaitham reads the last priest Kasala's runes about Deshret's forbidden knowledge, Rukkhadevata's rescue of his people and Deshret's sacrifice. Rahman accepts the truth and returns the Keepers. The sages' agents Morghi and Judar then confirm that the Akademiya, prompted by Il Dottore, plans to create a new god, and the group resolves to oppose the sages.

Revelations: - The rumour that King Deshret is returning is a misinformation campaign aided by the Akademiya, which nudges radicals into acting while hiding the sages' involvement.
- The sages are working to create a new god after the decline in the Akademiya's breakthroughs; the plot was proposed by Il Dottore.
- The Akasha can predict a user's activity for the day, which let the sages monitor Cyno.
- King Deshret's ruins contain a record, by his last priest Kasala, of the forbidden knowledge that drove his people mad, of Rukkhadevata saving them, and of Deshret's self-sacrifice.
- The dream samsara and "Divine Canned Knowledge" harvested from mad scholars are parts of the sages' project.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon with Cyno, Candace, Dehya and Alhaitham. Rahman, leader of an Eremite band and Dehya's friend, is the main antagonist and then ally. Isak and his grandfather, a Village Keeper, Shani, Razak, Uncle Anpu, Zaki, Delavar, Engur, Sharkan and Makan appear. Morghi and Judar are the sages' agents. Tighnari is mentioned as Cyno's friend, and Dottore is named but absent.

Consequences: The group returns to the village with the Keepers and the captured culprits and begins planning against the sages. The story proceeds to Act V.

Placement: Chapter III, Act IV. Released in Version 3.1. The previous act is Dreams, Emptiness, Deception; the next is Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises. Story order and release order match.

524.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi: Kasala's runes
524.content: Kasala is the last priest of King Deshret, whose runes in the buried ruins tell how Deshret's forbidden knowledge drove his people mad, how Greater Lord Rukkhadevata used her power to give them life, and how Deshret sacrificed himself while Rukkhadevata reverted to a small child. Alhaitham deciphers the text.

525.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi: Rahman and Dehya
525.content: Rahman leads an Eremite band and is Dehya's friend. He refuses to trust the Traveler's group and has Village Keepers hostage until Dehya offers her arm. He stops at the last second, saying that harming her would be like cutting off his own fingers. After the ruins, he apologises and promises to return the Keepers and share supplies.

526.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi: Dar al-Shifa
526.content: The abandoned Eleazar hospital outside Aaru Village, where Shani heard screaming, hides a concealed entrance. The group finds the Keeper Razak, with signs of a hurried withdrawal.

527.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi: The sages' new god plan
527.content: Morghi and Judar tell the group the sages plan to create a new god. Since Rukkhadevata's death the Akademiya's breakthroughs have been rare and in decline; Dottore proposed the new god, and the dream samsara and harvesting of Divine Canned Knowledge from mad scholars are part of the process.

528.content:
Labyrinth Warriors (also: Mystic Onmyou Chamber event, A Tricky Situation, Pushing On, Away With Obsessions and Falsehood, Path of the Taishou): The domain turns out to be a training ground built long ago by the onmyouji Kamuna Harunosuke so samurai, each paired with a shikigami, could hone their skill against monsters. The Fatui Harbinger Tartaglia joins the party inside, pursuing his own interests. By the end Shiki Taishou has full control of the chamber again, clears himself with the Tenryou Commission, and gives the Traveler a small replica of himself, Shiki Koshou. Xinyan was the event's reward character.

Plot: Part 1, A Tricky Situation. Katheryne points the Traveler to a Liyue musician who needs help renewing an expiring temporary travel permit. It is Xinyan, stranded when the Iridescence Tour she came to play in was cancelled. The Tenryou Commission is too stretched to process the permit: Kujou Sara explains that a nameless domain in Araumi is releasing strong monsters, and promises to see to the permit in exchange for help. After guarding the domain entrance, the party finds a moving paper figure, Shiki Taishou, the domain's overseer, who has lost much of his memory. Xinyan wins his trust with a rock song, and they enter together and meet Tartaglia, who joins them.

Part 2, Pushing On. The chamber rearranges itself. Sara contains escaped monsters and later gives Xinyan a long-duration permit and lodging. The Traveler, Paimon and Xinyan then return to Shiki Taishou secretly, rejoin Tartaglia and push deeper, fusing with replicas of Shiki Taishou to recover memory.

Part 3, Away With Obsessions and Falsehood. Shiki Taishou fuses with a powerful replica, recalls the chamber's origin and Harunosuke's last memory, and decides to keep guarding it. Tartaglia reveals his own investigation.

Part 4, Path of the Taishou. The Tenryou Commission accepts the original documentation and finds Shiki Taishou and the chamber innocent. He has restored it to a domain for honing martial skill and invites the party to try it.

Revelations: The Mystic Onmyou Chamber is a purpose-built training domain, not a source of evil. According to Shiki Taishou, Kamuna Harunosuke built it, and made him as its first shikigami, to defend Inazuma from the Abyss during the time of the cataclysm. Shikigami replicas were paired with samurai; they recorded the monsters defeated, and that data was fed back into the domain to create mirror monsters as training targets. Many samurai were wounded and many shikigami lost, and the Shogun's Army had already regained control of the situation, so Harunosuke disbanded the samurai and left, leaving Shiki Taishou to sleep inside.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon are the protagonists. Xinyan, the Liyue rock musician, is the emotional centre of the cast. Kujou Sara represents the Tenryou Commission and appears in the first two parts. Tartaglia, a Fatui Harbinger, fights inside the chamber and pursues his own goals. Shiki Taishou, a polite, self-doubting paper shikigami, is the event's main new character. Katheryne gives the first commission, and Watanabe and Yata Kouki are named Tenryou Commission soldiers who briefly appear.

Consequences: Xinyan receives a long-lasting travel permit and lodging in Inazuma from Kujou Sara and plans to keep visiting Shiki Taishou. The Tenryou Commission accepts Shiki Taishou's account, so the domain is left as a martial training ground that may go dormant if its charm magic runs out. The Traveler keeps Shiki Koshou, a replica that stays in contact with Shiki Taishou but cannot use shikifuda or charm magic outside the chamber. Tartaglia's inquiry about the Wanderer is left open.

Placement: Released in Version 2.2 and requires Adventure Rank 30 and completion of Archon Quest Chapter II Act III, Omnipresence Over Mortals. Inazuma is described as having stabilised by then. Tartaglia refers to the Wanderer as having gone missing with a Gnosis.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. The event was a solo roguelike-style domain. A player split their characters into a Combat party and a Support party, carried chosen shikifuda, and drew Charms in rooms called emplacements. Five trial stages unlocked every three days: The Ominous Demesne, The Brutal Divergence, The Vengeful Wood, The Echoes of Extinction and The Rending Absolution. Aged Tokens, earned in the first four stages, were spent in an event shop and, with enough accumulated, to invite Xinyan (Pyro) as a reward character.

529.content: A domain in Araumi, Inazuma, first described as nameless by the Tenryou Commission. Built during the cataclysm by the onmyouji Kamuna Harunosuke as an ever-changing training ground where samurai fight monsters made of charm magic, which turn to paper charms when defeated. It slept after Harunosuke left, until an unknown power woke its monsters. Its rooms rearrange themselves, and some doors are false.

530.content: Event-exclusive shikigami created by Kamuna Harunosuke to oversee the Mystic Onmyou Chamber. A small paper figure modelled on a samurai in dark armour. He wakes with amnesia, wants to prevent harm, fears he was created for evil, and recovers memories by fusing with replicas of himself. At the end he recalls a purpose of protection and chooses to keep guarding the chamber.

531.content: A replica of Shiki Taishou made as a gift for the Traveler. Shiki Taishou can communicate with it wherever it goes, and the wiki says he can hear and see what it does. Outside the Mystic Onmyou Chamber it cannot use shikifuda or charm magic, but it can still protect its holder.

532.content: In this event Xinyan says she signed up for an Iridescence Tour stop in Inazuma, pitched to her by a roadside recruiter as a famous Fontaine festival, though nobody she knew in Liyue had heard of it. The tour was cancelled when the organisers ran into trouble at sea, leaving her temporary permit about to expire with no sponsor permit, which is the event's starting problem.

533.comment: Labyrinth Warriors: Tartaglia in the Chamber
533.content: Tartaglia followed monster tracks into the domain and enjoys the endless fighting. He tells the party he does not care about allegiance and calls himself a weapon seeking improvement rather than victory. At the end he reveals he is looking for the Wanderer, who has gone missing with a Gnosis, and leaves the matter for the Traveler to find out.

534.content:
Lagenaria Chapter (Baizhu) (also: Lagenaria Chapter, Baizhu's Story Quest, The Heart of Healing): The Lagenaria Chapter is Baizhu's Story Quest (Version 3.6), set in Liyue. In its one act, The Heart of Healing, a boy named Ayu seeks help for his sickly father, and Baizhu discovers that the man is being kept alive and poisoned by the remains of a dead god. The act also shows how Baizhu and Changsheng share life force, and what Baizhu hopes to achieve through immortality.

The act has three quests: The Search for a Physician, The Quest for a Cure and The Formula for a Miracle. It requires Adventure Rank 40, A New Star Approaches, Hu Tao's Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away and the Alatus Chapter's Butterfly's Dream. The Chinese title refers to the hanging gourd, a traditional emblem of physicians.

Plot: A boy named Ayu seeks his sickly father Jialiang at Bubu Pharmacy. Baizhu helps find him near Luhua Pool, where Hu Tao is also present, and recognises god remains inside the man. He secretly keeps Jialiang alive by transferring some of his own life force through Changsheng. They trace a hidden poison to Ayu's home in Qingce Village and to the remains of a dead god named Chi in a tunnel, where Jialiang's wife Jiangli lies unconscious. Baizhu destroys the remains, and an Elixir of Immortality prepared by Qiqi lets Jialiang say goodbye. Baizhu also reveals to the Traveler why he seeks immortality: to be Changsheng's last host.

Revelations: Major for Baizhu's arc: he and Changsheng share a contract that has killed her earlier hosts young, and he seeks immortality to be her last host. A dead god named Chi lies beneath Qingce Village, and its remains are the source of Jialiang's illness and Jiangli's collapse. Hu Tao's grandfather's younger brother was Baizhu's master. All of this was revealed in Version 3.6.

Characters: Baizhu, the Traveler and Paimon, with Changsheng, Qiqi, Hu Tao, Xiao, Herbalist Gui, Ayu, Jialiang and Jiangli.

Baizhu is calm, self-sacrificing and evasive about his own health; Changsheng is dry and protective; Qiqi prepares medicine; Hu Tao is wary but cooperative; Xiao appears briefly and warns Baizhu. Ayu is a worried child and is not described as anything beyond that.

Consequences: Jialiang's family is reunited and spared from the god remains, and Baizhu's secret about Changsheng is shared with the Traveler. Hu Tao and Baizhu remain uneasy but cooperative.

Placement: Release order: 3.6. Story order: after Chapter I of the Archon Quests, Hu Tao's Papilio Charontis Chapter and the Alatus Chapter's Butterfly's Dream.

535.comment: Lagenaria Chapter (Baizhu): The Heart of Healing
535.content: Act I of Baizhu's Story Quest. Baizhu and the Traveler find Ayu's father Jialiang poisoned by the remains of a dead god beneath Qingce Village, destroy them, and use an Elixir of Immortality to give the family time for a goodbye.

536.content:
Lantern Rite (2021) (also: Lantern Rite 2021, Version 1.3 Lantern Rite event, The Origin of the Lanterns, Currents Deep Beneath the Lanterns, Light Upon the Sea, Mingxiao Convergence): The event story is told in three parts, "The Origin of the Lanterns", "Currents Deep Beneath the Lanterns" and "Light Upon the Sea", which together make up the All That Glitters section. In the first the Traveler learns what Lantern Rite is and how Xiao Lanterns are made; in the second a stranger near the lantern materials turns out to be an unrelated, bumbling thief, after help from Xiao and Kaeya's informant; in the third the Traveler and the Wangshu Inn staff bring a miniature festival to Xiao, who still refuses to enter the crowded city. It is a lighthearted event with a gentle character study of Xiao at its core.

Plot: Part I, The Origin of the Lanterns: Verr Goldet of Wangshu Inn explains that Lantern Rite is held on the first full moon of the first month to honour the heroes of the past, and that the lanterns guide them home. She quietly asks the Traveler to try to bring Xiao along. In Liyue Harbor the Traveler meets festival organiser Wang'ya, eats Grilled Tiger Fish at Yi'nian's stall, hears Madame Ping's story of Skybracer, and learns from Jingming how to make a Xiao Lantern.

Part II, Currents Deep Beneath the Lanterns: the Traveler gathers rare Plaustrite (Azurite and Vermillionite), notices a suspicious figure near the lantern materials, reports it to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, clears hilichurls for the Millelith, and with Xiao's help and a tip from Kaeya's informant finds the "plot" to be a clumsy plan to steal the giant floating Plaustrite.

Part III, Light Upon the Sea: Xiao still declines to visit the city, so Verr Goldet, Huai'an and the Traveler build a small stall below Wangshu Inn, serve Almond Tofu and Grilled Tiger Fish and hold a miniature Lantern Rite for him. He eats with them, walks the Traveler partway to the city, and stops at its edge.

Revelations: Madame Ping's account of Skybracer: the giant lantern is shaped after him, a flamboyant adeptus whose antlers were made of the essence of Rex Lapis's power and were Liyue's hardest material. In the fateful battle between gods, mountains began to collapse onto villagers below, so Skybracer had a friend cut off his antlers and used them to prop up the mountain. He fought on until his blood ran out. Mt. Tianheng still stands because of this, and his blood became the Bishui River. She frames this as a story and says the point of Lantern Rite is that people come together instead of staying alone.

Characters: Main: the Traveler and Paimon, Xiao, Kaeya (by his advice and informant), Madame Ping (Skybracer's story), Verr Goldet and Huai'an of Wangshu Inn, Smiley Yanxiao (the inn's chef). Festival staff: Wang'ya (organiser), Jingming (lantern maker), Jiangzhou (Ministry planner), Yi'nian (food stall), Bolai (merchant), the child Changchang, Jiayi and Xinghuo (Ministry and Millelith). Treasure Hoarders: Bei'er and Crafty, plus a lone apprentice thief. Kaeya's informant: Nimrod.

Consequences: The thief is handed to the Millelith and the festival goes ahead. The quest line ends before the lantern's release; the event's Mingxiao Convergence cinematic shows the giant lantern and the Xiao Lanterns rising on Lantern Rite night. Xiao has eaten at a small festival of his own and walks with the Traveler to the city's edge, but never enters it; the closing thread is that he will hear any call for help. The Xiao Market closes after the event with its rewards (a Crown of Insight and the "Celebration: Lantern-Light" namecard).

Placement: Released in Version 1.3 as a Flagship Event and set during the first Lantern Rite after the Traveler arrives in Liyue. It required Adventure Rank 23, the Archon Quest Chapter I Act I (Of the Land Amidst Monoliths) and the first act of Xiao's Story Quest (Alatus Chapter), whose Adventure Rank requirement was lowered for the event. It precedes the 2.4 Lantern Rite (Fleeting Colors in Flight) and the 6.3 Lantern Rite (A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon), both in the same series.

537.content: Liyue's giant lantern, released into the sky on Lantern Rite night as a joint effort of the city's people and the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Its lift comes from a huge floating Plaustrite, the largest in twenty years in 2021, chained at the Xiao Market. The 2021 design honours the adeptus Skybracer, with a stag-like figure whose antlers were a source of pride.

538.content: Madame Ping describes Skybracer as a show-off, proud of his antlers, which were made from Rex Lapis's essence and were the hardest thing in Liyue. During a battle of the gods he gave them up, using the blood-soaked antlers as a wedge to hold up a collapsing Mt. Tianheng, and fought on until his life ran out. The Bishui River is said to be his blood. She tells the tale as a story whose truth the listener may decide.

539.comment: Lantern Rite (2021): Xiao's refusal and the small festival
539.content: Xiao will not attend Lantern Rite, saying he dislikes crowds, and especially not at this time of year. The innkeepers and the Traveler instead set up a small stall with Xiao Lanterns, Almond Tofu and Grilled Tiger Fish below Wangshu Inn. He eats with them without enthusiasm, saying he does not understand human motives, and walks to the city's edge before turning back. He tells the Traveler he hears all calls for help in Liyue.

540.content: A suspicious man lingering near the lantern supplies is feared to be an arsonist. Trails lead via Xinghuo of the Millelith, a symbol left behind that Kaeya identifies as the Treasure Hoarders', and an anonymous letter in the hands of Bei'er and Crafty, to a meeting where the sender turns out to be an apprentice thief who only wanted to steal the giant Plaustrite by cutting its tethers and floating it out to sea. The Millelith arrest him.

541.content:
Leo Minor Chapter (Jean) (also: Leo Minor Chapter, Leo Minor, Master's Day Off, Jean's Story Quest): The Leo Minor Chapter is Jean's Story Quest, available since Version 1.0 and set in Mondstadt. Its single act, Master's Day Off, shows the Acting Grand Master worn down by the city's commissions. The Traveler and the other Knights quietly take the work off her hands and throw her a surprise party.

The act has four quests: When the West Wind Arises, then Margaret's Longing, Charles' Troubles and Sara's Worries (doable in any order), then Master's Day Off. It requires Adventure Rank 34 and the Trifolium Chapter's Act I, True Treasure. Its tone is warm and low-stakes, centred on how much the city relies on Jean.

Plot: **When the West Wind Arises.** In Mondstadt the Traveler and Paimon are asked by Sara of Good Hunter to send Jean a request to clear hilichurls from the road to Springvale, and by Charles of Angel's Share to have her send his quarterly tax records so Elzer can do the accounts. Margaret asks for help finding her cat, Prince. When the Traveler reports all this, Jean faints and Barbara tends to her. Kaeya passes the tasks on to the Traveler instead, saying he would rest easier if the Honorary Knight did them. Amber and Lisa take the original hilichurl and tax jobs.

**The three requests.** The Traveler protects Ernest's delayed delivery convoy from hilichurls, helps Sara with a flood of orders, and finds Prince; Venti explains that the cat took his astral strings, which cats are drawn to when rolled into a ball.

**Master's Day Off.** Barbara says Jean has gone to Windrise, where she always goes when troubled. There Jean admits she wants to be like Vennessa and fears her efforts fall short. An Abyss Mage appears, taunts her and flees; the Traveler helps Jean chase and defeat it. Swan then sends them to Angel's Share, where the Knights hold a surprise party. Jean learns the commissions were all done: Amber cleared the road, Lisa did the tax records and the Traveler recovered Prince and the strings. Kaeya reveals that the Traveler helped organise the party.

Revelations: The city takes Jean's tireless work for granted; Charles admits so, then feels guilty when Paimon points out the pressure on her. Jean's habit of going to the great tree at Windrise when confused is established. Her closing view of herself is as a Dandelion Knight, preserving the future Vennessa hoped for.

Characters: Jean is the focus. The Traveler and Paimon do most of the legwork. Amber, Lisa, Kaeya, Barbara, Venti, Diluc, Charles, Margaret and Sara also appear.

Kaeya delegates cheerfully and is revealed as an organiser of the party alongside the Traveler. Lisa quietly handles the tax returns. Barbara looks after the fainted Jean and knows where she goes to think. Venti appears with Margaret and is the one whose strings Prince took.

Consequences: Nothing in the main story changes. The chapter deepens Jean's characterisation and shows the Traveler as a trusted helper of the Knights.

Placement: Release order: Version 1.0, alongside the other launch Story Quests. It follows the Trifolium Chapter's True Treasure.

542.comment: Leo Minor Chapter (Jean): Master's Day Off
542.content: Master's Day Off is Act I of Jean's Story Quest (Leo Minor Chapter, 1.0). Overwhelmed by Mondstadt's everyday requests, Jean is given a surprise party at Angel's Share by the Knights. She leaves with a clearer sense of her role as a Dandelion Knight carrying on Vennessa's hopes.

543.content:
Lepus Chapter (Amber) (also: Lepus Chapter, Amber's Story Quest, Wind, Courage, and Wings): The Lepus Chapter is Amber's Story Quest (Version 1.0), set in Mondstadt. In its one act, Wind, Courage, and Wings, Amber supervises the Traveler's exam for a gliding licence. The exam is interrupted by a hunt for a criminal named Raptor, whom Amber catches by leaping into a canyon on a wind current.

The act has five quests: Glide With the Wind, License to Glide, Mondstadt Glider, They Call Him Raptor and Outrider Style. It requires Adventure Rank 8 and the Prologue's Act I, The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. "Lepus" is Latin for hare or rabbit; the Chinese and Japanese chapter names mean "little rabbit".

Plot: **Glide With the Wind.** Amber asks how the Traveler's gliding is going and admits she forgot to mention that a licence is required in Mondstadt, though the Traveler has glided without one. She will oversee the exam, since she gave them the glider, and hands them a guidebook. The book she gave at first was her favourite storybook, by mistake.

**License to Glide, Mondstadt Glider, They Call Him Raptor.** After studying the real manual, the Traveler passes the first test and meets Amber at Favonius Cathedral. During the next test the Knight Otto orders the Traveler down and demands the licence, taking them for an accomplice of Raptor, a thief who stole a priceless artifact the Knights had set as bait and then escaped. Amber explains herself and offers to help. Raptor was last seen in Springvale, where one of the sisters had put an Anemo mark on the artifact. They find clues and then hilichurls attacking the merchant Farrah, who says a man dropped from the sky into a hilichurl camp with a heavy object and fled.

Revelations: No world-level revelations. The Knights set bait traps for thieves, hilichurl camps threaten roads near Springvale, and gliding in Mondstadt requires an official licence earned by exam.

Characters: Amber, the Traveler and Paimon. Otto, Raptor and Farrah appear.

Amber is both exam supervisor and partner, enthusiastic and stubborn. Otto is the over-zealous Knight who first threatens arrest; Raptor is the criminal who falls from the sky.

Consequences: The Traveler earns an official Mondstadt gliding licence and an entry in the Wind Gliding Championship. The chapter is also a prerequisite for Razor's Lupus Minor Chapter.

Placement: Release order: 1.0. Story order: early, after the first Prologue act and before Razor's chapter.

544.comment: Lepus Chapter (Amber): Wind, Courage, and Wings
544.content: Act I of Amber's Story Quest. Amber gives the Traveler the real gliding manual (her own favourite storybook was handed over by mistake), supervises their licence exam and catches the thief Raptor by jumping a canyon on the wind.

545.content:
Lepus Miles Chapter (also: Lepus Miles, Lohen's Story Quest, A Knight's Legacy, A Knight's Merit, A Knight's Pursuit, A Knight's Resolve): The Lepus Miles Chapter is Lohen's Story Quest, released in Version 6.6. It has one act, A Knight's Legacy, in three quests, set in Mondstadt. Lohen is due to receive the title Benevolent Knight from the ailing Adorno and command the 5th Company, but he is secretly helping Theodore use Ursa the Drake's flesh to prolong Adorno's life and to chase power himself. Adorno dies, and Lohen is punished.

The three quests are A Knight's Merit, A Knight's Pursuit and A Knight's Resolve. It follows the Archon Quest An Elegy for Faded Moonlight (Song of the Welkin Moon, Act IV) and requires Adventure Rank 40. Its tone mixes dark comedy (Lohen's "friendship fee" and his grisly "patrol methods") with a tragedy about obsession and mortality.

Plot: Kaeya tells the Traveler and Paimon that returning expedition knights are to be honoured, and that Lohen is expected to be named the Benevolent Knight and given command of the 5th Company. Lohen, who does not want either, pays them a "friendship fee" to pose as his friends while he visits Adorno at Dornman Port, and tells Adorno carefully disguised, grisly tales of his "training" and "patrols". Adorno takes him on a day of small kindnesses and a monster patrol, where Diluc says someone has cleaned up the monsters before them. In a test of the Simulation Training Bubble, Type 02, Lohen fights Adorno's memory of Rerir, loses control and is hurt; Adorno reveals that Lohen was a child saved from Eroch's experiments, and Sucrose notes unfamiliar power in him. Lohen and Theodore then pursue Ursa-tainted monsters, Adorno is badly hurt shielding a child, and Lohen swears to confess the next day. Instead Lohen, Theodore and Adorno vanish to a hidden lab, where Theodore has been using Ursa's flesh to make a serum to prolong Adorno's life and Lohen has been helping for his own pursuit of power. Adorno comforts both. Lohen draws the escaped monsters while Varka, Diluc and the Traveler destroy Ursa's remains, and he rejects Ursa's offer of power. Adorno dies; Jean confines Lohen, rescinds his commendation and buries the Benevolent Knight title.

Revelations: - Lohen and Theodore were both children rescued by Adorno from Eroch and the Doctor's experiments.
- Ursa the Drake's flesh remained in a hidden lab, and Theodore restarted its serum experiments to prolong Adorno's life; Lohen joined for his own pursuit of power.
- Monsters carrying Ursa's mark appear near Dornman Port; they attack each other.
- Adorno, already ailing, dies after the lab episode and is buried with the Benevolent Knight title.
- Varka reports that Ursa was once an angel (hearsay), sealed by the first Grand Master Vennessa.

Characters: - **Lohen**: Vice Captain of the 5th Company, titled "Sharpest Arrow", the chapter's protagonist.
- **Adorno**: retiring Captain of the 5th Company, the Benevolent Knight.
- **Theodore**: trainee medic of the 8th Company, treating Adorno.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: pretend friends, witnesses and fighters.
- **Varka, Diluc, Kaeya, Sucrose, Jean**: the Grand Master, a former Cavalry Captain, the current Cavalry Captain, a researcher working on the bubble, and the Acting Grand Master who sets the punishments.

Consequences: Ursa's flesh at the site is destroyed. Adorno has died by the closing scene. Lohen is placed in solitary confinement, his commendation is rescinded, he is denied promotion, and the Benevolent Knight title is buried with Adorno.

Placement: Released in Version 6.6 ("Luna VII"). It requires An Elegy for Faded Moonlight, so it happens after the Nod-Krai expedition returns to Mondstadt. Story order and release order match. The chapter has no further acts as of 7.1.

546.content: The honorary title held by Adorno, earned when he rescued kidnapped children from Eroch's experiments. He wanted Lohen to inherit it with the 5th Company captaincy, and had once planned to leave the title to Theodore. After Adorno's death, Jean has the title buried with him.

547.comment: Lepus Miles Chapter: Ursa's Flesh and Serum
547.content: A serum drawn from the preserved flesh of Ursa the Drake. Eroch and a Doctor Segment first made it, Eroch's followers injected it and went mad, and Theodore later restarted production to prolong Adorno's life. Monsters carrying it fight one another and are far stronger than normal. Lohen takes a vial into the final fight as bait.

548.comment: Lepus Miles Chapter: Simulation Training Bubble: Type 02
548.content: A memory-recreating magic bubble based on Alice's work and used to welcome the expeditionary force, now being tested by the 10th Company as a safe combat training aid. It recreates enemies from knights' memories.

549.comment: Lepus Miles Chapter: Lohen's Friendship Fee
549.content: Mora that Lohen pays the Traveler and Paimon to pose as his friends when he visits Adorno. Paimon takes the payment readily. Lohen says he receives a special-missions allowance and has little use for it.

550.content:
Lightkeepers' Oath (also: Lightkeepers' Oath world quest, Oath Lantern quest): A Version 6.0 world quest on Paha Isle and Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. If the active character is a Lightkeeper (Flins or Illuga), the Traveler can read the eight "Oath Lanterns" that lie abandoned around the islands. Each lantern has a line of the Lightkeepers' oath carved around its base, and each brings up the ghost of its former bearer. At the end, Flins explains what the oath is and what a masterless lantern means.

The quest has no fight and almost no dialogue until its last scene. Its worth is thematic: it shows how the Lightkeepers treat their oath and their lanterns, and how seriously Flins takes the memory of those who fell. Without a Lightkeeper active, a lantern is only "a dim lantern", described as the signature equipment of a Lightkeeper.

Plot: With Flins or Illuga in the party, the Traveler touches an Oath Lantern and sees a line of the oath carved around its base. A ghost of a Lightkeeper appears. After the fourth lantern the rest are marked on the map. When all eight are read, Paimon suggests asking someone who knows the Lightkeepers, and they go to the Final Night Cemetery to find Flins.

Each lantern's inscription is one line of the oath. Together they run roughly: a vision of waves on the shore and a night sky devoured by silence; a declaration that whoever keeps the flame burning need not descend into that darkness; the Lightkeepers as those who shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snowy plains; a vow to use their bones and blood as fuel and make life greater than death; and lines about the winds awakening and leaves whirling, pale cheeks and burning eyes, freeing the heart from dreams of the living, and parting the snow-curtain of the sky to blast winter winds across the wasteland. The first three lanterns bring up female Lightkeeper ghosts and the later five male ghosts.

The third lantern has a hidden compartment with a yellowed note, written by a self-described humble Ratnik. The writer expects soon to be unable to speak of the lamp and asks whoever finds it to return it to the Lightkeepers.

At the cemetery, Flins greets the Traveler warmly "amidst the graves". The Traveler describes the lantern and its inscription. Flins identifies it as the oath everyone who joins the Lightkeepers swears. Each Lightkeeper normally carries a lantern of their own and gives up its care only when there is no other choice, so a masterless lantern marks a tragedy and fills him with sorrow. They knew this fate from the moment they swore. The one thing the living can still do is remember their oaths, and that was the dead's dearest wish: to bear and defend lanterns alight with eternal hope.

Revelations: The quest reveals the content of the Lightkeepers' oath and that every Lightkeeper carries a lantern that stays with them for life. Flins explains the oath in his own words and shows that the order remembers its dead through their oaths.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, with Flins as the one who explains. Illuga can be the active character instead of Flins. The lantern ghosts are unnamed.

Flins speaks in his usual courteous, slightly formal manner, but is solemn rather than playful. He treats the lanterns as memorials even though he names none of the dead.

Consequences: Completing the quest gives the rewards and changes nothing else in the world. It is characterisation and world texture rather than a plot step.

Placement: Introduced in Version 6.0 (Luna I), at the start of the Nod-Krai series. The wiki lists no prerequisite quest, only access to Nod-Krai and a Lightkeeper character as the active character, which means Flins or Illuga. The oath is quoted again in the Nightingale's Song world quests (6.3), so the quest can be read before or after them without conflict.

551.content: The Lightkeepers' oath is a set of lines every Lightkeeper swears on joining. In the Lightkeepers' Oath quest eight abandoned lanterns each carry a line, and Flins identifies "The winds awaken, the leaves whirl round" as part of the oath. Lightkeepers normally carry their own lantern and give up its care only when forced to. A masterless lantern marks a misfortune, and remembering the oaths of those who fell is all that can still be done for them.

key: Lost in a Foreign Land: Seeking
Fatui hideout in the Chasm quest
552.content:
Lost in a Foreign Land (also: Lost in a Foreign Land: Seeking, Katarina quest, Fatui hideout in the Chasm quest): A short Version 2.6 series in the Chasm's Underground Mines. The Traveler meets Katarina Snezhevna, a Fatui mage cut off from her supply line, and looks for her missing teammate Nikolay over three days.

The series is started by defeating a Fatui Electro Cicin Mage near the Glowing Narrows waypoint. It has two quests, Lost in a Foreign Land (day one) and Lost in a Foreign Land: Seeking (days two and three), and later steps wait for the daily reset.

Plot: Katarina invites the Traveler to her hideout and offers Fire-Water. She says everything the Fatui does prepares for a final battle against a common enemy and an inescapable long night. She later asks the Traveler to find Nikolay; the Traveler finds his insignia and diary scraps. On the last day Katarina has vanished, leaving a letter next to a Shadowy Husk.

On day one Katarina gives only her name, fights Floating Fungi alongside the Traveler and says to visit her hideout. She is out of black tea, sugar and milk, so she serves Fire-Water. She has not heard of the Traveler because her information comes through the Fatui supply line, which Paimon notes must have been cut off long ago. Awkwardly, she tells them to leave, then asks them to return. On day two she asks them to find Nikolay, who lured enemies away from the team. The Traveler finds his insignia and diary fragments describing a secret chamber with two exits and a swordsman in black, and a tunnel sealed by fallen rocks. Katarina says Nikolay would not flee; she hopes he fought to the end. If he is alive she would punish him as a deserter, and if dead she will be proud of him, in the spirit of the Fatui saying "If not us, then who."

Revelations: No world-shaking revelation. It shows that some Fatui members are cut off from news and loyal to ideals of sacrifice, and hints at the Fatui's wider goal of facing a common enemy.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Katarina Snezhevna, and by report Nikolay and Lyudochka.

Katarina is stern, proud and reticent about her mission. Nikolay is her missing teammate. Lyudochka, a friend from the House of the Hearth, appears only in her recollection.

Consequences: No lasting change to the world. Katarina's hideout is left empty and her fate is implied but not shown.

Placement: Released in Version 2.6 alongside the Chasm: Underground Mines content, in the same area as The Chasm Delvers. It is a small side story.

553.content:
Lost in the Snow (also: Dragonspine Joel quest, Joel's father quest): Joel is told to wait at the camp by a Knight of Favonius. The quest is a short search that ends without a reunion; the notes show that the father intended to keep his promise to bring Joel to see the snow. It leads on to the quest Snowy Silhouette: Hope and, later, links to the Version 2.3 event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms, where the father is found.

Plot: Joel, a child waiting at the camp, explains that his father promised to take him to see the snow. When the agreed time passed, Joel came to Dragonspine alone, only to be told by a Knight that his father had gone up toward the summit. The Knight would not let him follow. Joel asks the Traveler to look for him, and recalls that his father meant to follow the Snow-Covered Path first, then visit the outskirts of the Entombed City, then try for the summit.

The first note, at a campsite on the Snow-Covered Path, is cheerful. The father says the weather and supplies are good, and mentions finding a book from the series "The Boar Princess" that Joel must have slipped into his bag; he wonders if it is bringing him luck. The second note, found under snow that has to be melted with Pyro, is from a western-slope campsite, where he decides to try for the summit and says he will turn back if anything goes wrong. The third, in a cave near the summit, is scribbled: a snowstorm came suddenly, he lost half of his supplies, and rocks collapsed to seal the entrance. He plans to climb down a cliff and jump the rest into deep snow, adds that supplies will last only a few days, repeats his promise to Joel, and asks anyone who finds the note to put food in a bowl for the foxes that kept him company.

The group feed the foxes, which stay hidden, and report to Joel. Whatever the Traveler says, Joel refuses to believe the worst. He insists his father is a great adventurer who must have reached safety, is resting, or has made camp, and he decides to keep waiting at the camp.

Revelations: The father's three notes are the quest's entire evidence. The cheerful tone of the first gives way to danger in the third, and nothing in them says whether his climb down succeeded.

Epilogue: Later content (the Version 2.3 event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms) shows Joel's father, Joserf, found alive but with memory loss that leaves him recalling only Joel and Joel's mother. This quest itself never mentions that.

Characters: Joel, a child at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp, who trusts that his father is safe; the Traveler and Paimon; and an unnamed Knight of Favonius, who told Joel to stay. The father appears only through his notes.

Consequences: Joel stays at the camp to wait. The Traveler receives rewards of 300 Adventure EXP, 40 Primogems, 2 Hero's Wit, 4 Mystic Enhancement Ore and 30,000 Mora, plus 100 reputation with Mondstadt (game rewards, not in-world).

Placement: Added in Version 1.2, when Dragonspine became accessible. It is an optional Dragonspine world quest and not part of the Archon Quests. Later, the Version 2.3 event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms lists it as a prerequisite and resolves Joel's story.

554.comment: Lost in the Snow: Joel's father's notes
554.content: Joel's father left a trail of campsite notes on Dragonspine: cheerful ones at the Snow-Covered Path and the western slope, then a scribbled one in a cave near the summit, written after a snowstorm and a rockfall trapped him. He planned to climb down the cliff and jump into deep snow, and asked whoever read the note to feed the foxes that had kept him company.

key: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm
Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm World Quest series
555.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm
555.content:
Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm (also: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm World Quest series, Bona's adventure, Jade of Return quests): Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm is a four-act Natlan world quest series added in version 5.2. The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One enter the forbidden ruined city of Ochkanatlan to find the "Jade of Return", a treasure sought by countless adventurers. They are joined by an adventurer named Bona and a small green guide, Cocouik, and are hunted by a violent dragon.

The route leads from the city streets through the Core of Chu'ulel and an Altar of Primal Flame up to the sky-ship called the Tonatiuh. The legend of the Jade of Return turns out to be bait, the dragon is a corrupted former ruler, and what the party recovers is a second Golden Entreaty, one of the tokens needed to lift the Little One's curse.

Plot: **Act I, City Buried By Ash (Vaulting the Wall of Morning Mist).** Following a violent dragon, the party reaches Ochkanatlan, a ruin the Saurian Relics Association treats as forbidden. An explosion in the Vucub Caquix Tower drops them into the lower city. They find the notes of a nameless adventurer who came for the Jade of Return, meet a mysterious adventurer, and fight their way through Ashflow Street with the help of a small green guide whose rings of light can suppress Abyssal Blight. The dragon is shot down and driven off.

**Act II, A Dream of Gazing Upon the Distant Sky.** With Bona and Cocouik, the party looks for the Altar of Primal Flame so they can reach the Tonatiuh. Cocouik refuses to enter a ruin because of the Abyssal corruption inside. Below, the Traveler cleanses the Core of Chu'ulel and finds a second chunk of Pyrophosphorite wrapped in more of the nameless adventurer's notes. Offering both chunks on the Altar sends the group flying up through the clouds, and they land at the Tonatiuh.

**Act III, The Tonatiuh Quivers.** On the Tonatiuh the Traveler finds a stronger, flame-infused Pyrophosphorite that the Little One can handle, reunites with Bona and uses Firestones to break the rock holding the Jade of Return. The treasure is a Golden Entreaty. Bona then behaves oddly, the dragon snatches the Entreaty, and the group follows it. Cocouik helps the Traveler bring the dragon down, and a voice inside identifies itself as Och-Kan, former ruler of Ochkanatlan, asking for help against the corruption in his soul.

**Epilogue, The Chosen One's Promise.** The Traveler returns to the Tonatiuh and finds the Little One alive. Bona is nowhere to be seen. Paimon and the Traveler decide to keep the Golden Entreaty and carry it to the volcano.

Revelations: - The "evil dragon" that attacks the party in Ochkanatlan is Och-Kan, the former ruler of the city, whose soul was corrupted by poison and who was turned into a dragon.
- The Jade of Return is a Golden Entreaty. Och-Kan says it can cleanse Natlan's Abyssal filth but at a cost, and that he and the Little One both bear the Flamelord's Blessing. Two Golden Entreaties must be brought to the sacred mountain to remove that blessing.
- The legend of the Jade of Return was fabricated by Kukulkan, as bait for a trap.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, the Little One (a young Tepetlisaurus companion), Bona (a self-described adventurer of the Flower-Feather Clan), Cocouik (a small green guide), Och-Kan (the corrupted dragon), and Kukulkan (in memory scenes). Taika, Copan, Titu and Legba appear only in Och-Kan's memories.

Consequences: The party now holds a second Golden Entreaty and plans to take it to the volcano to help lift the Little One's curse. The unresolved question of Bona's nature remains, as does the matter of Kukulkan's plan.

Placement: Released in version 5.2. The series page lists Between Pledge and Forgettance as the previous series and Path to the Flaming Peaks as the next. The dialogue changes depending on whether Between Pledge and Forgettance has been finished.

556.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Bona
556.content: Bona describes herself as an adventurer of the Flower-Feather Clan who is chasing the Jade of Return. She is cheerful, impulsive and eager to prove herself, quick to claim she can read Cocouik's chirps and then admit she is guessing. According to Och-Kan's memories she is the daughter of Taika, who led an earlier expedition up the Tonatiuh. She disappears before the series ends and her nature is not explained.

557.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Cocouik
557.content: Cocouik ("Coco" to Paimon) is a small green dragonspirit-like guide. Bona's notes say she woke it from the heart of the machine using Pyrophosphorite and named it after turquoise. It leads the party to the Altar of Primal Flame, and its rings of light can suppress Abyssal Blight. It is frightened of corrupted ruins. Och-Kan later retains memories of his time as Cocouik.

keysecondary: Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash
558.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Och-Kan, the dragon of Ochkanatlan
558.content: Och-Kan appears first as the "evil dragon", the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, then speaks as the former ruler of Ochkanatlan. He says his soul was poisoned and turned into a dragon. Tribal legend says he oppressed his people to build the Tonatiuh, which attracted the Abyss; Bona notes that storytellers tell different tales about him. He refuses Kukulkan's plan.

559.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Jade of Return
559.content: The "Jade of Return" is a legendary treasure that countless adventurers have sought in Ochkanatlan. In the series it is found sealed in a rock on the Tonatiuh and is a Golden Entreaty. Och-Kan's memories show the legend was invented by Kukulkan to lure people into a trap.

560.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Altar of Primal Flame and the Tonatiuh route
560.content: The Altar of Primal Flame is a mechanism that sends travelers up to the Tonatiuh when offered Pyrophosphorite; the party offers two chunks to be safe. The Tonatiuh, a sky-borne vessel, looks to Paimon like a ball of yarn or snakes. Firestones, a variant of Pyrophosphorite found on the Tonatiuh, activate its own altar.

key: The Warm Rhythm of the Streets
The Reason We Are Gathered Here
561.content:
Lotos Somno Chapter (also: Lotos Somno, Nilou's Story Quest, To the Wise, The Warm Rhythm of the Streets, Show Canceled, The Reason We Are Gathered Here): The Lotos Somno Chapter is Nilou's Story Quest, released in Version 3.1, and as of 7.1 it has one act, To the Wise. After the Sabzeruz Festival, the Sumeru Akademiya orders the Zubayr Theater shut down and its stage demolished within 30 days. Nilou, backed by the troupe and the Traveler, stands up in a formal debate against the Akademiya's representative Sharif, and the confrontation turns into a quiet first step toward reconciliation between Sharif and his estranged daughter Inayah.

The act has three quests: The Warm Rhythm of the Streets, Show Canceled and The Reason We Are Gathered Here. It is a character piece about belonging and about how Sumeru's scholarly institutions treat art, not an adventure with combat set-pieces; the only fight is a brief rescue of Inayah from tigers outside the city. Nilou is shown nervous, kind and stubborn, and she is the one who has to carry the argument.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon find Nilou in the Grand Bazaar with more donated goods than she can carry. They help her haul them to the Zubayr Theater, with help from the porter Farhad, and the troupe starts a small party celebrating the festival's success. Sharif interrupts and demands to speak to the manager, Sheikh Zubayr, saying the Akademiya has decided to shut the theater down and demolish its stage in 30 days because of repeated rule violations. Zubayr objects that nobody communicated with him properly. Nilou explains that the Akademiya judges the theater's shows not intellectual enough. Inayah, a troupe member who ran away from home, argues with Sharif and addresses him as father. The Traveler suggests settling the matter by debate, a normal way of resolving disputes in the Akademiya, and persuades a reluctant Nilou to represent the theater.

The troupe and locals talk about what the theater means to them. Inayah slips away, and Nilou guesses she blames herself for bringing Sharif to the theater. They search near an old camp outside the city and rescue Inayah from a pack of Rishboland tigers. Nilou convinces her the fault is not hers, and Inayah agrees to help at the debate. The Traveler points out what Nilou's case is missing: the theater is not only a stage but a place of belonging for the people there now and in future.

Two days later the debate is held, with Safwan of the Akademiya as adjudicator. The first topic, whether the theater is useful, ends inconclusive. On the second, Nilou argues that Zubayr met all legal and documentary requirements for running a theater, and Safwan rules that threatening demolition before the Akademiya's discussions was premature. Sharif then notes that the Akademiya could instead revoke the troupe's performance license, which catches Nilou off guard, and Safwan agrees. Nilou argues that the theater is a place of belonging, but Sharif replies that such bonds are formed through work, much as scholars share knowledge and then move on to other projects. Inayah steps onto the stage and tells her father he is too wrapped up in his own world to understand relationships. The audience sides with her, and Sharif says, almost to himself, that it is a relief, and leaves, with Safwan following. The debate ends without a clear verdict.

Revelations: - The Akademiya's objection is that the theater's shows are not intellectual enough, and its tools are rule compliance and licensing.
- Inayah is Sharif's daughter; she did not get along with her parents and has lived at the theater.

Characters: - **Nilou**: dancer of the Zubayr Theater, the act's protagonist, who must speak for the troupe.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: advisers who propose the debate.
- **Sharif**: Akademiya official who issues the demolition order and argues the Akademiya's side. He is Inayah's father.
- **Inayah**: young troupe member, Sharif's daughter, estranged from her parents.
- **Sheikh Zubayr**: theater manager.
- **Safwan**: Akademiya scholar who adjudicates the debate.
- **Farhad**: a porter who helps carry the goods.

Consequences: The demolition is not carried out, Sharif suspends himself, and Inayah joins the troupe formally. The theater keeps its stage; the personal rift between Sharif and Inayah has only begun to heal.

Placement: Released in Version 3.1 and unlocked after Chapter III Act II of the Archon Quest and Adventure Rank 40. Story order and release order match. Only Act I exists as of 7.1.

562.comment: Lotos Somno Chapter: Zubayr Theater Dispute
562.content: After the Sabzeruz Festival, the Akademiya official Sharif orders the Zubayr Theater closed and its stage demolished within 30 days for ignoring Akademiya rules. Nilou argues the theater's case in a formal debate with Safwan as adjudicator. The demolition threat is ruled premature, and the debate ends without a clear winner.

563.comment: Lotos Somno Chapter: Sharif and Inayah
563.content: Sharif is an Akademiya official and Inayah's father. Inayah ran away from her parents and joined the Zubayr Theater. After the debate Sharif suspends himself and gives her a framed embroidery piece he made himself. Nilou expects reconciliation to be slow.

564.content:
Lupus Aureus Chapter (Cyno) (also: Lupus Aureus Chapter, Lupus Aureus, Cyno's Story Quest, Sands of Solitude, Oathkeeper, Golden Wolf Chapter): Cyno's Story Quest, in two acts. In Sands of Solitude (3.1) the Traveler helps the General Mahamatra track a ring smuggling Canned Knowledge out of the Akademiya, and learns it was part of a wider, hidden effort connected to a banned ruin, the Court of Desolation. In Oathkeeper (4.6) a blackmail letter to Cyno's old teacher leads back to the Temple of Silence, which wants the Hermanubis power Cyno carries.

Act I has three quests: Suspicious Smuggling Case, Chain of Interests and All Returns to Silence. Act II has five: The Mysterious Letter, After Repose, Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands, Sage of Sages and The Dead Past is the Living Present. Cyno's friends Tighnari and Collei appear in both acts; the Traveler is a close helper, not a bystander.

Plot: Act I: Nabil, a Matra, asks the Traveler for help with smuggled Canned Knowledge. Cyno is already investigating. Following Dori's tip about an auction in the desert, the group fights off hired Eremites and scorpions, presses a smuggler in Aaru Village, and traces the Matra seal on a shipment to Taj Radkani, Cyno's former superior. At the Court of Desolation Taj's resistance ends, the ruin collapses on him, and Cyno quietly rounds up the ring.

Act II: Cyno's old teacher Cyrus receives a blackmail letter. Its pattern leads to the Temple of Silence. The Temple's leader Bamoun wants Cyno's Ba Fragment transferred to his grandson Sethos. Cyno proposes a winner-take-all Rite of Duels, wins, and gives Sethos the leadership.

Act I - Sands of Solitude. Nabil tells the Traveler that smuggled Canned Knowledge is circulating. Cyno has already found the smugglers, and Dori's tip reveals the ring is really seeking the banned Court of Desolation. Hired Eremites and scorpions try to stop them, a tracker leads to a Kshahrewar researcher, and a Matra seal on a shipment points to Cyno's former superior Taj Radkani. At the Court, Taj shows he joined the ring to expose it, and the ruin collapses on him. Cyno then quietly arrests the rest.

Act II - Oathkeeper. Cyrus, Cyno's old teacher, is blackmailed. The paper's emblem is from the Temple of Silence, and Cyrus and Cyno head into the desert. At the Temple, Bamoun tells how Cyno and Sethos were given Ba Fragments of Hermanubis and demands Cyno's be handed to Sethos. Cyno proposes a Rite of Duels, wins, absorbs the second fragment, and appoints Sethos leader after Bamoun dies. Cyno shows the Traveler his hideaway at the Sanctuary of Surasthana.

Revelations: Cyno carries a Ba Fragment of Hermanubis, implanted in him as a child by the Temple of Silence.

The Canned Knowledge smuggling was a front for research into the banned Court of Desolation, aided by insiders in the Akademiya, and Taj Radkani joined it deliberately to expose it. The Temple of Silence is a surviving secret desert order whose leader, Bamoun, held two Ba Fragments of Hermanubis.

Characters: Cyno, the Traveler and Paimon.

Act I: Nabil, the Matra Taj Radkani, Dori, the smugglers Amainu, Amenzu and Bahari, the Eremite Jhuba, Tighnari and Collei. Act II: Cyrus, Aarav, Urraca, Sethos, Bamoun, Tighnari, Collei, Kaveh, Alhaitham, Naphis, Candace, Dehya, Faruzan and Lisa (by photographs).

Consequences: The smuggling ring is dismantled, with its mercenaries and Akademiya researchers arrested, and Taj Radkani dies in the Court of Desolation. In Oathkeeper Cyno absorbs the second Ba Fragment, Sethos leads the Temple of Silence, and Bamoun dies.

Placement: Act I unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after King Deshret and the Three Magi (Chapter III Act IV) and was released in 3.1 on 2022-09-28. Act II unlocks after Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises (Chapter III Act V) and was released in 4.6 on 2024-04-24, so it takes place after Sumeru's Archon Quest even though it was released much later.

565.comment: Lupus Aureus Chapter (Cyno): Court of Desolation
565.content: A banned desert ruin said to let people see beyond life and death and, in legend, to revive the dead. The Akademiya forbids research on it. A smuggling ring used a Canned Knowledge trade to find people interested in it. It collapsed into quicksand at the end of Sands of Solitude.

566.content: Cyno's former superior in the Matra, injured in an earlier mission and removed from live work but still respected. After his only son Murtada died following a prison term for investigating the Court of Desolation, Taj joined the smuggling ring in secret to expose it, and died in the Court's collapse.

567.comment: Lupus Aureus Chapter (Cyno): Temple of Silence
567.content: A secret desert order tied to Hermanubis, whose influence was fading without its guide. Its leader Bamoun held two Ba Fragments and had them implanted in two children, one of whom was Cyno. After the Rite of Duels in Oathkeeper, Cyno holds both and Sethos leads the order.

key: To Those Who Embark on the Expedition
568.content:
Lupus Majoris Chapter (also: Lupus Majoris, Varka's Story Quest, To Those Who Embark on the Expedition): The act has three quests: "Triumphant Warrior", "Fated Warrior" and "Lonely Warrior". It is split between Mondstadt, where letters from Varka carry the plot, and Nod-Krai, where Varka gathers the Wolf Spirit fragments and fights Roland. It closes with Varka returning to Windrise among his friends.

Plot: Lohen brings Varka's letters from Nod-Krai to Mondstadt, and the Traveler learns from Boreas at Wolvendom that Roland, the Abyss's replacement for Rerir, has corrupted the remains of Andrius. Dvalin carries the Traveler to Nod-Krai. There Varka and his knights gather Boreas's Wolf Spirit fragments, and Roland swallows Varka in a duel. Inside the wolf Varka draws on the longings of Rostam, Ravenwood and the Wandering Knight, calls Andrius back to the Ley Lines and fights his way out, to wake at Windrise.

Revelations: - The Nod-Krai expedition was partly meant to recover Boreas's Wolf Spirit fragments scattered around Nod-Krai.
- Roland, not Rerir, is the leader of the Abyssal wolf force, installed after Rerir's removal, and he has corrupted Andrius's remains.
- Boreas is a fragment of Andrius's soul and the Knight of Boreas serves as intermediary between the wolf and Mondstadt; very few know Andrius came from Nod-Krai.
- Varka's letters were meant to anchor him; he stored Boreas's soul in himself, not in his sword.

Characters: Varka (lead), the Traveler and Paimon, Venti, Lohen, Jean, Lisa, Sucrose, Mika, Noelle, Eula and Amber (letters), Kaeya, Rosaria, Diluc, Razor, Boreas/Andrius, Dvalin, Winfried, Ekbert, Leifhelm, Jahoda, Ineffa, Flins, Albedo, Durin, Roland, Vedrfolnir.

Consequences: Andrius chooses to return to the Ley Lines, the Abyssal Roland dissipates, and Varka returns alive to Windrise. Diluc's refusal to rejoin the Knights stands.

Placement: Released in Version 6.4 (Luna V) with an event period from 2026-02-25 to 2026-03-17; the chapter stays available. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and Act VIII of Song of the Welkin Moon, "True Moon" (quick start at Adventure Rank 28 during the event).

569.comment: Lupus Majoris Chapter: Wolf Spirit Fragments
569.content: Boreas's power and thoughts, divided into fragments across Nod-Krai. The expedition's goal was to collect them; only two remained when the Traveler arrived. Andrius gives one of his own in Razor's claymore.

570.comment: Lupus Majoris Chapter: Roland in the Wolf
570.content: In the quest Roland is the Abyss's replacement for Rerir and an imperfect copy of the historical Roland. He sees Varka as a lost soul and offers him time to rest before the duel, which Varka refuses. Inside the wolf Varka calls out to Andrius, who returns to the Ley Lines.

571.content: A set of letters (ten, per the wiki) sent from Nod-Krai through Lohen, including ones for Venti, Jean, Lisa, Sucrose, Mika, Noelle, Eula, Amber, Kaeya, Rosaria and Diluc, and a further one taken to Wolvendom. They announce the expedition's end and, in Varka's plan, anchor him to Mondstadt.

572.content:
Lupus Minor Chapter (Razor) (also: Lupus Minor Chapter, Lupus Minor, The Meaning of Lupical, Razor's Story Quest): The Lupus Minor Chapter is Razor's Story Quest (Version 1.0), set in Wolvendom, Mondstadt. In its one act, The Meaning of Lupical, the Traveler meets the boy raised among wolves, and with Amber helps clear his pack of blame for attacks on villages. Boreas, the Wolf of the North, tells Razor he is human, which leaves Razor questioning his identity.

The act has four quests: Wolves' Territory, Another Day as an Outrider!, Ravaged by Wolves and Fate's Chosen Lupical. It requires Adventure Rank 21, the Prologue's Song of the Dragon and Freedom and Amber's Wind, Courage, and Wings. Its tone mixes comedy (Razor first takes the Traveler's friend for Klee and later jokingly forgets Amber's name) with a serious question about belonging.

Plot: **Wolves' Territory.** In Wolvendom the Traveler and Paimon are attacked by slimes, one of which grows large. A boy, Razor, cuts it back down to size and the slimes flee. He had been hunting for his wolf pack and asks the Traveler to find raw meat, which falls short of what the pack needs. He mentions a "red burny girl" who often does the same; the Traveler thinks of Amber, but he means Klee. Back at Mondstadt's gate, Amber has not heard of Razor but is investigating reports of wolf attacks at Drunkard Gorge and Springvale. They find different kinds of fur and a stray Wolfhook seed, indicating the attackers came from Wolvendom, and the younger villagers refuse to wait quietly.

**Ravaged by Wolves.** Amber meets Razor in the wilderness. He smells blood and shows an injured wolf; his poor social skills at first make Amber suspect his pack. Razor says another pack from outside, led by a black wolf, has been attacking the villages.

Revelations: Boreas, the Wolf of the North, is angered by disturbances and tests Razor's worth. An outside wolf pack, not Razor's, is blamed for the attacks. In Boreas's view Razor is human, not wolf, and cannot take part in the wolves' fight.

Characters: Razor, Amber, the Traveler and Paimon; Boreas the Wolf of the North; Springvale villagers. Klee is mentioned by Razor.

Razor is protective of his wolf pack and socially awkward, which at first makes Amber suspect him. Amber tries to keep the villagers calm while she investigates.

Consequences: Razor stays in Wolvendom, uncertain about his identity, and the attacks are attributed to an outside pack. Boreas also allows the Traveler to spar with him afterwards.

Placement: Release order: 1.0. Story order: after Song of the Dragon and Freedom and Amber's Lepus Chapter.

573.comment: Lupus Minor Chapter (Razor): The Meaning of Lupical
573.content: Act I of Razor's Story Quest. The Traveler and Amber help Razor show that an outside wolf pack, not his own, attacks Springvale. Boreas tests Razor, vows the outsiders will pay, and reminds Razor he is human, leaving him thinking about who he is.

574.content:
Mantichora Chapter (Dehya) (also: Mantichora Chapter, Mantichora, Dehya's Story Quest, Lionsblood, Shade Upon Red Silk, Annals of the Scarlet Sands, Sincerity's Facade): Dehya's Story Quest. The mercenary known as the Flame-Mane suspects the Eremite brigade Dakan Al-Ahmar, led by her adoptive father Kusayla, of massacring caravans. With the Traveler and her employer's daughter Dunyarzad, she learns that Kusayla is dead, that the brigade is acting to avenge itself on its own paymasters, and that Kusayla secretly left her a letter about her origins.

The chapter has one act, Lionsblood, of three quests: Shade Upon Red Silk, Annals of the Scarlet Sands and Sincerity's Facade. It is the story of a brigade's last act and of Dehya choosing to honour the man who raised her without excusing what his men did.

Plot: Dehya admits to the Traveler and Paimon that Dakan Al-Ahmar has been robbing and killing travellers. Tracing goods found in a looted caravan back to Dunyarzad's father Shahzaman, she learns that Kusayla died years ago and the brigade's remnants are using letters forged in his hand to turn allies against Deshret's Relics, the main brigade. Dehya helps them storm Deshret's Relics' headquarters. In the aftermath she receives Kusayla's cane and a letter revealing she was a foundling.

Shade Upon Red Silk: Dehya, with Dunyarzad at the Grand Bazaar, tells the Traveler that Dakan Al-Ahmar has been stripping and killing travellers in hundreds of incidents. She plans to face the leader, who is her adoptive father, and wants to understand why the brigade has turned violent. Outside Caravan Ribat her contacts report a camp looted with no survivors. They capture the Eremite Sattar, who refuses to talk and tries to bite off his tongue, only to lose consciousness. Goods in the caravan turn out to come from Shahzaman.

Annals of the Scarlet Sands: Shahzaman explains that bandits once attacked the family in the desert when Dunyarzad was a baby, and Kusayla's Eremites saved them. Years later, an ageing Kusayla insisted that Dehya of the Blazing Beasts be hired as Dunyarzad's bodyguard to get her out of mercenary life. Shahzaman had sent only food and medicine to the brigade and refused weapons. He points the group to Jawad, an Eremite arms supplier at Lambad's Tavern, who sends them to the Valley of Dahri.
