Klee, freed from confinement for the festival, joins to help Razor find his "mommy"; Bennett brings a Small Lamp Grass as the Guild's ingredient. After they rescue a fruit cart from hilichurls, Rosaria presents a Mist Flower Corolla for the Church and bluntly tells Razor that his parents' story may not be happy. At the Dawn Winery Diluc agrees, after Kaeya's persuasion, to supply a barrel.

Act III (Aroma of the Past). Noelle and Sucrose give the Knights' ingredient, a Sunsettia improved by Sucrose's bio-alchemy ("Quadruple-Sweetness Sunsettia"). At Angel's Share the group collects the barrel and Diona mixes the brew after a misunderstanding about Razor wanting to drink. Under the great tree at Windrise, Venti gives dandelion seeds as the last ingredient to capture the wind's memory and says Thousand-Wind Wine is the original dandelion wine, tasting different each time because people add what they like. They bury the barrel there; Razor promises to open it with everyone when he is grown. On Windcoming Day Venti sings "Thousand-Wind Wine"; the wind rises, and Razor, smelling his parents' bottle, sees a vision of two adventurers on a cliff, who decided to save it for their son and chose the name Razor.

Revelations: Razor's parents left a box with a woolen puppet, a Ruin Guard part and a bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine, which the Knights have held for him. Thousand-Wind Wine is the first and rarest wine Mondstadt learned to make, and its character depends on whatever the brewer adds. A vision shows his parents as adventurers who called their wine unfinished and gave their son the name Razor. Details of their lives remain unknown.

Characters: Razor is the central figure; he is hesitant but warm. Klee and Bennett support him; Rosaria is blunt but kind; Lisa, his teacher, anchors the Knights' side; Noelle and Sucrose, Diluc, Diona and Kaeya provide the ingredients and logistics; Venti is the wine's guide and the singer of the closing song. Jean convenes the Knights and Mika reads Varka's letter.

Consequences: The bottle Razor brewed remains buried under Windrise's great tree, to be opened with his friends when he grows up. Razor now has his parents' bottle and a vision of them. No plot beyond the festival is affected.

Placement: Released in Version 3.1, 29 September to 17 October 2022, with the gift collection open until 24 October. The requirements were Adventure Rank 21, the Prologue Archon Quest and the Lupus Minor Chapter's first act. The story is set during Weinlesefest in Mondstadt and refers to Varka's expedition as still under way.

637.comment: Of Ballads and Brews: Thousand-Wind Wine
637.content: According to the event, Thousand-Wind Wine is the first and rarest wine that Mondstadters learned to make, and the many techniques involved mean each brew tastes different. Venti says it is the original dandelion wine, and that people have always been free to add what they like. In the event Razor's version takes an explorer's courage, a love tender and true, a defender's will and, last, dandelion seeds meant to capture the wind's memory.

638.comment: Of Ballads and Brews: Razor's parents' box
638.content: Varka asks that Razor be given a wooden box left by his parents. It holds a hand puppet of wool, a Ruin Guard part and a bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine. The bottle's smell later brings Razor a vision of two adventurers sharing the wine on a cliff, agreeing to save it for their son and giving him the name Razor. Their names and fate remain unknown.

639.comment: Of Ballads and Brews: Windcoming Day toast
639.content: At the festival market, everyone toasts after Venti performs "Thousand-Wind Wine". Klee is sad that no wind comes at first; later the breeze rises and Venti, winking at the Traveler, summons his powers. Townsfolk are shown spending time with families or remembering family figures.

640.content:
Of Drink A-Dreaming (also: Bartender Academy Week, Bartender's Academy Week, Angel's Share bartender event): Luka, who is running Bartender Academy Week, offers the Traveler and Paimon the run of the tavern's ingredients and unlimited refills as long as they are not wasteful, plus rewards when guests are happy. The bartender Charles teaches the basics and explains that beginners are no longer given alcoholic ingredients after an earlier student's mix knocked a customer out. Over three days friends from across Teyvat come to the counter, each with an order and a conversation, and a later Bartender Challenge tests the Traveler's skill. In the Afterword Luka offers them a job, which they decline to keep travelling together.

Plot: In the opening quest Luka greets the Traveler outside Angel's Share and pitches Bartender Academy Week, which is optional. Inside, Charles trains them on a first drink, warns that customers have special requests and says conversation matters as much as mixing. The Traveler then serves guests in seven Tavern Tales: Kaeya and Rosaria; Diluc; Jean and Lisa; Zhongli; Eula; Beidou and Ningguang; and Shenhe. After the event ends, Luka thanks them in the Afterword: business has boomed, most customers came for the Traveler, and he asks whether they would stay and work there.

Revelations: The Tavern Tales add small character moments rather than plot. Diluc recalls inventing Gray Valley Sunset as a boy; Rosaria's dislike of tea comes from a church memory; Eula admits she usually drinks alone because of her family name; Beidou teases Ningguang about her early days as a fruit seller, which Ningguang declines to dwell on; Zhongli puts his bill on the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's tab; and Jean and Lisa discuss Jean's difficulty relaxing.

Characters: Luka (event-exclusive, runs the Academy Week) and Charles (bartender at Angel's Share) frame the event. The Tavern Tales guests are Kaeya and Rosaria, Diluc, Jean and Lisa, Zhongli, Eula, Beidou and Ningguang, and Shenhe. Paimon helps the Traveler throughout.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. It leaves a standing invitation from Luka and Charles to visit Angel's Share, and Diluc says he wants to give the Traveler something once they have more bartending experience. Gameplay rewards include the furnishing Tavern Shaker: Grumous Oscillation and the namecard Celebration: Binge Vessel.

Placement: Released in Version 2.5, with entry after Interlude Chapter Act I and Eula's Aphros Delos Chapter Act I. The wiki does not date it in-world, so treat it as a light interlude with the Traveler and Paimon travelling together in Mondstadt.

641.comment: Of Drink A-Dreaming: Bartender Academy Week
641.content: In March 2022 Angel's Share, Mondstadt's tavern run by Dawn Winery, held a Bartender Academy Week hosted by Luka. Participants had access to the tavern's ingredients, with unlimited refills if they were not wasteful, and no alcohol for beginners. The Traveler and Paimon took part.

642.content: The seven Tavern Tales are the event's guest stories: When They Take Off Their Armor (Kaeya and Rosaria), Fine Wine From Yesterday (Diluc), Dandelion, Rose, and Windwheel Aster (Jean and Lisa), Surrounded by the Aroma of Tea (Zhongli), Solid Ice, Soluble in Wine (Eula), Docked on a Moonlit Night (Beidou and Ningguang) and Untainted Autumn Frost (Shenhe).

643.content: An event-exclusive NPC who organised Bartender Academy Week outside Angel's Share. He recruits the Traveler and Paimon, and later offers them jobs at the tavern.

key: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers
644.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers
644.content:
Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers (also: Flower-Feather Clan Tribal Chronicle, The Wingless One of Tlalocan, The Night Before the Trial, Guns and Wings): The Flower-Feather Clan's Tribal Chronicles chapter and Chasca's story. The tribe's Qucusaur Rider trials have left many applicants "Wingless", and a merchant caravan arrives with Phlogiston Wings, jetpacks powered by phlogiston. When a wild qucusaur, Chasca's old "sister" Coya, starts attacking merchants, Chasca and the Traveler discover that a plot to harvest phlogiston from captive qucusaurs is being run by Allpa, a trusted member of the tribe.

The chapter has three acts, all released in Version 5.2: The Wingless One of Tlalocan, The Night Before the Trial and Guns and Wings, the last needing the Archon Quest act The Rainbow Destined to Burn. Guns and Wings has three quests: Tracks Through the Wilderness, Mortal Pursuit and Time for the Showdown. The chapter shows Chasca's mixed identity as a human raised by qucusaurs and her ties to her adoptive father Cusco and her qucusaur mother and sister.

Plot: In Act I Chasca keeps watch over Coyllur, a Qucusaur Rider applicant who failed her trial and is at risk of becoming one of the Wingless. The Traveler cheers her up by indwelling a qucusaur, and Chasca's adoptive father Cusco asks the Traveler to persuade Chasca to take care of herself. In Act II, before the retried trial, merchants led by Isidore arrive after being attacked by a qucusaur and show the Phlogiston Wings they carry. Chasca finds a bloodstained feather she recognises. In Act III the applicants try the Wings, a qucusaur attacks the merchants again, and Chasca recognises it as her "sister" Coya. They trace the wings to a hidden airborne workshop attributed to a man named Tepal and find that Allpa, who helps run the trials, is the mastermind. The workshop is destroyed and Coya, with whom Chasca had fallen out long ago, has forgiven her.

Revelations: The Phlogiston Wings are made with phlogiston drawn from captured qucusaurs. "Tepal" was a front; the real mastermind is Allpa, who helps run the trials; Tepal himself had died long before. Coya's attacks were defence of her stolen chick.

Characters: Chasca is the lead and the chapter's emotional centre. Cusco is her adoptive father; Chimpu and Coya are the qucusaurs who raised her and her sister. Allpa is trusted organiser and villain, Mutota the tribe's chief, Coyllur, Zhunan and Mukki the applicants, Isidore the merchant, Puma Tepal's relative. Xilonen helps trace Tepal.

Consequences: Allpa and her followers are jailed in a part of the dismantled workshop. Captive qucusaurs are freed, though some drained of phlogiston still need rescue. Coya is injured saving Chasca but recovers, and the two reconcile. The tribe still has to decide how the Wings fit into the riders' future.

Placement: Released entirely in Version 5.2. Acts I and II need only the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame quest, but Act III requires The Rainbow Destined to Burn, so it takes place after the Abyss invasion and Chuychu's death.

645.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Phlogiston Wings
645.content: A phlogiston-powered jetpack operated by a handheld trackball, brought to the Flower-Feather Clan by merchants. Using them, "Wingless" applicants can fly without a qucusaur. They are made with phlogiston drawn from captive qucusaurs.

646.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Qucusaur Rider Trials
646.content: The Flower-Feather Clan's entry test. Applicants need combat skill and the approval of a qucusaur; those who repeatedly fail may give up and are known as the Wingless.

647.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Allpa
647.content: A Flower-Feather Clan member who helps run the Qucusaur Rider trials and, after learning of her son's death (per the wiki summary), is revealed as the mastermind behind capturing qucusaurs for phlogiston. She is arrested after the workshop is destroyed.

648.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Coya and Chimpu
648.content: Chimpu is the qucusaur who raised Chasca; Coya is her qucusaur daughter, whom Chasca calls her sister. After Chasca was returned to human society they drifted apart; Coya attacked the merchants because humans took her chick, Chime. She forgives Chasca.

649.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers Event Window
649.content: The Tribal Chronicles event ran from 2024-11-20 to 2024-12-10 with extra rewards for completing the chapter. The story remains available.

650.content:
Of the Land Amidst Monoliths (also: Chapter I Act I, Liyue Archon Quest Act I): Chapter I Act I of the Archon Quest, set in Liyue. The Traveler and Paimon reach Liyue Harbor in search of the Geo Archon at the annual Rite of Descension, only to see Rex Lapis fall from the clouds apparently dead. Suspected by association, they are rescued by the Fatui Harbinger Childe and told to seek the adepti at Jueyun Karst.

The act has four stages: Rite of Descension, An Impromptu Change of Plan, three quests that can be done in any order (Wangshu, Moulder of Mountains, Custodian of Clouds), and Dust to Dust. It introduces Liyue's reverence for its god, the Liyue Qixing, the Millelith, the Fatui presence in the harbor, and the hidden adepti. Released in version 1.0.

Plot: Venti has told the Traveler that Rex Lapis will appear in Liyue for the Rite of Descension. In Liyue Harbor the rite begins and Ningguang summons the god, but he drops lifeless onto the offering table and she orders the exits sealed. The Traveler is chased by the Millelith, rescued by Childe, and given a sigil to reach the adepti in Jueyun Karst.

**Rite of Descension.** Paimon explains that the Geo Archon is called Rex Lapis by Liyue's own people, since using the name Morax is considered impolite for outsiders. Locals such as Linlang, Guanhai and Bolai describe the yearly rite, in which the god gives guidance on Liyue's coming year, and send the pair to Yujing Terrace. They make wishes at the censers, then watch as Ningguang, who presides, calls the god down. As the clouds part, Rex Lapis's lifeless body crashes onto the offering table, and Ningguang declares that he has been killed and the exits must be sealed. The Millelith seize those who stood near the terrace. The Traveler tries to slip away but steps on a broken tile and is spotted. A Hydro user cuts down the guards and leads them off; he calls himself Childe, asks whether they met Signora in Mondstadt, and Paimon recognises him as a Fatui Harbinger. He says he had heard of their deeds in Mondstadt, kept his eye on them throughout the rite and so knows they did not do it, and sends them to the Northland Bank, where he gives them a Sigil of Permission and points them toward Jueyun Karst, the supposed home of the adepti.

**An Impromptu Change of Plan.** In Jueyun Karst the pair meet Moon Carver, who recognises the sigil. Millelith soldiers pursue them in, and Moon Carver tells the Traveler to see them gone; the Traveler fights them off. Told that Rex Lapis was killed at the rite and the Qixing are blaming onlookers, he is outraged, accepts that the accusation against the Traveler is unjust, and tells them to find Mountain Shaper and Cloud Retainer in the karst and the Conqueror of Demons, a guardian yaksha, at Wangshu Inn.

Revelations: Rex Lapis appears to have been assassinated at the Rite of Descension.

Childe is a Fatui Harbinger who had heard of the Traveler's deeds in Mondstadt and watched them throughout the rite. The adepti exist and are real. Rex Lapis is also an adeptus, the Prime of the Adepti, bound by contract with the other adepti to Liyue's protection. The Liyue Qixing are keeping the body out of sight.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Ningguang; Childe (Tartaglia); Moon Carver; Xiao.

Also Mountain Shaper, Cloud Retainer, Verr Goldet of Wangshu Inn, the inn's chef Smiley Yanxiao and its ghost, the brothers Li Ding and Li Dang on Mt. Hulao, and harbor locals including Linlang, Guanhai, Bolai, Ivanovich, Changshun, Gentry De'an, Fan Er'ye and Jifang. Venti is the one who sent the Traveler to Liyue.

Consequences: The Traveler is wanted by the Millelith and has accepted Childe's help; Childe promises to find someone who can break the stalemate over the Exuvia. The next act, Farewell, Archaic Lord, begins with that help.

Placement: Chapter I Act I, after Song of the Dragon and Freedom (the Mondstadt story) and before Act II, Farewell, Archaic Lord. Released in version 1.0. The quest requires completing the Mondstadt story and Adventure Rank 23.

651.comment: Of the Land Amidst Monoliths: Rite of Descension
651.content: An annual ceremony at Yujing Terrace in which the Liyue Qixing's Tianquan, as presider, calls on Rex Lapis to give the year's economic guidance. Last year's request was made by the Yuheng, and Bolai recalls seventeen predictions from it. In the quest, the god falls dead.

652.comment: Of the Land Amidst Monoliths: Sigil of Permission
652.content: Childe hands over a sigil at Northland Bank, saying only that it keeps the adepti from harming its bearer. Moon Carver recognises it and says many seasons have passed since one was last seen.

653.comment: Of the Land Amidst Monoliths: Jueyun Karst adepti encounters
653.content: Moon Carver tells the Traveler to look for Mountain Shaper, Cloud Retainer and the Conqueror of Demons. Xiao is shocked and says he will seek out the other adepti, Mountain Shaper is mostly concerned with its flowers, and Cloud Retainer threatens Liyue before accepting a contract for the food offerings.

key: Old Notes and New Friends World Quest series
654.content:
Old Notes and New Friends (also: Old Notes and New Friends World Quest series, Dual Evidence, Soheil's Wish, Invisible Barrier, Hidden Mercenaries, Desert's Remembrance): Old Notes and New Friends is a world quest series in the Great Red Sand, Sumeru, added in version 3.1 as a follow-up to Golden Slumber. In Aaru Village the Traveler and Paimon meet two Vahumana researchers, Kalantari and Soheil. Soheil dismisses the Traveler's desert finds until the Traveler enters King Deshret's Mausoleum and brings back proof, then sends them to check the ruins in his old notes.

The series has two main quests, Dual Evidence and Soheil's Wish, and Soheil's Wish branches into three exploration quests: Invisible Barrier, Hidden Mercenaries and Desert's Remembrance. It is light in tone: the slates the Traveler brings back turn out to hold leave requests, a love poem and a fable, and the story pokes gentle fun at Akademiya paper-writing culture while also showing real pressure on its researchers.

Plot: Dual Evidence. Back in Aaru Village, the Traveler and Paimon are approached by Kalantari, a student of the Akademiya who has read Tirzad's new paper on the late period of Al-Ahmar's civilization, in which the two are thanked as a gift from the desert. Kalantari hopes to get inspiration for his own stalled paper and offers to hire them as guides. Before they can begin, the older researcher Soheil of the Usaibia family arrives with a Corps of Thirty escort, Hulwani, to send young scholars back: the sage fears they will alert the matra or damage the ruins, and Soheil says forty-six leave applications arrived after Tirzad's paper appeared. Soheil sends Kalantari home but stays himself, and tells the Traveler and Paimon that he suspects Tirzad invented his account. Stung, they find the stone slate Tirzad left glowing and head into the Mausoleum. They light the three ritual sites, activate the great device in the Great Hall of Truths, and defeat a Primal Construct at the top of the Mausoleum. They return with a new slate. Soheil's attitude flips, and he apologises on behalf of himself and his family.

Soheil's Wish. Soheil keeps the slate and, because the sage forbids researchers to enter the desert but has said nothing against gifts, hands the Traveler his old archaeology notes as a "present". The notes point to three places, and the Traveler brings back the slates found at each.

Revelations: - The Mausoleum of King Deshret can be entered and cleared by following a stone slate left from Golden Slumber; its inner structure includes the Great Hall of Truths and a roof reached by an elevator.
- The late-period records of Al-Ahmar's civilization have mostly been lost, so a complete slate is an unprecedented find for Vahumana, according to Soheil.
- Soheil's real motive is ambition: he wants a sage's seat, and he admits the gap between researcher and sage is like that between a hilichurl and a slime.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Kalantari, a student and Vahumana researcher (a quest-only NPC); Soheil Usaibia, an older Vahumana researcher; Hulwani of the Corps of Thirty; and mentions of Tirzad, Jeht and the sage. Thutmose Eremites appear in Hidden Mercenaries.

Consequences: The cyclone above the Mausoleum is permanently turned off and Aaru's Shut becomes permanently accessible. Soheil changes from scornful to grateful and gives the Traveler repeated gifts of friendship.

Placement: Requires Golden Slumber to be finished and the next day's reset. Released in 3.1. Dual Evidence comes first, then Soheil's Wish, which has three exploration quests that can be done in any order and may be done in advance.

655.comment: Old Notes and New Friends: Soheil
655.content: Soheil Usaibia is an older Vahumana researcher of the Usaibia family. He was sent to Aaru Village to stop young scholars going into the desert, is dismissive of Tirzad's paper at first, then becomes warm once shown evidence. He covets a sage's position and openly says why. He is conscious of his age and the time left to him.

656.comment: Old Notes and New Friends: Kalantari
656.content: Kalantari is a student of the Akademiya from a family of merchants in Port Ormos. He has read Tirzad's paper and wants help getting out of a creative block. He is friendly, talkative and gets sent back to Sumeru City by Soheil in Dual Evidence. He is a quest-only NPC.

657.comment: Old Notes and New Friends: Thutmose
657.content: Thutmose is a group of Eremites in the desert who describe themselves as fanatical believers in Deshret in Soheil's old notes. The notes record two young leaders, one aggressive and one merciful. In Hidden Mercenaries their base is a hidden location near Lamb-Devourer Rock behind a door that opens to a spoken password.

658.comment: Old Notes and New Friends: Mausoleum slates
658.content: Stone slates are the quest items of the series. The Scarlet Sand Slate gives instructions in stages for the Mausoleum. The slates in the transparent ruins, in the Thutmose base and in the Tomb of Carouses hold, respectively, leave requests, a love poem and a fable, according to Soheil.

659.content:
Omnipresence Over Mortals (also: Chapter II Act III, Sword, Fish, Resistance, Duel Before the Throne, The Omnipresent God): Omnipresence Over Mortals is the third act of Chapter II of the Archon Quests, set in Inazuma and released in Version 2.1. The Traveler joins the Watatsumi Army's Resistance as captain of a special unit, discovers that the Fatui are the Resistance's secret sponsor and are supplying life-draining Delusions, and loses the soldier Teppei to them. With Yae Miko's help, the Traveler exposes Kujou Takayuki's betrayal, defeats Signora in a duel before the Shogun, and then fights the Raiden Shogun in the Plane of Euthymia, where the true Ei agrees to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

The act has nine quests, from Sword, Fish, Resistance to Wishes. It combines the war's resolution, the unmasking of the Shogun as a puppet made by Ei, the death of Signora, and the loss of the Electro Gnosis to the Fatui. It ends by pointing the Traveler to Sumeru.

Plot: **Sword, Fish, Resistance.** Teppei takes the Traveler to Watatsumi Island to meet Sangonomiya Kokomi. She explains that she accepted an anonymous letter offering the Resistance supplies as long as it kept fighting the Shogunate, and that she doubted the sender's motives but had little choice because the island lacked resources. On the Vision Hunt Decree she says the attitude of the Tenryou Commission and of the Raiden Shogun does not add up. She makes the Traveler captain of a special operations unit, Swordfish II, and promises Teppei a combat role. After a first task the unit investigates vanishing supplies around Fort Mumei, staying at Bourou Village, where Teppei, now captain of a unit himself, praises the new sponsor's supplies.

**Those Who Yearn for the Gods' Gaze.** The Fort Mumei search finds nothing, but the area feels strange. Teppei arrives with greying hair and a cough, blaming a cold, and explains the Tatarigami, a phenomenon that appeared after the Raiden Shogun killed Orobashi, the god of Watatsumi Island, during the Archon War. He warns that it harms health. Back on Watatsumi Island the Traveler finds Kokomi and Gorou examining a secret weapon an officer handed in: a vitality-absorbing Delusion, which reveals the Fatui as the sponsor. Kokomi orders all users recalled. The Traveler realises Teppei's boosted strength came from a Delusion and rushes to him too late. Teppei, who now looks like an old man, dies in despair, and the Traveler swears revenge on the Fatui.

Revelations: The Shogun who governs Inazuma is a puppet; the true Ei is in the Plane of Euthymia. The Fatui sponsored the Resistance with Delusions that drain the lives of their users, using Crystal Marrow gathered by the Kanjou Commission, and Kujou Takayuki colluded with them. Signora is dead. The Balladeer is Ei's prototype puppet and the Sixth Harbinger. The Electro Gnosis passes from Ei through Miko to the Balladeer. Ei agrees to end the Vision Hunt Decree.

Characters: **Traveler and Paimon**: the Traveler becomes a Resistance captain, loses Teppei, breaks the Delusion factory, defeats Signora and Ei.
**Yae Miko**: the shrine's guide and Ei's old friend, who rescues, trains and pushes the plan, and in the end persuades Ei to relent.
**Sangonomiya Kokomi and Gorou**: lead the Resistance; Kokomi accepted the sponsor's supplies despite her doubts.
**Teppei**: grows in confidence with the Delusion's help and dies of its effects.
**Kujou Sara and Kujou Takayuki**: Sara is turned against her adoptive father when his betrayal is proved; he confesses selfish motives.
**Signora and the Balladeer**: Fatui Harbingers; she is executed, he is the Sixth Harbinger.
**Raiden Shogun and Ei**: the puppet Shogun and the true Electro Archon, who is defeated and persuaded.

Consequences: The Vision Hunt Decree is abolished, the Fatui's Delusion scheme collapses, and Signora is dead. The Traveler leaves with the Resistance's campaign effectively over; Ei says she must reconsider how she rules. The Electro Gnosis is in the Balladeer's hands. The Traveler is pointed toward Sumeru.

Placement: Released in Version 2.1 as the third act of Chapter II, after Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow (2.0). Next in story order are Requiem of the Echoing Depths and The Crane Returns on the Wind. The act shares its name with the Chapter II title in some listings, so use "Act III" to be unambiguous. It requires Adventure Rank 30.

660.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: Swordfish II and the Fatui Sponsor
660.content: Kokomi accepted an anonymous letter's offer of supplies for the Resistance, with doubts about the sender. The Traveler is made captain of Swordfish II, a special operations unit. The sponsor turns out to be the Fatui.

661.content: Teppei uses a Fatui Delusion to gain combat strength, ages quickly, dismisses his symptoms as a cold and dies as an old man while the Traveler tries to reach him. His death drives the Traveler's personal vow against the Fatui.

662.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: The Delusion Factory
662.content: A Fatui plant that makes Delusions from Crystal Marrow collected by the Kanjou Commission. A notice there shows that Nathan, a supposed Resistance member, is a Fatui mole. The Balladeer is waiting inside.

663.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: Duel Before the Throne
663.content: At Tenshukaku the Traveler invokes the rule that a duel before the throne gives the winner a second chance, and challenges Signora. The Shogun approves. The Traveler wins, and the Shogun executes Signora with Musou no Hitotachi.

664.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: The Plane of Euthymia Confrontation
664.content: The Traveler defeats Ei in her inner world while the light of confiscated Visions brightens its darkness. Miko enters with the omamori, and persuades Ei, who lost companions and her sister Makoto, to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

665.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: Kazuha Blocks the Shogun
665.content: Outside Tenshukaku, Kazuha resonates with his late friend's Masterless Vision and combines its Electro power with his own Anemo Vision to block Musou no Hitotachi and push the Shogun back. It inspires the Resistance to charge.

666.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: The Electro Gnosis Sold
666.content: Ei gave her Electro Gnosis to Miko before entering the Plane, expecting Miko to sell it for something of equal value. Miko gave it to the Balladeer to save the Traveler.

key: On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb
To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown
The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated
667.comment: On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb
667.content:
On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb (also: To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown, The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated, White Birch Snowgrave series): On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb is a Snezhnaya World Quest series added in version 7.0, set in the White Birch Snowgrave. In two quests the Traveler and Paimon explore the Pale Crown Palace, the hidden former home and tomb of the Belyi Tsar, and the frozen mausoleum around it, where they recover one of the three missing fragments of the Eye of Graeae.

The quests are "To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown" and "The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated". The series runs concurrently with In the Dwelling of Life and Hesperides of Love and Hate, and all three feed into Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard.

Plot: To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown. The Eye of Graeae senses that one of the three pieces of its lost power lies inside the Pale Crown Palace. The palace was once the Belyi Tsar's private home and later his tomb, and the Eye also learns it was created there, in the hidden research facility Hvergelmir. The palace was a place where the Tsar welcomed humans alongside the fae, and where the flame of Kresnik was first kindled before it spread across what became Snezhnaya. After the Tsar died fighting the Abyss and waves of beasts around five hundred years ago, his remains returned to the palace and part of his body became the Tsar's White Birch.

The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated. With the Eye of Graeae, the Traveler and Paimon cross snow-covered ruins and royal halls, solving puzzles with statues and torches, and fight man-made monsters. A two-headed beast, "Zver", guards the Belyi Tsar's body and tells them to leave. Flashbacks show the Tsar, his servant Aksinya and the bio-alchemical work that produced Zver and other creatures. Zver was a failed prototype abandoned by its creator Koshchei; the Tsar saved it, gave it purpose and treated it as a loyal companion. Zver has guarded the corpse for centuries and hates those who wronged its master.

Revelations: - The Pale Crown Palace was the Belyi Tsar's private residence and later his tomb, and is where the Kresnik flame was first lit; the Tsar's White Birch grew from part of his body.
- Hvergelmir is where the Eye of Graeae was created; researchers there studied a Proto-Man held in an egg.
- Zver was a rejected prototype of Koshchei's, saved and trusted by the Tsar.
- The Eye of Graeae is a prototype made to house a "Key", and its memories were erased.

Characters: - The Traveler and Paimon.
- The Eye of Graeae ("Goggles"), whose past the series starts to open up.
- Zver, the two-headed guardian of the Tsar's body.
- The Belyi Tsar and Aksinya, shown in flashback; Aksinya also leaves the note at Hvergelmir.
- Researchers Izmaylov and Azazel, seen only in a vision of Hvergelmir's past.

Consequences: The Traveler recovers one fragment of the Eye of Graeae (a Pebble), and the series establishes that all fragments must be brought to the Court of Bliss. Zver is left defeated but not shown as killed in the available summary.

Placement: Story order: it is one of three parallel series after the Snezhnaya Archon Quest chapter that unlock Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard. Release order: version 7.0 with the other Snezhnaya World Quest series. Players who finish it first will see different conditional lines in Through the Gates of Ivory; for example, Aksinya's appearance at the false wedding and the Eye's comments about Pavlina's betrayal refer back to the Pale Crown Palace.

668.comment: On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb: Zver
668.content: Zver is a two-headed beast and man-made creature that guards the Belyi Tsar's body in the mausoleum below the Pale Crown Palace. Once an abandoned prototype of Koshchei, it was given purpose by the Tsar and has stayed loyal for centuries. It warns the Traveler away, is defeated in battle, and tells them the Eye of Graeae may not be trustworthy.

669.comment: On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb: Hvergelmir (research facility)
669.content: Hvergelmir was the Belyi Tsar's bio-alchemy research organisation, hidden under the Pale Crown Palace. In the Traveler's vision, researchers Izmaylov and Azazel monitor a Proto-Man in an egg and fear that a ban on alchemy would end their work. The ruined site later holds a fragment of the Eye of Graeae and a note from Aksinya.

key: Origin of the Sequence world quest
670.content:
Origin of the Sequence (also: Origin of the Sequence world quest, Ia-Ilimmu No. 59 Storage Array quest): A Version 6.7 world quest in the Lunar Highlands of the Frost Moon. The Traveler and Paimon find a set of giant towers at the Nuur Stone Circle, repair a damaged ancient terminal and recalibrate a stone dragon idol. Finishing it unlocks the Ancient Moon's Remnant at the circle.

The terminal calls itself the Ia-Ilimmu No. 59 Storage Array and cannot recognise visitors because its central module is damaged or missing. It asks for Nin-Kiggia to be contacted for maintenance, and finally reports that its primary energy system is not connected. The quest ends with that unresolved error.

Plot: Paimon marvels at the giant towers and thinks they resemble the Frostmoon Scions' sanctum. The Traveler examines a terminal, follows its prompts to repair data nodes, and calibrates a Secret Source Dragon Idol that appears. Four glowing markers light up around the area.

On approach, the terminal checks for vital signs, tries an identification sequence and fails. A security check on the kernel also fails; it blames a damaged or missing central module and tells the visitor to contact Nin-Kiggia. It then switches to a "universal greeting", welcoming the visitor to the Ia-Ilimmu No. 59 Storage Array, which is used mostly to regulate the Engraving and store research resources. A critical component failure has left service dependencies broken; the terminal asks for a self-diagnostic command to restore critical data nodes. Paimon admits she did not follow most of this, and decides that a storehouse must hold treasure.

After the Traveler repairs the nodes, the diagnostic fails to run on schedule and manual path recalibration is needed. A Secret Source Dragon Idol appears. Paimon proposes climbing on its back and bopping it a couple of times to get it working, which the Traveler does. The terminal then reports repair complete and thanks them and lifts its lockdown. Four glowing markers appear nearby. A final error says the primary energy system is not connected and asks for Nin-Kiggia or an auxiliary power source.

Revelations: The quest establishes that this ancient array is numbered No. 59, called Ia-Ilimmu, tied to something called the Engraving, and designed to be maintained by Nin-Kiggia. The terminal calls the repairs a self-diagnostic and does not explain what the towers do beyond that.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, plus the Ancient Terminal. Nin-Kiggia is only named, and does not appear.

Paimon supplies curiosity and a treasure-hunting attitude: she assumes a "storage" array means a storehouse. The terminal is polite, formal and fussy about titles and procedure, and repeatedly apologises for its limits.

Consequences: The Ancient Moon's Remnant at the Nuur Stone Circle becomes available, where Luna Sigils can be offered for rewards, and the Fragments of Ia-Ilimmu exploration objective is unlocked. The terminal remains partly broken because of its missing energy source.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII) with the Frost Moon area. Within the Sequence follows it, and the Moon Gazing series covers the wider setting. The wiki lists no formal requirement beyond reaching the Nuur Stone Circle.

671.comment: Origin of the Sequence: Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array
671.content: A damaged ancient installation at the Nuur Stone Circle in the Lunar Highlands of the Frost Moon. Its terminal calls it the Ia-Ilimmu No. 59 Storage Array, used to regulate the operation of the Engraving and to store research resources. After the Traveler repairs it in Origin of the Sequence, it still reports that its primary energy system is not connected and that Nin-Kiggia should be contacted.

672.content:
Orobashi's Legacy (also: Orobashi's Legacy: Prologue, Yashiori Island ward quests): Orobashi's Legacy is a six-part World Quest series on Yashiori Island, added in version 2.0. At Fort Fujitou the Traveler meets Kaji, who is studying why the island has endless rain and lightning. The cause is damaged ancient wards linked to the remains of Orobashi, a serpent god. The Traveler restores them across the island and the storm ends.

The parts are Prologue and Parts I to V. It requires the Archon Quest act A New Star Approaches, and the Ritou Escape Plan quest to reach its starting area. Finishing Part III opens the Formation Estate domain, and finishing Part V rewards the diagram for the Kitain Cross Spear.

Plot: Kaji, met at Fort Fujitou, is investigating the island's unceasing storm. He reasons it comes from the failure of a series of ancient wards connected to the remains of Orobashi. Orobashi, the guardian deity of Watatsumi Island, sacrificed itself after learning a forbidden truth Celestia wished hidden, led an invasion of Yashiori Island, and was slain by the Raiden Shogun, Ei, in a battle that carved Musoujin Gorge and scattered the god's remains. Their lingering power is what causes the Tatarigami.

In Parts I to III the Traveler visits Musoujin Gorge, Serpent's Head and Jakotsu Mine, finds missing Rock Pillar Warding Stones and Rock Pillar Pearls, and returns them to broken wards by solving Sacred Stone Puzzles.

Revelations: - The storm on Yashiori Island is a consequence of broken wards, not natural weather (Kaji's hypothesis, borne out by the quests).
- Orobashi's remains, scattered when the Raiden Shogun killed it, are the source of the Tatarigami.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Kaji (researcher), a Maguu Kenki as the final guardian. Orobashi and the Raiden Shogun appear in the history Kaji recounts.

Consequences: The storm and lightning over Yashiori Island cease and the Tatarigami are cleared from the repaired areas. Fort Mumei has surfaced near Watatsumi Island. Kaji leaves for the Kujou Encampment.

Placement: Released in 2.0 with Inazuma. Requires A New Star Approaches; Ritou Escape Plan is needed to reach the starting location.

673.content: A researcher the Traveler meets at Fort Fujitou, investigating the endless rain and lightning of Yashiori Island. He identifies the broken ancient wards as the cause and directs the Traveler to repair them. He moves on to the Kujou Encampment when the work is finished.

674.content: Ancient wards on Yashiori Island, linked to the remains of Orobashi, whose failure causes the storm. They are repaired by returning Rock Pillar Warding Stones and Rock Pillar Pearls to stone puzzles at Musoujin Gorge, Serpent's Head and Jakotsu Mine, with a last ward at Fort Mumei.

key: Awaken the Residual Pari in the Fravashi Trees
675.content:
Pale Fire (also: Pale Fire World Quest series, Awaken the Residual Pari in the Fravashi Trees, Fravashi Tree quests): Pale Fire is a world quest series in the Girdle of the Sands, Sumeru, added in version 3.6. Strange circular trees called Fravashi Trees hold the lingering remains of Pari who could not return home. With the Pari Sorush's help the Traveler awakens ten of them, collects the Plumes of Purifying Light they leave, and has the elder Zurvan explain what they are.

The series has a main quest, Pale Fire, and ten separate quests, one per tree, all named Awaken the Residual Pari in the Fravashi Trees, which can be done in any order. Doing any one of them unlocks Pale Fire, and completing all ten finishes it. The Traveler is formally addressed as Sorush's Yasnapati, and Zurvan asks them to help the Pari that have not yet returned.

Plot: At each Fravashi Tree, a ring-shaped tree that Paimon at first takes for a door, Sorush speaks with scorn for the sight of her own kind clinging on. She explains that these trees are Pari who fought to the end against the defilement corrupting the land and, with their last strength, turned into trees; being tainted, they were rejected by the Vourukasha Oasis. Paimon insists the Traveler cannot leave them to suffer alone. Sorush wakes the residual Pari with her power. It lashes out at hidden enemies and the Traveler must defeat the monsters that appear (two waves in the example read, hilichurls and Abyss mages with mitachurl support). A Plume of Purifying Light floats out of the tree, the obsession within cleared away.

After the first tree, Pale Fire starts. If the Traveler has not yet done The Splendorous Sky That Day, a pop-up advises learning more about the Pari. The Traveler brings news to Zurvan, who explains what a Fravashi Tree and the Plume are and that offering the Plume to the Amrita Pool lets the Pari return to the Vourukasha Oasis. She names the ritual and the Yasnapati who performs it, and asks the Traveler to bring back every Plume. When all ten trees are awakened, Zurvan thanks the Traveler and Sorush and tells Paimon a story about visiting Oceanids.

Revelations: - Fravashi Trees are Pari who exhausted their strength against the defilement of the land and were rejected by the Oasis as tainted.
- Plumes of Purifying Light let these Pari return to the Vourukasha Oasis when offered to the Amrita Pool.
- Humans who walked beside Pari once purified them in the desert; the Traveler as Sorush's Yasnapati takes on that role.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Sorush, the Pari who calls the Traveler her Yasnapati and Paimon "Pale Floater"; Zurvan, the Pari elder at the Vourukasha Oasis; and a Residual Pari of the Forest in each tree.

Consequences: Ten Fravashi Trees are cleared and their Pari are able to return to the Vourukasha Oasis; the Oasis looks livelier. The Traveler is recognised as a Yasnapati by Zurvan.

Placement: Released in 3.6, located in the Girdle of the Sands, Sumeru (Gavireh Lajavard, with the Oasis as the hub). The trees are scattered in spots including Tunigi Hollow, Asipattravana Swamp, the Temir Mountains and Madinat al-Nuhas.

676.content: A Fravashi Tree is a ring-shaped tree in the Girdle of the Sands that a Pari transformed into after exhausting its strength against defilement. Sorush says the Pari inside is stuck on obsessions of the past and has been rejected by the Oasis as tainted. Waking it triggers a short fight with spectral enemies and leaves a Plume of Purifying Light.

677.comment: Pale Fire: Plume of Purifying Light
677.content: The Plume is a glittering object that rises from a Fravashi Tree once its residual Pari is awakened. Zurvan says it carries memories that cannot return to the earth and comes from Simurgh's Khvarena; offered to the Amrita Pool, it lets the Pari return to the Vourukasha Oasis.

678.content: Yasnapati is a title Sorush uses for the Traveler. Zurvan says that in ancient times human warriors who walked with Pari held rituals to purify Pari scattered in the desert, and those with a special bond to Pari have been called Yasnapati ever since. Sorush instead credits the Order of Skeptics with the rituals.

679.content: A story Zurvan tells at the end of Pale Fire: long ago Oceanids from foreign lands crossed the desert in search of their dead god, found nothing, saw the Harvisptokhm and left. Their route became a legend for outsiders, who later read it as self-sacrifice in pursuit of pure innocence; pilgrims kept coming for a long time after the Oasis closed.

680.content:
Papilio Charontis Chapter (Hu Tao) (also: Papilio Charontis Chapter, Hu Tao's Story Quest, Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away): The Papilio Charontis Chapter is Hu Tao's Story Quest (Version 1.3), set in Liyue. In its one act, Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away, the Traveler meets the 77th Director of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and helps her intern Meng find out whether his childhood friend, who died young, has become a vengeful spirit. The answer is a gentle one, and the act ends with a funeral at the border between life and death.

The act has four quests: The Mysterious Wangsheng Parlor, In Pursuit of a Phantom, Friendships, Wishes, and Regrets, and Perfect Send-Off. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and the Archon Quest Farewell, Archaic Lord. The Chinese chapter name means roughly "Chapter of the Guiding Butterfly".

Plot: Meng, a nervous new intern at Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, takes the Traveler and Paimon for ghosts on Wuwang Hill. His boss Hu Tao, the 77th Director, tries and fails to recruit them for a deal with the Adventurers' Guild. Meng fears his late childhood friend, nicknamed Big G, has become a vengeful spirit. Hu Tao stages a mock exorcism of a panicking man, Luocheng, at a Ley Line Monolith, and Big G's harmless spirit turns up, lost in the city. After the Traveler gathers keepsakes from Big G's living friends Little Wu, Mumu and Congzi, Hu Tao leads the group into the border between life and death for a farewell. She also promises to keep looking for the Traveler's sibling.

Revelations: Minor lore: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor claims a founding role in ending an ancient plague born of accumulated Yaksha karma, and its directors tend the balance between life and death. The "border" between the living and the dead is a real, Ley-Line-disordered place that Hu Tao can enter with others. Spirits keep the form they had when they died.

Characters: Hu Tao, the Traveler and Paimon. Meng, Big G, Luocheng, Little Wu, Mumu, Congzi, Lan and the Ferrylady appear. Zhongli is mentioned.

Hu Tao is playful and theatrical but conscientious, and she hides real care behind pranks. Meng is anxious, earnest and grieving. Big G is a gentle spirit with a poor sense of direction and a fear of heights. Zhongli is referred to as the parlor's consultant but does not appear in person.

Consequences: The Traveler and Paimon gain a friendly acquaintance with Hu Tao, who promises to keep looking for the Traveler's sibling. The chapter is also a prerequisite for Baizhu's Lagenaria Chapter, along with the Alatus Chapter's Butterfly's Dream.

Placement: Release order: 1.3. Story order: after Chapter I of the Archon Quests (Farewell, Archaic Lord). Hu Tao reappears in the Lagenaria Chapter (3.6).

681.comment: Papilio Charontis Chapter (Hu Tao): Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away
681.content: Act I of Hu Tao's Story Quest. The Traveler helps Hu Tao and her intern Meng discover that Meng's dead childhood friend Big G is a harmless spirit who only wished to see his friends again, then collects keepsakes for a farewell held in the border between life and death.

682.content:
Paralogism (also: Interlude Chapter Act IV, Interlude Act IV, Crimes One and Two, The Hunger of Many): Interlude Chapter Act IV, set in Mondstadt as the Windblume Festival begins. Albedo is put on trial for murder, which proves a trap to expose an imposter made from the life force of the dragon Durin. Afterwards Albedo uses a Hexenzirkel trial to turn Mini Durin into a human.

The act has three quests: Crimes One and Two, The Hunger of Many and The Gardener. It follows Inversion of Genesis in the Interlude Chapter and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after that act and Traveler Observation Report. It was released in Version 5.6. It resolves Albedo's long watch over the fallen Durin on Dragonspine.

Plot: Odd behaviour among Mondstadt's townsfolk and a murder trial of Albedo greet the Traveler on their return for Windblume. The trial is staged to flush out a copy of Hertha, monsters attack the city, and Albedo and the Hexenzirkel's Alice help him create a human Durin.

Three quests. Crimes One and Two: Albedo is tried for murder and the Traveler investigates, until a second Hertha exposes the first as a copy spawned by Durin's remains. The Hunger of Many: monsters attack the city, Albedo explains the trial was a trap, and the Hexenzirkel is called in. The Gardener: after a chessboard trial set by Alice, Albedo turns Mini Durin human at the start of Windblume.

Revelations: The "murderer" Albedo is innocent of the disappearances; the strange behaviour and the Hertha accusing him come from imposters created from the dragon Durin's remains.

Albedo was stationed on Dragonspine to watch Durin, whose remains spawn mimics. Dahlia is secretly Barbatos' herald as well as an official of the Church. Mini Durin takes over the dead Durin's body to be reborn as a human with Albedo's alchemy.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Albedo; Jean; Kaeya; Venti; Dahlia; Durin (Mini Durin).

Also Diluc, Eula, Rosaria, Sucrose, Klee, Hertha and her imposter, Skeiron and Note, Alice, Barbeloth, Phonia, Amber, Barbara, Mika. Varka is voice-only by call and away at Nod-Krai.

Consequences: Albedo is cleared, the city survives the attack, Phonia is held, and Durin starts a new life as a human. The Traveler receives a Hexenzirkel gift.

Placement: Interlude Chapter Act IV, following Inversion of Genesis. Released in Version 5.6; between 5.6 and 6.0 Quick Start could open it at Adventure Rank 28 after A New Star Approaches. Completing it is required to unlock Song of the Welkin Moon Act I, A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves.

683.content: The Knights and Church jointly try Albedo for murder and illegal disposal of remains. Hertha prosecutes, Kaeya defends, Dahlia assesses and Jean presides because Varka is away. It was a pretext arranged beforehand to lure out an imposter.

684.content: Durin's life force produces spawn that consume people and take their form; acting on that power destabilises the other spawn. Albedo killed two spawn that had consumed people and buried what remained. The double of Albedo he killed on Dragonspine was different: a failed Homunculus Project specimen abandoned in Durin's stomach.

685.content: A pact among the Knights and Church of Favonius, the Anemo Archon and the Hexenzirkel for times of need. Varka secured the Hexenzirkel's aid, and Alice joins the conference as a giant Dodoco.

686.comment: Paralogism: The Game Before the Gate
686.content: Alice shrinks the party to fight on a chessboard at the Imaginarium Theater. After the first half Barbeloth turns the king and queen into the Ascended King and Sublimated Queen, and the Traveler and Albedo defeat them to earn the reagents.

key: Path to the Flaming Peaks World Quest series
687.content:
Path to the Flaming Peaks (also: Path to the Flaming Peaks World Quest series, Nahuatzin's Leap): Path to the Flaming Peaks (5.5) has a single quest, Nahuatzin's Leap. The party rides a Spiritway to the Skyfire Circlet, climb to the top and jump into the volcano. The golden text that has been guiding Little One grows clearer as they approach. Paimon is nervous about the height and the gaseous phlogiston, and notes that a Qucusaur grabs a statue and dives into the crater before them. The leap takes the party into the Ancient Sacred Mountain, the area explored in the following chapters.

Plot: Riding the Spiritway, Paimon wonders what is inside the volcano and worries it will be full of liquid phlogiston. On the Skyfire Circlet, Little One sees golden words telling it to climb to the highest pinnacle, hurl itself into the Sacred Mountain's flames, break the golden seal and reveal the radiance of remnant flames. They feel clearer to it than before. Paimon suspects whoever is speaking is inside the mountain.

At the summit, Paimon recalls being told there is a lot of gaseous phlogiston at the volcano's mouth; an attempt to jump without preparation sends them back to a waypoint. A strange statue near the rim is seized by a Qucusaur, which dives into the crater. The Traveler realises they can pass through the gas as the Qucusaur does. Paimon is frightened but agrees; Little One joins in, and the three leap together.

Revelations: The only story point is the confirmation that the golden voice leads Little One towards the Sacred Mountain and that the mountain's interior is reached from the Skyfire Circlet.

Characters: Little One, Paimon and the Traveler. Paimon provides the comic relief about weight and fear of heights; Little One responds with growls. Kimosi is mentioned in a conditional line. The golden-text speaker is unnamed here.

Consequences: Rewards are Adventure EXP, Primogems, Mora, Hero's Wit and Mystic Enhancement Ore. The leap opens the Ancient Sacred Mountain map, which the player can enter only through this quest.

Placement: Version 5.5. In story order it follows Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm and The Way Into the Mountain (which can no longer be started once the leap is done) and precedes Chronicler of the Crumbling City and A Finale Emberforged.

688.comment: Path to the Flaming Peaks: Skyfire Circlet leap
688.content: The Skyfire Circlet is the high rim around the volcano's crater. Paimon recalls being warned about heavy gaseous phlogiston at the crater mouth. A Qucusaur that steals a statue and dives in shows the way: the party must move through the gas the same way as the Qucusaur does. Golden text tells Little One to climb to the circlet's highest pinnacle and leap.

689.content:
Pavo Ocellus Chapter (also: Kaeya's Story Quest, Secret Pirate Treasure, Kaeya's Troubles): Kaeya's Story Quest, set in Mondstadt. Kaeya says his pirate grandfather buried a legendary sword and asks the Traveler to find it before Treasure Hoarders do. The hunt follows map clues around Mondstadt, and at the end Kaeya reveals it was a ruse to lure out a Treasure Hoarder leader.

The chapter has one act, Secret Pirate Treasure, of three quests: Kaeya's Troubles, Mystery of the Arcadian Ruins and Kaeya's Gain. It belongs to version 1.0 and unlocks at Adventure Rank 5 after The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. The Traveler can solve the clues with or without Kaeya's help.

Plot: After Stormterror's attack, Kaeya tells the Traveler his grandfather was a pirate who buried a sword from Celestia. Treasure Hoarders are active nearby. Following clues from an informant, the Traveler reaches the ruins, where Hoarder leader Izzard ambushes them. Kaeya arrives and reveals the treasure hunt was a trap.

Kaeya's Troubles: at Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Kaeya looks worried and leads the Traveler and Paimon to the courtyard. He says his grandfather, a pirate, buried a legendary sword from Celestia to avoid conflict among his fellows, and he fears local Treasure Hoarders will find the ruins. He suggests asking at the Adventurers' Guild.

Mystery of the Arcadian Ruins: no one at the Guild knows of the ruins. Kaeya says he found an informant who will only meet in Whispering Woods. They rescue her from monsters; she gives them a map with a riddle about three six-armed giants in the city in the lake, two guarding a statue and one the treasure. This points to the windmills of Mondstadt. A second riddle found at a windmill leads to a waterfall behind Springvale, where they find the map to the Arcadian ruins.

Kaeya's Gain: at the end of the ruins, Izzard ambushes the Traveler and Paimon. Kaeya arrives and reveals the treasure hunt was a ploy. Izzard flees and wakes a Ruin Guard, which the Traveler and Kaeya destroy before arresting him. Kaeya apologises for the deception and offers the Traveler the Harbinger of Dawn.

Revelations: The treasure hunt was a ruse to trap a Treasure Hoarder leader.

Kaeya admits he tricked the Traveler. The wiki summary does not confirm whether the sword exists or whether his grandfather was a pirate.

Characters: Kaeya, the Traveler and Paimon.

Izzard, a Treasure Hoarder leader, and the informant Vile.

Consequences: Izzard is captured and taken in for interrogation. Kaeya promises not to deceive the Traveler again and offers the Harbinger of Dawn.

Placement: Unlocks at Adventure Rank 5 after Prologue Act I, The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, and takes place after Stormterror's attack on Mondstadt. Released in 1.0.

690.comment: Pavo Ocellus Chapter: Secret Pirate Treasure
690.content: In Kaeya's Story Quest, Kaeya claims his pirate grandfather buried a legendary Celestia sword in ruins near Mondstadt. The Traveler follows riddles about windmills and a waterfall behind Springvale to the ruins, only to learn that Kaeya was baiting a Treasure Hoarder leader, Izzard.

691.content:
Perilous Trail (also: Interlude Chapter Act II, Perilous Trail Archon Quest): Interlude Chapter Act II. After the Chasm is reopened, the Traveler and Paimon meet Yanfei, Yelan, Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu at the Chasm Nail. The ground gives way and the group is trapped in a chaotic underground space, where they find Xiao hunting for news of his lost brother-in-arms Bosacius. Together they escape, and Xiao learns what became of him.

The act has five quests: The Unexpected Guest, Chasmic Maze, Danger All Around, End of the Line and At Tunnel's End, Light. It is a small-cast Liyue story that pairs the Traveler with characters who rarely meet, and it resolves a long-standing Yaksha question. During its first run it was a time-limited event with a lowered Adventure Rank requirement; the permanent act is canon for all players with the prerequisites.

Plot: Curious about the Chasm after the spiritstone incident, the Traveler and Paimon return to the Chasm Nail and run into Yanfei, then Itto and Shinobu, then Yelan. The ground collapses and the group falls into the Chasm's Bed, a looping space they cannot leave. Xiao, searching for Bosacius, helps them reach the surface with an ancient compass, nearly sacrificing himself.

Yanfei is at the Chasm Nail on secret business; Itto and Shinobu are chasing her (Shinobu came to Liyue for her Tongwen Academy certificate, which the Sakoku Decree had kept her from collecting). Yelan arrives and warns everyone off, Itto takes offense, and the ground collapses into the Chasm's Bed. There they meet Xiao, who is looking for Bosacius, and enter an illusion-filled domain that loops back on itself and keeps them from feeling hunger or time passing. Doors show each person's worst fear. Yanfei works out that it is an antlion's den of chaotic rules, they rescue Xiao from an illusion, and Itto punches open a new path. Treasure Hoarders and Fatui agents are beaten, Xiao ends a remnant of Bosacius' memory, and a Fantastic Compass lifts the group out. Xiao is hurled to safety and then rescued by Zhongli; Xiao and the Traveler agree those who died defending Liyue are heroes.

Revelations: The Nameless Yaksha of the Chasm battle was Bosacius, Xiao's missing comrade, who died defending Liyue.

The Chasm's depths hold a chaotic, illusion-laden space (the Chasm's Bed), which the wiki notes long predates the cataclysm and which was used to seal the invading monsters. The Fantastic Compass is an exorcism catalyst blending mortal magic arts with adeptal power.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Yanfei; Yelan; Arataki Itto (with Ushi); Kuki Shinobu; Xiao; Zhongli (indirectly).

Bosacius appears only as a memory remnant. Ningguang is mentioned in connection with Yelan. Fatui agents and Treasure Hoarders appear as enemies.

Consequences: Xiao finally knows what happened to Bosacius. Yanfei offers a Liyue tour to Itto and Shinobu, and Xiao invites the Traveler to Pervases' temple. The Chasm remains a dangerous place with more history below.

Placement: Second act of the Interlude Chapter, after The Crane Returns on the Wind and before Inversion of Genesis. Released in Version 2.7. It follows the Chasm world quest line (including the spiritstone) and the Traveler's search for their sibling continues in the background.

692.content: In Perilous Trail the Fantastic Compass is an exorcism catalyst combining human magic arts and adeptal power. A large version and a smaller one appear inside the Chasm's illusion space. Together they carry the group to the surface, but the compass is part of the illusion and cannot be taken out. According to the wiki's Bosacius history, it was brought to the Chasm by Boyang and Rongzhao in the original battle.

key: Forest Boar and the Little Witch event
693.content:
Phantasmal Pals (also: Little Hexenzirkel's Secret Base, Forest Boar and the Little Witch event): The story runs in three parts. In the first, Paimon and the Traveler meet Prune near Chinju Forest and learn that the little witches are looking after a talking Forest Boar named Popcorn, who turns out to be an imaginary friend. In the second, the Yumekui-Baku explain that Popcorn was warped by a nightmare fragment and the group collects the fragments. In the third, the nightmares are devoured, Popcorn is reunited with his now-adult human Homura, and Prune finally admits why she is searching for witches.

Plot: Part I, The Forest Boar and the Little Witch. Wanting a rest, Paimon and the Traveler head for Aisa Bathhouse, overhear rumours of a rampaging Forest Boar and a strange child asking about a witch, and go to Chinju Forest. There they meet Prune, who says she is a friend of Alice and carries a bell that detects magical fluctuations. The bell leads to a Cryo Whopperflower, then to a card asking children with imaginary friends to find the Dough King. Prune suspects a trap, but the little witches' secret base turns out to be a harmless hideout. Part II, If You Should Forget the Entrance to Dreams. The Dough King, a Yumekui-Baku, and a baku named Hyakujitsuhaku Shion explain that Popcorn is bound up with a nightmare fragment. The Traveler, Paimon, Prune and the four little witches collect three more fragments around Inazuma and share a meal with the baku. Part III, The Magic That Never Fails. The baku devour the fragments and Popcorn recovers his memory. He leads the group to Homura, an overworked young adult who has forgotten him; Prune confesses her own secret, and Alice reveals the larger design behind the quest.

Revelations: Popcorn is an imaginary friend who became visible and unstable after contact with a nightmare fragment, a materialised accumulation of negative emotions. His human, Homura, is now an adult overworked in her first job; the baku say her failure to resist her own nightmare signals emotional numbness. Alice tells the Traveler and Paimon that she never captured Descartes: his existence was close to fading because Prune, a precocious child who grew up too fast, was losing her childlike innocence. Alice invented the quest to send Prune to Mondstadt and the little witches, and chose Mondstadt because freedom nurtures imagination and she wanted Klee to have someone else to play with.

Characters: Main: the Traveler and Paimon, Prune, Klee, Qiqi, Sayu and Yaoyao. Also: the Dough King (Kohaku), Hyakujitsuhaku Shion (a Yumekui-Baku), Popcorn, Homura, Homura's boss, Kirara, Arataki Itto, Alice (voice and finale appearance), and Descartes. Imaginary friends who appear in the finale include Dodoco (Klee), Gena (Sayu) and Yuegui and Tuantuan (the pair from the Yaoyao minigame), as well as Descartes.

Consequences: Popcorn returns to normal, is reunited with Homura, and she resolves to deal with her work situation more openly. Prune joins the Little Hexenzirkel and is reunited with Descartes. Alice makes the little witches' imaginary friends visible for the celebration. Players received the weapon appearance Super Awesome Magic Key, which stays available after the event, and the five imaginary friends and a group photo as event items.

Placement: Released in Version 6.6 ("Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana"), 22 May to 8 June 2026, Adventure Rank 30 and the Chapter II Act I part "Ritou Escape Plan" required. Prune mentions in passing that she has climbed rooftops in Nod-Krai and that she moved to Mondstadt not long ago (Klee's words). It is a stand-alone story, not part of an Archon Quest.

694.content: A talking Forest Boar who is the imaginary friend of a young adult named Homura, who works for a company in Inazuma City. He was found wandering, fast and angry, with patchy memory, after a nightmare fragment materialised him. He repeats a rhyme Homura wrote as a child and insists she is the best no matter what. After the baku devour the fragments he recovers his memory and goes back to her.

695.content: A children's club founded by Klee, with Sayu, Yaoyao and Qiqi as the other members, plus Paimon and later Prune. Yaoyao suggested the "Little" because they still have growing to do. Membership needs only an invitation from Klee, who can give each member an introduction magic that Alice taught her. The group meets in a secret base, shares snacks and toys, and treats the Hexenzirkel's real witches as models. Not to be confused with the Hexenzirkel itself.

696.content: The Dough King, also called Kohaku, and the baku Hyakujitsuhaku Shion (who speaks of patients at a clinic and is in charge while Mizuki is away) explain that Yumekui-Baku are dough-bodied youkai who help humans regulate their emotions by devouring nightmares. They cannot easily carry tools, so they ask the Traveler's group to bring them the fragments. The baku fast beforehand and prepare the fragments with seasoning.

697.content: A fragment is a materialised accumulation of negative emotions. Popcorn carries the same signature as the one found near him, and there are three more at locations in Inazuma. Because devouring one early could make the others more volatile, the group gathers all four before the baku eat them together.

698.content: Prune presents herself as a professional investigator and a friend of Alice, but admits at the end that she is a Witch Hunter whose imaginary friend, the puppy Descartes, was gone after she lost a debate to Alice. Alice later says she did not take Descartes and had created the whole task to help Prune. Prune joins the Little Hexenzirkel and Descartes returns.

key: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle Chapter
The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar
The Tale of the Gate Stone
699.content:
Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle (also: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle Chapter, For a Green Island..., Gift of the Mirage, The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar, The Tale of the Gate Stone, Echoes of an Unfinished Past): Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle is a Nod-Krai World Quest series on Hiisi Island, added in Version 6.0 (Luna I). Four quests can be done in any order: a flustered young Frostmoon priestess named Verna tries to calm unstable kuuvahki at Thunderclap Reef, an angler is puzzled by empty waters, a child hunts for pretty stones, and a self-styled master thief hunts a crab. Each leaves a stone fragment on a large rock that later flies to a pillar at the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper. The fifth quest opens a sealed sanctum and meets the recorded echo of Aila, the first Moonchanter.

The tone is comic on the surface (a priestess who "trusts science", a thief with borrowed bravado) with a quieter thread: a robed woman who speaks in riddles keeps appearing and, in the end, is explained by Aila's recorded blessing. The series is also the Traveler's first sustained contact with Frostmoon Scions customs outside the main Archon Quest.

Plot: For a Green Island... In Thunderclap Reef the Traveler and Paimon meet Verna, a priestess in a kuuvahki-resistant suit who is on a secret mission to calm the reef's unstable kuuvahki. Her plan, which she calls science, is to throw charged stone fragments at two huge rotating boulders. Her Kraka robots fetch the fragments but get stuck, so the Traveler retrieves them; the first attempt makes things worse before a third fragment is found. A robed woman waits there, calls the Traveler the hero of "Elysium", hands over the last fragment in a Moon Mirror, and says she will wait at the Court of the First Edict. A Frostnight Scion wakes and must be defeated; afterwards the third fragment is freed and the boulders fly toward the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper.

Gift of the Mirage. The angler Pekkani, who is not a Frostmoon Scion and has no kuuvahki power, is catching no fish and asks the Traveler to look under the water west of the Frostmoon Enclave. Fragments placed on a stone there raise a platform and make a big rock fly off; the fish return.

The Tale of the Gate Stone. In the Frostmoon Enclave a child named Kasha is looking for pretty stones to give a friend named Mai, an outsider girl of about her age. The Traveler finds a kuuvahki-affected stone that Kasha senses wants to join a large stone; placing it makes the large stone rise and fly to the same pillar.

The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar. In a pit west of the Enclave a thief named Maite Veliu, who claims to be the heir of the legendary thief Reed Miller, recruits the Traveler to take a treasure from the Crab Tsar. The Traveler clears blocked passages with the help of rock crabs, breaks a Moon Mirror at the advice of the same robed woman, and defeats the Crab Tsar, which has been carrying a large stone. The stone flies away and the crab, ashamed, hides.

Echoes of an Unfinished Past. See below (this quest is unlocked after the other four).

Revelations: - The unstable kuuvahki at Thunderclap Reef worsened after two large stones fell from the sky; Verna says it has always been unstable since the first Moonchanter's time.
- The Court of the First Edict, a sacred site of the Frostmoon Scions, was sealed about five hundred years ago by Aila, the first Moonchanter.
- The robed woman is probably tied to Aila (see uncertainties). Aila's recording says its blessing only records awareness, and that she steered the Traveler with the fallen stones because the Traveler's thread would not catch in the loom of this world.

Characters: Verna, a young priestess who misquotes scripture, trusts robots and blames "science" for her plans. Pekkani, an angler. Kasha, a child of the Frostmoon Enclave who tells stories borrowed from outside. Maite Veliu, a young thief and Conch Gang member. The Crab Tsar, a large crab. Aila, the first Moonchanter, seen as a recorded echo. Solovei, a voice speaking with Aila. Ehrnrooth, Krodo and Rahetar, Frostmoon Scions who pursue the intruders. Paimon and the Traveler throughout.

Consequences: The large stones are returned to the pillar at the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper, and the Court of the First Edict is opened for the first time in five hundred years. Verna is taken to answer to the Lady Moonchanter. The Traveler gains Maite's IOU and notes, and the final quest's reward list includes Moonweaver's Dawn, presumably the sword Aila left (the wiki does not state this outright).

Placement: Released in Version 6.0 (Luna I, 2025-09-10) alongside the first Nod-Krai content. The four opening quests can be done in any order; Echoes of an Unfinished Past unlocks only after the other four. The wiki's chapter infobox uses the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter image.

700.comment: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle: Verna and the Kraka robots
700.content: Verna (full self-styled name Vernadska) is a young Frostmoon priestess in a kuuvahki-resistant suit and helmet who forgets scripture, trusts "science" and builds small Kraka robots. She introduces herself with a grand ritual line, takes the Traveler for a moon-blessed saviour, and hides that she is acting alone and against her faction's wishes because most Scions distrust technology. Her plans frequently go wrong and she admits she is panicking only after pretending not to.

701.comment: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle: Crab Tsar and Crab Tsar's Palace
701.content: The Crab Tsar is a large crab ruling a cave palace west of the Frostmoon Enclave. It was normally docile until it carried a fallen stone on its back; the stone made it aggressive toward smaller crabs and allowed it to pass through old Moon Mirrors. After the Traveler defeats it, the stone flies off and the crab hides in remorse. Maite calls the stone a "stone of desire", a name she says came from Hidimbi.

702.comment: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle: Maite Veliu and the Conch Gang
702.content: Maite Veliu is a young self-styled master thief who claims descent from the legendary thief Reed Miller and is a member of the Conch Gang. She talks big and gets scared easily, wants the Crab Tsar's treasure, and later pays back the Traveler with an IOU and notes. She mentions Katya in Nasha Town as the person the Traveler must settle bills with, and warns that the Frostmoon Scions are dangerous. Kasha's story of catching a girl called Mai fits her own account of being caught, though no quest says so outright.

703.content:
Pomum de Ambra Chapter (Emilie) (also: Pomum de Ambra Chapter, Emilie's Story Quest, Floral Debt, Blood Due): The Pomum de Ambra Chapter is Emilie's Story Quest (Version 4.8). Its single act, Floral Debt, Blood Due, takes the Traveler and Paimon to a flower exhibition in Port Ormos, Sumeru, where Emilie, a perfumer from Fontaine, is chasing rumours that the extinct flower "Auguste" has returned. A murder case follows that exposes the flower's dark origin.

The act has three quests named after perfume notes: Top Note: Floral Debt, Middle Note: Blood Due and Base Note: Auguste. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and completion of Masquerade of the Guilty, the Fontaine Archon Quest finale.

Plot: **Top Note: Floral Debt.** In Port Ormos the Traveler and Paimon meet Tighnari, who is helping with a flower exhibition. Paimon begins to sneeze and a stranger gives them incense that cures it: Emilie, a Fontaine perfumer. She explains the "Perfume Mania" of twenty years ago, when perfume prices soared. Only the perfume "Auguste" never fell back, because the flower it was named for went extinct when its flowerbeds burned. Rumours say Auguste has reappeared in Sumeru, and cheap counterfeits plague Fontaine's market, so Emilie has come to dispel the obsession. Her mentor Edgar, the exhibition's flower expert and creator of Auguste, is ill; she takes the group to a hotel to tell the rest.

**Middle Note: Blood Due.** The next day a guest, Lucien, is found dead in his room with no sign of forced entry; the only way in was through the room of his companion Sylvain. Emilie reasons that Sylvain's grief is genuine, though the sheriff Shyam fears he is the suspect. Sylvain confesses and reveals the truth about Auguste: it was produced by a Fatuus named Yelena using a Delusion, which wore down her body, and the flowers and perfume could harm people over long exposure. He hides the involvement of Yelena and Kirya. Edgar allows himself to be taken into custody. Emilie later finds that a Glaze Lily had been used to hide a sample of Auguste in a Slime Condensate mixture that releases scent at night, and concludes that the hotel was a trap laid by Kirya, who had been disguised as Edgar. Soon after, Edgar is reported attacked and missing.

Revelations: Auguste was created by a Fatuus, Yelena, with a Delusion, which wore down her body. The flowers and perfume were not dangerous in brief contact but could harm over the long term. The exhibition's flower expert "Edgar" and the schemer Kirya are the same man. The flower's extinction followed a fire in which Yelena died.

Characters: Emilie, the Traveler and Paimon, with Tighnari, Collei and Kirya (as Edgar). Yelena appears only through past events.

Emilie is the investigator and the emotional centre: precise with scents and people, and weary of the stories attached to her work. Tighnari and Collei assist on the Sumeru side. Kirya is both mentor and culprit. The sheriff Shyam, the Eremite Innam, the guests Sylvain and Lucien, and Oguz, Neriman and Sanjay appear in minor roles.

Consequences: Kirya is taken into custody by Eremites. For Emilie the myth of Auguste is closed and she releases a new perfume named after Yelena. The case has no world-level consequences.

Placement: Release order: 4.8. Story order: after Chapter IV Act V, Masquerade of the Guilty, though events happen in Port Ormos, Sumeru. This is not an Archon Quest.

704.comment: Pomum de Ambra Chapter (Emilie): Floral Debt, Blood Due
704.content: Act I of Emilie's Story Quest. In Port Ormos, Emilie and the Traveler investigate deaths linked to Auguste, a legendary flower and perfume created with a Delusion by the Fatuus Yelena, and catch the schemer Kirya.

705.content:
Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur (also: Chapter IV Act I, Fontaine Archon Quest Act I): Chapter IV Act I of the Archon Quest, set in Fontaine. After leaving Sumeru, the Traveler and Paimon arrive in the Hydro nation, meet the Archon Furina, and are drawn into a courtroom drama as the defence attorney for the magician Lyney, accused after a stage trick ends with a man dead and an audience member missing.

The act has three quests: Soloist's Prologue, The City of Rains and Remembrance, and Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights. It introduces Fontaine's trial-centred society, the water-level prophecy, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, the Fatui connection of Lyney and Lynette, and the investigators of the Spina di Rosula. Released in version 4.0.

Plot: At the Caravan Ribat the Traveler says goodbye to Dehya and heads for Fontaine. Furina has them charged with a minor law, but Lyney rescues them with a stage trick. Later, during Lyney's show at the Court of Fontaine, a man dies and a woman vanishes; the Traveler defends Lyney, and the trial ends with the real events exposed.

**Soloist's Prologue.** Before leaving Sumeru, the Traveler and Paimon meet Dehya, who offers a mercenary escort to the border and is turned down. At the Romaritime Harbor the locals Rena and Etienne explain that the Court of Fontaine works like an opera house, that Neuvillette and the Oratrice have ended false charges, and that Furina can only be seen by appointment. The Traveler meets Lynette, who says an area tied to a past memory is now underwater and that "they will be, too", and then her brother Lyney. Furina arrives with her entourage, welcomes the Traveler in her role as Archon, and declares a "duel" in court; she then points to a law against releasing a flying object on the first three days of a month and names Paimon as the offending object. Lyney snaps his fingers and a red cord of energy binds Paimon to the Traveler, so Paimon counts as a balloon that arrived attached, and Furina drops the matter, amused. Lyney explains the prophecy of rising water and gives the Traveler Magic Pockets to hand to residents near the waterline. The pair help him chase a pickpocket at the harbour, and Charlotte joins them on the aquabus to the court.

**The City of Rains and Remembrance.** At the twins' home they meet Freminet. Rain falls, which Lyney says usually happens when a trial is held. At the Beaumont Workshop, Truand of the Confrerie of Cabriere picks a fight, and Childe (Tartaglia), now in Fontaine, beats him; but Childe's Hydro weapons vanish mid-fight, and he says he has felt something stir in him. He recounts his time in the Abyss and his teacher Skirk, mentions he has been sparring with Fontaine's Champion Duelists, and entrusts the Traveler with his Vision before a duel against Clorinde.
