At the Fountain of Lucine a voice is heard, and Lynette offers a theory about tears and the fountain. In the opera house the Traveler sits next to Neuvillette, whom Lyney introduces. During the show, Lyney's box trick goes wrong: the tank falls and crushes the box, and Neuvillette locks down the house. Cowell is found dead in the box and the chosen audience member has gone missing, apparently the latest victim in the disappearances of young women. Furina names Lyney a suspect, turns the case into her second "duel", and invites the Traveler to act as defence.

**Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights.** The Traveler gathers evidence, meeting the sceptical Esmond and Navia of the Spina di Rosula, with her associates Silver and Melus. Lyney and Lynette demonstrate the box trick, and the group explores the tunnel under the stage. At trial, Furina exposes the twins as members of the Fatui's House of the Hearth, and Lyney confirms it. After a recess in which Lyney gives his account, the defence argues that Cowell used Primordial Sea water to change form. Esmond reports that Cowell's bag held labelled tubes of that water and that he belonged to a drug-selling organisation; Vaughn then produces the same water from Lyney's belongings. Navia arrives with the missing woman, who reappears from the magic box at Lyney's snap. She gives her name as Liliane (the harbour thief, not "Halsey") and confesses: terrified when the machine picked her and Lyney spoke of the Fortress of Meropide, she forced her way out of a soaked box, smashed a vase over Cowell's head in the confrontation, put him in the box, and hid in a costume chest. The Oratrice returns "Not Guilty" for the twins. Vaughn, exposed as Cowell's accomplice for presenting false evidence, begins to confess but dissolves into water before naming the "Boss". Afterwards Lyney explains the twins' past and apologises for the deception; Navia and her associates invite the Traveler to a farewell meal at Hotel Debord.

Revelations: Lyney and Lynette belong to the Fatui's House of the Hearth.

The twins are orphans who joined the House of the Hearth under the Knave, Arlecchino, who believes in the prophecy of Fontaine and intends to try to use the Hydro Gnosis to save Fontaine before taking it to Snezhnaya. A drug-selling organisation uses Primordial Sea water, and its member Vaughn dissolves into water on trying to name the "Boss". Childe is in Fontaine and his Hydro Vision is behaving oddly.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Furina; Neuvillette; Lyney and Lynette; Navia.

Also Dehya (farewell), Freminet, Clorinde (the Champion Duelist), Charlotte (reporter), Childe, Esmond, Cowell, Vaughn, Liliane, Truand, Estelle, Rena and Etienne, and Navia's associates Silver and Melus.

Consequences: Lyney and Lynette are acquitted but remain under suspicion for their Fatui ties. The Traveler has Childe's Vision in safekeeping. The act leads into Act II, As Light Rain Falls Without Reason, in which events around Childe unfold.

Placement: Chapter IV Act I, following Caribert (the end of Chapter III in Sumeru) and before Act II, As Light Rain Falls Without Reason. Released in version 4.0.

706.comment: Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur: Furina's court duels
706.content: Furina frames her meeting with the Traveler as a "duel" in court. First she tries to arrest them over a law against flying objects; later she becomes prosecutor against the Traveler as Lyney's attorney.

707.comment: Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur: The opera house incident
707.content: During Lyney and Lynette's first show, Cowell dies in a crushed magic box and a woman vanishes; the Traveler later shows she is Liliane the thief, who hid after striking Cowell.

708.comment: Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur: Primordial Sea water evidence
708.content: Tubes of Primordial Sea water in Cowell's bag point to a drug-selling organisation; Vaughn, who produced the same water from Lyney's belongings, dissolves into water before naming the Boss.

709.content:
Princeps Cretaceus Chapter (also: Albedo's Story Quest, Traveler Observation Report, The Rumored Alchemist): Albedo's Story Quest, set on Dragonspine. Sucrose asks the Traveler to help her master, the Chief Alchemist of the Knights of Favonius, with his research. Albedo, who believes the Traveler comes from another world, runs a series of experiments on their powers and nature, and ends the act with a quiet worry about himself.

The chapter has one act, Traveler Observation Report, of six quests: The Rumored Alchemist, The Genius Researcher and the Seed of Another World, then the First, Second, Third and Final Experiments (Elements, The World, Life, Withering Glory). It was released in version 1.2 and unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after For a Tomorrow Without Tears.

Plot: At Timaeus' alchemy store, Sucrose tells the Traveler her master Albedo needs help with an experiment on Dragonspine. Albedo concludes the Traveler is from another world and wants to see how life behaves outside Teyvat. Across five tests he examines their elemental ability, mind, cooking, movement and puzzle-solving. He decides they are much like an ordinary person of Teyvat, shows a flower grown from his otherworldly seed, and voices a private fear.

The Rumored Alchemist: Sucrose recognises the Traveler as the one who repelled Stormterror. She would like to study them herself, but says Albedo, a master alchemist consulted from across Teyvat, is troubled by an experiment, and is likely to reward help. He is on Dragonspine with Timaeus.

The Genius Researcher and the Seed of Another World: at the foot of the mountains the Traveler meets Barbara trying to bring Rosaria to choir practice; Rosaria refuses and is also looking for Albedo for a reason she will not share. They find Albedo sketching near a group of hilichurls, who attack; he finishes and explains alchemy until Rosaria leaves, bored. Recognising the Traveler as the Honorary Knight, he reasons their abilities mean they come from another world, and asks to experiment on how life functions outside Teyvat with a sample he has. Rosaria spies on them, wondering if he is a risk to Mondstadt.

The experiments: First, after a test against slimes, the Traveler drinks a potion extracting elemental power, with Starsilver Catalyst they find on the way to his mountain camp; Albedo remarks that peculiar people's essence differs from ordinary people's. Second, the Traveler tries and fails to break a pillar with their mind, cooks Sunshine Sprat, and finds an Anemo Crystalfly Extract and Electro Hypostasis Power with Elemental Sight; Albedo suspects Teyvat's natural laws affect them. Third, the Traveler jumps from a peak and crosses a lake; they are faster than the average Mondstadt citizen. Albedo says his interests are often fleeting because learning the truth gives him no satisfaction. Final: the Traveler solves a locked mechanism with Seelies, they find strange writing on a wall and Albedo copies it. Rosaria stops them, is persuaded the Traveler is no threat, sets up patrols and copies the script.

Revelations: Albedo believes the Traveler is from another world and studies them for it.

He finds the Traveler ordinary in nature but not in effect on his work. Strange writing is found on the wall of ruins in the Dragonspine foothills.

Characters: Albedo, Sucrose, the Traveler and Paimon.

Rosaria, Barbara and Timaeus.

Consequences: Albedo invites the Traveler back for future help. Rosaria starts patrols in the area and keeps a copy of the wall script, wary of Albedo.

Placement: Unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after Prologue Act II, For a Tomorrow Without Tears. Released in 1.2, with the Dragonspine content. The wiki trivia says that during the limited events The Chalk Prince and the Dragon and Shadows Amidst Snowstorms the requirement was lowered to Adventure Rank 20 with no story keys.

710.comment: Princeps Cretaceus Chapter: Traveler Observation Report
710.content: Albedo's series of tests on the Traveler on Dragonspine. He concludes the Traveler is like an ordinary person of Teyvat, though they come from elsewhere, and uses the otherworldly seed to bloom a flower. He ends by voicing a worry about losing control, and asks for the Traveler's help if it ever happens.

key: Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind
The Outlander Who Caught the Wind chapter
711.comment: Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind
711.content:
Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (also: Mondstadt Archon Quest, The Outlander Who Caught the Wind chapter): The Prologue, "The Outlander Who Caught the Wind", is the first Archon Quest chapter and is set in Mondstadt. The Traveler and their twin are stopped on their way between worlds by an unknown god, who seals the sibling away and strips the Traveler of power. The Traveler later wakes, meets Paimon, and goes to Mondstadt to seek the Anemo Archon, only to find the city threatened by the dragon Stormterror. With the bard Venti, who is the Archon Barbatos, the Traveler frees the dragon Dvalin from the Abyss Order's corruption, and Venti loses his Gnosis to the Fatui Harbinger Signora. The chapter ends by sending the Traveler to Liyue.

The chapter has three acts: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (Act I), For a Tomorrow Without Tears (Act II) and Song of the Dragon and Freedom (Act III), released in Version 1.0. It doubles as a tutorial for movement and combat and introduces the Knights of Favonius, the Fatui and the Abyss Order.

Plot: Opening and Act I. In the introductory quest Wanderer's Trail the twins, travelling from world to world, are confronted by an unknown god who calls herself the sustainer of heavenly principles and declares that "the arrogation of mankind ends now". The sibling is cubed and taken, and the Traveler is also sealed and left powerless. The Traveler awakes after an unstated time, and about two months before the story begins they save Paimon from drowning near Cape Oath. Paimon becomes their guide and suggests meeting the Seven to find the sibling. At Starfell Lake the Traveler activates an Anemo Statue of the Seven and sees a green dragon fly toward a forest. They find the dragon and a stranger trying to calm it, but the Traveler's power draws the dragon's attention, and the stranger leaves behind a crimson teardrop crystal. Amber, the Outrider of the Knights, offers to escort them to Mondstadt and gives them a Wind Glider. Stormterror, as locals call the dragon, then attacks, and the Traveler, helped unseen by the stranger, drives it off. Kaeya sends them to the Acting Grand Master, Jean, who asks them to deal with the Ley Line disruptions at the Four Winds' temples on Lisa's advice.

Act II. Back in the city, the Traveler is named an Honorary Knight after Jean rejects a Fatui diplomat who wants the dragon killed. Venti, who is the stranger from the forest, reveals that the dragon is Dvalin, one of the Four Winds, who is suffering and being exploited by the Abyss Order. Their plan to cure him needs the Holy Lyre der Himmel from the Favonius Cathedral. The Fatui seize it first; with the help of Diluc and Jean the party recovers it, repairs it with Dvalin's tears and summons the dragon at Starsnatch Cliff, but an Abyss Mage persuades him that Venti betrayed him, and the lyre is destroyed.

Act III. Diluc reports that an Abyss Mage has been killed at the winery and that its death released energy that was cutting Venti off from Dvalin. Venti breaks the barrier over Dvalin's hideout, the old Mondstadt of the tyrant Decarabian, and the party fights through hilichurls to a light actuator that Venti charges with Anemo power. The Traveler purges the corruption from Dvalin. Venti explains that he refused to order Dvalin to be free, since a command could not give freedom, and Dvalin leaves. Jean corrects the people's belief that the dragon appeared from nowhere.

Revelations: - The Traveler and their twin came from other worlds and were separated and sealed by an unnamed god; the Traveler has lost their power.
- Venti, the wandering bard, is Barbatos, the Anemo Archon.
- Stormterror is Dvalin, one of the Four Winds, who protected Mondstadt and was corrupted by the Abyss Order.
- The Fatui, acting through one of the Eleven Harbingers, will take a god's Gnosis by force. Signora removes Venti's.
- The Tsaritsa, the Cryo Archon, is one of the Seven and has broken from them since a catastrophe 500 years ago.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon: protagonists. Venti: the Anemo Archon in disguise as a bard. Dvalin: the afflicted dragon of the Four Winds. Knights of Favonius: Jean (Acting Grand Master), Kaeya (Cavalry Captain), Amber (Outrider), Lisa (Librarian). Diluc: winery owner and informal ally. Barbara: Church of Favonius deaconess. Signora: Fatui Harbinger, the chapter's villain. The Cryo Abyss Mage and the Abyss Order are the dragon's corrupters. The Traveler's sibling and the unknown god appear in cutscenes.

Consequences: Dvalin is freed and reconciled with Mondstadt; the people learn the truth of the dragon's attacks. The Traveler becomes an Honorary Knight. Venti loses his Gnosis, and the Fatui now hold it. The Traveler leaves for Liyue to seek the Geo Archon.

Placement: The first Archon Quest chapter, released in Version 1.0 and in story order before Chapter I. Its acts must be played in sequence: Act I, Act II, Act III.

712.comment: Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind: Wanderer's Trail Opening
712.content: In the opening cinematic the Traveler and their sibling are stopped by a white-clad god who calls herself the sustainer of heavenly principles and declares that "the arrogation of mankind ends now". She seals the sibling, then the Traveler, who loses their power. The Traveler later meets Paimon, who becomes a guide. The god is not named on screen; the wiki and later content identify her as Asmoday.

713.comment: Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind: Venti's Gnosis Taken
713.content: After the Dragon is calmed, Signora ambushes Venti outside the Favonius Cathedral and rips out his Gnosis, then flees before the Knights arrive. Venti tells the Traveler and Jean what a Gnosis is and who Signora is, and sends the Traveler to Liyue.

key: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine World Quest series
714.content:
Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine (also: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine World Quest series, Vagrants and Scamps, The Red and the Black, Questions and Answers, Sir Arthur case, Talochard and Curve case): Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine is a three-act world quest series in Fontaine, added in version 4.2. The steambird mascot Sir Arthur has vanished from the office of the newspaper The Steambird. The Traveler and Paimon help the Melusine detective Talochard, of the Marechaussee Phantom, and her investigation mek Curve to find him.

The series is a mystery with a comic start and a bittersweet ending. Its acts are "Vagrants and Scamps", "The Red and the Black" and "Questions and Answers". It requires the story quest "A Fontainian Message" to be complete.

Plot: Outside The Steambird's office the Traveler and Paimon settle an argument between the Melusine agent Talochard and the editor Jenck. Sir Arthur, the steambird, is missing. Euphrasie, the editor-in-chief, arrives with Curve, a Suppression Specialist Mek built by the scientist Mosso Lombroso, which the Marechaussee Phantom lets Talochard use for investigations. Clues lead from a drunk named Rocher to a boy, Kevin, and to a con-artist gang, the Elegant Tableware Confrerie, then to a Fatui officer who was hunting for Mosso's old research base and a threatening letter demanding Mosso's name be cleared.

The case turns out to hinge on a thirty-year-old scandal. Melo Lombroso, Mosso's granddaughter, reveals that Mosso staged his own disgrace to save Curve. A map hidden in a locket leads to Mosso's underwater base, where Jenck, who allied with the Fatui to take Euphrasie's post, triggers its self-destruction. Curve tells his first lie to get the others out and stays behind.

Revelations: - Sir Arthur's disappearance was not a random prank but connected to an old scandal: the thirty-year-old story that Mosso Lombroso had faked evidence for his lie-detector technology.
- That scandal was staged by Mosso himself. He had The Steambird publish the articles to draw public anger away from Curve and died in a duel instead of standing trial.
- Curve, the Marechaussee Phantom's investigation mek, sat in storage for thirty years before Talochard found him. His first lie lets the Traveler, Paimon and Talochard escape.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Talochard, a Melusine of the Marechaussee Phantom; Curve, a Suppression Specialist Mek; Euphrasie, the editor-in-chief of The Steambird, and Jenck, an editor; the drinker Rocher and his dog; the boy Kevin and his mother Madeleine; the con artists "Intrepid Valberry" and "Boss"; the Fatui Baulard/Baulande; and Melo Lombroso, Mosso's granddaughter. Mosso Lombroso appears through letters and recollection. Sir Arthur is the missing steambird.

Consequences: Sir Arthur is rebuilt, with Curve's recorded commendation of Talochard added to its voice library. Curve is lost with the research base. Jenck is found ruined. Baulande and his family leave to escape the Fatui.

Placement: Requires "A Fontainian Message". Released in version 4.2. Acts I to III are played in order over several in-game days.

715.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Talochard
715.content: Talochard is a Melusine agent attached to the Marechaussee Phantom who takes up the case of the missing steambird on her own account. She works with the investigation mek Curve. She is hard on herself when the case stalls, and her Poissonchant Pie is described as unique, which the group uses to trap the Confrerie. This entry covers the case only.

716.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Curve
716.content: Curve is a Suppression Specialist Mek built by the scientist Mosso Lombroso. Mosso's research was on lie-detector technology. Curve belongs to the Marechaussee Phantom and first lies at the destruction of Mosso's base, where he tells the group that his core can stop the self-destruct sequence. It can only open the door to the emergency room. He stays behind while the others escape.

717.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Sir Arthur
717.content: Sir Arthur is the steambird figure kept on a pedestal in the office of The Steambird. Its disappearance starts the case. Its parts are hidden at three places, and its head is held by Baulande. It is rebuilt after the case, with a voice library that contains Curve's commendation of Talochard.

718.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Jenck and Euphrasie
718.content: Euphrasie is the editor-in-chief of The Steambird. Jenck, one of her editors, helped the Fatui in order to take her post and set off the destruction of Mosso's base. He is later found broken and mute on the stage of the Opera Epiclese, with a note apologising to the Traveler, Paimon and Talochard.

719.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Baulard (Baulande)
719.content: Baulard, whose real name is Baulande, is a peripheral Fatui intelligence officer working for one of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers. He was searching for Mosso Lombroso's research base and took the first threatening letter from The Steambird's office. His wife Madeleine and son Kevin live in Fontaine. He hands over Sir Arthur's head and leaves with his family to escape the Fatui.

720.content:
Rapperia Chapter (also: Rapperia, Clorinde's Story Quest, Silent Night, Judgment Day, Hunters' Gathering, Buried Honor, Vanquishing Phantoms, Tabletop Troupe quest): Clorinde's Story Quest. She and Navia, both veterans of a local roleplaying club called the Tabletop Troupe, invite the Traveler, Furina and Lyney to play a new game about the Marechaussee Hunters. The script's author, Florian, has hidden a real purpose behind it, and the party ends up facing a real monster in a hidden vault and a church basement.

The chapter has one act, Silent Night, of four quests: Judgment Day, Hunters' Gathering, Buried Honor and Vanquishing Phantoms. It was released in version 4.7 and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty and The Little Oceanid. It shows the Champion Duelist's private life, her hobby as a Senior Game Master, and her private regard for the Hunters.

Plot: Clorinde and Navia recruit the Traveler for a game, Marechaussee Hunter: Judgment Day. Play begins in the Court of Fontaine and the party roleplays as Hunters. The party solves puzzles in an old vault, only to be attacked in the dark by a real Hunter, Florian, who is controlled by a monster. Clorinde calms him, and the party fights the Devorator in a church basement, with Florian offering himself as the target. Afterwards they learn the script was a cover.

Judgment Day: Navia and Clorinde, one player short, ask the Traveler to make a fourth. Lyney and Furina join, and Florian, the script manager, explains that the story is adapted from the real history of the Marechaussee Hunters, who hunted monsters with a swordsmanship passed down through generations. Clorinde will help by adding commentary.

Hunters' Gathering: the party roleplays as Hunters arriving in a hollow city that has sent a distress call. Players pick skills such as medicine, cooking and insight, and each can change how scenes go. They gather information, defeat monsters in a forest and find a chest.

Buried Honor: the next day the game moves to a set modelled on a prison, then a palace, and then to a hidden secret vault. The script seems to end, so Clorinde improvises. The party solves puzzles and collects three of four keys. In a darkened fight Clorinde defeats a 'guard', who turns out to be Florian. Florian says he is a descendant of Hunters, resented that his father died forgotten, and was driven by a voice. Clorinde reads it as a Devorator.

Vanquishing Phantoms: Florian asks to be the bait for the Devorator in the church basement. Clorinde accepts his request as a Champion Duelist. The monster takes him and he becomes a golem. The party defeats it by calling the names of the Marechaussee Hunters. Afterwards Florian explains and Clorinde forgives him.

Revelations: The script was a lure created by Florian, a descendant of Marechaussee Hunters, to get the last key from Clorinde. A Devorator was manipulating him.

The 'treasure' in the vault is a tablet of Hunters' names and their weapons. Clorinde herself is a Marechaussee Hunter, which she does not want publicised.

Characters: Clorinde, Navia, Furina, Lyney, the Traveler and Paimon.

Florian, the script manager of the Tabletop Troupe and a descendant of Hunters. Este and Walter, Hunters named on the tablet.

Consequences: Florian offers to turn himself in to the Garde, but Clorinde judges that he has suffered enough and sends him to return the keys. The vault is left undisturbed, with its secret kept among the party.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty and the Animula Choragi Chapter's The Little Oceanid. Released in 4.7. The setting spans the Court of Fontaine, the Fontaine Research Institute region and the Beryl Region.

721.content: A roleplaying club in the Court of Fontaine whose games let friends take part in a story. Clorinde and Navia are veteran members, and Clorinde is a Senior Game Master. Lyney is a casual member who is usually the game master of his own sibling games. Florian is a script manager who writes for the club.

722.content: A script manager of the Tabletop Troupe and the son of a Hunter. After his father died forgotten, bitterness and a Devorator drove him to steal Hunter keys and lure Clorinde to a hidden vault. Clorinde forgives him in the end, and he volunteers to be the Devorator's bait in a duel to restore his honour.

723.content: A monster active centuries ago that amplifies the desires and obsessions in people's hearts until they take over. Marechaussee Hunters sealed it away with a key in four parts. It reacts to the names of the Hunters of its own era.

724.content:
Requiem of the Echoing Depths (also: Chapter II Act IV, Liyue Chasm Archon Quest): Chapter II Act IV of the Archon Quest. The Traveler and Paimon investigate odd hilichurl activity in The Chasm, find the Inverted City, and meet Dainsleif again. Together they discover that hilichurls are gathering there to live out their last days, and stop the Abyss Order's attempt to amplify a pool that eases the Khaenri'ahn curse.

The act has four quests: In the Depths, an Unexpected Reunion; The Grave of the Guarded; Memories of Inteyvat; and The Black Serpent Knights' Glory. In it the Traveler asks Dainsleif directly about his background and about his past with their sibling, and it introduces Halfdan, one of his former subordinates. Released in version 2.6.

Plot: Yuehui, a miner, asks the Traveler to look into hilichurls in The Chasm. In the underground mines they find an Inverted City, and Dainsleif joins them. They learn that the hilichurls are gathering near a pool that weakens the curse, guarded by Black Serpent Knights. The Abyss Order tries to amplify the pool; Halfdan gives his life to delay it and the Traveler destroys the device.

In the Depths, an Unexpected Reunion: Paimon and the Traveler accept Yuehui's commission, suspect the Abyss Order, and go through the underground mines to an Inverted City that reminds them of the Defiled Statue. Dainsleif then steps out of a portal behind them, having pursued an Abyss Herald through it and lost it. The same thing happened when he last chased the Traveler's sibling into a portal. The Traveler asks about his background and about his relationship to the sibling: he says "Twilight Sword" was his title as captain of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard five hundred years ago, and that the sibling was his travelling companion in a search for their fates, though they "did not make it to the journey's end together". He changes the subject to the Order's likely plans, and they continue inward.

The Grave of the Guarded: Dainsleif suspects the hilichurls have come to The Chasm to live out their last days, because the place seems to ease the curse of immortality laid on Khaenri'ahns in the cataclysm, though he does not know how. Two Black Serpent Knights, once his subordinates who lost their minds to the curse, attack; a third Knight only stares at Dainsleif and retreats. At the Inverted City he judges it older than Khaenri'ah. After the party defeats more Knights they find the Knights were protecting a group of dying hilichurls. The earlier Knight halts reinforcements with a silent order. Dainsleif believes it is Halfdan, a royal guard elite whom he ordered to tell all Black Serpent Knights to protect the people of Khaenri'ah at all costs; despite the curse eroding their minds, the Knights are still trying to carry out that order. The group climbs to the summit and finds a water pool, a relic of the ancient civilisation and the source of the area's curse-weakening effect, surrounded by strange devices. Halfdan arrives and urges them to follow.

Memories of Inteyvat: Halfdan leads them to a hilichurl camp where the Traveler finds an Inteyvat, Khaenri'ah's national flower. Touching it shows a vision of the sibling and an Abyss Herald discussing amplifying the pool's properties, lifting the curse from the gathered hilichurls and restoring "the homeland". Dainsleif calls this futile given the curse's reality-altering nature and expects only more suffering for the hilichurls. The Traveler chooses to help him stop it, holding that the sibling has no right to subject others to near-certain suffering for the slimmest chance of redemption. As they leave, the Order starts its plan, an Abyss Herald delays them, and after it falls the group rushes back to the device.

The Black Serpent Knights' Glory: they enter the chamber as an Abyss Lector activates the amplification device, which causes agonising pain to everyone cursed. Halfdan sacrifices himself to hold the device back temporarily, giving the Traveler time to defeat the Lector and destroy the mechanisms. Afterwards Halfdan's soul appears, speaks briefly with Dainsleif and passes on. Dainsleif leaves to recover and to investigate the Order's Loom of Fate project; the Traveler and Paimon report to Yuehui.

Revelations: Black Serpent Knights are former Khaenri'ahn soldiers who still guard their people; the Order wants to remove the curse from hilichurls by amplifying an ancient pool.

Dainsleif's title "Twilight Sword" is that of captain of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard five hundred years ago, and the sibling was his travelling companion in a quest to find their fates. Hilichurls appear to gather at The Chasm to live out their last days because the place weakens the curse. The Inverted City is of an older civilisation than Khaenri'ah. The Abyss Order intends to remove the curse from the gathered hilichurls and "restore the homeland".

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Dainsleif and Halfdan.

Yuehui, a miner who commissions the investigation; the Traveler's sibling (seen in a vision); an Abyss Herald; an Abyss Lector; and other Black Serpent Knights. The hilichurls of The Chasm appear as people at the end of their lives.

Consequences: The amplification device is destroyed and Halfdan dies and passes on. Dainsleif goes to recover and to look into the Loom of Fate. The Traveler has stated openly that they oppose their sibling's plan.

Placement: Chapter II Act IV, following Omnipresence Over Mortals and The Crane Returns on the Wind and preceding Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark (Chapter III Act I, Sumeru). Adventure Rank 30 per the wiki. Released in version 2.6.

725.comment: Requiem of the Echoing Depths: Inverted City and the pool
725.content: In the depths of The Chasm's underground mines lies an Inverted City, which Dainsleif judges older than Khaenri'ah. At its summit is a water pool, a relic of the ancient civilisation, that weakens the curse of immortality on Khaenri'ahns. The Abyss Order's devices around it are meant to amplify this effect.

726.comment: Requiem of the Echoing Depths: Halfdan
726.content: Dainsleif identifies a Black Serpent Knight as Halfdan, a royal guard elite at the cataclysm whom he ordered to tell the Knights to protect the people of Khaenri'ah. Though cursed and mindless, Halfdan restrains other Knights and leads the party to the hilichurl camp. He sacrifices himself holding back the amplification device, and his soul speaks with Dainsleif before passing on.

727.comment: Requiem of the Echoing Depths: Inteyvat
727.content: The national flower of Khaenri'ah. In a hilichurl camp in The Chasm the Traveler touches one and sees a vision of their sibling and an Abyss Herald discussing the plan to amplify the pool and restore "the homeland".

key: Ritou Travel Permit World Quest series
728.content:
Ritou Travel Permit (also: Ritou Travel Permit World Quest series, Chisato's Letter): The quest follows Ritou Escape Plan, in which the Traveler secretly gets off Ritou with Chisato's help. The two belong to different institutions (the Hiiragi Clan leads the Kanjou Commission; Kamaji is a Kujou Clan member and a Tenryou Commission enforcer), and Kamaji worries that closeness between them could be exploited, so an outsider carries the letter.

Plot: Chisato asks the Traveler to take her letter to Kamaji. The Traveler may first speak to Sanada, a Tenryou Commission subordinate who sends them to find Kamaji himself, walking near the bridge. Kamaji recognises the handwriting with relief and agrees to approve the permit as a personal favour to Chisato, but asks the Traveler to wait at Kiminami Restaurant while he prepares it.

Revelations: - The relationship between Chisato and Kamaji is a private romance between a Hiiragi and a Kujou, which Kamaji says could be taken advantage of by others given their positions.
- Kamaji's cover story for the gift (a return courtesy toward Shinsuke) is one he tells Anna; he is open about the real reason with the Traveler.

Characters: Hiiragi Chisato (daughter of Hiiragi Shinsuke, head of the Hiiragi Clan), Kujou Kamaji, Kiminami Anna, Sanada (minor), Paimon and the Traveler. Takayuki and Shinsuke are only mentioned.

Consequences: The Traveler receives a Travel Permit, which allows free entry to and exit from Ritou, plus Adventure EXP, Mora and Hero's Wit. Speaking to Chisato again afterwards, following a certain dialogue branch, gives a 4-star Storm Cage artifact once.

Placement: Released in 2.6, as a follow-up to Ritou Escape Plan, among the Inazuma world quests that follow the Traveler's arrival in Ritou under the Sakoku Decree. It is unrelated to the main Archon Quest beyond its setting.

729.content: The Travel Permit is the document Kujou Kamaji issues in Chisato's Letter. It lets the holder move freely into and out of Ritou, which the Sakoku Decree otherwise restricts. It is issued as a personal favour to Chisato and not as a general policy.

730.content:
Rosa Multiflora Chapter (Navia) (also: Rosa Multiflora Chapter, Navia's Story Quest, Braving the Tides Together): The Rosa Multiflora Chapter is Navia's Story Quest (Version 4.3), set in Fontaine after Masquerade of the Guilty. In its one act, Braving the Tides Together, she oversees the rebuilding of Poisson, faces former Spina di Rosula members who resent her father, and decides how to honour her parents' legacy.

The act has three quests: Shimmering Memories, Lost and Inherited and Yesterday's Tears, Tomorrow's Light. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and completion of Masquerade of the Guilty. The chapter's flower name is a wild rose, echoing Spina di Rosula, the organisation her parents led.

Plot: **Shimmering Memories.** At the Court of Fontaine the Traveler and Paimon find Navia overworked, supervising Poisson's reconstruction without her attendants Melus and Silver. There is no aquabus line to Poisson, so they go by boat. There Florent, who has taken over some of Melus's duties, mentions a planned statue honouring Navia and her parents. Colter, having served his sentence in Meropide, arrives unaware that Melus and Silver have died or of Marcel's plot involving the Primordial Water. He asks about Romeuf and recalls the old quarrel: Romeuf wanted funds spent on Poisson, Callas backed the aquabus, and Romeuf left with his men on bad terms. Navia takes Colter to fetch a new uniform and shares macarons on an old road; something stirs in a bush behind them.

**Lost and Inherited.** In the town Navia notices they are followed, chases three men and defeats them. Their leader Martinat confirms they are Romeuf's men who were angered at seeing her drinking. She lets them go with a warning but asks Florent to increase security. The group stays at Fleuve Cendre and goes fishing; Navia speaks of her childhood immaturity, how Melus was hurt because of a mistake of hers, and how her mother's care inspires her own kindness. Meanwhile Martinat tells Colter the plan begins the next day.

Revelations: No world-level revelations. It deepens Navia's backstory, explains why Spina di Rosula split, and shows the state of Poisson after the flood.

Characters: Navia, the Traveler and Paimon. Florent, Colter, Romeuf and his men, Adele and Coralie appear.

Navia is portrayed as dutiful, generous and tired, willing to forgive but firm when people are endangered. Florent acts as her steady deputy; Colter is the sympathetic, embittered veteran; Romeuf is the rebel who left the organisation.

Consequences: Romeuf and his followers are arrested; Colter is dismissed but welcome to return; Navia plans an aquabus link for Poisson; and the town prepares a family statue.

Placement: Release order: 4.3. Story order: after Chapter IV Act V, Masquerade of the Guilty, in the aftermath of Fontaine's flood. This is not an Archon Quest.

731.comment: Rosa Multiflora Chapter (Navia): Braving the Tides Together
731.content: Act I of Navia's Story Quest. Navia and the Traveler foil Romeuf's plot to bomb the Clementine Line and bury Poisson, and she chooses to forgive Colter and carry her parents' legacy.

key: The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence
Fiction and Reality Inside and Outside the Frame
The Lone Isle Glimpsed Through Fog
732.content:
Roses and Muskets (also: Roses and Muskets Event Quest, The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence, Fiction and Reality Inside and Outside the Frame, The Lone Isle Glimpsed Through Fog, Where the Roses Bloom, The Two Musketeers' Triumph, The Two Musketeers film): Roses and Muskets is the Version 4.3 winter flagship event. The Traveler and Paimon help the Fontaine film producer Xavier make "The Two Musketeers" for the first Fontinalia Film Festival, with Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya as unpaid guest actors and Furina as director. While filming, Chevreuse of the Special Patrol investigates a murder that copies the original novel, and the resolution sets two siblings' grief for their murdered mother against Fontaine's law.

The story has four acts and an afterword: The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence, Fiction and Reality Inside and Outside the Frame, The Lone Isle Glimpsed Through Fog, Where the Roses Bloom and The Two Musketeers' Triumph. The event's reward was the claymore "Ultimate Overlord's Mega Magic Sword".

Plot: Xavier loses his investor and cannot pay his cast, so Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya volunteer, and Furina is persuaded to direct. Chevreuse joins as the musketeer and asks the Traveler for help with a murder echoing the novel. While filming goes on, they trace the gun to Fleuve Cendre and a novelist's roses. At the wrap party Chevreuse stages a trap that exposes the investor Morris, who hired the killer of the novelist's mother. The film wins the festival.

**Act I.** In the Court of Fontaine Xavier cannot get funding for his film of "The Two Musketeers". Chiori has found actors from Inazuma, and Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya agree to work unpaid. Furina, offered a dessert and a Kamera demonstration, agrees to direct. Chevreuse, introduced by Chiori, joins and tells the Traveler about a murder that mirrors the novel.

**Act II.** Filming begins at Hotel Debord, with Chevreuse and Ayaka playing sisters Tulipe and Iris. Chevreuse, the Traveler and Paimon investigate gun parts through workshops and Fleuve Cendre.

**Act III.** The final scene is shot in one take. The trail leads to the novelist Baptiste, who confesses, then privately asks Chevreuse to kill the true mastermind.

**Act IV.** The film is stolen and recovered. At a beach party Chevreuse stages a fake murder to make the investor Morris confess; Morris hired the killer of Elisa, and Veronique, the prop manager, had killed the earlier victim.

**Afterword.** Xavier's film wins and Chevreuse hands the three to Wriothesley.

Revelations: The novelist Baptiste and the prop manager Veronique are siblings whose mother Elisa was murdered twenty years ago on the investor Morris's orders.

The "second musketeer" is Veronique, who killed the earlier victim and left a Rainbow Rose as in the novel. Baptiste's quick confession was a diversion that gave her a chance at Morris.

Characters: Traveler, Paimon, Xavier, Furina, Chiori, Chevreuse, Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya.

Also Morris (the investor), Baptiste (the novelist), Veronique (prop manager), Bonnot (lighting), the extra Elain, Emilie, Wriothesley and the Special Patrol members Letellier and Turenna.

Consequences: Morris, Baptiste and Veronique are arrested and taken to the Fortress of Meropide. "The Two Musketeers" wins the festival, and the crew is credited as Musketeer Pictures.

Placement: Released in Version 4.3 and run from 21 December 2023 to 8 January 2024 (server time), with the shop open until 15 January. Act II unlocked on 22 December, Act III on 23 December, Act IV on 24 December and the Afterword on 26 December. It is an event story set after Chapter IV Act V.

733.comment: Roses and Muskets: Fontinalia Film Festival
733.content: A film festival organised by the Fontaine Film Association; the entry with the highest score wins the Furina Award. The name stayed after Furina's abdication. The first winner was "The Two Musketeers" by Musketeer Pictures.

734.comment: Roses and Muskets: The Two Musketeers
734.content: A Fontainian novel by Baptiste about sisters Tulipe and Iris, whose mother Rain is poisoned by aristocrats; the sisters become the two musketeers and leave a Rainbow Rose on each victim. Xavier produced the film, Furina directed and Ayaka and Chevreuse starred. A real murder in Fontaine copied the novel's roses.

735.content: Twenty years before the event, Morris hired an assassin to kill Elisa, a maid who had borne his two children. She hid the children under the floorboards and fought on. The children are Baptiste and Veronique, who grew up in an orphanage.

736.content:
Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center (also: Ruins Exploration, Return From the Mysterious Realm, Headlong Into the Sands, Fieldwise Center): The story has two acts. In Return From the Mysterious Realm, Collei, now an Akademiya consultant for an outdoor survival and rescue agency, brings the Traveler to Gandharva Ville, where Layla and Djer describe being swept into the ruin and repeating strange phrases. In Headlong Into the Sands, a team of Cyno, Sethos, Tighnari, Alhaitham, Kaveh and Layla enters the ruin with the Traveler and Paimon, gathers stone slabs and notes, and meets Thoth. The event's home base is the Fieldwise Center, where players start the minigames.

Plot: Act I, Return From the Mysterious Realm. At the Akademiya the Traveler and Paimon meet Collei and Cyrus; the Akademiya has hired Collei as a consultant for a planned survival-and-rescue agency. They learn that Cyno and Sethos have taken a strange case to Tighnari in Gandharva Ville. Layla was found delirious in the desert, repeating "How many moons are there in the sky?", and Djer, a member of the Temple of Silence found in the same state, repeated "don't eat Ajilenakh Nuts." Both heard a cat. Layla's other self fills in the gap and says the trouble started when Layla touched a device in the ruin. Act II, Headlong Into the Sands. After a two-day wait, the group enters the unknown ruin with Mehrak, who leads Kaveh and Alhaitham. They split up to find stone slabs, read Zandik's notes and meet Thoth, who explains the cat voice, corrects the memory problem, and tells his history.

Revelations: Thoth, the Ibis King and Scribe of Scribes among King Deshret's Seven Pillars, is imprisoned in Aaru with Sobek and Heryshaf and can occasionally speak through a cat. He explains that, when life became unbearable for the king, Deshret had him, Sobek and Heryshaf locked in Aaru, and that he could be freed if he found humans who gave the correct answers to three questions: what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, and what determines truth and falsehood. The questions came from King Deshret, who received them from the Mistress of Flowers. Goudarz said conspiracy and betrayal and received the power to deceive; Makhaira said she had nothing left to lose and received the power to be loved. A third, unnamed woman was tested on the final question; because Thoth is still sealed, her answer must have been wrong. Thoth adds that a young man named Zandik, who lived several centuries ago, refused his third gift, and that Zandik's companion had blue hair and pointed ears, which means Layla is a descendant of Tulaytullah.

Characters: Main: the Traveler, Paimon, Collei, Layla, Cyno, Sethos, Tighnari, Alhaitham and Kaveh, with Mehrak. Also: Cyrus (Sumeru), Djer, Thoth (as the cat), and cameos by Nahida and Nilou. Trial characters are used inside the ruin (for example Layla in Act I and several allies in Act II).

Consequences: Layla and Djer recover and Layla learns that her ancestry traces to Tulaytullah. The device that harmed them is left for the Traveler or Mehrak to switch off. Thoth remains in Aaru. Cyrus offers to ask friends for a star-related study topic for Layla.

Placement: Released in Version 6.1, 7 to 24 November 2025. Entry requires the Prologue Act III Song of the Dragon and Freedom; the Archon Quest An Elegy for Faded Moonlight and Cyno's Lupus Aureus Chapter are recommended. In an epilogue vignette Sethos says he has heard that the Hat Guy is taking care of something in Nod-Krai. It does not change main-story canon.

737.content: In this event the Ibis King speaks through a borrowed cat in the ruin beneath the desert. He is imprisoned in Aaru with Sobek and Heryshaf, is playful, proud of his chess record against his fellow prisoners, and treats ancient gifts as mere tools. He aided Layla and Djer by replacing overwhelming information with simple repeated phrases.

738.comment: Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center: Thoth's three questions
738.content: The three questions are: what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, and what determines truth and falsehood. King Deshret gave them to Thoth, having received them from the Mistress of Flowers. Goudarz answered the first with conspiracy and betrayal and was given the power to deceive. Makhaira answered the second with vengeance and was given the power to be loved. The third person is not named.

739.comment: Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center: Zandik's notes
739.content: Four Ragged Notes found in the ruin are assembled into the Ordered Notes of a student who found an unrecorded ruin, complained about the Akademiya's attitude to the desert, and wrote about the Seven Pillars before being trapped. The last page is signed Zandik. Thoth later says Zandik was clever, mistrustful and narcissistic, declined his third gift, and was tricked into staying with his companion.

740.comment: Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center: Layla's lineage and the incident
740.content: Layla was caught in quicksand while stargazing, entered a ruin, touched a device, and was left repeating "How many moons are there in the sky?" with no memory of the event. Her other self remembers it. Thoth tells her that Zandik's companion looked like her, with blue hair and pointed ears, which marks her as descended from Tulaytullah.

key: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual world quest series
741.content:
Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual (also: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual world quest series, Hanachirusato quest series): Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual is a World Quest series on Narukami Island, added in version 2.0. At Konda Village the Traveler meets a masked shrine maiden, Hanachirusato, who asks for help carrying out the ritual that purges filth from the roots of the Sacred Sakura and the Thunder Sakura. The Traveler lifts five barriers and cleanses the Depths of Mt. Yougou.

The series has four quests: A Strange Story in Konda, Sacrificial Offering, Cleansing Defilement (with the sub-quest Tanuki-Bayashi in the Forest) and Yougou Cleansing. The starting area requires the Ritou Escape Plan quest.

Plot: Arriving at Konda Village, the Traveler and Paimon meet Hanachirusato, a masked shrine maiden who gives the Traveler a ward and asks them to lift a barrier and look into strange happenings. After questioning villagers, the Traveler finds the key to a locked well and a seal under the ground, lifts the barrier with the ward, and defeats an Ochimusha that appears. Hanachirusato then explains the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual and asks for further help.

The Traveler collects the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Summary at an abandoned shrine near Mt. Yougou, but it is not enough, so they go to the Grand Narukami Shrine. There Inagi Hotomi explains more and hands over the Memento Lens. Back at the abandoned shrine the barrier is lifted and another Ochimusha is beaten. The Traveler then completes the rituals at Araumi, the Kamisato Estate and Chinju Forest. At Chinju Forest a bake-danuki sealed in stone, Ioroi, agrees to give up his ward after the Traveler plays with several tanuki.

Revelations: - Hanachirusato is filth condensed from the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu and ends by being cleansed with the rest (her own statement).
- The Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual must be performed regularly or the Sakura trees wither, which would be catastrophic for Inazuma.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Hanachirusato, Inagi Hotomi (shrine staff), Ioroi (a sealed bake-danuki), and villagers of Konda. Yae Miko and the Kitsune Saiguu are referred to rather than present.

Consequences: The Sakura roots are purged of their accumulated filth for the time being. Hanachirusato dissipates at the end. The shrine's planned ritual is not needed.

Placement: Released in 2.0 with Inazuma. The Ritou Escape Plan quest is needed to reach the starting location. The Kitsune Saiguu is a historical figure covered separately.

742.content: A masked shrine maiden met at Konda Village who guides the Traveler through the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual. She finally says she is filth condensed from the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu and must be cleansed too, and she fades away at the end of the series.

743.comment: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual
743.content: A periodic rite normally led by the Grand Narukami Shrine to purge accumulated filth from the interconnected roots of the Sacred Sakura and the Thunder Sakura. Minor cleansings set protective barriers; a major cleansing, needed every 60 years, breaks the barriers so that filth takes physical form and is destroyed.

key: Another Home There May Yet Be
744.content:
Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter (Nahida) (also: Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter, Sapientia Oromasdis, Nahida's Story Quest, Lingering Warmth, Homecoming, Another Home There May Yet Be): Nahida's Story Quest, in two acts. In Lingering Warmth (3.2) the newly dream-free Sumeru City takes up dream-sharing, and Nahida and the Traveler uncover a man who has trapped other dreamers in an artificial dream built from his uploaded mind. In Homecoming (3.6) Nahida, uneasy about a forgotten duty, helps elemental fungi from a lost homeland and finds that the dragon Apep, damaged when forbidden knowledge was purged, is in danger of dying.

Act I has three quests: Dream of Awakening, Dream of Falling and Dream of Farewell. Act II has two: Where Lies the Path Home and What Shape Does the Self Hold. A follow-up, Another Home There May Yet Be, is unlocked afterward but is outside the act.

Plot: Act I: A group called A Moment of Dreams meets in Sumeru City. After one member sleepwalks, Nahida and the Traveler find that several dreamers are being lured into a shared dream. Its owner, a scholar who uploaded his mind to the Akasha before it was shut down, keeps it alive with others' Jnana energy and a recreated lost wife. Nahida ends it and arranges for his consciousness to return to his body.

Act II: Nahida has a vague sense of an unfinished duty. Elemental fungi from a lost homeland lead her to Apep, the Dendro Dragon, which harbours a void left by the purge of forbidden knowledge. With a Fire Seed and her own power she helps heal it.

Dream of Awakening: Pedrush invites the Traveler and Paimon to the interest group. Nahida appears as a surprise guest and answers dream questions. Ilman says he sees his dead wife each night and continues their talk; Nahida says this is rare. The Traveler thinks privately of Rukkhadevata. Ilman sleepwalks toward a cliff and is saved; Nahida warns him off the site. The headcount shows Kathya has gone to Chatrakam Cave.

Dream of Falling: Kathya dreams of Professor Aisha, an Amurta researcher who gave her a plant that she promised would bloom as proof of her return; Nahida says it never would. The Traveler and Paimon help tell her. Nahida takes the group into the dreams of Debbi, who has lost friends in a shipwreck, and Ilman's family, then to the dream's owner, who explains how he built a 'hyper-realistic' person, his wife Emira, and planted devices in others to feed her Jnana energy. Nahida exposes him. After his creation turns into a monster and is slain, he wishes to die; Nahida refuses and promises to return his consciousness to his body in a Knowledge Capsule.

Dream of Farewell: the sleepers wake. Nahida gives the Capsule to Sitt at the Akademiya for a patient at Bimarstan, then gives the group a speech about moving forward. To the Traveler she admits she felt a warm pull in the dream that she once knew and can trace only to her unnamed past.

Homecoming: Nahida shows the Traveler a Dendro-charged object she found in the Sanctuary of Surasthana. A Floating Hydro Fungus leads her to a collapsed elemental fungus; she revives it and learns its people are an ancient race twisted by the forbidden knowledge, that she once promised to bring them home, and that home is Apep. They clear a Withering Zone, find further fungi, and learn Apep now has a large void. Nahida realises her forgotten task was to tend it. What Shape Does the Self Hold: in the Chasm they cleanse a fungus with the Fire Seed, which the Geoshroom warns is unstable. At Apep's Resort in Hadramaveth, Apep first drives them off, then swallows them. The Seed shatters, and the fungi sacrifice themselves to restore the Heart of Oasis. Apep recovers and tells its story.

Revelations: A scholar built a hidden shared dream from others' energy, and the dragon Apep is in danger of dying after the forbidden knowledge was purged.

Nahida's forgotten duty was to tend Apep and, with the fungi, to bring them home. The fungi's people are an ancient race corrupted by forbidden knowledge.

Characters: Nahida, the Traveler and Paimon.

Pedrush and members of A Moment of Dreams, Ilman, Kathya, Debbi, the dream's owner and Emira, Sitt, and the dragon Apep. Cyno is mentioned as someone Nahida will brief.

Consequences: The dream is broken and the dreamers wake; the scholar will face accountability. Apep is healed and wary. Nahida sets up a camp of fungi under her monitoring.

Placement: Both acts unlock at Adventure Rank 40 after Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises. Lingering Warmth was released in 3.2 on 2022-11-02 and Homecoming in 3.6 on 2023-04-12, so Act II follows Act I by several versions but takes place soon after the Sumeru Archon Quest.

745.comment: Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter (Nahida): Apep and the Fire Seed
745.content: The Dendro Dragon once ruled Sumeru's forests and was corrupted by forbidden knowledge. When Nahida purged it from Irminsul, Apep was left with a large void. The Fire Seed is a crystal Nahida and the fungi made to aid it. Its power, taken from Nahida, can heal Apep's Heart of Oasis, but it is unstable.

746.comment: Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter (Nahida): A Moment of Dreams
746.content: An interest group in Sumeru City where people share dreams, formed after the Akasha stopped. Nahida appears as a guest and guards dreamers against the shared dream.

key: Scenes from Life in Meropide World Quest series
747.content:
Scenes from Life in Meropide (also: Scenes from Life in Meropide World Quest series, Meropide daily-life quests, Fortress of Meropide world quests): Scenes from Life in Meropide is a series of twelve small world quests in the Fortress of Meropide, added in version 4.1. They are not chained together; each starts and ends on its own. The Traveler and Paimon do errands and favours for prisoners and guards, paid in Coupons, the fortress's currency, and glimpse the fortress's everyday routines, queues, jokes and regrets.

The quests unlock in batches. Seven become available during the quest "Game of the Rich", and access is also tied to finishing "Hereafter...". Three more open on the first daily reset after finishing "An Eye for an Eye" and the first seven, and the last two open on the next daily reset after those.

Plot: Each quest is a self-contained errand. In A Raw Deal the Traveler queues for the prisoner Decembre, who wants to post a birthday letter to his son, but he hands over the wrong letter. In Chit-Chat the Traveler negotiates for a study room on behalf of a scholar named Nakul. Dead End, Safe Operation, Treat the Symptoms and Unfinished Task are favours for Clynes, Caterpillar, the doctor Arderne and the photographer Nelly. Fists of Fury is a sparring bout, and Every Debt has a Creditor, Visible Hands and The Art of Negotiation involve guards and fortress bureaucracy. An Actor's Training and Memories close the series with a theatre rehearsal and a conversation with a former Institute researcher.

Revelations: - The fortress runs on Coupons, not Mora. Prisoners queue for mail, which is read and checked, and take small jobs and wagers.
- Clynes is a former Fontaine Research Institute researcher, and the quests refer to the Institute's accidents and its trouble with funding.
- Clynes says he can leave whenever he wants and chooses to stay.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, with prisoners and guards including Decembre, Nakul, Nizami, Clynes, Caterpillar, Mitul, Koblenz, the doctors Arderne and Lechlade, the amateur journalist Nelly and the guard Grainville, the guards Galvaryet and Maupoil, the clerk Monglane, and the Tri-Coupon Troupe's Meilhat and Fourmon.

Consequences: The quests have only small local effects: a stuck mark removed, a rift sealed, a photograph taken. They add a record of life in the fortress rather than change the main story.

Placement: Released in version 4.1. Availability comes in three batches tied to the archon quests "Game of the Rich", "Hereafter..." and "An Eye for an Eye", with the last quests opening after daily resets.

748.comment: Scenes from Life in Meropide: Coupons
748.content: Coupons are the currency used inside the Fortress of Meropide. Nakul says Mora is useless there. Prisoners buy food at the Coupon Cafeteria and goods at the Rag and Bone Shop with Coupons, and employ one another for errands.

749.comment: Scenes from Life in Meropide: Clynes
749.content: Clynes is a technician in the Fortress of Meropide who worked at the Fontaine Research Institute. He repairs devices, is the author of the Cipher Letter mark on the wall, and says he stays by choice. He mourns Butor, who died of illness, and Teilhard, who died in the Central Laboratory explosion, and says a fourth colleague was fired.

750.comment: Scenes from Life in Meropide: Decembre
750.content: Decembre is a prisoner nicknamed "Unlucky Decembre" for repeated failures at the mail room queue. He hands the Traveler the wrong letter, and later offers jobs to newcomers at a fraction of the real pay, for which Maupoil takes him to solitary.

751.comment: Scenes from Life in Meropide: Tri-Coupon Troupe
751.content: The Tri-Coupon Troupe is a two-person theatre group of prisoners, Meilhat and Fourmon, rehearsing "The Countess of Monte-Mer" and promoting it by loudspeaker. Fourmon says he was sentenced at the Opera Epiclese.

752.content:
Secret Summer Paradise (also: Veluriyam Mirage event, Bottleland event, An Invitation From Afar, Mirage Paradise in Crisis, Dreams and First Encounters): The Mirage is a glass-bottle world holding an amusement-park-like village. Idyia, who looks after it, welcomes visitors, and when the Traveler's group arrives the place is failing. Over three acts they gather four missing components for a spindle-like core (one from each of several residents), meet Sangonomiya Kokomi, Eula and Collei who are also there, and discover that Idyia is an Oceanid and that the residents are Hydro Eidolon copies of earlier visitors. The core is restarted with the help of Kokomi's relic, the Shinrou Casket.

Plot: Act I, An Invitation From Afar!: Klee, Kaeya, the Traveler and Paimon use a Magic Invite to reach the bottle-world of the Veluriyam Mirage and meet its host Idyia, who needs four components to repair the central hub. Act II, Mirage Paradise in Crisis!: the group repairs a fairground tent with Maymunah, rescues the trapped Lessig and obtains a candy-box component. Act III, Dreams and First Encounters!: they perform Zosimos's play for the last component, learn that Idyia is an Oceanid and that residents are Hydro Eidolon copies of past visitors, and restart the hub with Kokomi's Shinrou Casket.

Revelations: Idyia is an Oceanid. The residents of the Veluriyam Mirage (Zosimos, Maymunah, the cart caretakers and others) are Hydro Eidolon replicas of previous human visitors, created to carry on the visitors' dreams. The central components are gifts from those visitors. Visitors cannot take what they make in the Mirage into the outside world; some were angry at that and destroyed everything, while others asked for a replica of themselves to stay. Kokomi's Shinrou Casket works through wishes people have prayed over it.

Characters: Klee, Kaeya, the Traveler and Paimon; Jean (sends them), Alice (letter sender), Eula and Collei (already in the area), Sangonomiya Kokomi (seeking a lost relic), Idyia (host), Lessig (a Lawrence man, Eula's cousin), Maymunah (fairground manager), Zosimos (stage director), and the cart caretakers Ferdinand, Jeroney and Haddo.

Consequences: The central hub turns again and the Mirage returns to normal. Lessig offers to help maintain the domain. Klee gets the ride on the Choo-Choo Cart she wanted, and Idyia lets them enjoy the domain. Kokomi's search for the Shinrou Casket is only partly resolved on screen: the casket is borrowed from the core to help repair it.

Placement: Released in Version 3.8 as a Flagship Event, after the Sumeru Archon Quests (Song of the Dragon and Freedom is the entry requirement; Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and some Story Quests are recommended with a Quick Start). Event quests are self-contained and not part of the main storyline.

753.content: A limited-time summer event area: a domain hidden within a bottle in the middle of the Sumeru desert. Rumour says those who enter are granted their heart's desire. It is run by Idyia and populated by Hydro Eidolons who copy past visitors. The wiki notes it is not treated as a normal Domain in gameplay.

754.content: An Oceanid and the caretaker of the Veluriyam Mirage, who looks after it and likes to spend time alone at the top of the wheel when a visitor leaves. She gives visitors candy and helps them restore the central hub, and in the finale wishes for all visitors to achieve their true wishes.

755.content: A relic lost long ago from Watatsumi Island that Kokomi seeks. It records the prayers of those who come to it, building "shinki" that gives it its power, and is used to restart the Mirage's central hub.

756.content: A man of the Lawrence clan, cousin to Eula, who came to the Mirage to restore the clan's honour but found nobody cared about it. He triggered the disaster by touching a water orb. After being trapped and reconciling with Eula he helps maintain the domain.

757.content: A cart ride in the Mirage looked after by Ferdinand, Jeroney and Haddo. Klee wishes to ride it to the top of the wheel at the end of the story.

758.content:
Seirai Stormchasers (also: Seirai Stormchasers Part I, Seirai Stormchasers Part IV, Warding Stones quest, Peculiar Pinion): A version 2.1 world quest series on Seirai Island, Inazuma. The Adventurers' Guild cannot explore the island because of constant storms. Katheryne sends the Traveler to help two adventurers, Etsuko and Taisuke, and the Traveler meets a talking cat who knows how to seal the Warding Stones that keep the storm at bay.

The series has four parts. The Traveler follows a cat's tracks to the Asase Shrine, repairs its Offering Box for the cat Neko, learns how to seal four Warding Stones, and seals them, two on the ground and two in the sky. A boss, the Thunder Manifestation, is fought on a platform of floating stones, and the Traveler finds a strange feather, the Peculiar Pinion.

Plot: Katheryne says the guild's Seirai exploration is blocked by wild storms and suggests the Traveler help. On the island Etsuko explains that going toward the centre is too dangerous because of Balethunder, and that they have found broken stone structures they think are called Warding Stones.

Etsuko and Taisuke focus on the stones while the Traveler and Paimon follow strange cat tracks to a shrine in better shape and fairer weather than the rest of the island. There the cat Neko, who calls herself the provisional head priestess of the Asase Shrine, is worried about the damaged Offering Box, since Hibiki would grieve to see the shrine in a sorry state. She agrees to teach the Traveler about the Warding Stones in exchange for repairs, and describes the bird of most prodigious size the stones were meant to keep sealed.
The Traveler tells the adventurers (Taisuke is thrilled by the talking cat) and the group seals the first two stones. The other two prove puzzling until the Traveler realises they are in the sky, and goes up through a Phase Gate. Sealing them forms a huge platform from the floating stones, where the Traveler defeats a Thunder Manifestation and then finds the Peculiar Pinion.

Revelations: The Warding Stones were made to seal a huge bird, and breaking them let the storm and the Thunder Manifestation loose. The wiki's profile of Neko, built on this and later material, says the wards were broken in the time of Asase Hibiki and Ako Domeki, when a Shogunate fleet attacked, after which Hibiki and Domeki vanished and the island stayed in storm for around 500 years. This series itself tells only part of that, through Neko's words.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Katheryne; Etsuko and Taisuke of the Adventurers' Guild; the cat Neko.

Etsuko is a guild adventurer in the standard uniform and keeps Taisuke on topic. Neko is a large black cat with golden eyes who has lived for at least five centuries and styles herself provisional head priestess.

Consequences: The storm clears and Seirai Island is open to exploration. Neko stays at the Asase Shrine, and her story continues in the quest Neko Is a Cat.

Placement: Released in Version 2.1. The wiki lists Ritou Escape Plan as its requirement. Part IV is followed by A Particularly Particular Author in the quest ordering.

759.comment: Seirai Stormchasers: Neko of the Asase Shrine
759.content: Neko is a talking black cat who calls herself the provisional head priestess of the Asase Shrine on Seirai Island. She waited for Hibiki's return at the shrine and keeps it as tidy as she can; she first helps the Traveler in Seirai Stormchasers.

760.content:
Shadows Amidst Snowstorms (also: The Snowy Past, The Shadows Deepen, A Secret Born From Ashes, Dragonspine winter camp event): Act I (The Snowy Past) starts from Paimon's wish for a fruit-juicing machine and moves up Dragonspine, where the Traveler joins a camp run by Cyrus. Act II (The Shadows Deepen) follows a group stuck on the mountain by bad luck, a night at Albedo's camp and a painting session, then an ambush by the impostor Albedo. Act III (A Secret Born From Ashes) is a story-telling session in which Paimon and Albedo share tales; Albedo's, which the Traveler takes to describe real events about the impostor, and the event ends with Joel's reunion and a last scene in Mondstadt that returns to the juicer joke.

Plot: Act I, The Snowy Past: Paimon asks the alchemists Timaeus and Sucrose to build a fruit juicer that keeps juice fresh; they say it is beyond alchemy and suggest Albedo, who had just left looking grim. On Dragonspine the Traveler finds Cyrus holding winter training with senior and junior adventurers. Amber has been entertaining Joel, whose father is missing, and Eula, who has never built a snowman, joins them. Cyrus has a spare instructor slot, because Fischl, originally invited, was busy elsewhere, and Eula takes it for the newcomer Gerald. The Traveler meets Albedo, who says he is on the mountain for quiet and to gather Starsilver for paint, and who invites them to learn painting at his camp. His camp has been burgled, his alchemy notes taken; the footprints lead to a cavern and Albedo goes on ahead alone. When the Traveler hears Bennett's voice, they find him caged in a Fatui camp and free him. Albedo has disappeared.

Act II, The Shadows Deepen: Back at Albedo's camp the Traveler and Paimon find Amber, Eula and Bennett have wandered the mountain for days, plagued by avalanches and ill luck. Albedo creates chairs by painting them, cooks dinner and paints Paimon's portrait with the Traveler. The next day an avalanche separates the party and Eula senses something is wrong. In a cutscene Albedo starts to make a Cryo Solar Isotoma and is run through by a second Albedo, who turns into a plant. Eula cuts the thing down, and Albedo explains it is an extremely rare mutated whopperflower and that Dragonspine's dragon-blood-saturated land makes strange life possible.

Act III, A Secret Born From Ashes: The Traveler and Paimon trade stories at Albedo's camp. Paimon tells a horror tale about whopperflowers that replace the people they eat. Albedo tells a longer story about Subject One, a synthetic human who blends in among people, and Subject Two, a failed experiment revived by a dragon's power on a snowy mountain, who copies Subject One and makes a Subject Three, intending to replace him. Albedo says it is just a story, but warns that monsters touched by Durin's blood are, like him, creatures of Rhinedottir. The group returns to the camp, where Cyrus and Pallad present Joserf, Joel's father, found without memory and recovering. A final scene in Mondstadt's alchemy shop shows Albedo again with the mark on his neck and a joke about burying fruit in Dragonspine's snow.

Revelations: The "other Albedo" is a plant, not a human: Albedo identifies it as an extremely rare mutated whopperflower, and the event's boss is called the Fellflower. Albedo's second Act III story, framed as fiction, tells of two copies of a synthetic human; he says monsters touched by Durin's blood are creatures of Rhinedottir "just like me". When the Traveler protests that he is no monster he replies that he knows what he is and that he and the Traveler are both "different". In his story the copy erases the mark on its neck as a symbol of imperfection; in the final scene the mark on Albedo's neck briefly vanishes and returns, and the Traveler decides it was a prank.

Characters: Albedo (host, the target of the impostor), the Traveler and Paimon, Eula and Amber (Knights, present as helpers), Bennett (unlucky adventurer), Sucrose and Timaeus (alchemists, in Act I and III), and event NPCs Cyrus (Guild branch master), Reckless Pallad, Gerald (new recruit), Joel and his father Joserf. Fischl is mentioned as the original instructor who could not attend.

Consequences: Joel and Joserf leave Dragonspine together; the winter camp ends. The impostor is destroyed. The event's weapon reward was the sword Cinnabar Spindle. No further consequences are shown in the event.

Placement: Released in Version 2.3 as a Flagship Event; requirements were Adventure Rank 20, Prologue Act II, the Princeps Cretaceus Chapter Act I and Lost in the Snow. It is self-contained and not part of the Archon Quests.

761.content: A very rare mutated whopperflower that took Albedo's appearance and tried to replace him on Dragonspine. Albedo says conditions there are far from typical because dragon blood seeped into the land and passed to monsters by the ley lines, speeding mutation. It is the event's boss: it summons Arcane Fruits and releases Arcane Essence.

762.comment: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms: Joel and Joserf
762.content: Joel is a boy living at the Dragonspine camp whose father had gone missing. In this event Reckless Pallad finds Joserf, who has lost most of his memory but recognises Joel and starts to recover. He survived hunting alone in a cave while his legs healed. They leave together.

763.content: Throughout the event Bennett believes his bad luck rubs off on others and apologises for avalanches and falls. Eula, Amber and the Traveler reassure him it is not his fault. He jokes that guessing a Treasure Hoarder Insignia flip wrongly uses up bad luck. A miracle of misfortune with Pallad ultimately helps reunite Joel with his father.

764.comment: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms: Albedo's painting and Paimon's portrait
764.content: Albedo teaches the Traveler to paint at his camp and uses painted blueprints to create chairs through alchemy. The Traveler's portrait of Paimon is poor; Albedo reworks it into a flattering image that Paimon hangs up. He says alchemy can create living beings with enough research.

key: Shadows of the Mountains World Quest series
765.content:
Shadows of the Mountains (also: Shadows of the Mountains World Quest series, Shadow Pin quests, Titu's Shadow Pin quests): Shadows of the Mountains is a two-quest Natlan world series added in version 5.0, set in Tequemecan Valley. A tribal storyteller named Titu is watching a giant stone pillar, the Greater Shadow Pin, and its three smaller Lesser Shadow Pins, which hold back the Abyss. The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One help restore them and then find out what is trapped beneath.

The series is told through a storyteller's lens. Titu keeps returning to how tales are shaped and warped, and the central reveal is that a villain from local legend was a hero. It ends with an act of mercy, not a victory.

Plot: **Beneath the Crystal Rock.** At a sentry post in Tequemecan Valley the sentry Yukom is waiting for Titu to relieve him. The Traveler meets Titu beside the giant Shadow Pin. Titu explains that the Wayob are said in stories to have hung the pins to pin the shadow of the Volcano Lord, but in truth what is sealed beneath is the Abyss. Two of the three Lesser Shadow Pins have floated upward and the Iridescent Inscription, the language the ancient dragons used to wield phlogiston, has been squeezed out of them. The Traveler touches the inscription, breaks crystals to gather its power and fights Abyss-aligned monsters to push each pin back. The second pin's inscription has also been scattered and must be found in other places, with the Little One's nose pointing the way. Afterward the party asks Titu to tell the real story of the pins.

When all three Lesser Pins are set, the ground trembles. Black, Nightsoul-warped warriors appear, the Greater Shadow Pin falls into a deep cavity beneath it, and a hoarse voice cries out.

**Peace to the Slumbering.** Titu and the party climb down the hole. A tablet from Elder Traore explains that two Khaenri'ahn soldiers, Zephaniah and Irizar, guided the black flood to the seal site and stayed in it, and that the tribe's warriors sacrificed themselves with them. The Iridescent Inscription at the bottom is shattered into fragments and the party breaks the stones containing them while fighting Rifthounds. Voices behind the inscription reveal that more than two souls are locked in endless struggle with the Abyss. The Traveler unseals the inscription and defeats the two warriors, who thank them with their last words. In the Night Kingdom the Traveler and Paimon meet a beast with night-coloured fur who says the Night has forgiven them. Titu, relieved, plans to retell the story with the two soldiers as heroes and returns to take over Yukom's shift.

Revelations: - The Shadow Pins are giant solid-phlogiston nails driven into the ground by the Children of Echoes ages ago, each carrying an Iridescent Inscription, to seal the Abyss. The "Volcano Lord's shadow" is a metaphor.
- The "evil Khaenri'ahn soldiers" of tribal legend, Zephaniah and Irizar, were sealed in with the Abyss and fought it for centuries; Traore's tablet calls them heroes.

Characters: Titu (a Children of Echoes storyteller), Yukom (a sentry), the Traveler, Paimon and the Little One. Elder Traore, Zephaniah and Irizar, and the "Beast With Fur Like That of Night" appear through the inscription, boss fights and a vision. Sanhaj of the Masters of the Night-Wind is mentioned by Titu as a storyteller he reveres.

Consequences: The Greater Shadow Pin has fallen and the Abyss in the cavity is purified. The Iridescent Inscription is gone, the tormented voices fall silent, and Zephaniah and Irizar find rest. Titu intends to tell the tale of the golden-haired outlander, the flying white fairy and a small Tepetlisaurus, and to retell the soldiers as heroes.

Placement: Released in version 5.0, in Tequemecan Valley. Beneath the Crystal Rock begins by talking to Titu or by finishing a Lesser Shadow Pin challenge; Peace to the Slumbering follows automatically.

766.content: Titu is a Children of Echoes storyteller who also looks after the stone pillars. He is verbose, self-deprecating and keeps thinking in plots, joking that he is not a fighter. He says he loves heroes' stories most and tells them so that they are remembered. The quest has him come down into the cavity himself, because witnessing things through is a storyteller's duty. He is bad at turning up for his sentry shift, which annoys Yukom. Note that Titu is also the name of a member of Taika's expedition seen in Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm; the quests do not say they are the same person.

767.comment: Shadows of the Mountains: Shadow Pins
767.content: Giant solid-phlogiston pillars: one large and three small. They seal the Abyss and are driven into the earth by Iridescent Inscription. When the Abyss presses, the inscription is squeezed out and the pin floats upward. The Children of Echoes know not to disturb the phlogiston near them.

768.comment: Shadows of the Mountains: Zephaniah and Irizar
768.content: Two Khaenri'ahn soldiers whom Natlan folklore remembers as villains who brought the Abyss to the valley. Traore's tablet names them as friends who guided the dark flood to the place of the seal and stayed behind it as promised. They are fought as Black Serpent Knights with hoarse, pained voices; Zephaniah worries about leading the tribe away, and Irizar says he does not want a certain person to see him as he is.

769.comment: Shadows of the Mountains: Elder Traore
769.content: Traore was the elder, storyteller and shield and spear of the Children of Echoes at the time of the sealing. According to Titu he was the first to leap into the pit. He left the Boundary Marker Inscription, a three-part blessing, and is remembered as a hero.

770.content: Yukom is a sentry in Tequemecan Valley who keeps waiting for Titu to relieve him from his post. He is tired and exasperated with Titu but worried when the earthquake strikes.

771.content:
Silvermoon Hall: Selenic Chronicles (also: Selenic Chronicles, Silvermoon Hall reputation quests, New Moon's Embrace): A reputation-style series of quests for Columbina, the Damselette, at Silvermoon Hall in Nod-Krai, added in Version 6.0 (Luna I). It is unlocked by the quest The Dark Side of Memory and is read through the Record-Keeping Kuuhenki. It consists of eighteen short quests in three parts, with small personal moments rather than world-changing plot.

Each completed quest gives the party the New Moon's Embrace effect for a time, and finishing groups of quests unlocks rewards. The series is a quiet companion to Columbina's role in the main Nod-Krai story: it shows her with her kuuhenki, a young painter and her memories of home.

Plot: The Traveler visits Silvermoon Hall now and then to meet Columbina. Each visit is a short quest; the next becomes available after seven daily resets.

Part I (six quests): The Dark Side of Memory, Her Past, The Artist By the Moon's Side (I), Moonlight Sonata, Homecoming's Faint Glow and May the Moonlight Connect Us. The official blurbs say she takes a beam of moonlight and gives the Traveler the "Moon Goddess's Favor"; that she claims to have "run away from home" yet seems to have fond memories of it; that a young painter tries to introduce its goddess; and that a genius mechanic repairs her broken instrument.
