Yelan's report says Qianwei has pioneering ideas with weak detail, and Mingbo struggles to win people over. Both are shaken by Zhiyi's betrayal and resolve to continue working.

958.content: A Fatui ambassador who leads the scheme to plant Zhiyi near the Tianshu. Zhiyi poisons him at the celebration beneath Qingxu Pool, and he says the Fatui would kill him for failing.

959.comment: Umbrabilis Orchis Chapter (Yelan): Wenyuan, Shanghua and Wupei
959.content: Yelan's informants. Wenyuan and Shanghua check on the candidates; Wupei was missing at first and later said that Zhiyi had fallen overboard and no one had interacted with him.

960.content: Uncle Tian, the Tianshu, is old and wants a successor. He gives the assessment of candidates to Yelan, and sets no time limit. If none prove worthy, he agrees Yelan may take the post.

961.content:
Unfinished Comedy (also: Caterpillar's Story: Prologue, Game of the Rich, An Eye for an Eye, Hereafter..., Coupon Millionaire, Lanoire's escape from Meropide): Unfinished Comedy is a Fontaine World Quest series from version 4.1, set in the Fortress of Meropide. A prisoner called Caterpillar, who looks like a boy but says he is not a child, wants to get a young girl named Lanoire out of the fortress and back to her family. She was born inside and has no papers. The Traveler and Paimon join the plan, win a contest called Coupon Millionaire, and help the pair escape.

The series has three quests, played in order: Game of the Rich, An Eye for an Eye, and Hereafter... It requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind to have been completed, and begins when the Traveler is caught by the fortress searchlights, enters through the dormitory pipes, or teleports in once the fortress is unlocked during To the Stars Shining in the Depths. The Fontaine Reputation menu lists it as "Caterpillar's Story: Prologue", and its name echoes a 1957 Chinese film, The Unfinished Comedy.

Plot: **Game of the Rich.** The Traveler and Paimon are taken to reception in the Fortress of Meropide. The receptionist Monglane records them and sends them to the prisoner Darcy, who takes them to the guard Estienne. Estienne has invented a game called Coupon Millionaire: whoever earns the most Coupons wins a supervised job outside, under the sun. A small girl, Lanoire, says she will win because her friend Cater told her so, and a stricter new guard, Noailles, breaks up the crowd. The Traveler follows Lanoire around the fortress, meets Caterpillar and learns that she was born here, that her mother Agnes died of a long illness, and that she has family outside but no proof of identity. Caterpillar proposes using the game as an exit. The Traveler and Paimon join his team, the Kids Team, over several days of commissions.

**An Eye for an Eye.** The team wins and Estienne takes them outside at night, but Noailles intercepts them with Gardemeks. Caterpillar turns into an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue to fight. Noailles offers a deal, breaks it, and takes everyone back. Estienne and the guard Maupoil help them leave a second time, and the Traveler opens the Geode Mine Shaft's sealed passage. Noailles follows and is beaten, and Estienne takes him into custody. The group leaves.

**Hereafter...** Caterpillar leads Lanoire and the Traveler along a hidden path to a house with a garden of purple flowers at the foot of the mountains to the southeast. Earnshaw, her grandfather, takes her in. Caterpillar stays outside and tells Lanoire the first part of a story about a mage's apprentice and a little fish.

Revelations: - Lanoire was born inside the Fortress of Meropide. She is the granddaughter of Earnshaw, and her mother Agnes died of a chronic illness in the fortress.
- Caterpillar is not a child. He has been in the fortress for over four hundred years.
- Caterpillar is a hilichurl who can change how he looks; his real form is an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue.

Characters: Caterpillar ("Cater"), Lanoire ("Skylark" in the fortress), the guards Estienne, Noailles and Maupoil, the receptionist Monglane, Earnshaw, the Traveler and Paimon. Prisoners seen include Darcy, Genevieve, Poiret, Rave, Henaff, Delassaux, Nizami and Alvard. Clynes, Galvana and Galvaryet appear in support.

Consequences: Lanoire lives with Earnshaw in the Court of Fontaine Region, near Mont Esus. Caterpillar leaves, and goes on to the 4.2 Narzissenkreuz Ordo quests, where he travels with the Traveler, Ann and Seymour. After the series the searchlights outside the fortress no longer react to the Traveler.

Placement: Released in version 4.1, with the Fortress of Meropide. In story order it sits just before the 4.2 In the Wake of Narcissus series, which Hereafter... leads into.

962.content: Caterpillar, called Cater by Lanoire, is a prisoner in the Fortress of Meropide who appears as a white-haired boy. He says he is not a child. His real form is an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue; he says he is a hilichurl whom the mage Narzissenkreuz taught to speak and think. He says he has been imprisoned for more than four hundred years for his part in his master's plan. He helps Lanoire out of what he calls compassion, copying what a human would do.

963.content: Lanoire is a young girl born inside the Fortress of Meropide, nicknamed Skylark by the prisoners. She has no official identity there. Her mother Agnes died, and Caterpillar and Estienne have looked after her. She loves stories, flowers pressed in books and the Tasses Ragout. After the series she lives with her grandfather Earnshaw and the three dogs Prince, Princess and Hero.

964.content: Estienne is an easy-going guard in the Fortress of Meropide who invents the Coupon Millionaire game to decide who is sent on outside jobs. He bends rules, dislikes Noailles' rigidity, and helps Lanoire and Caterpillar get out. He says he would not take Lanoire out himself, because he would pay too high a price.

965.content: Noailles is a new, rule-bound guard in the Fortress of Meropide. Darcy says he dislikes Fonta and wants to close the Pankration Ring. He tries to recreate Caterpillar's lost records, calls the fugitives criminals whatever their documents say, uses Gardemeks without permission and breaks the deal he offered Caterpillar. He is beaten at the Geode Mine Shaft and taken into custody by Estienne.

966.content: Earnshaw is Lanoire's grandfather, a broad white-haired man who lives at the foothills of Mont Esus in the Court of Fontaine Region, in a house with a purple-flower garden. His daughter Agnes left after a quarrel and sent letters that he did not read. He cares for her three dogs, makes Tasses Ragout and takes Lanoire in at the end of the series.

967.content: Coupon Millionaire is a game Estienne runs in the Fortress of Meropide. Teams earn Coupons however they like, and the winner gets a supervised job outside the walls. The contest has few rules, which Genevieve criticises. The Kids Team, made up of Caterpillar, Lanoire, the Traveler and Paimon, wins with 2,003,480 Coupons, thanks to a stash Caterpillar saved earlier and used to hire helpers.

968.comment: Unfinished Comedy: Geode Mine Shaft Escape
968.content: The Geode Mine Shaft is the route the group uses out of the Fortress of Meropide. A locking mechanism there can only be opened by two people at once, and its terminal needs energy storage devices that attract a Flying Energy Thief, a trial device that disables whatever carries one. Noailles confronts the group here.

key: What the Skies Conceal, the Water Reveals
969.content:
Unreconciled Stars (also: Unreconciled Stars event, Fading Star event, Unknown Star, The Crisis Deepens, What the Skies Conceal, the Water Reveals, Where Ancient Stars Align): Unreconciled Stars was a Version 1.1 flagship event (16-30 November 2020, with the final act released on 26 November). Meteorites fell across Mondstadt and Liyue, and anyone who touched one fell into a deep sleep, dreaming of climbing a freezing mountain. The Adventurers' Guild sends the Traveler and Paimon out with the self-styled "Prinzessin der Verurteilung" Fischl and her raven Oz; they later gain the astrologist Mona. The trail leads to Leonard, an adventurer from about two thousand years ago who never climbed Pilos Peak, and to a Fatui Harbinger who is also hunting the meteorites.

The event is mostly an investigation story told with Fischl's theatrical speech and Oz's patient translation. It was limited-time: Fischl was the event's reward character, and the story is canon but not common knowledge for characters who were not present.

Plot: Act I (Unknown Star). Katheryne briefs the Traveler and Paimon: a meteor shower covered the countryside of Mondstadt and Liyue, and anyone who touches a meteorite sinks into sleep. Fischl and Oz are assigned as partners, since the Guild advises adventurers to travel in pairs. At Springvale the victims mumble about cold and rest, one remembers a snowy mountain path, and a villager asks for help finding a boy who ran to the nearest impact site. Fischl's Vision glows near the meteorite shards; clearing the shards wakes some sleepers, so the group concludes the meteorites are the cause.

Act II (The Crisis Deepens). Meteorites keep falling faster than they can be cleared. The search for a missing Dawn Winery delivery worker takes the party to Liyue, where the Millelith have turned Wangshu Inn into a relief station. A wandering Inazuman swordsman helps them briefly and leaves. At the inn Fatui skirmishers appear at the last meteorite and warn that a Harbinger is nearby. Fischl declares the sleep a curse and asks for someone expert in undoing curses; Katheryne names the travelling astrologist Mona.

Act III (What the Skies Conceal, the Water Reveals). Mona's hydromancy shows that the meteorites came from someone's constellation. At Qingce Village the party learns that the sleepers all dream of an enormous snowy mountain and feel compelled to climb it, as though the wish were put in their heads. Mona reads the name "Leonard". The Inazuman stranger returns and Mona abruptly teleports everyone away; the stranger is revealed to be the Fatui Harbinger Scaramouche, who had hoped to strike down the Traveler and orders his soldiers to keep researching the meteorites.

Act IV (Where Ancient Stars Align). Fischl and Oz step back to tend the growing number of sleepers. A book in the Mondstadt Library, "Of Mountains and Seas", written by Leonard, is half illegible until Mona reconstructs it: Leonard lived about two thousand years ago and never reached the top of Pilos Peak. Mona reasons that the mountain was levelled when Barbatos cleared the ice and is now Musk Reef. The party finds Scaramouche there, shaken, and he leaves after announcing that the stars are a lie. After fighting off his Fatui, they destroy the meteorite core, and Leonard's spirit speaks one last time before the sleepers can wake.

Revelations: The meteorites are fragments of Leonard's constellation, brought down from the sky, and the sleepers dream of climbing the mountain he failed to climb. Leonard was an adventurer who died without summiting Pilos Peak and instead put his efforts into designs for flying devices, the "Wings of Incompletion". The meteorites radiate elemental energy that lulls people into a hypnosis-like sleep, and a core meteorite contains a crystal holding his spirit. Pilos Peak no longer exists as a mountain: it is the small island Musk Reef.

Characters: Fischl and Oz lead the investigation by volume rather than method; Oz translates and keeps the party grounded. Mona supplies the astrology and an ego to match. Paimon asks the questions; the Traveler does the legwork. Katheryne dispatches them. The Harbinger Scaramouche (disguised as an Inazuman vagrant in Acts II and III) is the antagonist. Leonard appears only as a spirit in a cutscene.

Consequences: The victims wake when the core is destroyed. Fischl's event reward quest (the "Prinzessin's Pact") makes her obtainable. The Harbinger leaves Musk Reef after saying the sky is a hoax; the event does not follow up on his claim.

Placement: Released in Version 1.1 on 16 November 2020 and available until 30 November 2020 (final act released 26 November). It follows the Prologue Archon Quest (Mondstadt chapter) in release order and has no formal story prerequisite beyond Adventure Rank 20. In story terms it takes place with Scaramouche still a serving Harbinger; the event states no exact date relative to the Prologue.

970.comment: Unreconciled Stars: Leonard and Pilos Peak
970.content: In the Unreconciled Stars event Mona reconstructs a damaged book, "Of Mountains and Seas", by Leonard, an adventurer who lived about two thousand years ago. By forty he had conquered every domain of the world except Pilos Peak, which defeated him. Near the end of his life he put his hope into flying devices he called the Wings of Incompletion. Pilos Peak itself no longer exists above the sea; it is the small island of Musk Reef, which Mona matches to the legend that Barbatos cleared the ice and snow and reshaped Mondstadt.

971.comment: Unreconciled Stars: Scaramouche and the stars are a lie
971.content: In the event the Sixth Fatui Harbinger, Scaramouche (codename the Balladeer), first poses as a vagrant from Inazuma, then commands Fatui soldiers to keep researching the meteorites. He had planned to strike down the Traveler during the event. At Musk Reef he has been through the shared dream and says the stars and sky are a hoax, mentions "the Jester" with irritation, and leaves. Later canon identifies the Wanderer as this same person after he erased his identity from Irminsul (Version 3.3 playable); this event itself stays in Scaramouche's Fatui period.

972.content: Fischl introduces herself to the Traveler and Paimon in Act I as Prinzessin der Verurteilung from the Immernachtreich, with the raven Oz as her familiar. Oz openly translates her style ("Mein Fräulein means to say: hello"). By Act IV she steps aside to tend sleepers and tells the Traveler, out of her usual style, that she enjoyed their conversations, since most Guild adventurers only talk to her for Oz's scouting reports. Her character details belong in her own entry.

973.content:
Upstream Variations (also: Upstream Variations (Quest), Vodyanitsa's handwritten ticket quest, Happy-Quacky Phonograph Ducky quest): Upstream Variations is a World Quest series added in version 7.1. It is played over seven real-time days, one short scene per day, around Vodyanitsa, the principal soprano of the Korolevskiy Troupe. Over meals and visits she tells the Traveler and Paimon about a childhood friend who turned her tickets into social currency, and about the hollow feeling of singing to people who do not listen. The Traveler gives her a necklace-sized recording device, and she ends the week cheerful.

The quest is unlocked by completing "Wraith's Nocturne" and raising the Tidesong Cavern Meeting Point to Construction Level 2. The wiki notes that completing "White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking" first gives the best experience. Completing it gives a special reward, the Happy-Quacky Phonograph Ducky, which gives Vodyanitsa a new decorative appearance (game-mechanics information). It also gives Primogems, Mora and talent materials.

Plot: Day 1. At Podvorye Restaurant in Snezhnograd the Traveler and Paimon find Vodyanitsa at a table with only tea, sighing about a meeting with a "friend". She says food tastes like wax when she has to talk to that person, and meeting at a restaurant lets her pretend to eat instead. She orders a huge meal, then tells a story: a banquet in her honour, thrown by Lishnaya, head of a Snezhnayan guild, who praises the performance with exaggerated flattery. Vodyanitsa explains that Lishnaya was once a small girl who loved opera and worked part-time at the theater. Vodyanitsa gave her handwritten tickets, and the girl used to watch from behind the curtain. She stops the story there, gives the Traveler a blank notebook made at Maryyushka's Antykvariat with tickets inside, and says to bring it to the theater.

Day 2. The ticket is handwritten, so the theater policy sends the Traveler and Paimon backstage to watch from the wings. There Vodyanitsa continues. Lishnaya stopped using the backstage ticket, missed a performance with an excuse, and Vodyanitsa learned that a wealthy merchant sat in the seat she had saved. She says Lishnaya used the tickets to make powerful friends and is now part of the Zapolyarny elite. Vodyanitsa still thinks of her as a friend, because she does not like giving up on things that belong to her. She speaks of flower baskets from people who never come, and of the Water Imps' voices that she hears in the empty theater. Her tone turns bitter, then she suddenly asks if she scared them, claims a Water Imp named Xenia was speaking through her, and plays a prank. She offers a meal on her tab at Podvorye and says to meet at Sadov-Arbat. Alone, she repeats a lament as if answering voices, and names two Water Imps, Xenia and Paraskeva.

Revelations: - Vodyanitsa, a Water Imp, hears the voices of the dead Water Imps in the empty theater and keeps their songs alive through performance.
- She is hurt that many fans treat her handwritten tickets as status symbols, not invitations to listen.
- Her friendship with Lishnaya was real, and the break came when Lishnaya used a ticket for business.
- The Traveler promises to listen to and remember Vodyanitsa's songs, which ends the quest on a hopeful note.

Characters: - Vodyanitsa, the central character, presented as sociable and teasing in public and lonely in private.
- The Traveler and Paimon.
- Odette, the prima ballerina, who explains Vodyanitsa's motives.
- Lishnaya, a guild head, in flashbacks.

Consequences: Vodyanitsa gains a recording device and a promise from the Traveler to hear her songs. She plans to keep performing the Water Imps' music. The Traveler's handwritten ticket remains valid and now gives access to regular shows. Ineffa and Aino also receive tickets.

Placement: Story order: after "Wraith's Nocturne" (a prerequisite). It is recommended after "White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking". Release order: version 7.1. It shares the Korolevskiy Theater setting with "Variations on Belyi and Chernyi", where Odette plans a schedule; Vodyanitsa and Odette appear in both.

974.content: Vodyanitsa gives out tickets she writes by hand to people who love her singing but cannot get a seat. They are valid for nearly any show: the holder sits in an empty seat if there is one, otherwise backstage. She meant them as invitations to listen, but some people tried to bribe her, resold them for large sums, or used them to pose as connected. She plans to declare some tickets invalid.

975.content: Vodyanitsa has memorized every song a Water Imp performed at the Korolevskiy Theater and sings them at special shows. She says she hears Xenia and Paraskeva, two departed Water Imps, in the empty hall. Odette says that to Vodyanitsa, those voices never really disappeared. Whether they are real is left open.

976.content: Lishnaya is the head of a Snezhnayan guild and a member of the Zapolyarny elite. As a girl she loved opera, worked part-time at the theater and was Vodyanitsa's friend. Vodyanitsa says she later used her tickets for networking and to impress a wealthy merchant. Vodyanitsa has not given up on her.

977.content: A small wearable phonograph built by Aino at the Traveler's request, brought by Ineffa. It looks like Vodyanitsa's necklace and has limited recording space. Aino named it after her love of ducks and wanted ice cream for each replacement memory.

key: Valor's Afterglow: The Faint Light Remembered
978.content:
Valor's Afterglow (also: Valor's Afterglow: Return by Sundown, Valor's Afterglow: The Faint Light Remembered, Zhiqiong's Letter quest, Zhiqiong's departure): A three-part Version 2.6 world quest series in The Chasm: Underground Mines. After The Chasm Delvers, the young cartographer Zhiqiong still works for the exploration team. The Traveler helps her place measuring beacons, rescues her when she is trapped in the dark mud, and finds the letter she leaves when she goes deeper alone.

It requires The Chasm Delvers and is released as three quests on consecutive days: Valor's Afterglow, Return by Sundown, and The Faint Light Remembered. Its theme is what drives ordinary mortals without Visions to risk their lives for the chance of being remembered.

Plot: Part 1, Valor's Afterglow (Day 1). The Chasm is now safer, so Zhiqiong asks the Traveler to help place five measuring beacons built by Jinwu. The beacons track the dark mud and gather data for the scholar Khedive to analyse. The Traveler returns with her to the camp and is thanked. If the Traveler talks to her again, she explains why she is so stubborn and reckless: adventurers are drawn to danger, and she hopes to be remembered as one who faced The Chasm.

Part 2, Return by Sundown (Day 2). Jinwu is distraught: Zhiqiong went to retrieve the beacons and has been away five or six hours. The Traveler searches the beacon sites and finds her south of the Stony Halls, trapped in the dark mud and attacked by monsters. After clearing the monsters, the Traveler carries her to the camp. Khedive gives her medicine, and the Traveler brings her Jinwu's soup. Zhiqiong apologises and asks the Traveler to come back later.

Part 3, The Faint Light Remembered (Day 3). Zhiqiong has vanished from the camp, insisting on leaving. Jinwu and the Traveler go up to tell Muning, who learns she has gone and organises a search party. After the quest, the Traveler finds her abandoned camp in the southwest corner of The Glowing Narrows with her letter and a Frostglaze Crystal. The letter says she will follow a path deeper. Back at camp, Jinwu reads it and admits she cannot judge Zhiqiong.

Revelations: Zhiqiong's motives are laid out: she wants to be remembered, to put her own mortal names on the unmapped places of The Chasm, and to show how far someone not chosen by the gods can go. Her letter also questions how the gods and the Traveler regard ordinary mortals and their labour, asked at a time when Rex Lapis had only just left Liyue.

Characters: Zhiqiong: young, headstrong cartographer-adventurer who admires famed adventurers and keeps going despite injury. Jinwu: a veteran of the mines who builds the beacons and looks after the young adventurers, gruff and caring; she gave up on becoming great and feels she cannot judge. Khedive: a scholar of the team (Zhiqiong calls his terminology Sumeru jargon) who analyses the data and gives Zhiqiong medicine. Muning: a Ministry of Civil Affairs official at the surface who sees her as a friend and is angered by her risk-taking. Paimon and the Traveler: support her, rescue her, and disagree on whether to stop her.

Consequences: Zhiqiong's camp stays in The Glowing Narrows permanently. Collecting her letter gives the achievement "Valor's Afterglow" and unlocks a new viewpoint, The Court of Pillars. Her story is left open: the team does not know whether she will return.

Placement: Released in Version 2.6 as a direct follow-up to The Chasm Delvers. Each part is unlocked after the daily reset following the previous one. Release and story order match. Her letter says Rex Lapis has only just left, which places the series shortly after his departure from Liyue.

979.content: A quest item found in a camp in the southwest corner of The Glowing Narrows after The Faint Light Remembered. Zhiqiong addresses Jinwu, Khedive, Clitopho, Muning and the Traveler, asking questions about how the gods see mortals, and announces she will go deeper into The Chasm to mark it on her map with names that belong to mortals. The item text notes a slightly bitter scent of Qingxin.

980.content: Jinwu is a long-serving miner at the Chasm exploration team's camp. She builds the measuring beacons, cooks the soup for Zhiqiong, and watches over the young adventurers. She says she gave up on becoming great and has grown used to ordinary days, so she feels she cannot judge Zhiqiong's choice.

981.content: Muning is a Ministry of Civil Affairs official who helped Zhiqiong get her post in The Chasm. He is Zhiqiong's friend and, when she leaves, organises the Millelith search party. He tells the Traveler that the Ministry had decided to invite her as a formal consultant and guide.

key: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Schedule
982.content:
Variations on Belyi and Chernyi (also: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Schedule, Odette's schedule quest, Black Snow Swan schedule quest): Variations on Belyi and Chernyi is a Snezhnaya World Quest series added in version 7.0 and set at the Korolevskiy Theater. The Traveler and Paimon become Odette's temporary managers for two weeks. Odette is the troupe's prima ballerina, and she is about to premiere the ballet "Black Snow Swan" while also taking on a Fatui monster-clearing mission. The player fills in a schedule of hunts, rehearsals, fan meetings and rest, and the result decides one of five endings.

The quest is unlocked by raising the Korolevskiy Theater Meeting Point to Construction Level 2. It consists of a short setup quest and a longer "Schedule" quest. The planner affects Odette's inner sense of self ("Self-Identity"), how others see her ("External Recognition") and her energy (game-mechanics information); the wiki says that tasks matter more than points for the ending. The series grants Primogems, Mora and talent materials, and the Schedule quest grants a "Black Snow Swan Archive" item.

Plot: Setup. At the theater the Traveler and Paimon see a poster for "Black Snow Swan" and overhear Vodyanitsa trying to talk Odette out of taking a Fatui monster-hunting mission only two weeks before the premiere. Odette insists she can do both, and has applied knowing the schedule. Vodyanitsa makes her agree to let someone else plan her time. Odette chooses the Traveler, citing trust built when they were trapped in the theater and familiarity with the Fatui, while Vodyanitsa objects that she has known Odette much longer and says she would schedule too much rest. The Traveler is given the planner. The premiere is in two weeks and the Fatui mission assessment is in one.

Schedule. Each day the player chooses a type of activity: monster hunt, dance rehearsal, fan meeting, rest or relaxation. Special scenes appear depending on the choice (see below). Week one ends with the Fatui mission examination and week two with the performance.

Revelations: - Odette joined the Fatui as a child, hated it at first, and now finds the work calming. Odette also refers to working with Vodyanitsa through the Rokot.
- The Black Snow Swan is closely tied to Odette's childhood and her sense of difference.
- Sandrone, as Marionette, shows an unexpectedly gentle side and offers Odette advice and tea.

Characters: - Odette, the prima ballerina, central to every scene.
- The Traveler and Paimon, who are her managers.
- Vodyanitsa, who forces the arrangement and joins some scenes.

Consequences: Whichever ending occurs, Odette comes away with a clearer view of herself, though the way she gets there differs. The Traveler receives the Black Snow Swan Archive. The quest does not change Odette's standing in the Fatui or the troupe in any lasting way beyond its endings.

Placement: Story order: after the time the Traveler was trapped in the theater, which Odette mentions as the reason she trusts the Traveler. Release order: version 7.0. "Upstream Variations" (7.1) returns to the same theater and cast.

983.comment: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Black Snow Swan
983.content: A ballet adapted from a literary classic and staged by the Korolevskiy Troupe, with Odette in the lead. It explores the individual versus the collective and fate. The swan is born with feathers of a different colour, refuses to bow to fate, stops trying to fit in with the flock and flies alone into the clouds.

984.comment: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Odette's two lives
984.content: In this series Odette balances ballet with Fatui monster hunting. She says the work calms her and that she joined the Fatui as a child. The Traveler's choices decide which ending she gets, and the quest treats neither life as the wrong one.

985.comment: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Examination day
985.content: Sandrone, as the Harbinger responsible for the assessment, checks the area Odette cleared and passes her if enough work was done. She then gives Odette gruff advice not to bottle up her feelings, and invites her to tea.

key: A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land
986.content:
Varuna Gatha (also: Varuna Gatha World Quest series, Memory of Stone, Irate Iron Chunk, Slumbering Roots, A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land, Varuna Contraption quests): Varuna Gatha is a Sumeru world quest series set in Apam Woods, added in version 3.0 after The World of Aranara. The Traveler and Paimon meet the Aranara Arapandu, who is trying to repair the Varuna Contraption, an ancient machine that turns black rain into good rain. Spores, Fungi and strange rain have wrecked it, and Festival Utsava is near. With three of Arapandu's kin, the Traveler heals it.

The series has two parts. Varuna Gatha is the first quest and then three quests, Memory of Stone, Irate Iron Chunk and Slumbering Roots, can be done in any order, one per Aranara. The finale is A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land. Its reward is the ability to change the weather in Apam Woods using the Rhythm of the Source Water, and it unlocks the Sprouting Seedlings world quest.

Plot: Varuna Gatha. Near the Yasna Monument, Paimon and the Traveler find an Aranara surrounded by Fungi and rescue it. It is Arapandu, who says he has an important task for Festival Utsava, for Apam Woods and for Nara Varuna. He tells how the sun and moon were once lost, black rain gnawed the trees, and a golden Nara called Nara Varuna came, and with the Aranara fixed the Varuna Contraption, which washed Vana's pain away. Now the machine's branches and leaves have weakened and the Varunastra, its great structure, flaps wildly and brings heavy rain; Fungi and spores are everywhere. Arapandu cannot clear the Fungi himself because his Ararakalari is weak. The Traveler defeats Fungi on two trees, they reach a "rest stop" and find the first stone "branch" and three stone "leaves", and the Traveler turns the leaves to face the branch. Arapandu heals them with a dance. Three more such sites remain and Arapandu is worried about the three other Aranara: Aranakula at the Yasna Monument, Arabalika at the Ruins of Dahri and Arakunti at the Grove of Dreams.

The three companions. Memory of Stone: the timid Aranakula hides from the Fungi and sobs but accepts the Traveler's help, and the two go together by a safe route to clean spores from the Memory of Stone, a monument the Aranara made for Nara Varuna, then fix the branch and leaves there. Irate Iron Chunk: the Traveler meets Arabalika, a master of Ararakalari who says little, defeats Ruin Guards beside him, and finds that the branch is deep underground like roots. Slumbering Roots: in the Grove of Dreams the Traveler plays Aranara music to bring out Arakunti, a dreamy Aranara, and enters a dream to repair the sites.

A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land. With all branches and leaves healed, the Aranara descend beneath the Varunastra to the roots of the Contraption, clear spores and defeat a Winged Dendroshroom, the "bad bug" damaging it. The rain clears and the air improves. Arapandu teaches the Traveler the music to control the Contraption, Rhythm of the Source Water, and says the Traveler is worthy of Aranara friendship like Nara Varuna.

Revelations: - The Varuna Contraption is an ancient machine, made by Aramuhukunda and the Lord of Dendro, that turns bad rain into good rain and heals the land of Vana.
- The Contraption has fallen into disrepair: the Aranara no longer fully understand it, Nara Varuna and Aramuhukunda are gone from Vanarana, and spores and Fungi grew thick around it.
- The Contraption can be controlled by Aranara music, and the Traveler learns it.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; four Aranara: Arapandu (leader of the effort), Aranakula (timid, loves soil and seeds), Arabalika (strong, terse, a master of Ararakalari) and Arakunti (dreamy, linked to the Grove of Dreams). Araja and Arama of Vanarana are mentioned as organisers of the festival preparations. Silapna is a feature of the Grove of Dreams before which the Traveler plays music.

Consequences: The Varuna Contraption works again, the rain in Apam Woods improves and the worst of the spores recedes, though Marana remain. The Traveler learns the Rhythm of the Source Water. Aranakula hopes to restore the nurseries, and the wider thread about Vimara Village is left to Arapandu to follow up.

Placement: Released in 3.0 with the Sumeru launch. The wiki lists The World of Aranara as the requirement; the first quest begins southeast of the Yasna Monument. Memory of Stone, Irate Iron Chunk and Slumbering Roots start after Varuna Gatha and can be done in any order, and A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land follows them. The series leads to Sprouting Seedlings.

987.content: The Varuna Contraption is a machine created by Aramuhukunda and the Lord of Dendro in Vana to purify rain; the Varunastra is its great visible structure in Apam Woods. When Arapandu meets the Traveler it is out of order: spore-laden rain falls and Fungi spread. Its "branches" and "leaves" are stone sites spread across the forest and its roots are underground. After the quests, playing the Rhythm of the Source Water near it changes the weather.

988.content: Nara Varuna is an earlier golden Nara whom the Aranara remember for restoring the sun and moon and repairing the Varuna Contraption. The Aranara use the same words for the Traveler, and the Memory of Stone is a memorial for Nara Varuna. Canon in this series gives no further identity, and Nara Varuna is no longer in Vanarana.

989.content: Arapandu is an Aranara who leads the effort to repair the Varuna Contraption. He is earnest and gentle, speaks in simple storybook terms, and has a weak Ararakalari. He trusts Paimon despite her teasing, and later promises to look into Vimara Village.

990.content: Aranakula is a timid Aranara who is at ease with soil and seeds and who hides when Fungi are near. He keeps the Memory of Stone, dreads bad spores, and measures himself unfavourably against Arabalika. He hopes to revive the nursery flowers.

991.content: Arabalika is a terse, strong Aranara with a powerful Ararakalari who defends the Ruins of Dahri against Ruin Guards. He tests the Traveler's strength, warns Paimon not to be careless, and reminds everyone that Marana remain.

992.content: Arakunti is a dreamy Aranara who withdrew to the Grove of Dreams. He speaks in a drifting poetic way, enjoys music and mushrooms, and the Traveler must play Aranara music to draw him out.

key: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze
The Glede Returns to the Pavilion
993.comment: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze
993.content:
Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze (also: Vibrant Harriers event, Festive Affairs, Lantern Rite 2024, Hustle and Bustle, The Glede Returns to the Pavilion): The Lantern Rite theme combined Liyue's traditional kite-making with Fontaine's "Mechanical Vertical Lifting Device," arranged through Ningguang and the Fontaine writer Charlotte. The event also offered three festival activities (Paper Shadows A-Foraging, Joyful Beasts and Their Auspices and Iridescent Cloud-Striding) whose Festive Fever gave Xingqiu's outfit "Bamboo Rain" and a choice of 4-star Liyue character. The story is light and family-centred.

Plot: Part I, The Orioles Bask in Spring, the Heavens Present Auspices: Keqing and Charlotte tell the Traveler that this year's festival theme is kites, combining Liyue craft with Fontaine technology, and that the Qixing are holding a contest. Two strangers who call themselves Houzhang and Jiehu turn out to be Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver, looking for Xianyun because Jueyun Karst has been unusually quiet since she moved to the harbor. The Traveler helps Gaming deliver a shipment to Yilong Wharf, where Gaming asks to avoid his family. Xianyun, told of the pair, rushes off to buy them tea and invites the Traveler to her kite workshop at Mt. Aocang.

Part II, A Cloud-Sea Appeal, a Brilliance Revealed: over dim sum at Xinyue Kiosk, Gaming says he is not rich, his father runs a small tea business that could not compete with the Feiyun Commerce Guild, and he wants to be a wushou dancer while his father disagrees. At Mt. Aocang Xianyun teaches kite-making to the Traveler, Ganyu, Shenhe and Yaoyao; a mechanical kite from the pair of adepti interrupts, and Xianyun, angry, learns it was bought in festive spirit. Hearing Gaming's story, she resolves to help.

Part III, The Glede Returns to the Pavilion: a staged "bandit" ambush lets Gaming's father, Yip Tak, see his son protect him; Zhongli helps by speaking well of Gaming and of wushou dancers. Xianyun and Shenhe nudge the two into talking, and Charlotte, the 'important client', interviews Tak about his tea; Paimon explains she will take it to Fontaine along with her article, which could bring new customers from abroad. At the festival Gaming performs a wushou dance in the dark, Xianyun lifts the grounded kites with her own, and Tak finally accepts his son's choice.

Part IV, Hustle and Bustle: afterwards the Traveler goes to Qiaoying Village to find Hu Tao and runs into Navia and Clorinde (who came with Furina), then Furina, who is gathering props for a horror film with Hu Tao's help. Neuvillette had also come and left. Zhongli and Hu Tao have been helping with the props. Back in Fontaine Neuvillette gives Wriothesley the tea Clorinde owed him.

Revelations: The event shows Xianyun lives in Liyue Harbor and runs a kite workshop for her disciples. It reveals Gaming's background: his father is a tea merchant whose business could not compete with the Feiyun Commerce Guild, and Gaming left home over his wushou dream. It also shows that Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver feel neglected by Xianyun.

Characters: Gaming is the emotional centre. Xianyun is mischievous and caring, organising the plan to reconcile father and son. Zhongli, Shenhe, Ganyu and Yaoyao support; Charlotte gives Fontaine's perspective. Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver (as Houzhang and Jiehu) provide comedy. Furina, Navia, Clorinde, Neuvillette and Wriothesley appear in Part IV.

Consequences: Tak accepts that Gaming will pursue wushou dancing and Gaming decides to thank everyone who helped. Charlotte's plan to feature Tak's tea in Fontaine is expected, in Paimon's words, to bring him new business. Furina asks that Neuvillette take more time off, and he says he will consider it.

Placement: Released in Version 4.4 for the 2024 Lantern Rite, between the 2023 event The Exquisite Night Chimes and the 2025 event Springtime Charms. Parts I to III unlock in sequence; Part IV (Hustle and Bustle) opened on 11 February 2024.

994.comment: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze: Gaming and Yip Tak
994.content: In this event Gaming, a guard and wushou dancer who has left home, reconciles with his tea-merchant father Yip Tak. Tak feared the dance would not sustain him as he grew older and regretted having shown him wushou when he was young; he changes his mind after seeing Gaming's performance and perseverance.

995.comment: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze: Mechanical Vertical Lifting Device
995.content: Fontaine's popular Mechanical Vertical Lifting Device is combined with Liyue's traditional kite-making for the 2024 Lantern Rite after Ningguang contacts Charlotte. Zhenyuan sells it on her stall, and Xianyun lifts the rest of the kites with her own using adeptal power.

996.content:
Vimana Agama (also: Vimana Agama world quest series, Vimana Agama: First Chapter, Royinjan's Chapter, Jazari's Chapter, Dev Delver Chapter): A four-part Sumeru world quest series from Version 3.0, unlocked after the Aranara quest The World of Aranara. An Aranara named Ararycan has noticed that something is sickening the forest around Devantaka Mountain. The Traveler and Paimon team up with Jazari, an eager researcher from the Kshahrewar school, and Royinjan, an antique dealer in Port Ormos, to open a giant Khaenri'ahn Ruin Golem and reach the leaking Chaos Core beneath it. The pollution is traced to that core and to Abyss Order mages working in the cavern.

Tonally the series mixes comedy (Jazari's academic enthusiasm, Royinjan's haggling) with a quieter story about childhood friendship and forgotten memory. Humans lose the ability to see Aranara as they grow up, and the middle chapter shows what that costs. The series gives Ardravi Valley its Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain and introduces Dev's Cavern.

Plot: Araja and Arama send the Traveler to Ararycan, who has seen a suspicious figure near Devantaka Mountain. The figure is Jazari, who has Akademiya permission to study the mountain's giant Ruin Golem. Ararycan explains that filth is making the forest sick. Jazari thinks the golem's removed Chaos Core, sealed in Dev's Cavern, is leaking energy. To enter the golem the party needs an Amiti Device, which leads them to Royinjan, then to his childhood hideout in Vimara Village, then through the golem to the cavern, where they defeat Abyss Mages and an Abyss Lector and switch off the extraction device.

The chain of errands: Ararycan's report leads to Jazari, whose research needs an Amiti Device. Royinjan haggles over a wrongly identified Chaos Core, then admits the real device was his grandfather Hasad's and guides the party to his childhood hideout in Vimara Village. Three fragments (one in the hideout, two in the Linga and Yoni caves) are repaired by Jazari. Inside the golem the Traveler restores power and fights a cursed knight; the golem's arm falls and opens Dev's Cavern, where the Traveler defeats Abyss Mages and an Abyss Lector and shuts off an extraction device. Ararycan then leaves for Festival Utsava.

Revelations: The forest's illness around Devantaka Mountain is caused by a leaking Chaos Core in Dev's Cavern, tied to a Khaenri'ahn Ruin Golem, with the Abyss Order working in the cavern. Ararycan was once the friend of Royinjan and Amadhiah as children, but remembers nothing of it.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, with Ararycan (an Aranara), Jazari (a Kshahrewar researcher), Royinjan (an antique dealer) and Amadhiah (a Vimara villager).

Ararycan is a gentle, timid Aranara who speaks of itself in the third person. Jazari is an enthusiastic scholar of the Kshahrewar school with a research permit from the Akademiya; he is short of funds and a little boastful but sincere. Royinjan, who calls himself the Chief Antique Appraiser, is a shrewd merchant in Port Ormos and the grandson of the adventurer Hasad. Amadhiah is an elderly Vimara villager and Royinjan's childhood friend. Arama and Araja, Aranara from the Aranyaka series, send the Traveler to Ararycan. Nahida's All Schemes to Know offers optional glimpses of Royinjan's and Jazari's thoughts.

Consequences: The golem's arm is broken, the cavern is open, the Chaos Core is cut off from the extraction device and the forest's illness should slowly ease. Jazari remains in the golem to continue his research, and Ararycan will guard the forest after the festival. The final chapter gives a Sumeru reputation reward.

Placement: Released in Version 3.0 with Sumeru; it requires the world quest The World of Aranara and so follows the opening of the Aranara story. Order of parts: First Chapter, Royinjan's Chapter (with sub-quests Linga and Yoni, which can be done in either order), Jazari's Chapter, Dev Delver Chapter.

997.comment: Vimana Agama: Dev's Cavern and the Chaos Core
997.content: Beneath Devantaka Mountain lies a giant Khaenri'ahn Ruin Golem whose power core was removed and sealed underground in Dev's Cavern. In the Vimana Agama series the sealed core leaks pollution into the forest while an extraction device and Abyss Order mages work in the cavern. The Amiti Device, assembled from three fragments, opens the golem. The Traveler breaks into the cavern using the golem's arm and shuts off the extraction device.

998.comment: Vimana Agama: Royinjan and the Secret Base
998.content: Royinjan runs an antique shop in Port Ormos. As a boy he played in a secret base at Vimara Village with Amadhiah and a third friend he cannot remember, the Aranara Ararycan. Amadhiah drifted away from adventuring; Royinjan stayed on longer but later became an antique appraiser, partly inspired by the stories of his grandfather Hasad. They remain on tense but fond terms.

999.content:
Vulpes Zerda Chapter (also: Vulpes Zerda, Tighnari's Story Quest, The Unanswerable Problems, The Start of Contamination, Into the Hinterland, Heart of the Machine, Garden Memories): The Vulpes Zerda Chapter is Tighnari's Story Quest, released in Version 3.0, and as of 7.1 it has one act, The Unanswerable Problems. A strange contamination spreading through Avidya Forest sends Tighnari and the Traveler deep into the woods, led by Karkata, a mechanical crab that steals machine parts. They find that it was made by a researcher Tighnari knew at the Akademiya, who died in his laboratory.

The act has four quests: The Start of Contamination, Into the Hinterland, Heart of the Machine and Garden Memories. It is a quiet investigation story. The culprit is not a villain but a runaway experiment and an unfinished life, and the emotional weight lies in Tighnari's decision about what to do with the dead man's work.

Plot: In Sumeru City, Katheryne tells the Traveler and Paimon of a commission about contamination in Avidya Forest. They suspect a Withering Zone, but Katheryne says it looks like something else. They go to Gandharva Ville, where Tighnari is treating a boy named Yara. Tighnari wants Vasanti Grass for the cure, but the merchant Mahir has closed up shop: the merchants pooled money for machine parts that a crab-like machine stole and carried deep into the forest, and they dared not follow because of rumours of the contamination. The group lures the thief out with spare parts and drives it off; Tighnari sees that it cannot follow complex questions and is interested only in mechanical parts. He promises it more parts if it shows him its hiding place, sets traps, and recovers the stolen goods. With Collei's help he prepares Yara's medicine.

Tighnari and the Traveler return to the crab, which has not tried to escape, and it leads them on in return for more parts. They pass a glowing Sumeru Rose, which Tighnari explains is called the Ley Line Lodestar and glows unnaturally when nearby Ley Lines are dangerous. They notice no animals; Tighnari believes the animals have fled the disrupted Ley Lines. A purification device he made works and brings animals back. The crab darts away to a group of Ruin Machines, the pair defeat them and find Jasar, a herb-picker who wandered in and stayed too long in the contaminated area; Tighnari sends him to Gandharva Ville. At camp the two take turns on watch, the crab serves coffee, and Tighnari explains why the Akademiya banned research into mechanical life forms.

Revelations: - The contamination comes from Ley Line extractors, not a Withering Zone.
- Karkata was built by Abattouy, a former Akademiya researcher whom Tighnari knew.

Characters: - **Tighnari**: forest ranger and former Akademiya scholar, who leads the investigation.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: companions on the journey.
- **Katheryne**: Adventurers' Guild receptionist who gives the commission.
- **Karkata**: the mechanical crab that steals parts.
- **Abattouy**: the dead researcher, known only through recordings.
- **Collei**: Tighnari's apprentice, who helps make Yara's cure.
- **Yara, Mahir, Jasar**: a sick boy, a merchant and a herb-picker caught up in events.

Consequences: The extractors are shut down and the contamination ends. Karkata survives under Tighnari's care at Pardis Dhyai, and Abattouy's laboratory and most of his research are destroyed.

Placement: Released in Version 3.0 and unlocked after Chapter III Act II of the Archon Quest and Adventure Rank 40. Story order and release order match. Only Act I exists as of 7.1.

1000.content: A mechanical crab built by the researcher Abattouy, who tried to give it life and gave it instincts. It steals machine parts and has been programmed to make coffee. After Abattouy died, Karkata tried to repair him. Tighnari repaired Karkata and keeps it at Pardis Dhyai, perhaps as a research assistant.

1001.content: A researcher Tighnari knew at the Akademiya. He worked on making Karkata a living thing, built Ley Line extractors for power, and died of the energy overload. Tighnari buried him and destroyed most of his research and laboratory.

1002.content:
Vultur Volans Chapter (Alhaitham) (also: Vultur Volans Chapter, Vultur Volans, Alhaitham's Story Quest, The Illusions of the Mob, Fragmented Testimony, A Thorough Investigation, Pride and Prejudice): Alhaitham's Story Quest. As Acting Grand Sage, he joins the Traveler and the Matra in tracing a researcher, Ilyas, who was abducted by Vahumana scholar Siraj. Siraj is building a ranked 'hive mind' of followers, and Alhaitham, who rejected Siraj's paper years ago, takes it apart.

The chapter has one act, The Illusions of the Mob, made of three quests: Fragmented Testimony, A Thorough Investigation and Pride and Prejudice. It uses Alhaitham's blunt, unsentimental style to show how a group can become a trap for the people who join it.

Plot: Researchers at the Akademiya gossip about Alhaitham. Ilyas says Siraj abducted him; the Matra confirm it. Alhaitham explains that Siraj was a classmate whose paper on human evolution he rejected. The trail leads from Ilyas' former colleagues to Siraj's hideout, where Ilyas' own earlier choices come out. Alhaitham undermines Siraj's system and Cyno has him detained. Afterwards Alhaitham explains at home that he has resigned the Grand Sage post.

Fragmented Testimony: Ilyas asks to speak to the Matra. Alhaitham joins Aarav's investigation, and the group go to Lambad's Tavern to question Narendra, who sold electrical parts to Siraj. Alhaitham says he and Siraj were classmates, and that he rejected Siraj's thesis on human evolution when Azar asked his opinion. Ilyas wants his paycheck for his family in Gandharva Ville.

A Thorough Investigation: Makesh says Ilyas can collect his pay if he learns why Chandra withdrew. Chandra explains that, with the sages gone and the Akasha off, researchers wait for a famous name. Ilyas recalls Siraj calling him 'Siraj #36'. Alhaitham explains that Siraj wanted a rank-based hive mind with an overmind at the top. Janaki declined a membership because she was ranked #45, based on Jnana energy once taken by the sages. The House of Daena papers show Ilyas had been honoured for reporting his instructor's fraud. At Gandharva Ville, Ilyas' family says they have received threatening letters for his 'heroism', and he guides them to the hideout.

Pride and Prejudice: Ilyas vanishes at the hideout. Visions show his past, in which his report on Jani led to Raju's death and angered other colleagues, and that he later joined Siraj willingly. In the domain Ilyas says he wanted to meet them as himself before merging into the Hive. Siraj defends his project, Alhaitham says its model is unstable, and monsters appear. The collective begins to question Siraj and collapses. Cyno arrives and the Matra detain Siraj. At home Alhaitham explains why he disapproved of the thesis and resigned.

Revelations: Siraj wanted to merge scholars into a ranked collective mind. Alhaitham rejected his paper long ago.

Siraj ranked followers by Jnana energy the sages had extracted. Alhaitham resigned as Acting Grand Sage.

Characters: Alhaitham, Ilyas, Siraj, the Traveler and Paimon.

Matra Aarav, Cyno, Kaveh, and Akademiya figures Narendra, Makesh, Chandra and Janaki.

Consequences: Siraj is detained and his associates arrested. Alhaitham submits his resignation as Acting Grand Sage.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises (Chapter III Act V). Released in 3.4 on 2023-01-18, so it takes place after the Sumeru Archon Quest, once Azar has been replaced.

1003.content: A prominent Vahumana scholar and Alhaitham's former classmate who was expected to become a sage. His thesis on human evolution was sent to Azar, who asked Alhaitham's opinion, and Alhaitham rejected it. He built a rank-ordered collective of followers, the Hive, using their Jnana energy. It collapsed in the Vultur Volans Chapter and he was detained by the Matra.

1004.content: After Azar's removal Alhaitham became Acting Grand Sage but dislikes the title. He submits his resignation at the end of the chapter, worried that the longer he held it the more permanent it might become, and wants to return to his original duties.

1005.content:
Wanderer's Trail (also: Wanderers Trail, Genshin Impact opening quest, Traveler's awakening): Wanderer's Trail is the first quest of Genshin Impact's story. An opening cinematic shows the Traveler and their twin stopped by an unknown god who seals the Traveler and takes the sibling away. The Traveler then appears on a Mondstadt beach, tells Paimon that they intend to find out how long they were sealed, and follows Paimon toward a Statue of The Seven. It doubles as a movement tutorial.

It belongs to the Prologue and Act I, "The Outlander Who Caught the Wind", and was part of Version 1.0. The next quest is Bird's Eye View. The quest starts at Stormbearer Coast in Mondstadt and its tutorial teaches basic movement, climbing and stamina.

Plot: The opening cinematic is framed as the Traveler telling their story to Paimon: they fell into this world from another, and when they tried to move on, an unknown god barred the way. He names himself the sustainer of heavenly principles and says that the arrogation of mankind ends now. The twins fight him and are overpowered; the sibling is swallowed by a swarm of red and black cubes and condensed into one cube held in the god's hand. The Traveler tries to take their sibling back and is engulfed too, then the scene cuts to black.

On the beach, the Traveler explains that some seal robbed them of their power, so that they who once crossed world after world are now trapped. They do not know how many years have passed but resolve to find out. They woke alone, and only met Paimon two months earlier; Paimon says she would likely have drowned otherwise and promises to be a good guide.

The player then follows Paimon, defeats an optional Hydro Slime, unlocks a Teleport Waypoint, and comes to the foot of a cliff where there is no path. Paimon prompts the player to climb, notes that climbing uses stamina that needs time to recover, and says the planned route leads to a Statue of The Seven. She asks which of The Seven the Traveler is looking for, which leads into Act I.

Revelations: The Traveler has a twin who was taken by a god, was themself sealed and lost their power, and is searching for their sibling. The two had travelled between worlds before being stopped.

Paimon has known the Traveler for two months, since they saved her from drowning. The god's title, sustainer of heavenly principles, is the only description of him given here; the Prologue and later Archon Quests develop what that means.

Characters: The Traveler (Aether or Lumine according to the player's choice, named in the cinematic only through their sibling), Paimon, and the unnamed god who is later identified as Asmoday.

The twin is shown fighting beside the Traveler but is never heard speaking except through the Traveler's shout of their name. Paimon is the Traveler's companion and guide from here on.

Consequences: The quest sets the Traveler's goals: finding the missing sibling, and learning what the seal and the god mean. It leads directly into Bird's Eye View and the rest of the Prologue, where the Traveler seeks The Seven in Mondstadt.

Placement: Story order and release order agree: this is the first quest of the first act of the Prologue (Version 1.0) and precedes Bird's Eye View. Its cinematic event, the sealing, happens long before the present-day story; the beach scene is the story's present.

1006.content: At the start of Wanderer's Trail the twins stand on a structure in the sky while Paimon asks them about their journey. A white-clad god bars their path. The Traveler and their twin fight him without success, the sibling is cubed and taken, and the Traveler is also cubed and sealed. The god is unnamed on screen; the wiki names him Asmoday.

1007.content:
Waterborne Poetry (also: Waterborne Poetry event, Neighboring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala, Poetry Gala, Congenial Gathering, Tears Among the Leaves, Heart of the Deep): Part I introduces the gala and its riddle theme, Part II the couplet theme and an "inspiration walk," and Part III the reveal of Callirhoe's identity. The event also offered three mini-games (Hundred-Pace Hurling Rites, Inspiration Eruption, Mending Painting Prospects) that earned Poetry Gala Fervor, redeemable for the weapon Ballad of the Boundless Blue, a Crown of Insight and weapon refinement materials. After the story Hu Tao keeps trying to publish an anthology and Xiao quietly writes his first poem.

Plot: Part I, Congenial Gathering: at Wangshu Inn the Traveler and Paimon find Hu Tao and Venti trying to persuade Xiao, who declines to attend because of his karmic afflictions. At Stone Gate they meet Xingqiu and Chongyun, Diona (representing the Cat's Tail and Mondstadt's wine trade), and Mika and Noelle, sent by the Knights of Favonius to keep order. Hu Tao and Venti open the gala; the first theme is riddles, hung on lanterns. Chongyun mentions an investigation that Xingqiu promised to help with; it concerns something strange he saw near the water.

Part II, Tears Among the Leaves: the second theme is Liyue couplets, plus an "inspiration walk" in two groups. One group (the Traveler, Paimon, Diona, Chongyun and, joined later, Xiao) follows a poem written on a floating leaf upstream and replies with a poem of its own. The other (Xingqiu, Mika, Noelle) meets Callirhoe, a Fontaine visitor who wrote one of the riddles.

Part III, Heart of the Deep: Callirhoe is missing. A second leaf points upstream, and the party finds her surrounded by hilichurls and then transformed into a water droplet. She reveals she is an Oceanid and the spring fairy of Springvale from the story "Heart of Clear Springs," and with the group's help meets Old Finch again, reads him a poem and gives him a droplet of her power before her form fades.

Revelations: Callirhoe is an Oceanid (Mika explains Oceanids were familiars of the former Hydro Archon), and is the real spring fairy behind the Springvale story "Heart of Clear Springs." The boy of the story is Old Finch. Callirhoe has been recovering her power slowly in Springvale for decades, can hold a physical form only briefly, and her water droplet matches what Chongyun saw. She can now meet Finch in his dreams through the droplet she left him.

Characters: Hu Tao and Venti co-host and joke together. Xingqiu and Chongyun, Diona, Mika and Noelle form the companion group; Xiao and Zhongli join for parts. Callirhoe is the emotional centre, with Old Finch at the end. Mika and Noelle show the Knights of Favonius at work, with Mika's mapping skills guiding the final search.

Consequences: Callirhoe and Old Finch are reunited; she says she will meet him in his dreams. The group keeps her secret. Hu Tao pursues her anthology and Xiao finds calm in writing.

Placement: Released in Version 4.1 and set at Stone Gate in Liyue's Bishui Plain, with scenes at Wangshu Inn and in Springvale in Mondstadt. It is a flagship event outside Lantern Rite. The event story chains Congenial Gathering, Tears Among the Leaves and Heart of the Deep over three days.

1008.content: Callirhoe is an Oceanid who settled at Springvale after losing most of her power. She is the spring fairy of the story "Heart of Clear Springs." In Waterborne Poetry she appears as a poet from Fontaine, writes a riddle for the gala, and reunites with Old Finch, to whom she gives a droplet of her power.

1009.comment: Waterborne Poetry: Neighboring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala
1009.content: A three-day poetry gathering at Stone Gate organised by Hu Tao and Venti. The themes are Riddle Me This, pairing couplets with an inspiration walk, and freestyle poetry. Venti stresses authenticity, and Hu Tao hopes to publish an anthology.

1010.content:
We Will Be Reunited (also: Chapter I Act IV): Chapter I Act IV of the Archon Quest. After first travelling with Dainsleif, the Traveler and Paimon follow the Abyss Order's plan to build a mechanical god from a Defiled Statue, hear the outline of Khaenri'ah's fall, and end the act facing their own sibling, who leaves with the Order.

The act has four quests: Involuntary Sacrifice, A Herald Without Adherents, Dishonorable Trial and A Soul Set Apart. It moves from Abyss Order ruins in Liyue and Order camps around Jueyun Karst to Mondstadt (the Favonius Cathedral and Wolvendom) and then Stormterror's Lair. It is where Dainsleif first speaks to the Traveler of Khaenri'ah and where the Traveler meets their sibling again. Released in version 1.4.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon take an Adventurers' Guild commission about a Treasure Hoarder raid on Abyss Order ruins in Liyue. Inside they find a Defiled Statue of Barbatos hung upside down. With Dainsleif they work out that the Order wants to build a mechanised god and needs a Field Tiller's eye. They find the Field Tiller in Stormterror's Lair and Dainsleif takes its eye, but back at the ruins the Traveler's sibling intervenes and leaves with the Abyss Herald.

Involuntary Sacrifice: at the Liyue Adventurers' Guild, where they find Ganyu and Lan, Ganyu explains that Treasure Hoarders plan a heist on the Abyss Order and have posted a commission because the Qixing are too busy; the Traveler accepts. In the ruins they find a Defiled Statue of Barbatos hanging inverted, the dead Grand Thief of the Treasure Hoarders, and a tremor that sends them fleeing. An Abyss Herald stops them near the exit and, after a short fight, teleports away.

A Herald Without Adherents: outside, Dainsleif is surprised to see them. He has never heard of an inverted statue but, from the Traveler's description, ties it to the Abyss Order. Tracking Order groups around Jueyun Karst, he speaks of Khaenri'ah, which brings back part of the Traveler's memory of the fallen nation. A talisman he translates reveals the first phase of the Order's plan: attach the limbs of Osial, whom the Traveler fought alongside the Qixing and the adepti, to the Defiled Statue, and use the eye of the first Field Tiller in place of the orb a Statue of the Seven normally holds, to construct a mechanised god.

Dishonorable Trial: the Traveler goes to the Favonius Cathedral in Mondstadt while Dainsleif waits outside, having asked them not to mention the missing statue. Barbara confirms that one of the Cathedral's statues is missing and tells of the "Tyrant's Final Fury", missiles that struck people approaching Old Mondstadt for about a year before stopping. Rosaria reports that the Abyss Order is attacking Wolvendom. There the Traveler interrupts the Herald as it again subjects Boreas to a corrupting ritual, and the Herald flees. Boreas and Razor thank them, and Boreas recalls that a strange machine once entered his territory, which he fought and damaged before it fled.

A Soul Set Apart: combining Boreas' and Barbara's accounts, they conclude the Field Tiller is the machine behind the Tyrant's Final Fury, and Paimon realises it is the Weird Statue in Stormterror's Lair. Dainsleif extracts its eye and takes custody of it, and suggests destroying the Defiled Statue so the Order cannot restart the plan. Back at the ruins the Herald attacks with Abyss Mages; Dainsleif pins the Herald but is stopped by a sword shockwave. The interrupter is the Traveler's sibling.

Revelations: Khaenri'ah is named and its fall described; the Abyss Order is shown actively trying to make a mechanised god; the Traveler's sibling is alive and working with the Order.

Dainsleif's account of Khaenri'ah: a nation that never had a god, whose human civilisation flourished at a very advanced pace until it was destroyed by gods about five centuries ago. He says the Ruin Guards are a modern name for what were once called Field Tillers, powerful mortal weapons that wandered Teyvat after the destruction. The sibling identifies him as the Twilight Sword, a Khaenri'ahn royal guard under an immortality curse.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Dainsleif, the Traveler's sibling and an Abyss Herald are the principals.

Supporting cast: Ganyu and Lan (Liyue Adventurers' Guild), Barbara and Rosaria (Mondstadt), Boreas and Razor (Wolvendom), the dead Grand Thief of the Treasure Hoarders, and Abyss Mages. Osial is not present but his limbs are the Order's target.

Consequences: Dainsleif holds the Field Tiller's eye and the Order's attempt to build a mechanised god is halted for now. The Traveler's sibling has left again through a portal with the Herald, and Dainsleif followed them into it. The Traveler resolves to continue to Inazuma. The thread resumes in Requiem of the Echoing Depths, where Dainsleif recalls that the same thing happened when he chased the sibling into a portal.

Placement: Chapter I Act IV, following A New Star Approaches and preceding Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves. Unlocked in play by Bough Keeper: Dainsleif and the Lupus Minor Chapter Act I (The Meaning of Lupical). Released in version 1.4.

1011.comment: We Will Be Reunited: The Defiled Statue ruins and the mechanised god plan
1011.content: In Abyss Order ruins in Liyue the Traveler finds a statue of Barbatos hung upside down. Dainsleif had not heard of such a thing but ties it to the Abyss Order. A translated talisman states the plan: attach Osial's limbs to the statue and fit the eye of the first Field Tiller where a Statue of the Seven holds its orb, producing a mechanised god. Dainsleif takes the eye and recommends destroying the statue.

1012.comment: We Will Be Reunited: Field Tiller and the Tyrant's Final Fury
1012.content: Dainsleif says the Ruin Guards are modern names for Khaenri'ah's Field Tillers. Barbara describes the Tyrant's Final Fury as missiles that hit people near Old Mondstadt for roughly a year. Boreas recalls a strange machine that entered his territory long ago, was fought and damaged, and left. The Traveler and Paimon deduce it is the Weird Statue in Stormterror's Lair.

1013.comment: We Will Be Reunited: Twilight Sword
1013.content: In this act the Traveler's sibling calls Dainsleif the Twilight Sword, a royal guard of Khaenri'ah who failed to protect it and was cursed with immortality. Dainsleif knows the sibling as well. In Requiem of the Echoing Depths he tells the Traveler it was his title as captain of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard five hundred years ago.

key: People of the Springs Tribal Chronicle
Those Searching for the Mysterious Island
The Legend of the Mysterious Island
The Riddle of Sea and Sky
1014.content:
Where the Springs Return (also: People of the Springs Tribal Chronicle, Those Searching for the Mysterious Island, The Legend of the Mysterious Island, Journey to the Mysterious Island, Someone Trustworthy, Where the Koholasaurs Gather, The Riddle of Sea and Sky): The Tribal Chronicles chapter of the People of the Springs, which also serves as Mualani's story quest. The tribe has an old legend of a mysterious island, hidden in a rarely visited domain, that promises great wealth and glory. After helping the chief Amina expose a ring of tourist scammers, the Traveler learns the single condition for reaching the island: travel with companions you would trust with your life. The Traveler and Paimon ask Mualani to guide them, and together with two Sumeru scholars they complete the trip.

The chapter has three acts: Those Searching for the Mysterious Island, The Legend of the Mysterious Island and Journey to the Mysterious Island. It is a story about what a journey is for. The island is real, but the treasure the legend advertises is not what the first chief found, and the Traveler and Mualani choose to keep the ending secret so that the legend can go on inviting new guides.

Plot: Act I. While exploring the People of the Springs, the Traveler and Paimon rescue two Sumeru scholars, Karya and Viramdra, from Koholasaurs. The scholars are searching for the mysterious island for Viramdra's research, and Paimon decides she wants to see it too. They go to the tribe's chief to ask what is known.

Act II. The chief Amina tells them the legend of the first chief and the island, and asks a favour: pose as gullible tourists so that a gang of fake guides can be caught. The Traveler and Paimon are led around by Kaulu and Kaeho, who charge for photos and gear, until Kaulu's shortcut ends at a plainly fake "island" and he reveals his trick, only to be seized by Amina and a group of tribespeople. Amina explains the real requirement: the island can only be reached by a group of close friends who trust each other with their lives, so a hired guide is no use. Paimon realises they should ask Mualani.

Act III. Mualani agrees to guide the Traveler and Paimon, and the party also takes in Karya and Viramdra. Mualani buys camping gear, receives a copy of the first chief's map and a protective talisman from her teacher Nuu, then leads the group through four stages: sneaking into a valley of gathering Koholasaurs to copy a clue, working Phlogiston Nodes to open a way through a Spiritway and toward a giant whirlpool, a rescue of Viramdra, and a descent into a volcanic cave. There Viramdra recognises a golden glow as the island, Mualani turns the group back, and they discover the real answer at the tribe's founding statue.

Revelations: The mysterious island of legend is the place the People of the Springs live now. At the end of the cave journey, hidden text on the first chief's statue (visible only to those whose bodies carry volcanic dust from the underground space) tells how he went in search of the island to prove himself and travelled with friends who helped and trusted him. At the end he saw that the golden glow signalled an imminent eruption, chose not to press on, returned empty-handed, and realised that his surviving friends were the treasure. They went home together and founded the tribe.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon are the viewpoint pair. Mualani, the tribe's young surfer and guide, leads the main journey and is the chapter's emotional centre. Amina, the tribe's chief, appears in Act II and sets out the requirement for reaching the island. Nuu is Mualani's teacher and the keeper of a copy of the map. Viramdra and Karya are Sumeru Akademiya scholars: Viramdra of the Spantamad Darshan specialises in ores and minerals, and Karya is his assistant. Koolau is the tribe's top-ranked guide. Kaulu and Kaeho are the fake guides in Act II.

Consequences: Mualani completes her teacher's test and returns the talisman, which Nuu tells her to pass on to her own student one day. Karya and Viramdra part from the group, with Viramdra agreeing to keep the journey secret and promising to acknowledge Mualani in his next paper. The Traveler receives a commemorative group photo with Mualani. Amina's ring of scammers is exposed. The legend of the mysterious island stays in circulation, and the tribe's guides keep its true answer to themselves.

Placement: Release order: the chapter's three acts came with Version 5.0 (the wiki gives the event window as 2024-08-28 to 2024-09-17). Story order: Acts I and II require only the Archon Quest part Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, while Act III requires Into Eternal Night, in the Chapter V part Black Stone Under a White Stone, so it takes place after the Traveler and Mualani have visited the Night Kingdom together. Someone Trustworthy refers back to that trip as proof the Traveler and Paimon can trust Mualani.

key: Map Left Behind by the First Chief
1015.comment: Where the Springs Return: The Mysterious Island and the First Chief
1015.content: The People of the Springs tell of their first chief, once Natlan's most celebrated guide, who went in search of a mysterious island said to shine with gold and hold countless treasures, reached it, and left behind a map of strange symbols and riddles instead of claiming the treasure. Copies were given to the tribe's first members and are passed from teacher to student. Guides must read the map by experience. The stated requirement is to travel with friends you trust with your life. The island is in fact the tribe's own home, as revealed by a message on the founding statue only visible to those who went through the underground volcanic cave.

1016.comment: Where the Springs Return: Viramdra and Karya
1016.content: Two Sumeru scholars the Traveler meets in the People of the Springs. Viramdra, of the Akademiya's Spantamad Darshan, studies ores and minerals, has a blunt manner, and has lost earlier research to theft; he is driven by the belief that only a tangible result can prove his worth. Karya is his assistant, apologises for him, and eventually becomes the person who talks him down. Both travel with Mualani on the journey and part as friends of the Traveler's party.

1017.content: The top-ranked guide of the People of the Springs, who boasts of having been to the mysterious island alone and of having found rare crystals in an underground ruin. He turns Viramdra away as unskilled, then recommends Mualani to him, which Nuu suggests was because he thought she could not reach the island and so could not expose him. Nuu says Koolau never completed the trip, though Koolau denies it.

1018.comment: Where the Springs Return: Nuu's Choice
1018.content: Nuu is Mualani's teacher. He reached the mysterious island long before her and, with his companions, chose to tell no one so that the legend could keep inspiring young guides. He gives Mualani a talisman made from an unusual Spinel Fruit that turns out to match the fruit growing in the underground cave, and takes it back after she completes the journey. He tells her that a guide's duty is to deliver clients safely, not to prove anything.

1019.comment: Where the Springs Return: The Island Scam
1019.content: A small ring of tribespeople, including Kaulu and Kaeho, who sold tourists fake guided trips to the mysterious island, with photos and gear sold at inflated prices and receipts written in ink that faded. They claimed the fees as travel expenses so that the money was hard to prosecute, and used false names. Amina asked the Traveler and Paimon to pose as victims and gather evidence. Kaulu was caught after his fake island reveal.

key: A Commission From the Curatorium of Secrets
Return Home, Children of the Desert
1020.content:
Where Waves Meet the Reef (also: Nod-Krai Trade Expo event, A Commission From the Curatorium of Secrets, Encirclement of Bullets and Silk, Toys for the Children, Return Home, Children of the Desert, Tales of Many): The expo's one firm rule is that there must be no violence. The Traveler registers three headline exhibitors (Beidou, Navia with Clorinde, and Aino with Ineffa), then brokers a deal in which Yelan and Chevreuse may run their sting provided they do nothing that wrecks the expo and the Traveler takes part in every operation. The sting catches a ring of agents, but it also exposes Ashvapati, a Sumeru-born former Akademiya researcher who, by his own account, once designed weapons for a desert Eremite band that were turned against that band. He had lured the investigators to Nod-Krai to reach the man he blames, Sennedjem.

Plot: Part I: Nefer hires the Traveler and Paimon to help Jahoda coordinate the Nod-Krai Trade Expo, whose one rule is no violence. They bring in Beidou (selling an upgraded Guizhong Ballista), Navia with Clorinde (a Fontaine pneuma and ousia relay device) and Aino with Ineffa (blueprints for the Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots). Yelan and Chevreuse reveal that their goods are bait for the same international arms ring; Nefer lets them proceed so long as the expo's protected deals are not disturbed and the Traveler joins every operation.
Part II: Yelan, Chevreuse and their allies trap the ring's buyer aboard the Flagship while the other agents are rounded up. The Traveler subdues the buyer and Chevreuse corrals a runaway agent.
Part III: Beidou's prototype ballistas vanish. The trail leads to Ashvapati, the guild member guarding three orphaned children, whose letter confesses a past as an Akademiya exile who designed weapons for a desert Eremite band that were turned against it.
Epilogue: Ashvapati lures Sennedjem, the man he blames, to a meeting and plans to die with him under a salvo of rockets. Beidou's ship turns the rockets into fireworks, Sennedjem is arrested, Ashvapati is spared charges but expelled from the guild, and Dori sells the children a gemstone that grows an oasis.

Revelations: The mastermind of the arms ring is Sennedjem, a former Eremite who sold weapons to the very band that had sheltered him, and who now poses as a Fontaine philanthropist. Ashvapati, the children's guardian and a Voynich Guild member, is a former Kshahrewar researcher who designed those weapons and tracked Sennedjem for years; he lied to the guild about almost everything but his desert origins. He planned to die with Sennedjem but is talked down. Nefer's home is the desert too, she says, and she hopes his story shows another way of life there; she names Lesser Lord Kusanali as a reason the Sumeru of today is changing.

Characters: Nefer, who runs the Curatorium of Secrets, hires the Traveler and Paimon. Jahoda is the harried Voynich Guild manager and the event's reward character. Beidou, Navia, Clorinde, Chevreuse and Yelan carry the investigation, and Aino and Ineffa supply the defense bots. Ashvapati, Ati, Neb and Raya form the central family, and Dori is the Sumeru merchant who helps resolve it. Sennedjem is the antagonist, and Khaemwaset, Ashvapati's rescuer, appears only in flashback. Tarno is a messenger, and the ring's agents are nameless.

Consequences: The ring's agents and Sennedjem are taken into custody by Fontaine's Special Security and Surveillance Patrol (Maison Gardiennage) to face a public trial; Yelan considers her objective met. Ashvapati is not charged by the Fontaine authorities and is expelled from the Voynich Guild by Nefer, who urges him to take the children back to the desert. He accepts the oasis gemstone for the children. The expo ends as an unusually memorable one in Nefer's judgement.

Placement: A Version 6.5 (Luna VI) flagship event, running 27 April to 14 May 2026 in three phases (27 April, 29 April and 1 May). Players needed Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom; the Archon Quest True Moon was recommended first. The story is set in Nod-Krai and mentions Sumeru under Lesser Lord Kusanali. The Part I side quests are concurrent, and Parts II and III each begin two in-game days after the previous part.

1021.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Nod-Krai Trade Expo
1021.content: An annual market held on the shoreline southeast of Nasha Town once shipping routes reopen, organised by the Voynich Guild and billed as the biggest "legal" black market in Teyvat. The town began as an unregulated black market, and the expo preserves that spirit of unrestricted trade.
