The guild takes a cut from seller and buyer and promises safety to all, so violence is forbidden, but deals struck outside the expo are not protected. This 6.5 edition was unusually large.

1022.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Ashvapati and Sennedjem
1022.content: Ashvapati is a Voynich Guild member and guardian of Ati, Neb and Raya. By his own letter he is an expelled Kshahrewar scholar who was taken in by the Eremite chief Khaemwaset and built toys for children until Sennedjem, a trader who had left the oasis and then returned, convinced him to design Ruin Drake lures. Sennedjem sold the designs to enemies of the oasis, the camp was burned, and Ashvapati saved only three children. Sennedjem later became a rich arms supplier and, by his own claim, a Fontaine philanthropist. All of this is told by Ashvapati and Sennedjem themselves.

1023.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Ati, Neb and Raya
1023.content: Three orphaned children, raised by Ashvapati, who run a toy booth at the expo. Neb loves building mechanisms and wants an Aino bot blueprint; Ati prefers practical purchases such as clothing; Raya hopes everyone can stop arguing. Jahoda promises to look after them. They are not involved in the arms ring, and in the end they ask Ashvapati to remain their uncle even after learning the whole truth.

1024.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Yelan and Chevreuse joint operation
1024.content: Yelan of Liyue's Ministry of Civil Affairs and Chevreuse of Fontaine's Special Security and Surveillance Patrol come to Nod-Krai after the same international arms-trading network, each carrying a trap product (Beidou's ballista as the bait). After Nefer's mediated deal they pool intelligence: the Traveler must be included in every move, and the expo's own rules must not be broken. They capture twenty agents and the buyer without casualties, then pursue Ashvapati as the best lead. Afterwards each returns to their duties; Chevreuse praises working together.

1025.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Dori's oasis gemstone
1025.content: A gemstone made by the mage Alice which, planted in the ground, grows a spring and then an oasis even in a desert. At the expo Dori sells it for the price Alice set, "whatever keeps the kids happy", which she fixes as what Ati, Neb and Raya earned. In the Tales of Many, Alice and Nicole test a pricing scheme paid in virtues like courage and kindness rather than Mora, which sold little.

1026.content:
Whirling Waltz (also: Whirling Waltz Event, Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland event, Eclectic Escapades, Movie Masterpieces, Mellow Manor): Whirling Waltz is the Version 5.6 spring flagship event. After overhearing old friends at a Court of Fontaine newsstand, the Traveler and Paimon are invited to run the Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland, a film-themed amusement park. Friends from across Teyvat arrive as visitors and consultants, and the story is told in light, character-focused Friendly Encounters rather than a quest chain.

The park has three attractions: Eclectic Escapades, Movie Masterpieces and Mellow Manor, plus a Theme Restaurant run by the chef Escoffier. The player upgrades attractions, hires staff and chooses theme dishes to raise revenue. The event's reward was the bow Sequence of Solitude.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon manage the Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland. As the park grows, Varesa from Natlan sets up a fruit stall, Sigewinne and Lynette become consultants for Mellow Manor and Eclectic Escapades, Dehya's mercenary band partners with them, and Furina becomes consultant for Movie Masterpieces and invites the Traveler and Paimon to co-direct a film with Escoffier.

**Varesa.** The Natlan orchard owner comes to promote her fruit after a letter from Escoffier. She goes shopping for clockwork parts for Iansan's gym equipment, tries Movie Masterpieces and then opens the Vibrant Orchard stall.

**Sigewinne.** The Fortress of Meropide's head nurse likes animated films and shows them to inmates. She becomes Mellow Manor's consultant after being called away to treat an inmate who tried to copy a film recipe.

**Lynette and Lyney.** Lynette arrives alone because Lyney is exhausted from watching a director's horror films. They coax him to the park, and Lynette consults for Eclectic Escapades.

**Dehya.** She was a guest star in a Fontaine adventure film, and the Blazing Beasts agree to pass desert commissions to the Traveler and Paimon.

**Furina.** The park's patron surveys visitors and becomes consultant for Movie Masterpieces.

Characters: Traveler, Paimon, Furina, Escoffier, Varesa, Sigewinne, Lynette, Lyney and Dehya.

Also Giustina, Iansan, Uncle Scimitar and Freminet (mentioned in dialogue), plus many staff recruited at the Staff Center.

Consequences: No lasting plot change is shown. Dehya's offer of Blazing Beasts commissions and Furina's plan for a film with Escoffier are left open.

Placement: Released in Version 5.6 and run from 9 May to 26 May 2025 (server time) in three phases (9, 11 and 13 May). It is a standalone event set in Fontaine, after the Fontinalia film festival of Roses and Muskets. The next Fontaine summer event, Sunny Summer Fontinalia, comes in Version 6.7.

1027.content: A film-themed amusement park in Fontaine named after Furina's friend Surintendante Chevalmarin. Its attractions are Eclectic Escapades, Movie Masterpieces and Mellow Manor. The Traveler and Paimon work as managers; Escoffier cooks for the Theme Restaurant.

1028.content: Dehya's mercenary band passes far-flung, high-pay, high-risk commissions in the region west of the Hypostyle Desert, north of the Desert of Hadramaveth, east of Ardravi Valley and south of the Ashavan Realm to the Traveler and Paimon, who will receive notice by letters through the Adventurers' Guild.

1029.comment: Whirling Waltz: Fortress of Meropide film screenings
1029.content: Under the Fortress's new regulations, well-behaved inmates can spend Credit Coupons to watch films up to three times a week. Sigewinne runs the projector and has shown animated films such as My Neighbor Kokoro and the long Dom and Cherry series.

key: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking
1030.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking
1030.content:
White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking (also: Chapter VII Act III, Snezhnaya Archon Quest Act III): Chapter VII Act III of the Archon Quest. The Tsaritsa Anastasya, back in Zapolyarny Palace after killing the monster behind the snowstorms, suspends Project Stuzha because of a curse of death. The Traveler finally meets her, learns why she wants the Gnoses, and helps a Seal of Life plan that draws out Rhinedottir.

The act has three quests: Light and Shadow, Intertwined; Sparks Converging Upon the Tundra; and One Move Left to Make. It places the Traveler in the Tsaritsa's court for the first time, shows her daily memory-recording habit and the sealed relic left by the Third Descender, introduces Vesna's authority over life, and ends with a theft in the Northland Bank vault. Released in version 7.1.

Plot: Tartaglia tells the Traveler and Paimon that suspending Project Stuzha has lightened the Veche, and arranges an audience. Danica, the Tsaritsa's head maid and personal attendant, tests the Traveler over a game of Mora. At court Anastasya cancels all investigation of the Traveler and speaks to them privately. Pierro and Mitya show a plan to counter the curse using Vesna's power over life. When Seals of Life go missing from Northland Bank, the Traveler and Vesna find a creature stealing them, and Rhinedottir arrives, as the Tsaritsa had intended.

Across three quests the Traveler is tested by Danica, attends the Tsaritsa's court, hears why she seeks the Gnoses and sees the seal left by the Third Descender. Pierro's Mirror of Remembrance reveals Ronova's collaboration with Rhinedottir, and Vesna's power of life inspires the Seal of Life collection. When seals are stolen from Northland Bank, the Traveler and Vesna find a creature of the Ruler of Life, and Rhinedottir arrives, as the Tsaritsa had planned.

Revelations: Project Stuzha is on hold because of the curse of death. The Tsaritsa wants all seven Gnoses to unlock a seal left by the Third Descender and to gain strength against the Heavenly Principles. Her authority is love, which she refuses to use.

The Tsaritsa records every day with a transcription prism because she does not trust memory; like a Stellar Linchpin, the prism holds the Third Descender's power and is free from certain laws of Teyvat. Vesna carries the Ruler of Life's authority, via the first Vila. Ronova used a loophole in the Heavenly Principles' monitoring cycles with Rhinedottir's help to kill and revive without being caught. Seals of Life are memory bubbles that could resist death.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Tartaglia, Danica, Vesna, the Tsaritsa Anastasya, Pierro, Mitya, Pantalone, Sandrone, Rhinedottir and Naberius.

Others: Pulcinella (court report), Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa (volunteers), Councilor Belozersky, Pevtsova of Svetloledovka, the suspect Avaz, and Lyney, Lynette and Freminet (briefly, at the end). Capitano is mentioned. Ronova and Asmoday are discussed but absent.

Consequences: The Traveler gains unrestricted access to Zapolyarny Palace. Project Mistilteinn waits on a way to counter the curse of death. Rhinedottir has agreed to meet the Tsaritsa again in seven days.

All seals go back to their owners; Pantalone returns to Vesna a beacon made from a sample of her power. Avaz is handed to Fatui Internal Affairs. The act leads directly into A Rekviem for the Underworld.

Placement: Third act of Chapter VII, between Wraith's Nocturne and A Rekviem for the Underworld. Released in version 7.1.

The act requires Adventure Rank 18; its place in the chain is Act II, then Act III, then Act IV. Acts I and II are 7.0 content and Acts III and IV are 7.1 content.

1031.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Court at Zapolyarny Palace
1031.content: At the Traveler's first court session the Tsaritsa Anastasya hears reports from Pulcinella and Mitya, halts Project Mistilteinn until Ronova is dealt with, and orders all investigations of the Traveler to end. She asks the Traveler for the Pyro Gnosis, explains her aim to face the Heavenly Principles, shows a seal left by the Third Descender, and states that her authority is love but she refuses to use it.

1032.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Mirror of Remembrance
1032.content: A massive prism in the Armory Palace used to extract memory fragments for review. Through it Pierro shows that Ronova collaborated with Rhinedottir. It is distinct from the transcription prism with which Anastasya records each day because she distrusts her own memory.

1033.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Seal of Life
1033.content: A bubble holding an impactful memory, extracted by Vesna through her small authority of life, that could defy death if enough are gathered. Donation is obligatory for officials and nobles and voluntary for the public through Northland Bank. The collection draws a thief, a creature made by the Ruler of Life, and ends with Rhinedottir restoring every seal.

1034.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Vault confrontation at Northland Bank
1034.content: Vesna and the Traveler infiltrate the bank's deep vaults, meeting Pantalone, who had anticipated them. The False Horned Steed drains the seals through portals until the Tsaritsa freezes it. Rhinedottir lets it escape and reclaims the stolen power. The Tsaritsa offers her information on Asmoday and a meeting in seven days.

1035.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Danica
1035.content: The Tsaritsa's head maid and trusted personal attendant, from the Postelnitskaya family, which has served the Tsaritsa for three generations. She tests the Traveler with a Mora game taught to her by her mentor Capitano, and later apologises and brings hot milk. The Tsaritsa persuaded her mother and grandmother to let her travel abroad (her father was a mercenary) before she returned when her homeland needed her.

1036.content:
Windblume's Breath (also: Windblume's Breath event, Windblume 2023 event, Floral Pursuit, Ballads of Breeze, Breezy Snapshots): The event's in-game blurb frames it as the honeyed scents of the Windblume Festival wafting on the wind again, a festival of romance in the city of freedom, with a note found by accident leading the Traveler on another fantastical journey. Floral Pursuit introduces "Floral Chess", a new game created by the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild; Ballads of Breeze has seven songs and a score editor; Breezy Snapshots has nine photo requests for a photobook. Rewards include Primogems, a Crown of Insight and the Claymore Mailed Flower.

Plot: No continuous storyline is documented. Each segment is a self-contained activity. Floral Pursuit is a six-stage challenge (Ordered, Inverted, Observant, Obstructing, Shimmering and Pursuing Wind), unlocking daily from 3 March, in which the player collects Bloom Balloons while avoiding Ersatz Balloons. Ballads of Breeze unlocks one song per day, and Breezy Snapshots has three sets of three photo requests from Fassben.

Revelations: The event reveals nothing new about the main story. Its only lore weight is the Mailed Flower's text: the Windblume as a symbol, once lost to time, now a sign of love and gladness in times of peace, with a legend of a nameless shepherd who handed out "flowers" and an account that a noble took Ludi Harpastum away.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon take part. Fassben the Adventurer is the commissioner of Breezy Snapshots. Cyrus is named in his remarks. The Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild created the Floral Chess game used in Floral Pursuit. No other named characters have verified roles.

Consequences: No lasting consequences for the story. The Mailed Flower, a four-star Claymore with the passive Whispers of Wind and Flower and Elemental Mastery as its second stat, could be earned during the event. Collei's Windblume and a Windblume Kamera were also among the rewards.

Placement: Released in Version 3.5 as a Flagship Event, requiring Adventure Rank 18 and the Prologue Act III "Song of the Dragon and Freedom". For the best experience, Chapter III Act V "Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises" and Albedo's "Princeps Cretaceus Chapter" Act I were recommended; the Quick Start option let players without them enter anyway. It follows the earlier Windblume event "Invitation of Windblume" (Version 1.4), whose title is also a Ballads of Breeze song.

1037.content: A Windblume's Breath activity in which the Traveler collects Bloom Balloons and evades Ersatz Balloons across six daily-unlocking stages. It is described as Floral Chess, a new game made by the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild.

1038.content: The event's seven-song rhythm performance mode, with a score editor, Windsong Lyre, Floral Zither and Festive Drum interface styles, and shareable scores.

1039.content: Fassben the Adventurer is making a photobook of Mondstadt for the festival and asks the Traveler to photograph set locations with a Kamera. The nine requests, in three sets, cover Mondstadt, Dadaupa Gorge, Stormterror's Lair and Dragonspine.

key: Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence
1040.comment: Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence
1040.content:
Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence (also: Dornman Port lighthouse ghost quest): A light world quest at Dornman Port, Windrest Peak. The old lighthouse's alarm keeps flashing, the keeper Winslow is terrified of ghosts, and the tavern regular Odolf asks the Traveler to investigate the ruins under the tower. The cause is an Eye of the Storm drawn by a tampered mechanism.

It begins at the group of regulars by the Devil's Cut tavern and ends at the lighthouse base. The quest requires Song of the Dragon and Freedom and was released in Version 6.5. It mixes mild humour with a small moral about honesty.

Plot: At the tavern the regulars say the lighthouse alarm keeps flickering and that locals whisper of the ghosts of old knights. Odolf, who lives nearby, asks the Traveler to help Winslow. They enter the ruins beneath the lighthouse, block drafts, solve the alarm doors, survive a cave-in, and defeat an Eye of the Storm. Odolf then tells Winslow the ghosts have calmed down.

Lennart and Matthew tell the story: Winslow first shouted that the Abyss had come, the Knights searched several times and found nothing, and the alarm still flickered. Odolf, back from a business trip in Snezhnaya, wants to check for himself. Winslow, panicking, has locked the main doors, so Odolf leads the Traveler through another entrance known only to locals. In the ruins the Traveler pushes crates and breaks a rock pile to block wind currents that trip the alarm, fights Hydro and Electro Slimes in a cemetery, and glides over a gate with Anemograna. A strong wind falls from above: an Eye of the Storm. After it is defeated the alarm stops. Odolf tells the shaken Winslow that the wind was the unhappy fallen knights, now soothed, and covers a loud cave-in with a story about "super spiritual arm wrestling". Winslow says he has been tending the graves, and Odolf encourages him to keep doing so.

Revelations: The "ghost" is Odolf's own doing.

In the optional post-quest talk, Odolf confesses he adjusted the alarm mechanism and added a lure for elemental creatures, meaning only to frighten Winslow a little so he would give up moving the old graves of knights who died fighting the Abyss. He thought a few Anemo Slimes would drift away, then left on business to Snezhnaya, and the lure instead drew an Eye of the Storm. He did not want Winslow to end up so frightened.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Odolf, Winslow, Lennart and Matthew.

Odolf is a local who talks in flowery proverbs and knows the lighthouse's secrets; Winslow lives at the old lighthouse and is anxious and prickly; Lennart and Matthew are tavern regulars, with Lennart staying out of it after too much drink. The Knights of Favonius appear only as having searched the ruins before.

Consequences: The alarm stops, Winslow calms down and keeps cleaning the graves, and Odolf's secret stays between him and the Traveler. A teleport waypoint in the Knights of Favonius Ruins opens.

Placement: Released in Version 6.5 (Luna VI, 2026-04-08), set in Windrest Peak and requiring Song of the Dragon and Freedom. It is a stand-alone local story with no bearing on the main plots.

1041.content:
Within the Sequence (also: Within the Sequence world quest, Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array terminal): A very short Version 6.7 world quest at Nuur Stone Circle on the Frost Moon. When the Ancient Moon's Remnant there reaches level 5, the Traveler examines an ancient terminal that greets them with the titles of old Natlan rulers.

It follows Origin of the Sequence, which repaired the terminal. It has one step, no combat and no named NPC. The wiki treats the name as unofficial.

Plot: The Traveler raises the Ancient Moon's Remnant to level 5 and then examines the terminal. It runs a self-diagnostic, reports that lockdown is lifted and says an unreadable number of cycles has passed.

The terminal's greeting varies. Variants welcome the Master of Flame and Wisdom, Xiuhcoatl, and his companion, the Sovereign Ruler of Natlantea, either Ix Raq'lapuj Chue'q Buluk or Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon, or greet only one of them. It then gives a general welcome to "friends from afar" to its data array.

Revelations: The quest answers nothing. It shows that this storage array, labelled No. 59 Ia-Ilimmu in the prelude, recognises Xiuhcoatl and Natlantean sovereigns by title, a link between the Frost Moon works and Natlantea that the quest does not explain.

Characters: The Traveler only; the ancient terminal speaks. Xiuhcoatl and the Natlantean sovereigns are named but absent.

Consequences: Completing the quest unlocks the achievement The Inner Light. No other change to the world is recorded.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII) as Frost Moon content. It follows Origin of the Sequence and requires the Ancient Moon's Remnant at Nuur Stone Circle to be raised to level 5.

1042.content:
Wraith's Nocturne (also: Chapter VII Act II, Snezhnaya Archon Quest Act II, Curse of Death theater incident): Wraith's Nocturne is Act II of Chapter VII, the Snezhnaya Archon Quest. At a rehearsal of the ballet "Spirit Seeker" in the Korolevskiy Theater, a blizzard traps the audience, among them Odette, who is secretly the saboteur "Lelek", the Fatui Alyosha and the singer Vodyanitsa. Each night two people die without a mark, and the Traveler relives each death in a dream of climbing a spiral staircase. The cause is the Curse of Death of Ronova, Ruler of Death. In the end Pierro explains why Paimon was taken to the Armory Palace.

The act follows Everwinter Without Mercy and precedes White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking. It was released in version 7.0 and requires Adventure Rank 18. It has five quests: The White Curtain Falls, Lelek's Confession, Winter's Mysterious Silence, Wraith's Nocturne (the quest) and Mistilteinn.

Plot: The Traveler attends the theater hoping to find Tonia, Tartaglia's sister, and to ask about Lelek. A blizzard seals everyone in. Two people die each night, the Traveler dreams of each death beforehand, and gradually the dead turn out to be ghosts or fellow victims of the Curse of Death. Ronova reveals herself, is driven off, and everyone wakes with no memory. The Traveler then rescues Paimon from the Armory Palace, where Pierro explains the curse and Project Mistilteinn.

Trapped by the blizzard, the group finds two dead on the first morning and Odette admits she is Lelek. Further deaths follow each night; the cast discover that Shram and the girl called Tonia (really Ptashka) are ghosts, that Mitya has died without knowing it, and that Alyosha is Ronova in disguise. Ronova kills Odette and Chugunov, is struck by the Traveler and Mitya, and vanishes, and everyone wakes with no memory. In the Armory Palace, Pierro shields Paimon from Ronova and explains the Curse of Death and Project Mistilteinn.

Revelations: - Odette is Lelek, and publicly admits it in the theater; she trained under Signora.
- Ronova, the Ruler of Death, has been manipulating the theater through a Curse of Death, and her symbol is a red eye.
- Some of the people in the theater were not alive: Shram, a water imp's boyfriend from over four hundred years ago, and "Tonia", whose real name is Ptashka, a girl who had Frostblight. Mitya had also died earlier at the Armory Palace without remembering it.
- The Curse of Death is triggered by moments of technological progress that could threaten the Heavenly Principles, killing everyone nearby; the revived forget what happened.
- A Descender's soul cannot be carried into the ley lines.
- The Fatui, with the Tsaritsa, intend to challenge the Heavenly Principles.

Characters: Traveler: dreams each death, wakes after dying, and joins the Fatui's side to protect Paimon. Paimon: absent in the theater, missed by the Traveler, then the object of Ronova's and Pierro's interest. Odette: a ballerina and secret Lelek, trained under Signora. Alyosha: a Fatui whose appearance Ronova wears. Vodyanitsa: the singer and the Traveler's "Guardian Angel". Mitya: a researcher tied to Project Mistilteinn, dead without realising, whose carved eye proves decisive. "Tonia" / Ptashka: a ghost girl who answered to the name Tonia, believing her own brother had chosen it as a code name; she is not Tartaglia's sister. Valeriy: an Armory Palace officer escorting Mitya, who organises watches. Chugunov: a merchant who knew Tonia was a ghost. Ronova: the Ruler of Death. Pierro: arrives at the end. The Tsaritsa, Vesna and Danica appear in the closing scene.

Consequences: The Curse of Death is understood and the Traveler has now met Ronova in person. Project Mistilteinn is paused until Ronova can be dealt with. Odette and Chugunov survive; Chugunov shuts down the Iskra Manufacturing Plant. The Traveler allies with Pierro, and the Tsaritsa returns to Zapolyarny Palace.

Placement: Chapter VII Act II, after Everwinter Without Mercy (Act I) and before White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking. Released in version 7.0 with Act I. Requires Adventure Rank 18.

1043.comment: Wraith's Nocturne: The Korolevskiy Theater Incident
1043.content: During a "Spirit Seeker" rehearsal a blizzard trapped the audience, and each night two people died with no wounds. Some of the people present were ghosts. The Traveler experienced the deaths as spiral-staircase dreams chased by a black mist. It ended when Ronova revealed herself, was struck by the Traveler and Mitya, and everyone woke in their seats with no memory.

1044.content: In the theater a girl who answered to the name Tonia was actually a ghost: a child ill with Frostblight whose brother Razyk had snuck her out of hospital to see a show, where she fell asleep. When the Traveler said her brother had sent them and called her Tonia, she assumed her brother had chosen it as a code name. Chugunov knew and treated her as his late daughter Iskra. She tells the Traveler her real name is Ptashka and leaves. The real Tonia, Tartaglia's sister, is introduced in the epilogue.

1045.content: A mercenary who understands Vodyanitsa's water imp song, found to be a ghost from over four hundred years ago who died in the theater protecting his water imp girlfriend. He apologises for the deaths he caused and leaves into the storm.

key: Scions of the Canopy Tribal Chronicle
1046.content:
Yupanqui's Turnfire (also: Scions of the Canopy Tribal Chronicle, A Mysterious Visitor From Huitztlan, A Hero's Rite, Kinich's Deal, I, Flame Bearer, The Last Turnfire Night): The Tribal Chronicles chapter of the Scions of the Canopy, which also serves as Kinich's story quest. The tribe holds Turnfire Night to honour the hero Burkina and his Saurian companion Kongamato, who fought the Abyss, and to keep the Abyssal energy still within Kongamato stable. This year the ritual is in trouble, and the tribe wants the Saurian hunter Kinich to bear the flame. The Traveler is drawn into the matter, and Kinich solves it his own way through a deal with an Abyss Lector.

The chapter has three acts: A Mysterious Visitor From Huitztlan, A Hero's Rite and Kinich's Deal. It unlocks after the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame in the Archon Quest. The chapter title refers to the Turnfire, the ritual flame; a book called "Yupanqui's Turnfire" also appears in Act III.

Plot: Act I. At the foot of Coatepec Mountain the Traveler and Paimon meet two children of the Scions of the Canopy, Huni and Toba, who are looking for baby Yumkasaurs and were told by a man named Sanka that helpers were coming. Ajaw is already with the Yumkasaur whelp Pocchi and explains that the babies' mother was overcome by Abyssal energy, attacked her tribe and her young, and died. The children say they had been telling Sanka stories about their tribe, including that Kinich is the current Turnfire bearer, when he fled. Learning that the visitors know Kinich, the children point them to the village.

Act II. In the village Trinidad, Huni's father, first doubts the visitors but warms to them when Huni says they ate with Kinich. He explains Turnfire Night, honouring Burkina and Kongamato, and the current crisis: five months after the last ceremony Kongamato has shown signs of instability, and in its rage it attacked Trinidad's own Saurian companion Nanna, whom the tribe believes died. The tribe had hoped Kinich would be the flame-bearer but he named a price, which they took as a refusal, so Trinidad asks the Traveler to take that place. At the same time Kinich and Ajaw confront Sanka. The Traveler completes a stage of the ritual at the summit of Coatepec Mountain while Kinich watches in secret.

Act III. Kinich asks the Traveler to find out what Trinidad's ritual really involves, then explains his own plan. Over the next day the chapter shifts to a search for Ponche's stolen book, a ruins mural and a meeting in a cave where Kinich reveals he has struck a deal with Sanka, who is really the Abyss Lector Enjou. On Turnfire Night Kinich produces the Beastly Rift device, Trinidad destroys the device in a panic, and Kongamato wakes and has to be calmed by the Traveler and Kinich using Kinich's Ancient Name.

Revelations: Kinich bears the Ancient Name Malipo; from the memories he has of Burkina, he concludes that Kongamato killed Burkina and wants to die, and that the tribe's honour for it hides this. Sanka, the stranger who pumped the children for stories about Kinich, is Enjou, an Abyss Lector who admits to being only a clerk in the Abyss Order. The Turnfire ritual is not a normal ceremony of respect but a means of stabilising Abyssal energy in Kongamato, and the elders disagree on whether to destroy it.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon are the viewpoint pair. Kinich, the Saurian hunter who names a price for every job, drives the plot and keeps his reasoning to himself until late. Ajaw, bound to Kinich by contract, sides with Sanka for part of the story but the betrayal is bait. Trinidad is a worried elder whose companion Nanna is hurt; Wayna is another elder who values Kongamato as tribal heritage. Huni and Toba are children of the tribe. Enjou, under the alias Sanka, is the Abyss Lector.

Consequences: Kongamato survives and agrees to remain in its ruined state to train future heroes. Trinidad is badly burned but expected to recover. Kinich owes the Traveler a favour and says he will do anything for them in future. Enjou leaves, Nanna is returned to Huni's family, and the Beastly Rift plan is spent. The tribe records the story of Malipo's manifestation, preserved by a scholar of Ancient Names.

Placement: Release order: all three acts came with Version 5.0; the wiki gives the event window as 2024-09-17 to 2024-10-08. Story order: the chapter requires only the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame in the Archon Quest part Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn, and the wiki lists the Inazuma quest From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku as a recommended earlier quest for Act I. Trinidad recognises the Traveler from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

1047.content: A ceremony of the Scions of the Canopy that honours the hero Burkina and his Saurian companion Kongamato, both of whom fought the Abyss. Burkina died and Kongamato was left with Abyssal energy that lets it live unnaturally long but is highly unstable, so the ritual flame, the Turnfire, is used to keep that energy stable. In the year of the chapter, five months after the last ceremony, Kongamato showed signs of instability and its rage hurt Trinidad's Saurian companion Nanna, whom the tribe believed it killed.

1048.content: The Yumkasaur companion of the hero Burkina, afflicted by Abyssal energy in the fight that killed him. It lives unnaturally long, and the tribe treats it as a source of history, pride and faith. Kinich believes it killed Burkina and wishes to die. After the Last Turnfire Night it agrees to live with its shame and allow Kinich to use its ruined vessel for training future heroes, and a transparent shell forms around it that the elders interpret as insulation against Abyssal energy.

1049.content: Two elders of the Scions of the Canopy. Trinidad, Huni's father, wants the Abyssal energy purged from Kongamato even though it would probably kill it, and is badly burned when he rushes to the Turnfire. Wayna endorses the Traveler's participation but refuses to let Kongamato be killed, and afterwards reports the elders' interpretation of the shell around it.

1050.content: Kinich's plan to contain Kongamato. He discovered Beastly Rifts, hidden spaces opened by the Abyss, while hunting riftwolves. In exchange for being left alone in his historical research, the Abyss Lector Enjou, who had been using the alias Sanka, supplied one. The plan was to clear a rift and put Kongamato in it. Trinidad smashed the device on Turnfire Night, and the problem was then settled by Kinich's Ancient Name instead.
